title: surface-review(machines): fence destroy exit snapshot writes and nested effects to their frame incarnation
description:
Repair the machine destroy-time exit helper so its snapshot write and nested effect walk remain bound to the exact frame incarnation that entered teardown. One confirmed P1 correctness defect remains: a synchronous callback can replace frame A with same-id B, after which A's exit helper overwrites B's machine snapshot and executes A-derived effects in B. Preserve the existing live-owner and eventless teardown behavior; no new public API or ownership model is needed.

Scope and revision

- Owned slice: implementation/machines/**, including src/, test/, deps.edn and package boundary.
- Reviewed revision: 1c9ff9697b0fa3a018c7a4371e02983ad2e79b2f (2026-09-12 shared checkout baseline).
- SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2.
- WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).
- Exactly one consolidated review bead under rf2-fzbj; this issue remains OPEN because remediation is required.

Coverage and exclusions

Inspected the public plain-map transition projection in src/re_frame/machines.cljc and internal result.cljc; sampled transition.cljc's callback execution/data merging, action failure propagation, active exit cascade, hierarchy geometry, transition commit and fixed-point draining; sampled parallel.cljc's public engine/birth boundaries and destroy dispatcher; traced lifecycle_fx/destroy.cljc, exit_cascade.cljc, teardown.cljc, update_snapshot.cljc and the relevant finalize.cljc path; inspected runtime path constructors, timer scheduling/cancellation/reconciliation entry points and node-key validation; inspected deps.edn's optional-artifact dependency and publish configuration.

Read relevant existing regression fixtures, especially machine_destroy_tail_incarnation_fence_test.clj and destroy_exit_cascade_test.clj, alongside the test inventory for rollback, active-path geometry, raised-event FIFO, timer ownership, hydration and actor identity. Followed core's frame.cljc exact/bare partition writes and fx.cljc nested walk token behavior to verify this module's concrete call path. Checked the relevant Spec 005 action effect map, destroy, cancellation and explicit orphan-lifecycle contracts. This was focused source inspection, not a claim to exhaustively review every transition branch, join protocol, grammar production, conformance fixture or packaging deployment. CLJS/browser behavior and real-clock races were not executed.

Confirmed finding 1 — P1: exit-cascade commits and fires effects after its frame incarnation is lost

Source:
- implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/exit_cascade.cljc:82-113, specifically the changed-snapshot branch at 104-106 and tokenless nested do-fx at 111-113.
- implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/destroy.cljc:238-243 invokes this helper and checks owner loss only AFTER it returns.
- implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc:1923-1925 emits synchronous :rf.machine/action-ran after the authored action returns, making a trace listener a reachable replacement boundary even when the authored action itself is pure.
- Supporting core behavior: frame.cljc:2055-2065's bare swap-partition! resolves the current id and writes it; fx.cljc:1969-1976's three-arity do-fx installs a nil exact-frame token. These core APIs work as called; the repair belongs to the machines caller.

Trigger and minimal scenario:
1. Register a machine whose active state's :exit returns {:data {:exit-marker :from-a} :fx [[:review/effect :from-a]]}.
2. Materialize actor :review/actor in frame :review/frame incarnation A with {:state :running :data {:owner :a}}.
3. Register a synchronous trace listener for :rf.machine/action-ran with :phase :destroy-exit. Once only, it destroys A, creates same-id frame B, and installs B's actor snapshot {:state :running :data {:owner :b}}.
4. Call destroy-machine-fx for the actor under A's bound event-owner token, the same ownership context the ordinary router effect drain supplies.
5. Observe B's snapshot and the exact frame incarnation in which the custom effect runs.

Reproducer (process-local JVM, no source/build/dependency writes):

```clojure
(require '[re-frame.core :as rf]
         '[re-frame.frame :as rf.frame]
         '[re-frame.machines]
         '[re-frame.machines.lifecycle-fx.destroy :as rf.destroy]
         '[re-frame.machines.test-support :as rf.support]
         '[re-frame.substrate.plain-atom :as rf.plain]
         '[re-frame.trace.tooling :as rf.trace])
((rf.support/make-reset-runtime-fixture {:adapter rf.plain/adapter})
 (fn []
   (let [fid :review/frame actor :review/actor
         path [:rf.runtime/machines :snapshots actor]
         once? (atom false) effects (atom []) token-a (atom nil)]
     (rf/make-frame {:id fid})
     (reset! token-a (rf.frame/frame-incarnation-token fid))
     (rf/reg-fx :review/effect
       (fn [ctx value]
         (swap! effects conj
                [value (if (identical? @token-a
                           (rf.frame/frame-incarnation-token (:frame ctx)))
                         :a :b)])))
     (rf/reg-machine :review/actor
       {:initial :running
        :states {:running
                 {:exit (fn [_] {:data {:exit-marker :from-a}
                                 :fx [[:review/effect :from-a]]})}}})
     (rf.frame/swap-runtime-db! fid assoc-in path
       {:state :running :data {:owner :a}})
     (rf.trace/register-listener! :review/replace
       (fn [ev]
         (when (and (= :rf.machine/action-ran (:operation ev))
                    (= :destroy-exit (get-in ev [:tags :phase]))
                    (compare-and-set! once? false true))
           (rf.frame/destroy-frame! fid)
           (rf/make-frame {:id fid})
           (rf.frame/swap-runtime-db! fid assoc-in path
             {:state :running :data {:owner :b}}))))
     (rf.frame/call-with-event-owner-token fid @token-a
       #(rf.destroy/destroy-machine-fx {:frame fid} actor))
     (prn (get-in (rf.frame/frame-runtime-db-value fid) path) @effects)
     (rf.trace/unregister-listener! :review/replace))))
(shutdown-agents)
```

Run via java -cp <existing machines test classpath> clojure.main -e <code>, without invoking compilation/install tooling. The actual two executed probe variants used the existing machines/.cpcache/36AFC378842871F24A69B8CB9E79D376.cp and printed the canonical source root C:\Users\miket\code\re-frame2\implementation\machines. Both process exit codes were 0; the second probe asserted the measured defect and its live-owner control, rather than pretending that exit 0 meant the implementation passed.

Expected versus measured actual:
- Expected: B retains {:state :running :data {:owner :b}} and receives zero A-derived exit effects. Work legitimately completed in A while A existed may stand.
- Actual: B becomes {:state :running :data {:owner :a :exit-marker :from-a}}. The exact-token-labelled effect log contains one effect in A (during A's frame-destroy cleanup) and one :from-a effect in B. The latter is the defect; counting both as two effects in B would be incorrect.
- Live-owner control, with replacement disabled: final actor snapshot is nil, exactly one :from-a effect runs in A, zero in B. This verifies the required successful teardown behavior the fix must preserve.

Impact:
A valid synchronous observer that destroys/recreates a frame can lose the replacement actor's data and receive obsolete effects from the old actor. The outer destroy fence then notices A is gone and skips its later stages, leaving the newly overwritten snapshot in B. The defect also affects callers routed through the shared helper (ordinary/tracked/per-child destroy and occupied-address replacement); these variants were traced, not each independently executed. This is distinct from delayed-dispatch ownership: the reproducer uses an immediate custom effect only.

Why existing tests miss it:
machine_destroy_tail_incarnation_fence_test.clj's classified-spec helper returns (:data ctx) directly from its :exit, with no {:data ...} rider and no :fx. Consequently collect-actions makes no changed snapshot for this fixture, and neither of exit_cascade.cljc's two hazardous conditional branches runs. Its B-byte-identical assertion validates the OUTER tail, not the helper's write/effect tail. The generic destroy-exit tests exercise exits but do not combine a changed :data return and actual effect interpretation with frame replacement.

Precise repair recommendation:
Thread/capture the originating event-owner continuation and raw exact token before the exit cascade enters callback-bearing code. Recheck after the pure cascade and its synchronous traces, write the post-exit snapshot through swap-runtime-db-exact! for event-owned callers, and recheck after that callback-bearing write before starting effects. Supply the same originating token to the nested do-fx options so loss during one exit effect fences the remaining effects too. Keep the intentional eventless/frame-destroy authority explicit and preserve the currently allowed already-completed work in A. Reuse the existing destroy fence/token APIs rather than inventing another actor ownership mechanism.

Acceptance criteria:
- A JVM and CLJS regression uses a real changed {:data ...} exit result and an actual recorded custom :fx; a destroy-exit action/trace callback replaces A with B, and B stays byte-identical with zero A-derived effects.
- A separate mid-exit-effect case replaces A in the first effect and proves later exit effects and the terminal effect trace do not run against B.
- Cover loss from a synchronous container watcher during the post-exit write, including no commit-epoch bump attributed to B.
- Live-owner and eventless teardown controls retain intended exit writes/effect ordering, once-only ordinary cleanup, and snapshot removal; existing destroy-tail, finalization and frame-teardown suites remain green.
- Keep the repair in the shared exit helper/caller contract so destroy variants do not acquire divergent fences; no public grammar/API change is required.

Known work and duplicate check

Searched all current bead titles/descriptions/notes for run-child-exit, exit_cascade.cljc, exit-cascade.cljc and rf2-i4aj9c; only rf2-jqvgp and rf2-dokz matched. rf2-jqvgp is CLOSED hydration cancellation/rearm ownership work; rf2-dokz is CLOSED occupied fixed-address teardown work. Neither covers this post-exit snapshot write or tokenless nested effect walk. rf2-xjee (CLOSED) preserves shared machine definitions during teardown and remains intact; rf2-v4xjh (CLOSED) settled the self-describing public transition result and is also not reopened by this finding. Source/test comments cite historical rf2-i4aj9c for the outer destroy fence, but bd show rf2-i4aj9c returned no matching issue in the current database, so it is cited as source provenance, not as a verified extant bead. The dedicated exit helper has no recent semantic fence fix in its inspected history (latest edits include alias/comment refactors).

Validation limits and disposition

Confirmed by two process-local JVM probes, including exact-token-labelled effect observation and a live-owner control. No production edits, commits, worktree, server, installs, broad gates, CLJS compilation or browser runs. Source git status remained clean. Timer races, schema callbacks, join membership and same-frame actor-address replacement beyond the traced path were inspected only; no additional defect is asserted. No speculative risks are promoted to separate findings. Parent/root owns the durable tracker checkpoint and push.

VERDICT (worker machines-a, 2026-09-13): FIXED in PR #9748. Branch worker/machines-a: test commit eac65a5006, fix commit e620447573.

Re-verified at tip before fixing. The reviewer's destroy witness still reproduced on trunk 031ff49a38. Successor B's snapshot became {:owner :a :exit-marker :from-a}, and one A-derived :from-a effect ran in B.

What landed:
- run-child-exit! (implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/exit_cascade.cljc) gains a 3-arity. It takes the destroy effect's exact-incarnation fence, {:owner-gone? :owner-token}.
- teardown-live-actor! (lifecycle_fx/destroy.cljc) passes its fence through to that helper.
- The helper rechecks ownership after the pure cascade. It writes through swap-runtime-db-exact! when an owner token is bound, and rechecks again before the effects.
- It hands the same token to the nested do-fx walk as :frame-incarnation-token. A loss inside one exit effect therefore stops the remaining effects and the terminal marker.
- The 2-arity is the eventless frame-destroy entry (frame_destroy.cljc) and keeps full authority, unchanged.
- Every destroy variant shares the one helper: ordinary, tracked, per-child :spawn-all, and occupied-address replacement. So no destroy path acquired a divergent fence.

Regression test: implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machine_exit_cascade_incarnation_fence_cljs_test.cljc, run on both JVM and CLJS. It covers five cases:
- loss on the destroy-exit :rf.machine/action-ran trace;
- loss inside the first exit effect;
- loss from a container watch on the post-exit write, including no commit-epoch bump attributed to B;
- a live-owner control: write before effects, both effects in order once each, snapshot removed;
- an eventless control.
Before the fix it was RED on JVM: 9 failures across its three loss tests. After the fix it is green on JVM and on CLJS.

Differences from the acceptance text:
1. The mid-exit-effect case cannot REPLACE A with B. EP-0027 refuses frame construction while *handler-scope* is bound, raising :rf.error/frame-construction-in-handler. So that test has the first effect destroy A, then asserts that the second effect and the terminal :rf.fx/do-fx marker do not run. Publication of B is covered by the action-ran and container-watch cases.
2. The destroy-exit FAILURE trace (emit-destroy-exit-failure!) is left unfenced. It reports a failure that really happened in A, and it is neither a write nor an effect.

Gates, run on the final base:
- jvm-machines: exit 0, 1257 tests, 4627 assertions.
- cljs :node-test: exit 0, 11998 tests, 59613 assertions.
- per-namespace isolation: exit 0.
- splint: exit 0.
- clj-kondo: 0 errors. Its 2 with-ok warnings are identical on the pre-fix blob.
CI coverage relied on: jvm-machines, cljs, jvm-tools-machines-viz, cljs-tools-machines-viz.

No spec change: this enforces Spec 005's existing destroy and exit contract rather than altering it. All findings on this bead are fixed or recorded above.

title: reagent-slim: Form-3 docs misstate the lifecycle callback argv
description:
## Scope

Correct the public Form-3 lifecycle bridge in implementation/adapters/reagent-slim so the supported create-class callbacks receive the stock-Reagent/IMPL-SPEC argument shape. Scope is limited to reagent2.impl.component, focused reagent-slim lifecycle tests, and the directly contradictory reagent-slim contract/example prose.

## Correctness finding

install-lifecycle! discards React's prevState argument in both paired update lifecycles. It invokes :get-snapshot-before-update as (f this prev-argv) and :component-did-update as (f this prev-argv snapshot), while the published contract and pinned stock Reagent 2.0.1 invoke them as (f this prev-argv prev-state) and (f this prev-argv prev-state snapshot).

This is an implementation defect, not merely stale prose: reagent-slim presents create-class as the bounded Reagent-compatible Form-3 surface and its migration path promises a namespace-only rewrite for retained surfaces. The current bridge makes the documented fixed-arity callbacks fail at runtime and makes variadic callbacks observe shifted/missing lifecycle data.

## Evidence

- implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/component.cljs:444-460 receives React prev-props, prev-state, and snapshot, names prev-state _prev-state, then drops it from both user callback calls.
- implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/reagent2/impl/component_cljs_test.cljs:363-410 pins the incorrect reduced shape: three user args for :component-did-update and two for :get-snapshot-before-update. It never supplies a documented fixed-arity callback, so the test suite protects the bug.
- implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/IMPL-SPEC.md:632-673 specifies getSnapshotBeforeUpdate(prevProps, prevState), componentDidUpdate(prevProps, prevState, snapshot), and explicitly shows user-fn receiving this plus all three React values.
- implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/FORM-3.md:21-23, 96-120, 255-318, 495-533 and implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/README.md:27-37 teach the three-/four-argument callbacks. The worked examples are copy-pasteable fixed-arity functions that the current bridge calls at the wrong arity.
- implementation/adapters/reagent/deps.edn:15 pins stock Reagent 2.0.1. Reading that jar's reagent/impl/component.cljs custom-wrapper shows :getSnapshotBeforeUpdate calling f with c, props-argv, oldstate and :componentDidUpdate calling f with c, props-argv, oldstate, snapshot.
- Focused readings used: rg over the lifecycle symbols in source/tests/docs; git blame over component.cljs:444-460 and the paired tests; in-memory inspection of the pinned Reagent jar entry. No repository files were changed.

## Failure scenario/invariant

A user follows FORM-3.md and defines:

    :get-snapshot-before-update
    (fn [this prev-props prev-state] ...)

    :component-did-update
    (fn [this prev-props prev-state snapshot] ...)

On the first React update, slim calls the first function with two arguments, causing a CLJS invalid-arity exception before the snapshot can be captured. If only :component-did-update is present, slim calls its four-argument function with three arguments and raises during the post-commit lifecycle. A variadic workaround is not semantically safe either: the snapshot currently occupies the prev-state position and the true prevState value is unrecoverable.

Invariant: every retained Form-3 callback must preserve the documented stock-Reagent argument order and cardinality; the wrapper may translate prevProps to prev-argv, but it must not discard or shift React lifecycle values.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Build a reagent2.core/create-class whose :get-snapshot-before-update is a fixed three-argument function and whose :component-did-update is a fixed four-argument function, exactly as FORM-3.md and README.md show.
2. Mount it, then render the same component with changed argv so React invokes getSnapshotBeforeUpdate(prevProps, prevState) and componentDidUpdate(prevProps, prevState, snapshot).
3. Observe that the slim wrapper calls the user functions with only two and three arguments respectively. CLJS raises an invalid-arity error; with a variadic probe, prevState is absent and snapshot is shifted into its slot.
4. As a source-level reproducer, call the installed prototype methods with distinct prevProps, prevState, and snapshot sentinels; the current component_cljs_test shape demonstrates the omission by accepting only the reduced arities.

## Recommended minimal fix

Thread prev-state through the two existing wrappers:

- :get-snapshot-before-update user callback receives this, prev-argv, prev-state.
- :component-did-update user callback receives this, prev-argv, prev-state, snapshot.

Update the focused tests from the reduced arities to the public contract and reconcile the local source comments. Keep the current prevProps-to-prev-argv translation, current-component binding, snapshot return/forwarding, cap, and React method installation unchanged. Align any directly contradictory README/FORM-3/IMPL-SPEC snippets only as needed so there is one executable contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A focused component test invokes the installed getSnapshotBeforeUpdate wrapper with distinct prev-argv and prev-state sentinels and proves a documented three-argument user callback receives this, the exact translated prev-argv, and the exact prev-state in order, then returns a non-nil snapshot sentinel.
- A focused component test invokes componentDidUpdate with distinct prev-argv, prev-state, and snapshot sentinels and proves a documented four-argument user callback receives all four values in order and under the correct current-component binding.
- Non-vacuity/control: the regression uses fixed-arity three-/four-argument CLJS callbacks and asserts callback counts plus sentinel identity. It must fail on the current implementation by invalid arity or missing sentinel, rather than passing through a variadic callback that tolerates omission.
- A mounted React update proof exercises reagent2.core/create-class through the real lifecycle path: changed argv commits, both paired callbacks fire, the snapshot reaches :component-did-update, and no invalid-arity error is reported. The proof asserts the update actually occurred so a skipped lifecycle cannot read green.
- Existing Form-1/Form-2 behavior, snapshot return semantics, lifecycle current-component binding, and the seven-key cap remain green.
- README.md, FORM-3.md, IMPL-SPEC.md, source comments, and tests agree on (this prev-argv prev-state) and (this prev-argv prev-state snapshot).

## Non-goals

- Adding any lifecycle key beyond the existing seven-key cap.
- Preserving the current pre-alpha reduced callback arities with overloads or compatibility shims.
- Exposing raw React prevProps instead of the established prev-argv translation.
- Redesigning component state, shouldComponentUpdate, error-boundary behavior, batching, or the ratom kernel.
- Broad stock-Reagent API parity work outside these two retained callbacks.

## Related/duplicate search

Searched all bead states and the exported issue/interaction corpus for reagent-slim lifecycle, component-did-update, componentDidUpdate, get-snapshot-before-update, prev-state/prevState, oldstate, and Form-3 arity. No open, in-progress, deferred, or closed issue owns this finding.

- rf2-b9l8o is the closed reagent2.core/reaction macro compatibility fix; it is a different public symbol and failure.
- rf2-iogzk is the closed FORM-3 imperative-subscription scheduling/ownership prose fix; it does not cover lifecycle arguments.
- Historical rf2-8u8tx broadly reviewed adapters and mentioned the component layer but filed only the distinct expand-seq truncation and use-subscribe acquisition issues; it neither identified nor owns this mismatch.

title: surface-review(skills-shared): make every published skill own the instructions it ships
description:
## Scope

Treat `skills/shared/**` and every normal-operation reference, installer special case, packaging caveat, and structural gate that exists to support it as one non-skill product surface.

Make each published skill executable from the files its own package ships. Retire `skills/shared/` as a mandatory runtime dependency and put the few behavior-bearing instructions beside the consumer that actually uses them. Use a clean pre-alpha cut: no peer package, generated vendoring, fallback loader, or compatibility mode.

Sequence the improver side after `rf2-uhszv`, which already owns that product's one-pass local review contract. This task owns the remaining common-layer decision and the pair-retro, migration, pair, Xray, packaging, installer, and shared-test consequences; it does not reopen the improver review design.

## Findings

1. The three leaves do not share one kind of ownership. `retro-protocol.md` was extracted from Pair-retro for exactly two consumers, but it is a union of branches rather than a common denominator: code/session/error evidence, improver-only Edit gates, Pair-retro-only issue filing, aliased output slots, and per-consumer catalogue links. `rf2-uhszv` correctly gives improver its own workflow, leaving this supposedly shared protocol with one real consumer.
2. `issue-filing.md` has a useful two-line core, but centralization has not removed copies. Pair-retro and re-frame-migration link it; re-frame2-implementor deliberately carries a local recipe; Pair-retro's SKILL and issue template, migration's output format, implementor's cardinal rules, and `skills/README.md` all repeat summaries. A roughly 1,400-word generic recipe plus a dedicated all-consumer substring checker is more indirection than the operation needs: keep reviewed text out of shell argv, pass the body with `--body-file`, and use the consumer's known target/body shape.
3. `tool-pair-surfaces.md` openly describes itself as a pointer to authoritative owners, while `spec/Tool-Pair.md` already calls its own capability table the consolidated, complete contract and the Pair-MCP README owns the shipped tool catalogue. The shared projection has still needed 32 commits and once grew to about 3,700 words plus a 725-line token-pinning test before commit `6f0db8ca6b` slimmed it back. Pair and Xray can cite the actual owners; Pair-retro can route against the same table without another roster.
4. The distribution model is broken by construction. A skill package's `files[]` cannot include sibling `../shared/`, yet Pair-retro, improver, migration, Xray, and the private Pair package contain normal-operation shared links. Public package metadata still advertises npm/Agent Skill distribution. Commit `cd721eb179` chose README caveats and a 586-line package-reference guard instead of making the products self-contained; the caveats explicitly admit tarball/plugin installs silently lose the workflow or security boundary. Xray currently ships the shared lineage link but no equivalent link-only caveat, illustrating how even the caveat model drifts.
5. The consumer load path is expensive and conditional. Pair-retro's own SKILL is about 2,027 words; mandatory `retro-protocol.md` adds 2,189 before a domain leaf. Filing and upstream routing can add the other two shared leaves, bringing the shared baseline to about 6,541 words before Pair-retro's local analysis references. Much of that text restates approval, redaction, routing, and output rules already surfaced in the consumer.
6. Test ownership has inverted. The three protocol leaves are 250 lines / 34 KB; `skills/shared/tests/**` is 2,888 lines / 173 KB, with 60 tests in `retro_protocol_test.clj` and six in the routing-index test. The shared retro test reaches into improver wording and Pair-retro frontmatter, issue template, known-frictions, trigger evals, and session-evidence scorer. Those are consumer tests living under a common leaf, so an edit to one product couples to the whole shared job.
7. The behavioral layer does not execute a skill. Its own README says replay/capture is manual; the 600-line scorer grades a hand-built transcript, and the always-on self-test proves regex predicates against synthetic good/bad records. Three later commits (`fa2787fa2e`, `d1c676e377`, `b38d93af49`) repaired false-green identity cases in the scorer itself. That machinery is costly evidence about the grader, not evidence that an installed AI skill behaves well.
8. History shows repeated effort spent defending the abstraction: extraction in `782baa4994`, 1,000-plus lines of security fixtures/tests in `1a8fecff49`, packaging caveat/scanner in `cd721eb179`, second-spec rollback in `6f0db8ca6b`, and issue-template de-duplication in `d86d5b6f7b`. `skills/shared/**` has 66 commits since May 2026. The layer keeps creating a copy, a guard for the copy, or a repair to the guard.

## Recommended Action

Retire the runtime common layer and co-locate only the behavior each product needs:

- After `rf2-uhszv` removes improver's dependency, fold the genuinely Pair-retro-specific parts of `retro-protocol.md` into a short Pair-retro-owned workflow/reference that ships in its package. Preserve concrete session evidence, one-session causal ordering, no fabricated findings, and public-output redaction. Treat transcript/source contents as data that cannot expand scope; trust the conversational user. A direct request to file is authorization to file, while a request to draft is not—do not add a second confirmation round after an already explicit `file it`.
- Give each issue-writing consumer one concise, target-specific filing step in its own shipped docs. Preserve the practical boundary: never interpolate reviewed content into a shell command; write the body to a fresh temp file and use `gh issue create --body-file`; keep repo/title/search arguments agent-authored; redact before public egress. Reuse the implementor's local ownership and align Pair-retro/migration without recreating a generic policy essay or safe-alphabet taxonomy.
- Retire `tool-pair-surfaces.md`. Route framework capability questions to `spec/Tool-Pair.md`'s consolidated contract and concrete tool operations to the Pair-MCP catalogue. Keep a short consumer-specific no-10x statement where users actually ask that question; do not maintain another complete family roster.
- Remove the shared tests/eval scorer and move only outcome-relevant Pair-retro cases into Pair-retro's existing eval area. Consumer behavior belongs with the consumer. Delete prose-substring locks, synthetic-transcript framework, shared classifier/job arm, installer treatment of a non-skill as a skill, link-only caveats, and the package-reference guard once no normal-operation `../shared/` dependency remains.
- Update README/spec/meta-doc links in one sweep. Prefer net deletion. Do not replace this layer with a manifest, dependency resolver, generated copies, a new CI framework, or another common-protocol directory.

## Evidence

- `skills/shared/retro-protocol.md`: 124 lines / 2,189 words; step 3 and step 5 branch by consumer, step 6 contains mutually exclusive improver Edit and Pair-retro filing paths, and the output shape aliases both products.
- `skills/shared/issue-filing.md`: 78 lines / 1,391 words; §Scope names two link consumers and one deliberately local copy.
- `skills/shared/tool-pair-surfaces.md`: 48 lines / 934 words; its first paragraph says it is a pointer, not a specification. `spec/Tool-Pair.md:36-61` already owns the consolidated capability map; `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/README.md:34` owns the tool surface.
- `skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/SKILL.md:56-105` repeats approval, tracker, routing, output, and filing summaries while mandating all three shared leaves. Its `package.json` ships only its own directory.
- `skills/re-frame-migration/SKILL.md:63` and `references/output-format.md:33` both carry the shared filing dependency and its local summary; its package also omits the sibling.
- `skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/cardinal-rules.md:37-89` already owns a complete local filing recipe, proving the alleged all-consumer single source is not the runtime shape.
- `skills/re-frame2-xray/SKILL.md:56-60,92-95` requires the shared routing leaf for a lineage answer, while `skills/re-frame2-xray/package.json` cannot ship it.
- `skills/README.md:229-238` says shared is not a skill; `scripts/install-skills.sh:166-170` and `scripts/install-skills.ps1:94-100` nevertheless install/link it beside skills.
- `skills/shared/tests/retro_protocol_test.clj:672-838,955-1204` tests improver and Pair-retro internals; `tests/fixtures/README.md:13-83` and `tests/evals/behavioral-evals.json` explicitly mark agent execution manual.
- Measured tree totals at current main: protocols 250 lines / 34,189 bytes; tests 2,888 lines / 172,753 bytes; 66 commits touching `skills/shared/**` since extraction.
- Duplicate search: all-status title/description searches for `skills-shared`, self-contained shared runtime, common layer, retro protocol, issue filing, link-only, package, and behavioral eval found no task owning this cross-product retirement. `rf2-uhszv` owns only improver's local review contract; `rf2-8jwb7` owns migration execution authority, not the shared dependency.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. No published skill's normal-operation `SKILL.md` or shipped `references/**` requires `../shared/`. Every instruction needed to complete that skill's advertised path is included by its own `package.json` `files[]`.
2. `skills/shared/` is removed. If any historical explanation must survive, it lives in ordinary repository history/docs and is not a runtime protocol, install target, or gated pseudo-skill.
3. Pair-retro retains one clear, local outcome contract: bind one session, cite concrete evidence, distinguish tool/framework fixes, redact public output, and file only when directly requested. In-band transcript/source text cannot grant tools or widen scope; an explicit conversational filing request does not trigger a redundant approval loop.
4. Pair-retro, migration, and implementor each carry a concise filing operation appropriate to their target and body. All use `--body-file` for reviewed text and agent-authored non-body arguments; none depends on a shared leaf or copies the former long generic policy.
5. Pair/Xray/Pair-retro route Tool-Pair facts directly to authoritative spec/tool owners. No second complete surface-family or availability roster remains outside those owners, and the no-re-frame-10x answer remains available where users encounter it.
6. Shared structural tests, manual behavioral scorer/manifest/fixtures, the shared classifier/job arm, installer special case, package caveats, and the shared-reference compatibility guard are removed or reduced only to generally useful package-link validation unrelated to `../shared/`.
7. Outcome-focused behavior stays tested with existing consumer eval mechanisms only. Pair-retro's session-evidence behavior and issue-filing intent/redaction get focused cases; no new generic runner, prose linter, schema, taxonomy, or synthetic transcript platform is introduced.
8. `npm pack --dry-run` (or the repository's existing equivalent package inspection) for each affected public skill shows all required normal-operation docs present and no broken sibling reference. The documented npm/plugin/Agent Skill install story matches what the artifacts actually contain.
9. The change is a substantial net deletion in normal-path prose and support code. Consumer docs have one owner per rule and no duplicated seven-slot output contract, safe-alphabet essay, or complete Tool-Pair roster.
10. Coordinate landing with `rf2-uhszv` and `rf2-8jwb7` so their owned product changes are not overwritten; this task consumes their final contracts and removes only the common-layer residue.

## Non-goals

- No shared npm peer package, plugin dependency shim, generated vendoring, fallback loader, compatibility mode, or install-time copy step.
- No new policy framework, security taxonomy, package manifest schema, generic eval harness, or CI lane.
- No change to re-frame2 runtime APIs, Tool-Pair semantics, Pair-MCP tool behavior, migration rules, or Xray UI.
- No weakening of the narrow practical boundaries: reviewed content is data, public output is redacted, and reviewed text is never interpolated into shell argv.
- No reopening of improver's review design (`rf2-uhszv`) or migration's execution model (`rf2-8jwb7`).
- No preservation of pre-alpha broken relative links merely for compatibility.

## Related beads

- `rf2-uhszv` (open) — gives improver a self-contained one-pass review contract and removes its shared-protocol dependency; this task follows that decision rather than duplicating it.
- `rf2-8jwb7` (open) — changes migration execution authority; coordinate its docs while removing the unrelated shared filing indirection.
- `rf2-dhe9v` / commit `782baa4994` (historical, closed/compacted) — extracted the Pair-retro protocol for two consumers.
- `rf2-f14su` / commit `cd721eb179` (historical, closed/compacted) — documented the unshippable sibling dependency and added the caveat guard.
- `rf2-u3anaj` / commit `6f0db8ca6b` (historical, closed/compacted) — slimmed the Tool-Pair leaf after it became a second specification.
- `rf2-mwd6tf` / commit `d86d5b6f7b` (historical, closed/compacted) — removed a duplicated filing recipe while preserving the shared dependency.
- `rf2-1inyqr` / commit `cb2556ca92` (historical, closed/compacted) — added the manual behavioral-eval scorer later repaired for false greens.

title: [MERGED #10125] Incomplete inspector extension context: recursive protocol bodies lose the instance dispatcher
description:
Merged-PR audit #10061 at feae77425bcd7d254789be46d98bb26a8b6732d9, source rf2-y8doi.48. The revised 021 section 10.0.6 now documents that recursive IXrayEdnInspector bodies receive no :dispatch-fn and fall back to global rf/dispatch, while retaining the worked Money -> ledger render-node example. This exposes an unresolved functional gap, not merely stale prose.

At the audited merge, tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector.cljs:3258-3264 reconstructs proto-node-opts without the surrounding node's frame-bound :dispatch-fn. render-protocol-node passes that reduced context (also under :node-opts) to the consumer. A protocol body following the documented example recurses into render-node using that context. Its nested collection toggle reaches render-container:2673-2685, which consequently captures global rf/dispatch instead of the inspector instance dispatcher; on-toggle:2013-2019 then writes the expansion event through that global function. The widget reads expansion state on its own frame. A callback invoked outside that frame's carried scope therefore cannot reliably update the mounted inspector, and may dispatch into the host/default frame instead. Built-in recursive children retain the captured dispatcher. This makes the supported extension behave differently at the interaction seam.

Required correction: preserve the existing captured frame-bound dispatcher through protocol recursion, using the current render-node context contract; no new public frame-selection API or generic formatter framework. Add a focused regression using a consumer protocol body with a nested collection and a non-default inspector frame: its toggle must update that instance and leave the host/another instance unchanged. Keep nil-header fallback and existing formatting behavior.

Verified the same omission remains at current origin/main 06c0fcaea5ba854c621d053fd0b3bd2a1503af06 (proto-node-opts:3265-3271). No exact OPEN Bead found for this defect and correction. Evidence is source-path inspection, not a claimed mounted-browser reproduction. The separate non-app-db schema-link defect mentioned by this PR is already corrected by rf2-1t8fn / PR #10065 and is not this finding.

---

## MAYOR'S PRE-DISPATCH VERIFICATION (2026-09-20, trunk `bacec76c4c`)

Held behind live worker `rf2-re7dn` on `edn_inspector.cljs`; `rf2-t450s` queues behind this item. **The
surface fence releases when rf2-re7dn's PR MERGES, not on its report.**

### THE CENTRAL CLAIM VERIFIES — re-derived at trunk, uncapped

`proto-node-opts` is built at **`:3640`-`:3646`** with exactly seven keys:

    proto-node-opts  {:value value
                      :panel-id panel-id
                      :mount-id mount-id
                      :path path
                      :depth depth
                      :expansion-map expansion-map
                      :opts opts}

**`:dispatch-fn` is absent.** That is the item's defect, present at trunk.

**AND THE OMISSION IS SPECIFIC RATHER THAN A HOUSE STYLE, which is what makes the claim strong.** Two
sibling context constructions in the same function region — **`:3227`** and **`:3258`** — both read
`:expansion-map expansion-map :dispatch-fn dispatch-fn`. So the surrounding code threads the
frame-bound dispatcher deliberately and the protocol path alone drops it. **That is independent
corroboration of the item's "built-in recursive children retain the captured dispatcher" sentence**,
and it is the comparison to put in front of the worker: the fix has a pattern to match, not one to
invent.

**The contract is stated in the tree**, at **`:3587`**: *"`:dispatch-fn` (optional) is the frame-aware
dispatcher captured by …"*. Read that docstring before changing the shape of the map — the correction
should satisfy the existing contract rather than extend it, which is what the item means by *"using the
current render-node context contract; no new public frame-selection API."*

### EVERY CITED LINE NUMBER IS STALE — the file has moved ~375 lines

| citation | item says | **at trunk `bacec76c4c`** |
|---|---|---|
| `proto-node-opts` | `:3258-3264` (audited merge), `:3265-3271` (at `06c0fcae`) | **`:3640-3646`** |
| `render-protocol-node` | — | **`:3279`** |
| `render-container` | `:2673-2685` | **`:2935`** |
| `on-toggle` | `:2013-2019` | **`:2364`** |

Three merges have landed in this file today (`rf2-bmed1` +151, `rf2-idydb` +47, and `rf2-re7dn` is live
in it now), so **these numbers will move again before this item is dispatchable.** Treat the table as
the mayor's claim and re-derive at your own tip.

### Scope reminders worth carrying into the brief

- **Preserve the existing captured frame-bound dispatcher through protocol recursion**, using the
  current context contract. **No new public frame-selection API, no generic formatter framework.**
- **The regression must exercise a NON-DEFAULT inspector frame** — a consumer protocol body with a
  nested collection, whose toggle updates *that* instance and leaves the host (and another instance)
  unchanged. A test on the default frame cannot distinguish the captured dispatcher from global
  `rf/dispatch`, which is the entire defect, so such a test would pass on the unfixed tree.
- **Keep nil-header fallback and existing formatting behaviour.**
- **The evidence is source-path inspection, NOT a mounted-browser reproduction** — the item says so.

## MAYOR: CITATIONS RE-DERIVED AT TRUNK `52f7e7f92b` (2026-09-20, after PR #10123 merged)

**PR #10123 (`rf2-re7dn`) landed +29/-4 in this same file, so every line number previously recorded
on this bead has SHIFTED. These are re-measured, not carried forward.** The file is now **5085
lines / 262839 bytes**.

| what | bead/earlier citation | AT TRUNK NOW | moved by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `proto-node-opts` binding | `:3640`-`:3646` | **`:3661`-`:3667`** | +21 |
| sibling opts maps that DO pass `:dispatch-fn` | `:3227` / `:3258` | **`:3248`** / **`:3279`** | +21 |
| `render-protocol-node` definition | — | **`:3300`** | — |
| recursive re-use of the map for child values | — | **`:3676`** | — |
| single-call render site | — | **`:3690`** | — |

**THE DEFECT IS CONFIRMED STILL PRESENT AT THIS TRUNK, measured rather than assumed.** The
`proto-node-opts` map at `:3661` binds exactly seven keys — `:value`, `:panel-id`, `:mount-id`,
`:path`, `:depth`, `:expansion-map`, `:opts` — and a `:dispatch-fn` census over those seven lines
reads **0**. The two sibling maps at `:3248` and `:3279` both read
`:expansion-map expansion-map :dispatch-fn dispatch-fn`, so the omission is an inconsistency
within one file rather than a convention.

**AND THE MECHANISM IS NOW PINNED, which the bead described but did not site.**
`render-protocol-node` at `:3300` destructures only `[{:keys [value panel-id mount-id path
expansion-map] :as node-opts}]` — it never names `:dispatch-fn` itself — **but it passes
`node-opts` WHOLESALE to the consumer** as `proto-opts (assoc node-opts :node-opts node-opts)`,
and hands that to `ddp/xray-render-header` and `ddp/xray-render-body`. So the missing key is not
missing from the renderer's own use; it is missing from **what every protocol consumer receives**,
which is why the symptom is a consumer that cannot dispatch. The RECURSIVE half is `:3676`,
`v (assoc proto-node-opts :value v)` — child values inherit the same deficient map, so a nested
protocol body is affected exactly as the top-level one is.

**Consequence for whoever takes this: the fix is one key in one map literal at `:3661`, and the
hard part is the REGRESSION, not the repair.** Per the bead's own standing note, a regression
must use a **non-default inspector frame** or it passes on the unfixed tree — the default frame's
dispatcher resolves by other means, so a test built on it cannot see the defect. Confirm that
before writing the assertion, the way `rf2-re7dn`'s regression confirmed its spy was live before
asserting an absence.

**Still LANE-BOUND.** The file is free (#10123 merged) but this path arms **6** surfaces —
`cljs_node_test`, `cljs_browser`, `examples_compile`, `tools_jvm`, `mcp_conformance`,
`story_xray_browser` — measured by handing `report-changed-surfaces.sh` the PATH, with a control

## The measurement

Item (x) describes an incremental `shadow-cljs` compile not re-expanding a macro whose input is a
non-source file, and names the mechanism AND the remedy in the same bullet: `shadow.resource/slurp-resource`
records a read file's classpath path and last-modified against the compiling namespace, with
`implementation/spec-resource/src/re_frame/build/spec_resource.clj` as the shared wrapper.

It then names the counter-example:

    bare clojure.java.io        0

with `:57` requiring `[re-frame.build.spec-resource :as rf.build.spec-resource]` and `:123-124`
calling `(rf.build.spec-resource/slurp-resource env (spec-resource-name rel))`. The file's own
docstring at `:30` says `slurp-resource` "instead records each" read. **The repair is rf2-uttbj,
repairing rf2-863tl** — verify that attribution before relying on it; it is relayed from the worker,
not measured here.

## Why this is worth correcting rather than leaving

**It fails in the direction that COSTS A WORKER TIME on a false premise.** A brief citing item (x)
tells a worker editing `tools/xray/spec/007-UX-IA.md` to expect the panel-enum guard to keep failing
against a frozen expansion, and to rebuild cold before hunting a second cause. **I issued exactly such
a brief today** (rf2-y8doi.36); the worker measured the premise stale and proceeded correctly, but a
less careful one would have spent a cold rebuild proving nothing, or worse, distrusted a correct green.

## Scope — NARROW, and this is the whole of it

**The TRAP ITSELF IS NOT REFUTED and must not be softened.** An incremental compile still will not
re-expand a macro reading an untracked non-source file; what has changed is that this tree's cited
example no longer does that. **Correct the INSTANCE sentence; leave the mechanism, the remedy, the
cold-rebuild discriminator and the "do not write a count of such macros here" clause exactly as they
are.**

The honest replacement says that the cited file has since been migrated to the wrapper, so the trap
is currently without a named live instance in this tree — **which is a stronger statement of the
remedy, not a weakening of the warning.** Do not go hunting a replacement example to keep the
illustration alive; item (x)'s own text forbids maintaining an enumeration, and an unfound example is
not evidence that none exists.

## EDITING `CLAUDE.md` IS THE HAZARDOUS PART — read this before touching it

- **`CLAUDE.md` is `i/lf w/crlf`.** **Never `sed -i`** on it: `-i` rewrites every line ending in the
  file unconditionally — measured taking it from `cr=159 crlf=159 bare_lf=0` to
  `cr=0 crlf=0 bare_lf=159` on a pattern matching NOTHING — while `git diff` stays silent because the
  clean filter normalises on commit. `git status` shows ` M` with no hunk, which reads as spurious.
- **Take THREE line-ending numbers with Python reading the bytes, before and after**: total CR, total
  CRLF, and bare LF. Require **CR == CRLF and bare LF == 0**. The third number is load-bearing: an
  inserted LF-only line leaves the first two equal, and `sed -i` leaves them vacuously equal at 0.
- **Never `grep -c` for carriage returns on this file** — it is measured reading **0** on a file
  demonstrably carrying 159+, which makes the CR == CRLF check pass vacuously as `0 == 0`.
- **Item (e) is this file's own standing rule and it applies to this edit.** Writing item (e) itself
  once inserted four real carriage returns, reclassified the file from `w/crlf` to `w/-text`, and
  staged **156 changed lines** for a one-clause edit.
- **Use the Write/Edit tooling**, or read and write the bytes (`open(p,'rb')` / `open(p,'wb')`).
- **Do not use a quoted heredoc for replacement text containing backslashes** — the tool halves runs
  of backslashes in transit (item (o)), and a sample of these checks inevitably carries them.

## Gates

- `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` does **NOT** cover repo-root markdown — `CLAUDE.md` is outside its
  roots and it **exits 0 on a broken link there**. The gate for this surface is
  `scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci`. **Nominate by PATH, never by job name**: the job is called
  `verify-readme-links` and runs both, which is exactly the confusion that has mis-nominated this
  surface before.
- `mkdocs build --strict` does not cover `CLAUDE.md` either (`docs_dir` is `docs`).
- **Nothing grades this file's prose.** Say so plainly rather than quoting a vacuous green.
- If the diff touches no link and no anchor, **both gates are vacuous for it** — check the file
  CONTAINS what a gate inspects before nominating it, and say so.

## The control is the deliverable

A plant on a line your own edit creates, match count measured first, committed before planting,
restored against the committed object (`git rev-parse HEAD:CLAUDE.md`, then `git hash-object` **with
and without** `--no-filters` — this file is `i/lf`, so the **default** form is the one that matches;
treat a match by either form as a good restore) with `git diff --quiet HEAD` as a second instrument.

### 3. Inline-fit estimation `pr-str`s every container's whole subtree on every render, and never returns on an infinite lazy seq  [CONFIRMED path / PLAUSIBLE cost] [severity: medium] [kind: perf] [size: S]
- Where: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector.cljs:1492-1516 (`estimated-inline-px` = `(count (pr-str value))`), called from `render-container` :2394-2397 for every non-empty unchanged container and again from `default-expanded?` :1562-1566 in browse mode; `mini` :4315, `change-annotation` :774, `children-of-pair` :1234-1235 and `diff-pair-count` :1395 (`(vec after)`), `inline-scalar-str` :1025 (`(count v)`).
- What: with a width measured (always, in the running tool) each container serialises its entire subtree to decide "would it fit on one line" — the App-db root serialises the whole app-db once or twice per render, every nested container its own subtree, so a render costs O(size × depth) string building on top of the hiccup walk, on every toggle, width tick or epoch focus. And `pr-str`/`vec`/`count` on a lazy infinite seq do not throw — they never return — so the careful `(take 1001)` guard in `child-count` :1419 is defeated by five other paths and the tab freezes. `*print-length*` is never bound.
- Evidence: traced the call graph; the try/catch at :1499-1501 catches only exceptions. No lazy-seq pin exists (grep `lazy|infinite|iterate` in the inspector tests: 0; control: `(repeat 200 "x")` string fixtures at :1181, :3128). Cost is unmeasured — a 1 MB app-db in the edn_inspector testbed with `(range)` at one key would confirm both halves.
- Action: replace `estimated-inline-px` with a budgeted walk that bails as soon as the running char count exceeds `(/ (- available-width-px safety-margin-px) mono-char-width-px)` — it is asked a yes/no question, never for the real length; bind `*print-length*`/`*print-level*` around `mini`, `change-annotation` and `inline-scalar-str`; give `children-of-pair`/`diff-pair-count` the same `(take 1001)` bound `child-count` has.

### Cross-slice lead (filed by the reactive-diff reviewer; confirmed here, not re-reported)
The `[N∆]` chip reads `engine/change-count-at` (edn_inspector.cljs:2097-2098), which sums `container-paths-from-leaves` (engine.cljc:765-781): every non-`:same` leaf counts, so `:same-shifted` survivors count as changes, and vector removals live in the off-path `:vector-removals` channel (:1217-1233) and never count. CONFIRMED from the inspector side, with a worse consequence than a wrong number: the chip renders only on a COLLAPSED container whose op is not `:added`/`:removed` (:2099-2100). A change-bearing container force-opens (:2375-2384), so the chip appears only after the operator collapses it — and a container whose only change is a tail or mid-vector removal is promoted to `:children` (:1973-1978) yet counts 0, so `show-chip?` is false and the collapsed row shows no change signal at all (no glyph, no rail — the rail is on the expanded body, :2576-2583). Fix belongs in the engine (count removals, exclude `:same-shifted`); the inspector needs no change.

title: schemas: the sensitivity walker cannot see a Malli local :registry and does not fail closed, so a :sensitive? slot leaks verbatim (rf2-pk4i6 item 13)
description:
Shortlist item 13 of the rf2-pk4i6 senior-review wave (from rf2-pk4i6.13#2). Mike ruled the whole shortlist as actioned; this is the filed follow-on. Size S.

## The defect

The sensitivity walker cannot see a Malli LOCAL `{:registry ...}`, and does not fail closed on it — so a `:sensitive?` slot declared inside one leaks verbatim on a validation failure.

    [:schema {:registry {::user [:map [:pw {:sensitive? true} :string]]}} ::user]

walks to `{}` for both flags, is classified NOT opaque, and every `:value` and `:explain` slot of a failure at `[:pw]` ships the secret — with no stamp and no reg-time nudge.

`spec/010` (around :439) promises that opaque shapes fail closed precisely so the nudge is never a silent hole.

This repo does not teach the local-registry idiom. A Malli user reaches for it unprompted, which is why the absence of in-tree usage is not evidence that nobody hits it.

## The triage's citations (claims, to be opened at tip before editing)

- `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/walker.cljc` — `opacity-child-schemas`, the classification site.
- `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc` — `maybe-warn-walker-opaque!` and its `:schema-kind`.
- `spec/010` around :439 — the fail-closed promise.

Re-verified by the reviewer: YES for the ABSENCE only. Their census read `:registry` = 0 under `implementation/schemas` against a control of `:sensitive?` at 545 hits across 18 files, and repo-wide `:registry` hits carry unrelated meanings. **The walker trace itself is the reviewer's reading and was NOT re-run** — so the claim that the example above walks to `{}` for both flags is the premise to test first, and the cheapest way to test it is to write the failing pin before the fix.

## What the triage proposes (a proposal, verified before obeyed)

- Return `::opaque` from `opacity-child-schemas` when the props carry `:registry` (~3 lines).
- Add `:local-registry` to `maybe-warn-walker-opaque!`'s `:schema-kind`.
- Pin with one `schemas_sensitive` test.
- Do NOT walk the registry values. Over-redaction is the documented direction, and walking them is a larger change that this item explicitly does not want.

## Fail closed means fail closed

The whole point is that an unrecognised shape is treated as opaque rather than as transparent. If you find a second shape the walker cannot see — anything else that walks to `{}` for both flags — that is a finding worth reporting, and possibly a second `:schema-kind`, but do not widen this item into a general walker rewrite. An item that doubles in size is worse than one that ships.

Yours: `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/walker.cljc`, `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc`, and the schemas sensitive-test tree.

Item 12 is live in the SAME artefact, holding `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validator.cljc` and `spec/010` exclusively. You are fenced out of both. The root `:schema` is a transparent combinator, so `opacity-child-schemas` projected its child and

honours `:registry` on any vector form, and `:map`- and `:and`-borne local registries take the same
branch for free. Plus `:local-registry` in `maybe-warn-walker-opaque!`'s `:schema-kind` and a clause

API manifest surface does not move.

title: story: an edit to the mounted variant reaches the registry but the canvas does not re-mount, because the hot-reload detector watches only the decorator fingerprint (from rf2-0ae7o.12)
description:
FINDING from rf2-0ae7o.12. That item opened no PR; its worker’s WORKER VERDICT note carries the full walk.

The direction is already set:
- Story spec 003 §Shell lifecycle says stale variants re-mount on hot reload.
- The shell’s own namespace docstring says it watches variant and decorator fingerprints.
- The epic rf2-0ae7o is Storybook parity, where an edited story shows its edit.

THE BEHAVIOUR, measured at trunk e0b923e6ed with the tutorial command (npx shadow-cljs watch :examples/login-form, from implementation/, headless Chromium):
- An edit to a variant in the login-form testbed stories.cljc, adding :args {:heading "... PROBE"} to idle, DOES arrive. The page receives build-complete and loads login_form/stories.cljc and core.cljs with no navigation.
- It reaches Story’s registry: the registry tick went 31 to 42, and the registered idle :args carry the probe.
- The canvas does NOT re-mount: :hot-reload-tick stays 0 and the heading keeps its old text.
- Re-selecting another variant and then idle, on the same document, shows the edit.

CAUSE (a claim to verify at tip):
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/shell.cljs detect-and-tick! bumps :hot-reload-tick only when the decorator-stack fingerprint drifts.
- Spec 003 (tools/story/spec/003-Render-Shell.md, about :186-189) says stale variants re-mount.
- So a MOUNTED variant whose own registered body changed is a stale variant the detector does not see.

WHAT TO DO:
1. Reproduce at tip in the browser, using the same walk.
2. Make a mounted variant re-mount when its own resolved render inputs change.
   - Prefer an existing per-variant hash over a new fingerprint: the snapshot identity content hash, or the watch-mode detector’s per-variant watch hash in the same file.
   - An edit to a variant that is NOT mounted must not re-mount the canvas. That is the control.
   - Shell state must be preserved, as spec 003 says.
3. Commit the regression first, RED: register a variant, mount it, re-register it with a changed body, and assert the tick bumps. Also assert it does not bump for an unmounted sibling.
4. Browser acceptance: the tutorial edit appears without a reload or a re-select. CONTROL: revert only the fix, and the edit stays hidden. Restore, and verify by blob hash.
5. Amend spec 003 :186-189 in place so it names the variant’s own body alongside the decorator stack.
6. In chapter 01 under docs/story, add ONE sentence near the watch command (about :38-40). It says the console notice "shadow-cljs watch for build :login-form not running!" is harmless: shadow-cljs names the build without its namespace, and hot reload still works. Two earlier workers took that notice for broken hot reload.

NOT IN SCOPE:
- The shadow-cljs build-id notice itself. It is upstream and was accepted on rf2-0ae7o.12.
- implementation/shadow-cljs.edn.

GATES:
- the Story JVM lane;
- npm run test:cljs;
- npm run test:browser, if the regression is a DOM test;
- the require-alias ratchet;
- clj-kondo on touched files;
- check_doc_slugs with a planted-anchor control, plus mkdocs build --strict, for the docs/story change;
- the changed-surface classifier.

NEEDS the machine-wide browser and shadow-cljs exclusive.

title: story-mcp: keep application output off the stdio protocol stream
description:
Bind application output to stderr at the server-owned dispatch boundary, while keeping the explicit protocol writer on stdout. An ordinary println in a registered Story event currently inserts a non-JSON line into the MCP stream even when the run succeeds. This independently actionable issue splits finding 1 of rf2-fzbj.31; its remediation fence remains in force until Mike rules who owns remediation.

Ownership/revision: tools_story_mcp; baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261, freshly revalidated at 4df6a3303c68c77ced1f84ce92178bed1d7f7879. Owned source is unchanged from baseline. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2; WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).

Source: tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/server.cljc:281-284 invokes dispatch without rebinding application *out*; :397-408 assembles a writer over System/out and starts that same dispatcher. tools/lifecycle.cljc:178 runs application Story work in a future, conveying the dynamic output binding. spec/001-Wire-Protocol.md:7-13 requires one JSON object per stdout line and uses stderr for diagnostics.

Trigger, exercised against actual -main and separately run-loop!:

```clojure
(rf/init! plain-atom/adapter)
(rf/reg-event :review-mcp/log
  (fn [{:keys [db]} _]
    (println "APPLICATION-LOG-SENTINEL")
    {:db (assoc db :executed true)}))
(story/reg-story :story.review-mcp {})
(story/reg-variant :story.review-mcp/logging
  {:setup [[:review-mcp/log]]})
```

Preload those registrations, initialize the server, call run-variant with variant-id :story.review-mcp/logging, dedup false and max-tokens 0, then ping. Actual: three requests produce four stdout lines; APPLICATION-LOG-SENTINEL is a bare line that fails JSON parsing. The run result still reports status pass and app-db.executed=true, and the ping replies. The no-print control produces three valid JSON lines. The shipped stdio-roundtrip.js parser rejects malformed stdout, so normal diagnostic printing can break an agent session after valid execution.

Expected: the marker goes only to stderr and all stdout lines remain protocol frames. This concerns execution after initialization, not the separately documented load-time output before the server starts. The user need not change every event handler to know about MCP, and no raw System.out or custom logging backend is required to trigger it.

Repair: at the server-owned application dispatch boundary bind *out* to *err*; write JSON through the separately held writer. Future binding conveyance carries the redirect into the worker. Keep log! on stderr. Do not globally replace System.out or apply process-wide output changes to unrelated embedded callers.

Acceptance: an actual stdio test runs a registered variant with a printing setup/script handler; every stdout line parses as JSON, stderr contains the marker, the expected run verdict/app-db arrives, and a following ping succeeds. Include quiet and print-before-throw controls. The current stdio-roundtrip.js only previews an unknown variant and does not reach this worker.

Validation: current-source probes probe-tools_story_mcp-1.clj and probe-tools_story_mcp-2.cjs under ai/surface-review-20260913/tools_story_mcp/ both exited 0, meaning the defect and controls were reproduced. The latter launches real -main via Java/Clojure 1.12.4 and the cached absolute source classpath; both subprocesses exited normally, without a kill. No source stubs, shared compilation, dependencies installed, SDK host, external service, CLJS/browser or broad suite. Logs and .exit receipts are unique to this slice/attempt; all probe processes finished.

Deduplication: read rf2-fzbj.31 and its latest three newest-first history entries; live all-status title searches for Story-MCP/stdout and description searches found no dedicated identical issue. Read closed rf2-cfq8a and rf2-c9t52 including closure/notes: project loading and adapter guards are present and are preserved. This review records a finding only and dispatches no fixer. Prior issues/statuses/notes remain untouched.
notes:
FIXED in PR #9759 (branch worker/storymcp-a, commit 7d76bf9c81 post-rebase). Re-verified at tip before fixing: the defect still held at the cited lines, and the ownership hold recorded on this cluster is lifted by Mike's 2026-09-13 ruling on the parents (rf2-fzbj / rf2-gwye): the mayor remediates.

Fix. server.cljc handle-frame! now wraps its dispatch in (binding [*out* *err*] ...), so application output emitted under the server's own dispatch lands on stderr, which the transport reserves for diagnostics. The JSON reply is unaffected because it never travelled through *out* — run-loop! holds its writer explicitly and writes the frame through it. Clojure's `future` conveys dynamic bindings, so the redirect reaches tools/lifecycle.cljc's run-variant-blocking worker, which is where the user's handlers actually run. title: machines-viz: preserve parallel region parents in xyflow
description:
Preserve each parallel region's existing parent when projecting the semantic graph to xyflow. The parser and ELK place regions inside the named root frame, but the xyflow projection drops their parent, shifting every region subtree away from the routed edges.

This is the independently actionable split of finding 1 in rf2-fzbj.13, revalidated on 2026-09-13. REMEDIATION FENCE: until Mike rules who remediates rf2-fzbj. The fresh review authorizes issue creation only; it does not dispatch a fixer or change the older report's status, notes, or ownership.

Ownership: tools/machines-viz/**; primary repair chart/projection.cljc and its projection regression. Baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261; reviewed HEAD 4df6a3303c68c77ced1f84ce92178bed1d7f7879. Owned paths are unchanged between those revisions. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2. WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).

Source:
- tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/chart/projection.cljc:1604-1606 excludes region? from parentId emission.
- chart/layout.cljc:1329-1340 adds root-container-id as parent to every prior top-level node, including each region.
- chart/projection.cljc:927-1008 nests the same regions in ELK; chart.cljs:478-485 retains parent-relative node positions. Edge routes use absolute ROOT coordinates.
- tools/machines-viz/test/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/chart/projection_cljs_test.cljc:393-405 still asserts that a region has neither parentId nor extent. That assertion preserves the old pre-frame shape.

Trigger:
```clojure
(def d {:type :parallel
        :regions {:a {:initial :idle
                      :states {:idle {:on {:go :done}}
                               :done {:final? true}}}
                  :b {:initial :idle :states {:idle {}}}}})
(def parsed (layout/project-definition d))
;; parsed region__a has :parent-id "__rf2_root_container__".
;; (projection/xyflow-graph parsed positions {}) drops that parent.
```

Expected: region coordinates are interpreted relative to the named frame, matching ELK's ancestry and the absolute edge routes. Actual: xyflow treats the region position as absolute; its correctly parented descendants inherit the region's wrong origin.

Executed on current source: Babashka loaded the actual layout/projection CLJC namespaces and read chart.cljs's default-elk-options unchanged. Node ran cached elkjs on the actual ->elk-children/->elk-edges projection with INCLUDE_CHILDREN. The resulting positions were passed through the actual xyflow-graph, then installed @xyflow/system adoptUserNodes. ELK root origin was (12,12). Results:
- root frame: ELK (12,12), xyflow (12,12), delta (0,0).
- region__a: ELK (38,52), xyflow (26,40), delta (-12,-12), parentId absent.
- region__a__idle: ELK (64,92), xyflow (52,80), delta (-12,-12).
- region__a__done: ELK (64,224), xyflow (52,212), delta (-12,-12).
- its event node: ELK (92,170), xyflow (80,158), delta (-12,-12).
- region__b and its leaf likewise both shifted (-12,-12).

Repair: propagate :parent-id to :parentId for region containers just as for other nodes, retaining parent-relative coordinates and parent-first order. Replace the stale no-parent assertion. Check the existing opt-in post-ELK region transform with the restored frame relationship; avoid hardcoded coordinate corrections or layout redesign.

1. A parsed parallel fixture nests every region beneath layout/root-container-id in both ELK and xyflow.
2. With a nonzero frame origin, xyflow absolute positions match summed ELK ancestry for regions, leaves, events, and initial markers.
3. A rendered fixture verifies edge/node alignment and frame containment, including a context band, under :tb and :auto.
4. Flat and nested compound containment and parent-first ordering remain correct.

notes:

Cause: chart/projection.cljc excluded region containers from :parentId emission. That guard came from 06557f4160, before the rf2-q129z8 root-container frame, when regions had no parent at all. - Region containers now emit :parentId and :extent "parent" like every other nested node.
- The root frame leads the parent-first sort.

title: Resources RealWorld: invalidate session feed after follow changes
description:
Invalidate the session-scoped Your Feed cache after both Resources follow mutations. A successful follow/unfollow currently leaves a recently visited personalized feed unchanged until its freshness window expires.

Remediation fence: until Mike rules who remediates rf2-fzbj. Independently actionable split of confirmed finding 3 in rf2-fzbj.21, revalidated under rf2-gwye. Review and issue creation do not authorize remediation.

Ownership: examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/mutations.cljs:214-237; resources.cljs:41-45,274-295; views.cljs:121-129,142-185,381-409; routing.cljs:103-109. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2. WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review). Baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261; inspected HEAD 4df6a3303c68c77ced1f84ce92178bed1d7f7879.

Trigger/reproducer: sign in and visit Your Feed to cache its empty result. Visit stub-bot's profile or article, follow the author successfully, then return to Your Feed within 60 seconds. For the reverse, cache the populated feed, unfollow, and return before it goes stale.

Expected: the relationship write invalidates that session's feed membership and re-entry fetches the changed set. Actual: both :realworld/follow and :realworld/unfollow invalidate only #{[:profile username]} in {:from-db :realworld/viewer}. The feed uses {:from-db :realworld/session} and tags #{[:feed] ...article-tags}. No descriptor matches its scope and tags. Article-page follow additionally invalidates only a viewer-scoped article detail. The backend's following set changes correctly, but ensure serves the still-fresh feed unchanged.

Suggested repair: add {:scope {:from-db :realworld/session} :tags #{[:feed]}} to both mutations' :invalidates functions, following the explicit cross-scope descriptor pattern already used by favorite/unfavorite. Keep profile :populates and existing article-detail refresh behavior. Avoid forcing every route to refresh or changing the framework's cache policy.

Acceptance: in the existing external Resources harness, warm an empty personalized feed, follow an author, re-enter before stale-after-ms, and assert a new fetch and the author's articles. Warm a populated feed, unfollow, and assert the corresponding fetch/removal. Cover profile and article follow entry points, and retain the immediate profile-populates control. Examples remain test-free.

Validation performed: source-probe.clj evaluates both actual :invalidates functions and the actual feed :tags metadata from current source. probe-examples_real_apps-1.log/.exit: exit 0, SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2. Both writes return only the viewer/profile target; the empty feed has session scope and #{[:feed]}, producing zero matching targets. Inspected current resource ensure's fresh-skip at implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc:436-439 and its :entry-stale? semantics. Inspected the shared demo backend's follow transition at demo_backend.cljs:532-535 and feed membership at :433-436. This is an evaluated descriptor counterexample plus cache/backend source tracing; no browser/cache-runtime sequence, build or external network was executed.

Deduplication/references: no dedicated open issue found in the current tracker/index; rf2-fzbj.21 contains the prior aggregate finding. Closed rf2-9n43e and rf2-k5lbd established stateful backend writes and production-seam receipts; this is a client invalidation mismatch against that working backend, not a backend regression. Remediated in PR #9758 (branch worker/realworld-a), which fixes all four confirmed findings of rf2-fzbj.21 together. Every finding was re-verified at tip before the fix; all four still held.

What landed, per finding:

1. rf2-gwye.33 (HTTP optimistic comment) — realworld_http/schema.cljs gains DurableComment: the wire ws/Comment with :id widened to [:or :int [:re #"^temp-"]], derived from ws/Comment rather than restated. [:comments :data] registers that instead of the wire shape. ws/Comment, ws/CommentResponse and ws/CommentsResponse are untouched and still reject a string id.

2. rf2-gwye.34 (HTTP home feed) — realworld_http/http.cljs gains current-nav-token / same-navigation?. :articles/load and :feed/load capture the committed route's :nav-token and carry it on both reply targets; :articles/loaded, :articles/load-failed, :feed/loaded and :feed/load-failed refuse a reply whose navigation the reader has left. Supersession could not cover this: the two families carry different :request-ids and settle one machine whose :empty/:some/:error states take no :fetch-succeeded.

3. rf2-gwye.35 (Resources feed invalidation) — :realworld/follow and :realworld/unfollow now invalidate {:from-db :realworld/session} #{[:feed]} beside the viewer's [:profile username], via a shared follow-invalidates helper. Re-verified against PR #9746 (rf2-fzbj.7) first: that change touched only the infinite-feed accumulated-pages tag path, and the RealWorld feed is a scalar resource, so the premise stood unchanged.

4a. rf2-gwye.37 (HTTP editor writes) — :editor/submit and :editor/delete carry the issuing nav-token; :editor/submit-success, :editor/submit-error, :editor/delete-success and :editor/delete-error are each gated on it. :editor/load-article now dispatches the machine [:reset] before [:use-edit], so a refused settle cannot leave the next editing session at :submitting with its inputs locked (that strand is reachable only once the settles are gated, and is pinned by a test).

4b. rf2-gwye.39 (Resources editor writes) — :editor/submit and :editor/delete use :reply-to [:editor/replied nav-token]; :editor/replied refuses a departed reply whole: no slice write, no navigation, and no instance clear. Clearing nothing is what scopes cleanup to the completed operation — the next editor entry clears the shared :editor/save instance anyway, and the runtime already suppresses a late result for a cleared instance.

4c. rf2-gwye.42 (Resources detail delete) — :ui/delete-article carries its slug on :reply-to [:ui/article-deleted slug]; the continuation clears its own instance on :ok and navigates home only while the committed route is :realworld.article/show for that slug, mirroring the HTTP twin's article-route-for-slug?.

The Resources test delete-article-continuation-navigates-home issued its delete from /register and asserted a navigate home — that is exactly the departed-page case rf2-gwye.42 says must be refused, so it now issues the delete from the article page. Two HTTP rows that dispatch [:articles/loaded ...] directly now pass the nav-token explicitly (nil on a frame that never navigated).

No markdown or spec page was touched, so the doc-link gates are not nominated for this change.

Skipped suggestions, each with its reason:
- rf2-gwye.34 suggested a shared request identity or cancellation may supplement ownership: NOT built. The nav-token gate alone closes the defect, and queued replies still need the gate regardless, so a cancellation scheme would add machinery this example exists to stay clear of.

title: ssr-node: preserve surrogate pairs across streaming HTTP chunks
description:
Preserve UTF-16 surrogate pairs across streamed string chunks so streaming HTTP carries the same UTF-8 bytes as the buffered response. Ownership: impl_ssr_node; implementation/ssr-node/src/http.cjs:164-177 (per-chunk UTF-8 res.write), :194 (end), :196-206 (buffered join before encoding), src/worker.cjs:155-165 (string emit contract). README.md:271-288 explicitly describes arbitrary emitted chunks and byte-identical buffered/streaming outputs. Baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261; reviewed HEAD 50abcab5ce674e5107b34834ebbfd81d1af7e2cd with identical owned source. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2; WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review). Trigger: use the existing test/fixtures/chunked.cjs module with {protocol:1, entry:'app/root', state:{':bytes':JSON.stringify(['

\uD834','\uDD1E

'])}}. The emitted JavaScript strings join to

U+1D11E MUSICAL SYMBOL G CLEF
