title: [tools/story/play] Type steps bypass React controlled-input change handlers
description:
Snapshot 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd; tools/story/src/re_frame/story/play/dom.cljc unchanged at mayor HEAD 90e9b0008ac96bb59e0e9f6ec03de8e1d650f21d.

The supported [:type selector text] step does not deliver an on-change to ordinary React-controlled text inputs. It directly assigns node.value and then dispatches input/change. React's installed own-property setter updates its internal value tracker during that assignment, so both synthetic events are filtered as 'value did not change'. The helper returns true anyway, and runner_events records a successful action/skip. The DOM briefly displays text without the component state receiving it; a later render can restore the old text, or submit sees the old value.

Exact path:
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/play/dom.cljc:130-144 type! sets (.-value node) at :137, then dispatches input and change at :142-143.
- play/runner_events.cljc:706-720 exec-type! trusts the true return and records step-skip (a completed action), without checking application state.
- tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md:1013 promises DOM text input for :dom/:browser; recorder exports that same step, so this affects hand-written plays and recorded interaction replay.
- Real consumer: tools/story/testbeds/login_form/views.cljs:42-57 has controlled email/password inputs with :value from a Reagent atom and :on-change writing that atom. Submitting (:37-40) reads the atom, not raw DOM.value. A normal type-email/type-password/submit play can therefore submit empty credentials despite visibly filled DOM inputs.
- Installed react-dom 19.2.0 source, implementation/node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom-client.development.js:1540-1571: trackValueOnNode defines a setter that updates currentValue before invoking the native setter. :1592-1605 updateValueIfChanged compares that tracker with node.value. :3537-3540 and :3587-3589 gate text input/change extraction on that comparison. Both events emitted by Story return false after its direct assignment.

Executed bounded dependency-algorithm probe, Node exit 0 (~0.35s): extracted the ACTUAL installed React trackValueOnNode/track/updateValueIfChanged function source (between 'function trackValueOnNode(' and 'function getActiveElement('), evaluated with checkFormFieldValueStringCoercion=noop and isCheckable=false, and provided a tiny prototype-backed input object. No React mount, CLJS compilation or browser was run.

Minimal core of the probe after extracting those actual functions as api:
```javascript
class Input {
  get value() { return this.raw || ""; }
  set value(v) { this.raw = String(v); }
}
const node = new Input();
node._valueTracker = api.trackValueOnNode(node, "value", "");
node.value = "Ada";  // Story's assignment
console.log(api.updateValueIfChanged(node)); // false
Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(Input.prototype, "value")
  .set.call(node, "Grace");
console.log(api.updateValueIfChanged(node)); // true (control)
```
This verifies the actual tracker comparison seam, not a full DOM play. The source path above establishes that text input/change uses it. No live login/HTTP interaction was performed.

Smallest repair: set the input/textarea's native value in a way that represents a user edit to React, then emit the appropriate bubbling event; do not mutate React private tracker fields or simulate an entire keyboard. Keep the plain-DOM fallback and supported node types coherent.

Focused acceptance: mount a real React/Reagent controlled text input, run the public :type step, and assert its on-change/state receives the text and a rerender retains it. Include textarea and the actual login form or a minimal equivalent submit snapshot. Pair a plain DOM input control. Restoring the direct node.value assignment must make the controlled-input state assertion fail. Existing no-DOM cannot-run behavior stays unchanged.

Dedupe: active+closed searches controlled/selector/play and value-tracker memory found no matching issue. Story UI/capture reviewer confirmed no ownership overlap; controlled-input title matches are UIx test naming/Hicasso documentation, not this runner. Source principal-path review plus isolated React algorithm probe only; no full suites/builds/browser executions.
notes:
--- 2026-09-07, worker/story-a, PR #9366 (open, not merged) ---

FIXED, and the bead's diagnosis was exactly right — confirmed not by re-reading
React's source but by REPRODUCING the symptom under real React 19 in Chromium
(see the sabotage run below).

Repair, by construct: `play/dom.cljc`'s `type!` assigned `(.-value node)`
directly. React redefines `value` as an OWN accessor on every controlled input
(`trackValueOnNode`); that setter records the incoming value in the tracker and
THEN forwards to the native setter, so the `updateValueIfChanged` comparison
gating synthetic `input`/`change` extraction reports "value did not change" and
both events are discarded. `type!` returned true regardless and
`runner_events/exec-type!` recorded a completed action.

The write now goes through the `value` setter declared on the node's DOM
PROTOTYPE, obtained by a new `native-value-setter` that walks the prototype chain
past any own-property setter a framework installed on the node. That is the write
a real keystroke performs: React's tracker stays stale, so React synthesises the
change. Deliberately NOT done, per the bead: no mutation of React's private
tracker fields, no keyboard simulation, no general input-driver abstraction. The
chain walk (rather than naming `js/HTMLInputElement`) is what keeps textarea /
select / custom elements on ONE path; a runtime whose chain declares no `value`
setter falls back to the plain assignment, so the plain-DOM path is preserved.

WHICH LANE COVERS IT — this is the part a unit test cannot do.
  The assertions require a real React render (the value tracker does not exist
  without one), so the suite is
  `tools/story/test/re_frame/story/play/type_controlled_input_dom_cljs_test.cljs`.
  The `-dom-cljs-test$` suffix (rf2-2hrj8) puts it in shadow's `:browser-test`
  build — Playwright + Chromium, real React via `react-dom/client` — which is the
  lane that decides this bead. `:node-test` also loads the file (its `cljs-test$`
  regex matches the suffix) but every test self-gates on `(browser?)` and exits
  early, so a green there is NOT evidence for this bead and is not offered as any.

  `npm run test:story-play-scripts` (the Playwright `:script` CI runner over the
  testbeds, login_form included) is the other browser lane on this surface. It is
  not the acceptance lane here because its rows assert a play's terminal
  pass/fail status, not the component state behind it; the login_form deck's
  variants do not currently drive a type→submit→assert-credentials path, so it
  would have stayed green through this bug. The DOM suite asserts the state.

EVIDENCE — the bead's own stated acceptance, discharged directly:
  "Restoring the direct node.value assignment must make the controlled-input
  state assertion fail." Done, measured. With `type!` reverted to
  `(set! (.-value node) text)`, `npm run test:browser` went from
  807 tests / 4398 assertions, 0 failures (captured exit 0)
  to the SAME 807/4398 with 3 failures (captured exit 1), the three being:
    - type-step-reaches-controlled-input-on-change
        actual: (not (= "ada@example.com" ""))
    - type-step-reaches-controlled-textarea-on-change
        actual: (not (= "line one" ""))
    - typed-credentials-reach-the-submit-snapshot
        actual: (not (= {:email "grace@example.com" :password "hopper"}
                        {:email "" :password ""}))
  That last line is the bead's predicted real-consumer symptom, reproduced: a
  submit handler reading component state receives EMPTY credentials while the DOM
  inputs are visibly filled. The plain-DOM control and the `native-value-setter`
  mechanism test stayed GREEN under the revert, so the sabotage discriminates the
  controlled path specifically rather than breaking everything.
  `dom.cljc` was restored afterwards and verified by byte hash (identical to
  pre-plant), not by reading a diff.

The suite also carries `direct-assignment-is-the-regression`, which performs the
OLD write on an identical mounted input and asserts the controlled state does NOT
move. It is the permanent form of the sabotage above: reverting `type!` reds the
tests around it rather than quietly passing, and if React ever stops filtering
that write this test says so.

Covered in the suite: controlled input, controlled textarea, a login-form submit
snapshot read off component state (a minimal equivalent of
`tools/story/testbeds/login_form/views.cljs`), a plain-DOM input control, the
regression control, and the prototype-setter mechanism asserted directly.

Not touched: `spec/017-Testing-Story.md` or any other `tools/story/spec/**` page.
Spec unchanged because the contract at :1013 (DOM text input for `:dom`/
`:browser`) was already correct — this was an implementation that did not meet
it, not a contract that needed changing.
close_reason: PR #9366 merged; mayor fast-forwarded and verified HEAD == origin/main at 59841a06d5. type! now writes through the node's DOM-prototype value setter instead of assigning directly, so React's synthetic onChange fires and controlled inputs receive typed text. THE FAILING-FIRST EVIDENCE IS THE STRONGEST OF THE THREE: reverting type! to the old assignment turned npm run test:browser red on exactly three tests, one reading actual: (not (= {:email \"grace@example.com\" :password \"hopper\"} {:email \"\" :password \"\"})) — the bead's predicted symptom reproduced under real React 19 in Chromium. That is the right kind of care — naming which lane cannot see your change is worth more than a green from one that cannot.

### Cross-cutting themes (read these before the docs)

1. **Facade re-exports of home namespaces protect nobody.** SSR (seven copies), trace/epoch (the facade spelling the spec teaches is JVM-only), observability (every stream 4–5 ways) and registry introspection all found the same shape: the "documented facade exception" exists for single-import ergonomics, and the corpus shows every consumer already requiring the home namespace. The bundle-DCE argument that justified the home-ns verbs is contradicted by the actual require graph (`re-frame.core → re-frame.trace → re-frame.trace.tooling` is unconditional). One rule would settle four docs: a surface has ONE home; the facade carries registrars and the front porch, nothing else.
2. **Per-kind aliases beside a generic grammar.** Fifteen introspection fns, seven HTTP verb helpers, seven schema-setter names: each family is a projection of a grammar that already exists and that the tools already use. The demand bar (Principles) has ruled on them retroactively.
3. **Imperative pairs the frame lifecycle should own.** Routing already folded `install-url-listener!`/`remove-` into `:url-bound? true` on the frame (rf2-g8pbwg); resources' revalidation pair is the same shape with one caller.
4. **Substrate naming drift.** Hicasso arrived with its own spellings for view definition, sub reads, hooks and mount verbs where UIx and Reagent had already settled on others; the mechanisms differ where the substrate forces it, but the names diverge where it does not (`use-subscribe` vs `use-sub`, `render!` vs `mount!`, `defview` around `reg-view*`).
5. **Parked surfaces whose park has lapsed.** Machines' `:system-id` family was parked in July "until the facade audit rules"; that audit (rf2-2hpxo) closed 2026-09-04 without it in scope. HTTP's interceptor fx pair, `:accept`, `:abort-signal`, `:decode-schemas`; boot's `install-adapter!`, `adapter-disposed?`, `init-platform`, `feature-loaded?`, `require-feature!`: all zero consumers after months of corpus growth.

## Ethos bar (how to judge proposals)

- **One way for the common case; power available, not ambient.**
- **Values over dynamic scope** where async and isolation matter.
- **Data-driven registration** with a single registration grammar.
- **Empirical:** if `examples/` never use a form, it is not front-porch — and if a shipped surface has zero consumers after months of opportunity, the demand bar has ruled on it retroactively. Codex's qualification, adopted: zero calls is strong evidence for deleting a convenience that data already covers, and weaker evidence that a lifecycle capability with its own timing or ownership is equivalent to another operation.
- **A dual is legitimate only when its discriminator is written down** (ENSURE/SCOPE, fx-override tiers, fn-vs-fx). Unwritten discriminators are option soup wearing a uniform. Wave 3 adds: a written discriminator that the corpus does not respect, or that the require graph contradicts, is not enough either.
- **Masterpiece, not option soup** — pre-alpha is the cheap moment to shrink; every deferred deletion races the alpha tag.

# Implementation API: fewer ways, stronger concepts

Review date: 2026-09-05. Tracking bead: `rf2-snkw`.

This began as an independent source review and now incorporates selected, source-checked insights from the [Fable corpus](../fable/README.md), at the user's request. It is not an implementation change. Proposed forms below are design proposals, not instructions for using the currently shipped API.

## Findings

| Area | Overlap | Recommendation | Judgment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Subscription inputs](subscription-inputs.md) | Arrow chains and input-producing functions describe the same dependency relation, but change the computation's argument shape. | One named `:inputs` slot; consistently vector-valued derived inputs. | Also enables derived inline-image subs and earlier literal checking; explicit migration required. |
| [Registration inspection](registration-inspection.md) | Generic registry reads, feature-specific getters, and positional/map source-selection forms. | Two generic reads with one explicit source-selection grammar; ordinary collection operations for projections. | High tooling payoff; preserve genuine source-store versus frame-generation distinctions. |
| [HTTP request construction](http-requests.md) | Seven verb functions merely construct the already-public managed-effect data. | Make the effect data canonical; remove the verb-constructor family. | Straightforward reduction, but common GET calls become longer. |
| [HTTP reply addressing](http-replies.md) | Unified and split destinations can be mixed, requiring override precedence. | Keep both useful styles, but make `:reply-to` mutually exclusive with `:on-*`. | Revised after Fable's login evidence: deleting split routing would add application ceremony. |
| [Schema backend configuration](schema-backend.md) | Three scalar setters duplicate an existing partial-map installer. | Keep `set-schema-fns!`; separate fixture restoration from application configuration. | Small, clear cleanup; modest application impact. |
| [Resource lifecycle and scope](resource-lifecycle-and-scope.md) | Manual listener setup repeats frame lifecycle ownership; resolver sugar changes callback input meaning. | Frame-owned revalidation; one declared-input resolver contract. | New from Fable; removes an actual boot-order obligation and a callback-shape exception. |
| [View adapter ergonomics](view-adapter-ergonomics.md) | Root recipes, hook names and view descriptor shapes drift across adapters. | Shared root-handle grammar, `use-sub` for value hooks, consistent view lookup. | New from Fable; preserve substrate machinery while reducing application boilerplate. |
| [Machine child completion](machine-child-completion.md) | Single-child finality and fan-out's hand-dispatched completion encode the same terminal fact differently. | Final-state completion works under both `:spawn` and `:spawn-all`. | New from Fable; a reusable child no longer knows its parent's join vocabulary. |
| [Trace and epoch inspection](trace-and-epoch-inspection.md) | Trace reads have platform-specific aliases; a tool's data-clear action calls a policy-reset helper; whole-history projection duplicates record composition. | One platform-complete read surface; policy-preserving trace clear; record-level projection. | Added on the second reread; clearer tool behavior without merging history systems. |

The strongest next design discussions are subscriptions, inspection and reusable child completion. The clearest everyday ergonomic wins are frame-owned revalidation and consistent adapter boot. Schema configuration remains an easy small cleanup. Neither list size nor deleted-function count is the objective: the objective is fewer concepts a programmer or AI must remember to accomplish a real SPA task.

## What Fable added or changed

Fable's most useful contribution is distinguishing surface reduction from application simplification. Its login example changed my reply recommendation; its resource and UIx examples identify setup code the library should own; its child-completion comparison exposes avoidable coupling between otherwise reusable machines. The [synthesis notes](intermediate/fable-synthesis.md) record which proposals were adopted, narrowed or left out and why.

The [second reread](intermediate/fable-reread-2.md) adds concrete capability and migration evidence to subscriptions and one focused trace/epoch finding. It also records Fable's withdrawal of the bulk-schema deletion and adoption of explicit registry source selection. This is now nine focused areas; agreement between reviews is not counted as fresh evidence where one review simply adopted the other's proposal.

I did not import every deletion. In particular, retain bulk app-schema registration's up-front path validation, keep distinct state stores out of the generic registrar merely for symmetry, and do not use diagnostic traces as a machine control protocol. This corpus remains focused on a manageable set of improvements, not a catalogue of every questionable key.

## Method and bounds

I used the [API reference](../../../../spec/API.md) and [generated API manifest](../../../../spec/api-manifest.edn) as discovery aids, then examined implementations, registration metadata, and actual consumers. The manifest also covers tool namespaces; its total row count is not a count of implementation APIs reviewed.

The review followed core registration, frames, dispatch, subscriptions, images, configuration, introspection and listeners; feature surfaces including routing, resources/mutations, machines, schemas and HTTP; and rendering/SSR and test-support boundaries. Candidate findings were checked against authored Clojure/CLJS source in `/examples` and `/tools`, with focused implementation tests used to identify supported cases absent from the applications. Each finding names the evidence and the use-case distinctions it must preserve.

The [intermediate evidence ledger](intermediate/evidence-ledger.md) records useful implementation observations, search boundaries, and rejected simplification candidates. All deliverables are in the mayor's checkout; intermediate notes are confined to `intermediate/`.

“Known use cases” means those found in this repository during this review, not a claim about every external application. Searches establish checked-in examples, not production popularity or the absence of dynamically resolved calls. Tests were read as evidence of contracts; I did not execute runtime tests or benchmark proposed APIs. This is not a line-by-line correctness certification of the entire implementation.

The philosophical yardsticks are the user's pre-alpha posture and the repository's [Vision](../../../../spec/000-Vision.md) and [Principles](../../../../spec/Principles.md): a small computational model, data before magic, regularity, addressable definitions, and useful public inspection. The existing spec also values migration compatibility. Where these pull in different directions, the finding states the conflict instead of describing a proposed break as an existing obligation.

## Similar-looking operations I would keep

| Surface | Why the distinction earns its place |
| --- | --- |
| `dispatch` / `dispatch-sync` | Enqueueing and synchronous run-to-completion have different ordering and reentrancy contracts. |
| `subscribe` / `subscribe-once` / `compute-sub` | Owned reactive observation, a released live-runtime snapshot, and computation over supplied state have different lifetimes and inputs. |
| Frame scoping / frame ownership / `capture-frame` | Ambient synchronous scope, creating and disposing a frame, and carrying a frame capability across asynchronous work solve different problems. |
| Registration macros / function entry points | Source capture at a literal definition site and higher-order/computed registration are distinct capabilities. |
| Resource ensure / refetch / release / invalidate | Establishing demand, requesting freshness, ending ownership, and marking data stale are not synonyms. |
| Raw resource state / resource subscriptions | Durable runtime entries and derived presentation status are different representations, not aliases. |

| Flows / subscriptions | Drain-time materialization and reactive derivation have different execution semantics. |
| Mount / hydrate / render / unmount semantics | These remain distinct transitions. The adapter finding nevertheless standardizes their handle grammar and expresses hydration as an explicit first-render mode. |
| Single / bulk app-schema registration | The bulk operation validates its input before applying registrations; it is not simply an interchangeable spelling of an arbitrary loop. |
| Scoped test overrides / explicit stub installation | Automatically restored fixture scope and deliberately installed testbed behavior have different ownership. |

These decisions follow the relevant implementations in [core](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc), [resources](../../../../implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources.cljc), [Hicasso](../../../../implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc), [schemas](../../../../implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas.cljc), and [HTTP test support](../../../../implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/test_support.cljc).

Several apparent cleanup targets have already been retired or consolidated, including the old event-registration variants, multiple frame-construction helpers, per-setting core configuration setters, and per-stream listener names. Throwing retirement stubs are migration diagnostics, not additional working APIs; they are not counted as findings here.

## Recommendation

Prefer subtraction that leaves ordinary Clojure values and functions doing more of the work. Do not replace these families with a larger options language, a generic plugin framework, or a compatibility matrix. Equally, do not merge operations whose timing, ownership, or meaning differs merely to shorten the API index.

Each linked finding contains its own use-case inventory, proposed API, counterargument, migration implications, and focused acceptance evidence. No runtime code or normative specification was changed by this review.

## Corrections and boundaries that matter

**Bulk schemas are not equivalent to `run!`.** Fable's proposed replacement omits the current up-front batch/path validation and vector return. [Storage](../../../../../implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc) makes both visible. Preserve the convenient batch operation rather than pushing that coordination into application code.

**Completion traces are not a control API.** `:rf.machine/done` in finalization is an emitted diagnostic trace. The proposed universal completion behavior requires runtime-owned delivery to joins; it should not depend on listeners or trace availability. The current join source also expressly describes its exact-attempt record as causal correlation in a trusted program, not authentication. Preserve that correlation without importing security ceremony.

**Consistent root names do not make lifecycle differences disappear.** I initially retained mount/hydrate/render distinctions outright. The stronger conclusion is to preserve their semantics while adopting one handle grammar. I favor the existing Reagent `render!` name over Fable's proposed broad rename to `mount!`; the valuable change is the shared recipe.

**A captured frame does not subscribe a React component.** A direct `capture-frame` operation may help callbacks, but it cannot substitute for a value hook's re-render contract. Scope a subtree when eliminating an explicit-frame hook spelling.

**Fifteen getters need not imply fifteen true registrar kinds.** Fable's broader registry proposal absorbs side tables and virtual kinds. The Codex target keeps actual event descriptors for machines and preserves specialized frame-state collections where they represent other facts. Simpler querying should not require a larger conceptual registry.

**Zero observed calls is evidence, not a deletion algorithm.** It is strong support for removing a redundant convenience already covered by data. It is weaker evidence that a specialized lifecycle capability is equivalent to another operation. The accepted additions show actual application boilerplate or coupling, not just low counts.

## Remaining Fable themes: not imported as a second backlog

The index also proposes changes to observability/egress, trace and epoch reads, SSR/head access, machine system IDs, boot/configuration, registration clearing, routing internals and test isolation. These remain useful dossiers in Fable's corpus; I did not copy their full deletion lists into Codex or mark their claims independently verified.

A promising cross-cutting guideline is one documented home for an operation, with facade convenience justified by real authoring benefit. It supports the already-accepted inspection and adapter cleanup. It does not, by itself, justify removing every facade export, collapsing frame-owned sinks into dev streams, merging schema enforcement policies, or creating a universal clear/query/configure language. Those are separate design decisions with more scope than the high-value changes above.

The resulting corpus now contains eight focused areas, not the sum of both reviewers' proposed deletions. It retains the user's posture: elegant, powerful SPA authoring; low friction; ordinary data and functions; no new framework merely to tidy the old one.

## What a bead is here
- One bead = one independently shippable, single-worker unit (roughly ≤ one worker-day), split by hot-zone ownership. Hot-zone files (one-toucher, serialised): `spec/Conventions.md`, `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md`, `spec/API.md`, `spec/Tool-Pair.md`, `spec/Spec-Schemas.md`, `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`, `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md`, `spec/005-StateMachines.md`, `spec/002-Frames.md`, `implementation/deps.edn`, `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn`, `.github/workflows/*`.
- The docs, spec, examples, skills, tests and manifest updates for a change go IN THE SAME bead as the code change. Do not file separate "update docs" beads. Exception: one consolidated "doc drift" bead per area for stale lines no code bead will touch.
- **Two-reviewer findings** (README lists them) → implementation beads, dispatchable, `ruling: none`, unless the doc itself says a ruling is needed for that slice.

- **One-reviewer larger design decisions** (README lists them) → ONE `type: decision` bead per area, `ruling: RULING`, carrying the options, the recommendation, codex's caution, and the list of implementation beads to file when ruled. PLUS separate implementation beads for the ruling-independent parts: dead code with zero consumers, defects the review found (silent drops, fenced-out facade fns, stale eval forms), and doc drift.
- Every implementation bead description MUST be self-contained (the `ai/` dossier is local-only and may be deleted) and MUST enumerate: the target API (signatures, before/after code), the deletion list, consumers to migrate by file with counts (examples/, tools/, testbeds/, implementation/**/test), spec pages (flag hot-zone ones), docs pages, examples, skills (`skills/**`), tests to add or change, `spec/api-manifest.edn` regeneration, the conformance corpus / mcp-conformance if affected, migration README entry if a v1-era name changes, and the acceptance evidence.
- Sequencing: express dependencies with `deps:` (existing ids as `type:id`; beads in this or another spec file as `blocks:@<area>.<n>` — the coordinator resolves them). Note which beads share a hot-zone file so the mayor serialises them.
- Priority: P2 for two-reviewer implementation beads and for defects; P2 for the High decision (observability); P3 for one-reviewer medium decisions and drift; P4 only for genuine nice-to-haves.
- Fold trivia into the nearest bead rather than filing it. Aim for the SMALLEST number of beads that carries all the work; typically 2–5 per area.

title: skill(re-frame2-improver): canonical storage-validation fix throws on absent/corrupt localStorage and skips rehydrate
description:
## Scope

Correct the canonical "After" in `skills/re-frame2-improver/references/schemaless-events.md` for a durable session value read from localStorage through a recordable coeffect. Keep the leaf's trust-boundary and replay-boundary lessons, the coeffect runtime, and the six-leaf catalogue unchanged.

## Correctness finding

The recommended recordable supplier claims to return nil when localStorage is absent or corrupt, but its materializer throws in both cases before validation can make that decision.

The first expression passed to `some->` is `(.getItem js/globalThis.localStorage "session")`. `some->` can short-circuit only after that expression returns; on Node/headless/server hosts, where `globalThis.localStorage` is absent, the direct method call throws. A malformed stored string likewise makes `js/JSON.parse` throw before `m/validate` runs. The framework catches a recordable-generator exception and skips the declaring handler, so this is not the advertised nil/clean rejection path.

This is a copyable canonical fix in a static-review skill. An agent can correctly identify the original body-read and replace it with a replay-recordable coeffect, yet still ship a boot/rehydration failure on ordinary stale storage or in Node-based tests.

## Evidence

- `skills/re-frame2-improver/references/schemaless-events.md:105-122` owns the canonical correction. Lines 109-110 describe `:session/stored` as a recordable generator yielding "nil if absent/corrupt". Line 112 directly invokes `.getItem` on `js/globalThis.localStorage`; line 113 invokes `js/JSON.parse`; only line 114 reaches Malli validation.
- Evaluation order is load-bearing: in `(some-> (.getItem js/globalThis.localStorage "session") ...)`, the direct method call is evaluated before `some->` can test for nil. Missing `localStorage` therefore is not a nil input to the pipeline.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/cofx.cljc:793-842` catches supplier exceptions and returns the `:threw` outcome after emitting `:rf.error/coeffect-exception`. Its public delivery contract at lines 1113-1117 says a throwing supplier sets `:rf/skip-handler?`; the recordable arm does that at line 1182. Consequently `:session/rehydrate` does not run.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:196-206` is the shared fx/cofx platform predicate. Missing `:platforms` defaults to `#{:client :server}`, so the sample's supplier is eligible on a server frame rather than being fenced away.
- The shipped canonical comparator is total over these cases. `examples/core/todomvc/db.cljs:35-45` catches parse failures in `storage->todos`; lines 66-84 start `some->` from `(.-localStorage js/globalThis)`, so the property itself can be absent before any method invocation.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/todomvc_cljs_test.cljs:17-24` explicitly documents the executable Node control: Node has no localStorage, the property-first `some->` short-circuits to nil, and the supplier returns its empty value. Lines 76-80 drive that cold-boot path.
- History isolates the miss. Commit `14fafe6103` made the sibling localStorage write example SSR-safe with `:platforms #{:client}` and a guarded globalThis access, but the coeffect sample retained a direct method call. Commit `bb25f3c56b` upgraded the sample to a recordable generator without making its materialization total.

## Reproduction / failure scenario

1. Follow the leaf's canonical correction and register `:session/stored` exactly as shown.
2. Dispatch `[:session/rehydrate]` in the Node/headless CLJS environment used by repository tests, where `globalThis.localStorage` is absent.
3. The supplier attempts `undefined.getItem`, emits `:rf.error/coeffect-exception`, and the framework skips `:session/rehydrate`. It does not deliver nil as the sample promises.
4. Browser control: make `localStorage["session"]` contain malformed JSON and dispatch the same event. `JSON.parse` throws; Malli validation is never reached; the handler is again skipped.
5. Positive control: begin the pipeline with `(.-localStorage js/globalThis)` and catch access/parse failure before validation. Missing or malformed storage produces the explicitly chosen invalid/absent value, which is then recorded and delivered without rerunning the host read on replay.

## Recommended minimal fix

Make the sample's materializer total over the two cases its own docstring promises:

1. Resolve `(.-localStorage js/globalThis)` as the first `some->` value, then call `.getItem` only when that property exists.
2. Catch property-access and JSON-parse failure at the small storage-decoding boundary, returning the documented nil (or change the prose and handler coherently to consume an explicit data-shaped invalid result).
3. Run the always-on Malli validation only after parsing succeeds; keep `:recordable? true` so the resulting fact, including the absent/invalid outcome, is captured and replayed verbatim.
4. State the server/headless posture in the example. The smallest existing-repo shape is universal and nil-on-absent, matching TodoMVC. Do not merely add `:platforms #{:client}` while leaving a universally dispatched handler requiring the coeffect: a platform-skipped required recordable fact follows the missing-required path rather than the promised nil path.

Keep this local to the leaf and its focused proof. No generic storage framework is needed.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The canonical After never invokes a method on a possibly absent `globalThis.localStorage`; the property lookup itself is inside the nil-short-circuiting path.
2. Malformed JSON is caught at the materialization boundary and becomes the documented nil or an explicitly documented data result. It cannot escape as a coeffect supplier exception.
3. A focused CLJS/Node proof with no `globalThis.localStorage` shows the supplier returns the chosen absent value and the declaring handler runs; the proof fails if the direct `.getItem js/globalThis.localStorage` form is restored.
4. A malformed-JSON control shows Malli is not called on an unparsable value, no `:rf.error/coeffect-exception` is emitted, and the handler follows the documented invalid/absent branch.
5. A valid conforming JSON control is validated, recorded, and folded into app-db; a valid but schema-invalid JSON value is rejected by the always-on validation branch.
6. The prose still distinguishes trust validation from replay recordability and does not weaken `:recordable? true`.
7. Skill link/package/eval documentation gates remain green. Because no existing gate executes fenced CLJS, the PR handoff explicitly records the corrected snippet's manual comparison with the tested TodoMVC materializer.

## Non-goals

- No changes to coeffect generation, exception recovery, platform gating, schemas, replay, epoch, or SSR runtimes.
- No new anti-pattern leaf, generic localStorage abstraction, compatibility shim, or broad catalogue rewrite.
- No policy change requiring every browser read to be client-only; this sample may deliberately be universal and yield nil off-browser.
- No redesign of session/auth state, storage format, or UI response to an invalid persisted session.
- No package-link or installation-metadata work.

## Duplicate and history check

Targeted all-status searches of `.beads/issues.jsonl` covered re-frame2-improver, session/stored, rehydrate plus localStorage, corrupt storage, JSON.parse plus cofx, coeffect-exception plus localStorage, missing localStorage, Node, and cofx platform. Git history searches covered the same sample and its recordable-coeffect migration. No bead owns this accidental supplier-throw path.

Distinct nearby work:

- `rf2-0o5dx` (closed) fixes the URL body-read fixture's recordability requirement; it does not address storage materialization or supplier exceptions.
- `rf2-237ug` (closed) fixes frame capture in recommended views.
- `rf2-uhszv` (closed) owns the one-pass critique workflow.
- `rf2-nvbz` and `rf2-1c60` (open) own cross-package links and install/packaging metadata, respectively.

## Uncertainty

Fail-loud corruption could be a valid product policy, but it is not the policy this sample states: it explicitly promises nil for absent/corrupt storage and gives the handler only that branch. Either policy can work if made deliberate and coherent. The present accidental supplier throw plus handler skip is the defect.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #9232 (branch worker/skimprov-a, head 0225e0cf99b40cc733bc3e62389359a62f0e080f).

PREMISE HELD, confirmed at source. The canonical After in skills/re-frame2-improver/references/schemaless-events.md started its some-> from (.getItem js/globalThis.localStorage "session"), so the method call was evaluated before some-> could test anything: absent localStorage (Node/SSR/headless) threw, and a corrupt entry threw out of js/JSON.parse before m/validate ran. Every evidence claim in the bead checked out — cofx.cljc run-supplier-under-scope catches the throw into [:threw nil]; deliver-declared-cofx maps :threw to (assoc acc :rf/skip-handler? true); fx.cljc runs-on-platform? defaults to #{:client :server}; a platform-skipped generator takes emit-missing-required-cofx! (which is why :platforms #{:client} is NOT the repair); examples/core/todomvc/db.cljs is property-first and catches parse failure; the Node control test documents the short-circuit.

THE FIX IS DOC-SIDE, NOT CODE-SIDE. The runtime behaves as specified — a supplier that throws SHOULD skip its handler. The skill's sample was simply not total. No implementation/ change was needed or made.

ABSENT vs CORRUPT, settled separately (the bead left the policy open and asked for a deliberate one):
- ABSENT (no globalThis.localStorage on Node/SSR/headless; getItem nil on first run) — ordinary cold boot, not caller-controllable, sane default exists. MUST NOT THROW: a throw breaks every new app and every Node test. Repaired by starting the some-> from the PROPERTY.
- UNUSABLE/CORRUPT (unparsable JSON, or parsed-but-fails-Session) — anomalous, but also not caller-controllable and with the same sane default (treat as no session). ALSO MUST NOT THROW, and the reason is not leniency: the framework turns a supplier throw into :rf.error/coeffect-exception + :rf/skip-handler?, so :session/rehydrate silently never runs. That is a boot step that did not happen — HARDER to diagnose than the nil the handler already handles. Fail-loud is a legitimate policy for corrupt persisted state; a supplier throw is not how it is spelled. The doc now points an app that must act on the difference at a data-shaped result instead.
So: same delivered value, different reasons, and the doc no longer collapses them into one unexplained clause.

ALSO CORRECTED, beyond the bead: the document now blocks the plausible WRONG repair. The sibling :local-storage/set fx in imperative-effects.md carries :platforms #{:client} and is fine (for an fx a platform skip is benign), so an agent would reach for it here — where it produces a different, subtler bug (missing-required rather than nil). Stated explicitly.

EVAL 28 (behav-schemaless-body-read-trap) graded the recordable-generator shape but never graded totality, so the defect could pass it. Gains one totality expectation. Evals are gated structurally and graded by an external LLM harness — THERE IS NO EVAL EXECUTOR IN THIS REPO, so that is a durable record of the contract, not behavioural coverage.

AC 3/4/5 asked for focused CLJS/Node proofs. Those are not reachable in-fence (implementation/ was fenced off) and AC7 already concedes no gate executes fenced CLJS. Delivered instead: tests/storage_materializer_test.clj, a bb structural fixture over the DOCUMENT, 6 tests / 14 assertions, PROVEN DISCRIMINATING in both directions — restoring the direct .getItem form fails 2 assertions (the absent case), removing the decode catch fails exactly 1 (the unusable case), so the two conditions are pinned independently; the Before-block control keeps passing throughout. Plus the AC7 manual comparison against the Node-tested TodoMVC materializer, recorded in the PR body.

NOT YET CI-WIRED: skills/re-frame2-improver/* has no arm in report-changed-surfaces.sh and no skills-structural step. Wiring needs the classifier arm + workflow step + the _changed-surfaces.test.cjs mirror, all outside this fence. Filed as rf2-z65e (the same local-only-then-wired path re-frame2-setup and re-frame2-pair-retro each took).

Gates green and each proven live rather than trusted on exit 0: check_doc_slugs (planted broken anchor on the added line -> exit 1, restored -> 0), check_skill_eval_docs (planted duplicate id -> exit 1 naming A4 uniqueness; note the improver is deliberately absent from its TARGETS per rf2-hpq96d, so its coverage here is id/name uniqueness ONLY), api-manifest skills-check (exit 0, 575 public-var references checked), check_skill_description_budget, check_skill_eval_packaging, check_readme_links --ci. mkdocs build --strict does NOT cover skills/ and was not nominated. title: skill(re-frame-migration): per-feature pre-publish edge must inherit M-0 pinned route
description:
## Problem

The migration skill gives mutually exclusive instructions for a required per-feature dependency while re-frame2 is unpublished. Its canonical M-0 branch says to add core and adapter with an author-supplied `:local/root` or pinned `:git/url` + `:git/sha`, continue the migration, and explicitly says "Do not leave the dep alone." The edge-case paragraph at the end of the same operational leaf instead says a per-feature artifact that is not published should be left alone and deferred until it lands.

That stale sentence can make a programmer or AI complete a required M-27..M-33 source rewrite without adding the module that implements it. This is the live pre-alpha path, not a theoretical future branch.

## Exact evidence

- `skills/re-frame-migration/references/setup.md:164` says pre-publication migration is fully doable with `:local/root` or pinned `:git/url` + `:git/sha`, that a first release is not a precondition, and: "Do not leave the dep alone, and do not stop and wait for a release."
- The same file's `## Edge cases` paragraph at `setup.md:220` says: "Per-feature artefact not yet published. Same shape as M-0's 'no v2 version' edge case: leave the dep alone, flag in the report, the author updates manually when the artefact lands."
- `skills/re-frame-migration/references/inventory-and-plan.md:17` defines the unpublished target as N coordinates: core, adapter, and every used per-feature artifact, each using the chosen git-SHA/`:deps/root` or sibling `:local/root` route.
- The authoritative corpus at `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:67-84` says today's route is one pinned git coordinate per artifact, every later M-27..M-33 artifact rule inherits M-0's route, and the migration continues without a release.
- `skills/re-frame2-setup/references/deps-versions.md:78-104` owns the concrete local-root and git-subdir shapes; its artifact-path table at `:87-93` covers schemas, machines, routing, flows, HTTP, SSR, and epoch.
- Each feature is genuinely a separate artifact: `implementation/{schemas,machines,routing,flows,http,ssr,epoch}/deps.edn` has its own `:clein/build :lib` and a local-root dependency on core. Core+adapter cannot provide these namespaces by themselves.
- `skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-cross-cutting.md:405-420` records the consequence: without the feature artifact/require, registrations throw `:rf.error/<feature>-artefact-missing`, framework fxs/events report no handler/fx, or the flows/epoch paths silently degrade.

## Reproduction and impact

1. Migrate a v1 app that uses `rf/on-changes` and approve M-21's `reg-flow` destination (or trip any other M-27..M-33 feature rule).
2. Because no artifact is published, follow M-0 correctly and add core plus the adapter with one pushed SHA and their `:deps/root` values.
3. Reach `setup.md`'s explicit "per-feature artefact not yet published" edge case and follow its nearest instruction: leave `day8/re-frame2-flows` alone/absent and defer it.
4. Apply the flow rewrite and `re-frame.flows` require. The namespace cannot resolve without that module; if the require is also missed, the façade registration throws or the runtime fx no-ops. The migration cannot satisfy its compile/boot done-bar despite following the skill.

The instruction is especially hazardous for an AI because it is phrased as a specific exception after the general rule. Reporting the omission does not make the migrated SPA runnable, and postponing a mandatory coordinate contradicts the skill's end-to-end execution contract.

`git blame` shows the stale per-feature sentence came from `140e3b20419` (2026-05-12). Commit `d24f2029a6` later fixed the same "leave the dep alone / wait for release" dead end in setup's M-0 paragraph but did not touch the edge-case copy. Commit `40964cd77f` (rf2-snjn5) then fixed the authoritative corpus's M-0 and all M-27..M-33 copies so they inherit one route.

- Keep the trigger-to-artifact matrix in `breaking-changes.md` and path recipes in `re-frame2-setup/references/deps-versions.md`; link them rather than restating either matrix.
- Extend existing Rule 6 minimally with a setup-edge-specific assertion and fixture. It must reject the exact positive stale paragraph while continuing to allow M-0's explicit negation. Use the existing checker; do not add another linter or policy layer.

This is deliberately one prose correction plus one regression tooth. It restores the elegant one-decision model already established by M-0.

6. Manually verify the corrected paragraph names both supported pre-publish routes and that its links/anchors resolve. No application runtime gate is required for this prose-only correction.

## Non-goals

- No artifact publication, group-coordinate rename, version/SHA selection, release scheduling, or change to the future post-publish route.
- No change to the per-feature artifact split, public runtime API, M-27..M-33 trigger mapping, or module manifests.

title: surface-review(examples-substrates): keep the runnable slim-counter bundle free of its CI SSR fixture
description:
## Scope

Separate the runnable Reagent Slim counter under examples/substrates/reagent_slim/counter from the CI-only pure-CLJS-SSR bundle-isolation fixture that currently owns its only Shadow build entry. Keep the stock/slim counter comparison focused on the existing counter app and keep the adapter-owned S3-005/S3-008 isolation proof non-vacuous in a dedicated build. Limit changes to the slim counter entry/fixture seam, the paired Shadow/package/checker configuration, directly coupled staging/checker tests, and prose that describes this comparison.

## Correctness finding

The repository presents examples/counter-slim-and-fast as the runnable “same app, different package” counterpart to examples/counter, but its only build does not invoke reagent-slim.counter.core/run. It invokes reagent-slim.counter.bundle-isolation-entry/run, which executes test-only pre-mount SSR work, pulls reagent2.dom.server and its serializer into main.js, creates a throwaway frame, clears its subscription cache, and writes globalThis.counterSlimPrerender.

This is not just extra source beside the example. Both documented launch paths compile and serve that same contaminated build, so the runnable artifact and the bundle a reader is invited to compare against stock contain and execute a CI harness that the stock app does not. The comparison therefore changes two variables at once: substrate/package and an SSR fixture. It undermines the folder’s central teaching claim that the app is held constant, especially because the catalogue explicitly says the interest is what the bundle does not contain.

## Evidence

- implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1259-1270 declares :examples/counter-slim-and-fast and points its :init-fn at reagent-slim.counter.bundle-isolation-entry/run, explicitly not reagent-slim.counter.core/run.
- examples/substrates/reagent_slim/counter/bundle_isolation_entry.cljs:1-29 says it is gate plumbing, is the build’s init-fn, and passes prove-pure-cljs-ssr! into the app boot before mounting.
- examples/substrates/reagent_slim/counter/bundle_isolation_fixture.cljs:1-54 requires reagent2.dom.server, calls render-to-static-markup, writes counterSlimPrerender on globalThis to defeat advanced DCE, and clears the transient subscription cache.
- examples/substrates/reagent_slim/counter/core.cljs:96-126 exposes an optional on-frame boot arity and a with-new-frame branch whose only caller is that fixture. The supposedly plain teaching file therefore still carries a public-looking harness seam even though its zero-arity run does not use it.
- examples/substrates/reagent_slim/counter/README.md:13-22 says the meaningful diff from stock is only the package/import and adapter, calls core.cljs the plain idiomatic example, labels both sibling fixture files “not app practice”, then at lines 49-55 tells the reader to launch the build whose init-fn is the fixture entry.
- examples/substrates/README.md:7-15 defines the track as “same authoring language, different package”, says each example changes exactly one place, and says the interest is what the bundle does not contain. Lines 84-95 route the slim command through the same build.
- examples/README.md:163 repeats that the interest is what the bundle does not contain.
- implementation/package.json:46 makes test:reagent-slim:bundle-isolation release examples/counter-slim-and-fast, while line 53 routes dev:example through the normal standalone runner. examples/scripts/serve-example.cjs:149-210 resolves the selected build and compiles it unchanged; there is no teaching-entry substitution.
- implementation/scripts/check-reagent-slim-bundle-isolation.cjs:135-182 defines counterSlimPrerender and a reagent2.dom.server-only literal as required positive sentinels. Lines 275-364 read out/examples/counter-slim-and-fast and require those SSR sentinels in that bundle, confirming the contamination is load-bearing for the gate rather than dead source.
- Git history identifies the incomplete separation. Commit b2ae161b17 (rf2-vyl0vt, “prune scaffolding from Reagent-family examples”) moved the fixture out of core.cljs so the source looked clean, but deliberately repointed the one example build to the new gate entry. It separated files, not the runnable artifact or core’s fixture-only boot seam.

## Failure scenario / impact

A programmer or coding agent follows the catalogue and compares the release outputs of examples/counter and examples/counter-slim-and-fast to understand the substrate cost. The stock bundle contains the counter client. The slim bundle contains the counter client plus a forced server serializer, a DCE anchor and fixture orchestration, and it performs an unrelated static render/global write before mounting. Any size, reachability, startup, or “what ships” conclusion attributes fixture-only differences to Reagent Slim.

The same problem appears without bundle analysis: running the advertised slim example executes code every comment calls CI-only and “not app practice”. Reading core/run is not enough to discover what the official page actually boots; the authoritative build config chooses a different entry. The invariant for a comparison example is simple: its documented runnable build must boot the code it teaches, and gate-only work must not be reachable from that runnable entry.

## Recommended minimal fix

Restore :examples/counter-slim-and-fast to reagent-slim.counter.core/run. Give bundle_isolation_entry and bundle_isolation_fixture a dedicated, non-runnable Shadow build with a separate output directory, and make test:reagent-slim:bundle-isolation release and inspect that output. Keep the existing stock build as the methodology control and retain all six isolation contracts, including the two positive SSR sentinels that make S3-005 non-vacuous.

Move the fixture-only orchestration out of core’s optional on-frame boot arity so the teaching boot is the same small install-then-mount shape readers actually run. Update the checker diagnostics, targeted Shadow/staging/script-policy tests, and the few comparison paragraphs that currently conflate the runnable example and gate fixture. Use an existing local convention for the dedicated check build id; do not introduce a build registry or generalized harness framework.

## Non-goals

- No change to Reagent Slim, stock Reagent, core frame, rendering, SSR, or adapter APIs.
- No removal or weakening of the pure-CLJS-SSR non-vacuity proof, stock-Reagent absence proof, react-dom/server absence proof, or mirror slim-absence proof.
- No bundle-size threshold or performance claim.
- No new browser/Playwright example matrix; examples remain test-free learning surfaces and adapter behavior remains adapter-testbed-owned.
- No extraction or redesign of the counter’s events, subscriptions, views, frame id, or mount lifecycle.
- No cross-product of examples across every substrate and no general example-manifest redesign.
- No effort to make the dedicated gate fixture user-runnable or to teach its orchestration as app practice.

## Related / duplicate search

Searched all issue states in .beads/issues.jsonl with targeted rg queries for counter-slim-and-fast, bundle-isolation entry/fixture, counterSlimPrerender, reagent-slim bundle isolation, teaching build, runnable fixture, and same-app bundle. No issue owns this separation.

Closest records are not duplicates:
- rf2-fmns2 (closed) owns the three-view-layer login comparison and its cross-runtime isolation proof, not the slim counter entry.
- rf2-k5r9t (closed) added the Reagent client-root lifecycle and migrated example mounts; it does not separate test and runnable builds.
- rf2-vyl0vt is represented by commit b2ae161b17 and physically moved fixture code out of the teaching namespace, but intentionally kept the one runnable build pointed at the gate entry. This finding is the remaining artifact-level half of that cleanup.
- rf2-5x1xt (closed) fixes missing UIx consumer dependencies and is unrelated.
- rf2-cdoo (open) concerns Reagent Slim after-render ordering, not examples or bundle reachability.

## Uncertainty

The exact dedicated build id and output prefix should follow whichever current non-page/check-build convention best fits Shadow configuration and CI surface classification. The required outcome is not a particular spelling: the documented :examples/counter-slim-and-fast output must be fixture-free, and the isolation checker must consume a separate output that remains deliberately fixture-full. No runtime execution was needed for this review; the entrypoint and reachability contradiction is explicit in source/config and in the gate’s required sentinels.
acceptance_criteria:
1. :examples/counter-slim-and-fast uses reagent-slim.counter.core/run as its init-fn, remains listed by the standalone example runner, and both documented launch commands serve that build.
2. A focused config/staging assertion proves the runnable build resolves to core/run and does not silently regress to bundle-isolation-entry.
3. The runnable advanced main.js contains neither counterSlimPrerender nor the reagent2.dom.server-only SSR presence sentinel. The check is non-vacuous by also proving ordinary Reagent Slim client sentinels are present.
4. A separate non-runnable build owns reagent-slim.counter.bundle-isolation-entry/run and emits to a distinct output directory not staged or advertised as the counter example.
5. test:reagent-slim:bundle-isolation releases that dedicated build and the stock counter, and its checker reads the dedicated slim output.
6. The dedicated gate bundle still contains counterSlimPrerender plus the serializer-owned static-markup sentinel, contains the ordinary slim client sentinels, and contains none of the stock-Reagent or react-dom/server sentinels. The stock bundle retains its own positive controls and remains free of slim sentinels.
7. The teaching core no longer exposes an optional callback/throwaway-frame seam used only by the bundle fixture; core/run and any retained boot helper express only the runnable app lifecycle.
8. The slim README and substrate catalogues distinguish the runnable comparison from the dedicated CI fixture without teaching the fixture as application code or weakening the “same app, different package” claim.
9. Targeted checker self-tests, example staging/manifest tests, npm run test:examples-compile, and npm run test:reagent-slim:bundle-isolation pass, with a planted reachability/config regression demonstrating the new separation check fails on the old shape.
close_reason:
Fixed by PR #9253. The premise held and was worse than stated: :examples/counter-slim-and-fast booted bundle-isolation-entry/run, and the fixture cost 15,837 bytes raw / 4,743 bytes gzip on the runnable :advanced bundle (646,418->630,581 raw, 187,923->183,180 gzip) — enough to INVERT the example's own lesson. Against the stock control (634,267 raw / 184,268 gzip) the slim bundle read 3.7 KB gzip LARGER than stock before the fix and reads 1.1 KB SMALLER after it, so a reader following the catalogue would have attributed a fixture-only cost to the slim substrate on the one example whose subject is bundle size.

AC1-AC9 met. Runnable build now boots reagent-slim.counter.core/run (AC1). Contract 0 in check-reagent-slim-bundle-isolation.cjs pins both :init-fns off shadow-cljs.edn and runs first (AC2). Contracts 2/3/5 widened to both slim bundles, so the fixture bundle is proven to hold the SSR sentinels and no stock-Reagent or react-dom/server ones, and the stock bundle keeps Contracts 1+6 (AC6). core/boot!'s on-frame arity and with-new-frame branch are gone; core/run is install-then-mount (AC7). Slim README gains a 'the bundle you run is the bundle you compare' section; IMPL-SPEC 12.2/12.3 and the test.yml comment corrected. examples/README.md and examples/substrates/README.md needed no edit — their 'what the bundle does not contain' claim was already the right claim and is now simply true (AC8). Gates, captured exits: bundle-isolation 0 (8 contracts, 41 sentinel + 2 entrypoint checks); check-examples-compile 0 (58/58, zero warnings); test:scripts 0 (122/122); check_readme_links.py --ci 0, proven live by plants on both edited markdown files. title: surface-review(examples-machines): clear stale login errors when leaving :error-shown
description:
## Scope

Correct the error lifecycle in `examples/capabilities/machines/state_machine_walkthrough/**` and strengthen its existing out-of-tree headless coverage. Keep the three-attempt lockout, managed-HTTP stub, draft slice, tag-driven view, and test-free examples policy. This is a small correctness/teaching repair, not a redesign of machines or forms.

## Finding

The walkthrough records each failed reply into machine `:data :error`, but neither transition out of `:error-shown` clears it:

- `:walkthrough.login/dismiss -> :idle` has only a target.
- `:walkthrough.login/submit -> :submitting` has only a target.

The view renders the error row whenever `err` is non-nil and the machine is not locked; it does not condition the row on `:error-shown`. Consequently, clicking the visible **Dismiss** button changes the banner to `idle` but leaves the same error and Dismiss button on screen. Further Dismiss clicks are unhandled no-ops in `:idle`. Submitting directly from `:error-shown` likewise carries the old error into the new `:submitting` request. The initial `:idle -> :submitting` transition does run `:clear-error`, but that is too late to make Dismiss dismiss anything and does not cover direct retry.

This is exactly the kind of copyable SPA pattern an example must get right: status and error data disagree, and a control named Dismiss has no visible effect.

## Evidence

- `examples/capabilities/machines/state_machine_walkthrough/core.cljc:74-75` already defines the minimal reusable `:clear-error` action as `{:data {:error nil}}`.
- `core.cljc:98-101` writes the failure message into `:data :error`.
- `core.cljc:126-128` declares both exits from `:error-shown` without `:clear-error`.
- `views.cljs:44-45,69-76` subscribes to the error and renders the row/button solely from `(and err (not locked?))`; after Dismiss, `locked?` is false and `err` is unchanged.
- Spec 005, `Action effect map — {:data :fx}` (`spec/005-StateMachines.md:737-755`), says `:data` is merged into existing machine data. Reusing `:clear-error` therefore preserves `:attempts`; no custom reset/event/sub is needed. The implementation performs that merge at `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc:2025-2029`.
- The current guide's corresponding full transition (`docs/machines/tutorial.md:193-197`, repeated at 435-439) does clear the error on direct retry. The walkthrough's namespace says to read it beside the guide and its README calls this the chapter flow, so this is behavioral drift, not an intentional alternate policy. The guide view hides errors by exact state; the walkthrough intentionally does not, making Dismiss's missing clear observable here.
- Existing out-of-tree coverage misses it: `implementation/core/test/re_frame/examples_test.clj:906-922` dispatches Dismiss twice but asserts only the eventual `:locked-out` state. It never reads `:walkthrough.login/error` after Dismiss or inspects a direct retry snapshot.
- The runnable build is correctly declared at `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1723-1730`, but `npm run test:examples-compile` is compile/warning coverage only (`examples/TESTING.md:15-23`; `implementation/scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs:57-82`), so it cannot detect this state/data mismatch.
- History explains why it survived. The original browser spec (introduced by `58adfc02e7`) clicked Dismiss and asserted only that the banner said `idle`, never that the error row disappeared. Per-example browser specs were intentionally removed by `2d2f4aff53`; the present framework test inherited the same narrow assertion. The June 26 draft-slice refactor `2dc95699af` retained the data-only error render. The Aug 13 guide rewrite `6012a7b21a` added `:clear-error` to direct retry but did not update this example.

## Recommended bounded fix

Reuse the existing machine-local `:clear-error` action on both transitions that leave `:error-shown`: Dismiss to `:idle`, and Submit to `:submitting`. This is two table entries, preserves `:attempts` by the documented merge rule, and makes the current view truthful without adding a state predicate, another tag, another subscription, or view-local cleanup.

Extend the existing `state-machine-walkthrough-runs-headless` test in `implementation/core/test/re_frame/examples_test.clj` with focused transition assertions for both exits. Briefly align the example prose/comments with the now-explicit lifecycle. Keep tests outside `examples/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Starting from `{:state :error-shown :data {:attempts 1 :error "bad creds"}}`, a Dismiss transition produces `:idle`, sets `:error` to nil, and preserves `:attempts` at 1; therefore the existing error-row predicate becomes false.
- From that same failed snapshot, a direct Submit transition produces `:submitting`, clears `:error`, preserves `:attempts`, and still emits exactly the existing `:rf.http/managed` request effect through `:submitting` entry.
- The browser-facing Dismiss control no longer remains visible after it is clicked; a fresh request never carries a stale visible failure.
- Existing lockout behavior is unchanged: first two failures remain retryable, the third reaches `:locked-out`, attempts becomes 3, and the terminal failure message is retained for the locked snapshot.
- The existing out-of-tree JVM example test covers both clear paths; no `*.spec.cjs` or test file is added under `examples/`.
- The focused core JVM test namespace and the existing example compile gate pass.

## Non-goals

- No machine runtime/API/spec changes.
- No new error tag/subscription, state-specific rendering branch, form framework, schema, or validation.
- No change to retry count, draft preservation, HTTP reply shape/stub timing, final/resting-state semantics, or locked panel.
- No resurrection of per-example Playwright tests and no broad cleanup of the related `examples/core/login` feature.

## Duplicate search

All-status `rg` over `.beads/issues.jsonl` used `state_machine_walkthrough`, `state-machine-walkthrough`, `walkthrough.login`, `login-dismiss`, `dismiss`, `clear-error`, `stale error`, `error-shown`, and retry/error combinations. The only beads naming this example are closed `rf2-ujdn0` (copyable capability launch recipes) and closed `rf2-wuten` (the skill's example catalogue); neither owns runtime error lifecycle or Dismiss behavior. No relevant open, deferred, or closed duplicate was found.

## Uncertainty / witness

Per the review brief, no runtime gate or browser launch was executed during research. The result follows directly from the transition table, documented/implemented merge semantics, subscription, and render predicate. The implementer should first add the two focused assertions against the current table and capture the expected red (error remains `"bad creds"`), then make the two action changes and turn them green.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #9243 (branch worker/exmach-a).

MECHANISM DIFFERS FROM THE ITEM'S RECOMMENDED FIX, deliberately. The item recommended reusing :clear-error as a transition :action on BOTH exits from :error-shown (two table entries). Implemented instead as ONE entry -- :exit :clear-error on the :error-shown state node -- because the machine layer already owns this lifecycle question and the example simply was not using it. :exit is a per-state hook in the spec/005 state-node grammar, keyword-resolved through the same machine-local :actions map, and docs/machines/concepts.md -- the chapter this walkthrough's own ns docstring pins it to -- states the rule in one line: 'Use :entry for work that should happen whenever the state is entered ... Use :exit for cleanup.' The example already showed the :entry half on :submitting; this adds the missing :exit half. Stating the invariant once on the state that owns the error covers both current exits and any third edge added later, which is precisely the failure mode that produced this bug (the guide clears on one edge and not the other). Every acceptance criterion in the item is behavioural and all are met; every non-goal is respected -- no runtime/API/spec change, no new tag, sub, schema or state-specific render branch.

ACCEPTANCE, measured on the JVM by driving the real table through machine-transition, from {:state :error-shown :data {:attempts 1 :error "bad creds"}}:
- Dismiss -> :idle, :error nil, :attempts 1.
- Direct submit -> :submitting, :error nil, :attempts 1, exactly one :rf.http/managed fx.
- Lockout unchanged: third failure -> :locked-out, :attempts 3, terminal message retained.
- First failures still retryable.
- LIVENESS CONTROL: the same table with :exit stripped back off still shows the stale error on both paths, so the green is not vacuous.

STALENESS WINDOW: opens the instant the machine leaves :error-shown; closed only by the next :idle -> :submitting submit. title: core/configure!: non-map calls silently no-op when host builds elide assertions
description:
## Slice reviewed

implementation/core/**, with the actionable center at implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc, public symbol re-frame.core/configure!. Governing contract and focused coverage inspected at spec/API.md and implementation/core/test/re_frame/configure_test.clj. This is the one finding selected after source/API/spec/test/call-site/history review of the slice.

## User-visible and maintainer impact

configure! is a front-porch process-configuration API. Its public contract says it accepts one nested map and that a non-map argument fails loudly. Today that safety depends on the host compiler retaining language assertions. In a legitimate assertion-elided consumer build, a stale keyed-form call such as (rf/configure! :trace-buffer), a vector, or nil silently returns nil and applies nothing. The programmer can therefore believe trace, epoch, or elision configuration was installed when it was ignored. This is especially awkward in pre-alpha, where the retired keyed form is exactly the mistake migration can produce.

The correction is high leverage and low friction: one always-on public-boundary check, one canonical structured error, and focused dual-posture tests. It strengthens the minimal API without adding a validator framework or policing unknown map keys.

## Independently verified current behavior

At repository tip 1ad17a77fe:

- implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2594-2596 implements the entire top-level shape check as (assert (map? config-map) ...).
- With the namespace compiled normally on Clojure 1.12.0, direct calls with :trace-buffer, [:trace-buffer {:events-retained 3}], and nil each throw java.lang.AssertionError.
- In a fresh JVM process, loading re-frame.core inside (binding [*assert* false] (require 're-frame.core)) and then making those same three calls makes every call return nil. No subsystem runs and no diagnostic is emitted.
- The upstream Clojure 1.12.0 assert macro explicitly omits its check when *assert* is false.
- The locally resolved ClojureScript 1.12.145 compiler binds *assert* false when :elide-asserts is true, and the CLJS assert macro only emits code when *assert* is true. Therefore the same source check is absent from such CLJS output.
- The current focused test command, run from implementation/core, is green: clojure -M:test -n re-frame.configure-test ran 5 tests / 28 assertions with zero failures. This demonstrates the coverage gap, not safety under assertion elision.

## Concrete evidence and history

- implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2554-2605 — configure! docstring and implementation; lines 2578 and 2595-2596 promise/enforce the map shape via assert.
- implementation/core/test/re_frame/configure_test.clj:281-293 — configure-non-map-arg-fails-loud explicitly couples all three examples to AssertionError, but compiles only in the ordinary assertion-on posture.
- spec/API.md:872 and :896 — the API is front-porch and says a non-map argument fails loud / MUST be a map.
- git blame attributes the assert to 6730961c897 (2026-06-19), refactor(api): configure! single nested-map entry point (rf2-dzxixe). That commit deliberately retired the keyed form and described non-map input as fail-loud, so silent acceptance under elision contradicts the intended change rather than introducing a new policy.
- bd show rf2-dzxixe reports no matching issue in the current tracker.

## Recommended change

Replace the language assert with an explicit always-on when-not map? check routed through the existing re-frame.error/throw-error! helper already required by re-frame.core. Add one canonical category (suggested name :rf.error/configure-bad-arg), with :where rf/configure!, a short recovery hint to pass one nested map, and bounded/type-oriented received context rather than echoing arbitrary application configuration. Update the error catalogue/projection where project conventions require it.

Preserve the deliberately ergonomic map behavior exactly: valid composed maps still configure known subsystems in the present order; missing keys leave state untouched; unknown top-level keys remain silent no-ops. The reason to use the existing structured-error chokepoint is consistency and AI/tool discoverability, not a broader validation system.

## Bounded implementation scope and non-goals

In scope: the top-level argument guard, its canonical error entry/projection, the focused configure tests, and a genuine assertion-elided verification posture for both runtimes.

Non-goals: do not reject unknown top-level keys; do not validate every nested subsystem option here; do not restore the retired keyed arity; do not redesign configuration schemas/order/merge semantics; do not introduce a general argument-validation abstraction.

## Duplicate search

Tracker searches were run across all statuses before filing:

- bd search "configure" --status all --limit 200 --long: no matches.
- "elide asserts configure", "non-map configure", "configure assertion", "AssertionError", "assertions disabled", and "elide-asserts": no matches.
- broad "assert" search returned four closed issues, all unrelated (routing fixture syntax, Hicasso prose, API-manifest classification, and a prefetch roster assertion).
- description search for configure! returned five unrelated surface/doc facade issues; none concerns core configure argument validation.
- The historical rf2-dzxixe reference is not present in the current tracker.

## Uncertainties

The JVM failure and silent-no-op postures were executed directly. The CLJS conclusion was verified from the resolved compiler and macro sources, but this review did not build a standalone release bundle; the acceptance criteria intentionally require that executable CLJS probe. The exact new error-id spelling should follow the catalogue owner's naming convention; the stable requirement is an always-on canonical structured error, not the suggested token.
design: Keep the patch local to the existing public boundary. A representative shape is (when-not (map? config-map) (rf.error/throw-error! ...)); re-frame.core already requires re-frame.error. Do not move known-key dispatch or tighten the additive top-level vocabulary. Prefer a focused compile-time negative control over a test that merely rebinding *assert* after re-frame.core has already loaded.
acceptance_criteria:
- A non-map passed to re-frame.core/configure! throws one canonical ExceptionInfo error in ordinary Clojure and when re-frame.core is compiled with *assert* false; tests cover at least the retired keyword form, a vector, and nil.
- A ClojureScript test/probe compiled with :elide-asserts true proves the same non-map call still throws the same :rf.error/id; an assertions-on CLJS control remains covered.
- Existing valid-map semantics stay unchanged: all known keys in one map are applied in documented order, a missing key leaves that subsystem untouched, and an unknown top-level key remains a nil-returning no-op.
- The focused tests no longer require AssertionError as the public contract; they assert the canonical id, :where, recovery/reason shape, and avoid requiring raw arbitrary config values in ex-data.
- The error catalogue/API projection is updated as required, and the implementation/core Clojure suite plus the relevant CLJS and production/elision probes pass.

title: re-frame2-pair skill guide still recommends the fail-open compile-only server-test command
description:
## Finding

PR #9130 corrected the pair-MCP artefact's local `:test` alias and tool-side README after proving that `shadow-cljs compile server-test` is not a test verdict: its `:autorun` prints failures but the compile still exits 0. The skill-facing testing guide still presents that exact compile-only command as the MCP server test suite in two live places:

- `skills/re-frame2-pair/docs/TESTING.md:5` says the server "carries its own test suite" under `shadow-cljs compile server-test`.
- `skills/re-frame2-pair/docs/TESTING.md:188` says the MCP server suite runs as `shadow-cljs compile server-test` plus the descriptor-manifest drift gate.

The canonical command is `npm test` from `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/`; `package.json` chains the compile to `node out/server-test.js`, and Node's exit code is the verdict. The tool-side `test/README.md` now states this explicitly.

## Impact

A programmer or AI following the skill guide can receive exit 0 over real test failures—the fail-open signal #9130 fixed everywhere inside the tool fence. The skill guide is especially likely to be used as an execution recipe, so leaving the stale spelling defeats the discoverability half of the fix.

## Disposition

Update both skill-guide references to make `npm test` the suite command. If the compile phase is mentioned, label it only as a build/autorun phase and state that `node out/server-test.js` supplies the test verdict. Keep the explanation compact and point to the tool's test README rather than duplicating the incident transcript.

## Duplicate search

All-status Beads searches for `compile server-test`, the exact skill-doc path, `pair-mcp test command`, `MCP server suite`, `Node run is a verdict`, and `server-test verdict` returned no owner. `rf2-7r9w` owns and closed the tool-side fail-open; this bead owns only the two out-of-fence skill-document references it explicitly left behind.
