title: Make reply completion-time pair coverage exhaustive
description:
## Finding

The non-success completion-time matrix checks a pair only when at least one of its `*-with-time` / `*-no-time` builders exists. If both keys are deleted or misspelled, `:when (or with-builder no-builder)` silently removes that family/situation from both the primary propagation/omission test and its adversarial controls. `time-pair-exclusions` is a separate manually maintained vector, but no test proves that every omitted pair has an explicit exclusion.

## Evidence

- `implementation/reply-conformance/test/re_frame/reply_vocab_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:428-460` defines the three pair axes and the three deliberate exclusions.
- Lines 616-649 assert that a half-pair is invalid, but the `:when (or with-builder no-builder)` filter means a zero-pair is invisible.
- Lines 847-871 repeat the same declared-pairs-only traversal for the drop/nil-fill controls.
- Lines 651-665 validate entries already present in `time-pair-exclusions`; they do not establish completeness or exclusivity against the supported `:error`, `:cancel`, and `:stale` builders in `families`.
- Concrete false-green: delete both `:error-with-time` and `:error-no-time` from the HTTP descriptor. HTTP still has its ordinary `:error` builder, all envelope/status/work-id validations still run, and the completion-time pair plus controls silently skip HTTP error. No exclusion is required or reported.
- The current JVM tier passes 27 tests / 533 assertions. The issue is structural non-vacuity under matrix drift, not a present production failure.

## Impact

A future descriptor refactor can remove an entire completion-time obligation while keeping the suite green. That reopens the exact umbrella gap this tier exists to close: a family can stop proving that a supplied causal completion timestamp propagates and an absent timestamp is omitted.

## Recommendation

Add an executable partition/bijection check over every supported non-success family/situation: it must declare exactly one of (a) a complete with-time/no-time pair or (b) one explicit exclusion with a reason. Unsupported baseline situations should declare neither. Reuse that validated partition to drive the primary and adversarial tests, avoiding independent skip logic.

## Risks and contracts

Do not impose `:completed-at` on terminals whose production builder deliberately does not accept or durably use it (HTTP stale, machine cancel, timer cancel). Preserve unsupported route/timer error/cancel distinctions. This is a test-matrix completeness fix, not a production timestamp policy change.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every supported `:error`, `:cancel`, or `:stale` row is classified as either a complete time pair or one explicit exclusion.
2. A family/situation with neither classification fails with a diagnostic naming the family and situation.
3. A half-pair, duplicate pair-plus-exclusion, duplicate exclusion, or exclusion for an unsupported situation fails.
4. A focused mutation proves deleting both keys from one currently paired row makes the suite red.
5. Existing propagation, omission, reply validation, and drop/nil-fill controls remain green in JVM and consolidated CLJS lanes.

title: pilots package: nothing tells the pilot WHERE to read the published documentation, and the read fence does not affirmatively allow docs/core/ in the checkout
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 02:55 AUSEST by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal, assembling both workspaces from docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/. Tip d1e6a707a3.

THE GAP. The pilot's brief makes the published documentation the reference for everything: 'Everything you need is in the published Hicasso documentation... It is your reference for everything: what to type, what things are called, why something broke, how to test, how to build for production.' Nothing in the package then says where that documentation IS.

- workspace.md's six assembly steps never build the docs site, never copy the pages in, and never record a URL. Step 6 copies only the brief and the blank log.
- The workspace layout block lists re-frame2/, app/, BRIEF.md and FRICTION-LOG.md. No docs.
- friction-log.md's template header asks the pilot to fill in 'Docs read from: <published site URL or local build>' — a field whose answer the package never supplies. There is no published site (the installation page still says the artefact is not published), so 'published site URL' is not available, and 'local build' is never described.

AND THE FENCE DOES NOT CLEARLY PERMIT THE ONE COPY THAT EXISTS. The only copy of those 29 pages is docs/core/hicasso/ inside the re-frame2/ checkout. workspace.md's read fence is headed 'The checkout is a build input, not a reference work' and its Allowed column has exactly three rows: resolving dependencies via :local/root; running a tool a published page names, at the path that page gives; reading error text and stack traces. Reading documentation is not among them. The Not-allowed column names spec/, docs/design/ and other examples — but not docs/core/, so the page neither permits nor forbids it.

A pilot reading the fence literally concludes the checkout may not be read as a reference work, that docs/core/ is part of the checkout, and therefore that it has no reachable documentation at all. A pilot reading it loosely reads the docs and cannot tell whether it has just logged a leak. Either way the citation-enforced fence — which is the instrument rf2-hic-069's audit consumes, and the thing that makes the blinding mechanical rather than impressionistic — is ambiguous at the one point it is used on every single entry.

WHAT IT IS NOT. This is not the same as gap G1/G2/G3 in pilots/README.md. Those record that the published happy path routes through a checkout at three points. This is that the package never states where the pilot's primary reference lives, nor that reading it is allowed.

FIX (the least thing). One line in workspace.md's assembly — an explicit step naming where the pilot reads the 29 pages from, either a locally built site or the docs/core/hicasso/ path — and one row in the fence's Allowed column saying that reading docs/core/hicasso/ IS the published documentation and is clean, so a citation to it is not a leak. The friction-log header field then has a defined answer.

WHY IT SURVIVED REVIEW. The package was written before any workspace was assembled; the omission is only visible to somebody executing the page, which is what this rehearsal did.

FILED, NOT FIXED.
notes:
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03 03:5x AUSEST. THE PILOT READS THE PUBLISHED DOCUMENTATION, AND UNTIL A SITE EXISTS THE PUBLISHED DOCUMENTATION IS THE CHECKOUT COPY OF IT. The fence must say so affirmatively; ambiguity at the one point the fence is used on every task is worse than either answer.

THE RULE, and it is mechanically decidable rather than a list that will drift: ALLOWED is anything under docs/ THAT THE PUBLISHED SITE BUILDS. That set is exactly mkdocs.yml docs_dir minus its exclude_docs block, so it is checkable by running the build rather than by consulting prose — and it gives the right answer for free on the hard cases: docs/design/ is in exclude_docs, so it stays forbidden by the same rule that permits docs/core/hicasso/, with no second sentence needed. NOT ALLOWED is everything else in the checkout: spec/, implementation/ source, other examples, ai/, and the design trees.

WHY THIS AND NOT THE NARROW FORM. Writing "docs/core/hicasso/ is allowed" would work today and reintroduce the ambiguity the moment a pilot follows a link out of those 29 pages into docs/core/ or docs/ssr/ — which the pages themselves do. A real adopter browsing a site can reach any published page; the fence should model that reader, not a subdirectory.

WHAT ELSE HAS TO MOVE WITH IT, because a permission that the assembly steps do not realise is still a gap:
  - workspace.md read fence: add the Allowed row, in the table own voice, and keep the heading "The checkout is a build input, not a reference work" HONEST by saying what the exception is and why it exists — there is no published site yet, and the installation page says so.
  - friction-log.md "Docs read from:" must have a supplied answer. Give it one: the local checkout copy of the published documentation, at the path, with the note that no published site exists yet.
  - The workspace layout block lists re-frame2/, app/, BRIEF.md, FRICTION-LOG.md and no docs. Say where the docs are in that block, or the pilot has to infer it.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE: the citation-enforced fence stays the instrument rf2-hic-069 audit consumes, and it stays MECHANICAL. This ruling makes it decidable; it does not loosen it. A pilot that reads spec/ has still leaked.
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03 04:2x AUSEST, on the judgement call the pilotpkg-a worker referred up. THE BRIEF CHANGE STAYS. It is inside my ruling intent and the worker found a carrier I missed.

WHAT IT DID BEYOND THE RULED THREE SITES. My ruling named three things that had to move together: the read fence in workspace.md, friction-log.md "Docs read from:", and the workspace layout block. The worker also changed BOTH PILOT BRIEFS, and its reasoning is the correct one: the brief is what the assembly ACTUALLY HANDS THE PILOT, and it said the checkout may not be read "for anything other than the two mechanical uses". So with the permission recorded only in the operator page and the prohibition still in the pilot own document, THE PILOT RECEIVES THE PROHIBITION AND NEVER THE PERMISSION — which is this bead defect restated one document over.

That is not scope creep. My three-site list was an enumeration of carriers, and I enumerated it wrong; a ruling that fixes three of four carriers leaves the bug live. Outcome 7 in both briefs was correctly left untouched, which is the line I would have drawn myself.

AND THE WORKER CAUGHT A HOLE IN MY RULING OWN MECHANISM, which is the part worth recording. I wrote the permitted set as "anything under docs/ THAT THE PUBLISHED SITE BUILDS — exactly docs_dir minus exclude_docs", specifically so it would be mechanically decidable and would settle the hard case (docs/design/ is in exclude_docs, so it stays forbidden by the same rule that permits docs/core/hicasso/). IT FAILS ON A DIFFERENT HARD CASE I DID NOT CONSIDER: mkdocs_hooks.py on_pre_build STAGES ROOT spec/ INTO docs_dir, so the built site DOES serve spec/ — and a rule worded that way would have PERMITTED the one tree the fence most needs to forbid. The worker scoped the rule to the CHECKOUT docs/ tree instead, which closes it without a second sentence.

I find that instructive against myself: the staging hook is the exact mechanism I have been correcting other people about all session, after being measured wrong on it twice, and I still wrote a rule that the hook silently inverts. A mechanically-decidable rule is only as good as the mechanism you checked it against, and I checked mine against exclude_docs and not against the hook.

VERIFICATION I AM SATISFIED WITH: exclude_docs read at source (six entries) AND confirmed by RUNNING the build — site/design does not exist, site/core/hicasso/ has exactly 29 pages. That is the difference between reading a config and observing its effect.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9049 — reopened the exact owner for one missed carrier. The four edited pages correctly make the checkout copy of the published docs reachable, but docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/README.md:30 remains untouched and still states categorically that the checkout is only a build input, that a pilot may not read it for answers, and that the permitted boundary is dependency/tool execution. That directly contradicts the new workspace/brief rule allowing the published pages under docs/ that the site builds. Minimal completion: amend this one governing-package paragraph to name the documentation exception in the same terms; do not widen the fence or reopen the settled manifest/outcome-7 work. No duplicate issue.
close_reason: FIXED in PR #9058, the one missed carrier the #9049 audit reopened this for. docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/README.md:30 now names the documentation exception in the four already-edited pages' own terms rather than a fifth phrasing: 'build input, not a reference work - with one exception' and 'an exception about where the documentation is kept, not about what may be studied' from workspace.md:39; 'anything under docs/ the site builds, which is where docs/core/hicasso/'s 29 pages live' from the read-fence table row at workspace.md:43; 'Reading them is not reading the checkout' from inside both briefs' fences; 'there is no published site yet' from friction-log.md's template header. The paragraph's second half -- the prohibition list (implementation/, spec/, docs/design/, other examples, tracker, history) and the executing-versus-browsing line -- is carried over verbatim, so the fence is not widened. The manifest and outcome 7 were not reopened. Heading text unchanged, since the audit cites headings as anchors. Verified by a planted broken link on this exact line that took check_doc_slugs.py red and was then restored and confirmed by git blob hash.

title: [method] the reap route stops at the empty sink: an id keys TWO locations and the doc names only the expensive fallback
notes:
FILED 2026-09-02 01:28 AUSEST by the acting mayor, from the Method reread loop (loops.md §6),
against a rule I had just spent a whole Hygiene loop enforcing. This is the §6 category
"hazards recorded without their discriminating test" — the hazard is on the page, the cheap
test that discharges it is not, and the doc jumps straight to the expensive fallback.

WHAT THE DOC SAYS TODAY. loops.md §5 Reaping records the empty-sink hazard correctly and at
length: "beware a per-agent scratch sink that merely shares the id"; "An empty file keyed by
the id says nothing whatever about whether a report exists - it is a fact about that file";
"the sink read empty for fifteen of seventeen worktrees, every one of those fifteen
transcripts sat complete elsewhere". It then says "the id names a FILE only once you know
which file is the agent's OWN; until then it names a directory to search", and the NEXT
paragraph - headed "When no id was recorded at all" - gives the path search: grep every
transcript for the worktree path, rank by hit count, confirm by the report's own claimed root.

THE GAP. Between "the sink is empty" and "grep 4.6 GB of transcripts" there is a step the doc
never names: TRY THE ID AT ITS OTHER LOCATION. An agent id is not one path. Here it keys both
a per-task scratch sink AND the real session transcript store, under different roots and a
different filename convention. The doc's own evidence already implies a second location exists
- "their real transcripts sat complete elsewhere" - but it never turns "elsewhere" into a step,
so a reader who has just been told the sink lies goes to the path search, which is two orders
of magnitude more expensive and, per the doc's own warning, many-to-one and misrankable.

MEASURED TODAY, one hygiene pass, 40 candidate worktrees.
  - 38 had a ledger id; 2 had no row at all.
  - Scratch sink keyed by id: NON-EMPTY for 9, exactly 0 bytes for 31. Consistent with the
    doc's "fifteen of seventeen", so the recorded constant is NOT stale - the remedy is
    incomplete.
  - Second id-keyed location: held a complete transcript for ALL 31 of the empty-sink ids.
    Zero misses. 29 of the 31 opened their final message with a quotable completion sentence;
    the other 2 (adapterswitch, twosmall) ended on interim status and were correctly REFUSED
    the reap - the route works in both directions, which is what makes it a test rather than
    a shortcut.
  - Path search was needed for exactly 2 of 40, both unindexed: timerincarn-jqvgp resolved
    cleanly (92 hits in the worker's own transcript against 1 in each peer, and its report's
    claimed root matched), and http-issuance did not (every hit was 1 - peers naming it and
    nothing else), so that tree stays.

So the expensive fallback earned its place once in forty, and the doc points at it thirty-one
times too often.

PROPOSED, small, and it belongs inside the existing Reaping paragraph that already warns about
the sink rather than as a new block. Say that an id can key MORE THAN ONE location; that an
empty one is a fact about THAT location and not about the id; and that the step between them is
to enumerate the id's other locations before falling back to the path search. Keep the path
search exactly where it is, as the route for an id that was never recorded - which is what it
is actually for.

GENERICITY. State it as "an agent id may key several locations" rather than naming this host's
directory layout. A transcript path the platform documents as an implementation detail is not a
contract - loops.md says so itself two paragraphs later - so the durable instruction is
"enumerate the id's locations", not "look in <path>".

SEQUENCING - MANDATORY. docs/the-mayor-method/ is SOLE-TOUCHER hot-zone. PR #8962
(worker/methodstep-ute0q, rf2-ute0q + rf2-f7fby) is OPEN against loops.md and
dispatch-prompt-template.md right now. DO NOT DISPATCH until #8962 merges.

GATE: python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py plus python -m mkdocs build --strict (exclude_docs
does NOT hide the-mayor-method/). Run mkdocs as "python -m mkdocs" - bare mkdocs returns 127
here, which is NO VERDICT rather than a pass. Neither gate reads prose, tables or rendering:
verify those by hand and say so in the PR body.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #8966, verified on main at b99e95fefa (docs(method): name the id's other locations as the step between an empty sink and the path search). Verified by MERGE, not by PR state. The repair sits INSIDE the existing empty-sink paragraph in loops.md section 5 Reaping - an id may key several locations rather than one, an empty one is a fact about THAT location and not about the id, and the step between them is to enumerate the id's remaining locations before falling back to the path search, which is left verbatim and in place as the route for an id that was never recorded. Carries the forty-worktree measurement including the both-directions discrimination (29 quotable reports found, 2 correctly REFUSED on interim status). Written generically - 'an id may key several locations', no host directory layout - as the bead required, since the page itself says two paragraphs later that a platform-documented transcript path is not a contract. No harm - I dispatched after the merge - but the note outlived its condition. Re-run standalone, green.

title: surface-review(skill-xray): make one debugging question land on one first Xray surface
description:
## Scope

Treat skills/re-frame2-xray/** as one distinct published tour product. Make a concrete programmer question land quickly on the one existing Xray surface to open first, then reveal only the detail needed for that surface.

Rework the top-level skill, its panel references, README/package descriptions, eval material, and the small docs mirrors that restate the skill's routing contract. Preserve Xray's shipped two-mode UI and all current panels. Keep the actor boundary explicit: Xray is the visible human panel; re-frame2-pair is the agent-facing runtime reader and driver.

## Findings

1. The file that calls itself a “compact tour/router” is already an encyclopedia. skills/re-frame2-xray/SKILL.md is 4,723 words / 33,441 bytes / 442 lines before any reference is loaded. A basic “which panel?” request passes through the Redux analogy, launch APIs, all hotkeys, the full 10-tab Dynamic table, the 5-tab Static table, chrome, exclusions, implementation ids, and retired-control warnings before reaching an answer.

2. Progressive disclosure does not reduce the expensive case. Every deep panel question routes to one references/panels.md catalogue: 6,380 words / 49,571 bytes / 853 lines. A one-panel question can therefore load 11,103 words / 83,012 bytes across SKILL.md plus panels.md. The repository's own leaf discipline is 250 lines / 16 KB unless a catalogue cannot be split profitably; this catalogue can be split along the existing question/scope seams, so one question need not pay for fourteen unrelated tabs.

3. Xray's useful information architecture is not adequately described by the first Dynamic-versus-Static fork. Six Dynamic tabs rebind to the focused epoch; Resources mixes process-global, observed-frame, and trace evidence; Graph, Frames, and Hicasso sit in the Dynamic shell but do not rebind to the selected epoch; Static catalogues are process-global with a few per-frame live projections. The skill knows this in its scope matrix, but the normal tour remains mode-first and inventory-first. A programmer starts with “what changed?”, “why did this render?”, “what is registered?”, or “where does this value come from?”, not with an internal tab roster.

4. The package has tab descriptions but no compact panel-tour gesture. The useful daily path is: choose frame, choose event when the question is event-shaped, start at Epoch, branch to state/render/raw/specialist evidence, and use Static only for definitions. docs/xray/02-panel-tour.md states a five-step version, but SKILL.md does not make it the entry path and neither surface handles the non-epoch Dynamic tabs cleanly. The result is a list of destinations instead of a fast route through them.

5. The Pair handoff is directionally right but its slogan is wrong. “Xray owns the seeing; Pair owns the driving” implies that a read-only live-runtime inspection belongs to Xray. Pair's actual first-contact sequence is discover-app → orient → targeted read, and it owns read-sub, get-path, snapshots, trace/epoch reads, DOM/UI reads, and Hicasso evidence as well as writes. rf2-7htk7 independently establishes the desired singular boundary: Xray for the human panel, Pair for programmer/AI runtime access. The Xray evals reject one write prompt (“dispatch this”) but have no negative read-only agent prompt.

6. The same volatile inventory and caveats are copied through SKILL.md, references/panels.md, references/shared-components.md, README.md, package.json, plugin.json, eval prose, skills/README.md, and docs/skills/re-frame2-xray.md. Drift is visible now: the package README's scope sentence names Graph and Frames as non-epoch exceptions but omits Hicasso; docs/skills/re-frame2-xray.md lists Esc as a focus-gated spine shortcut while the owning launch leaf says it is modal-local; docs/xray/index.md says every tab rebinds to the focused epoch, contradicting the current scope matrix. More copied warnings or prose locks will not make this easier to use.

7. The 30 evals mostly protect churn facts. Fourteen answer-quality cases pin launch calls, retired labels, exact tab counts, hidden mount facades, future hotkeys, and control precedence. Those facts have value, but there is no answer-quality route for the everyday Epoch, Views, Trace, Routes, Resources, or Hicasso questions; no read-only Pair disqualifier; no score for giving one first surface without dumping the whole inventory; and no check of which reference leaf was loaded. The harness is manual and records no observed end-to-end panel-tour result.

8. History confirms an accretion loop. The package has 69 commits since its May introduction and SKILL.md itself has 39. Commit b7798297d9 tried to tighten body ownership and add progressive disclosure, yet the body is now 4,723 words and its one panel leaf is 6,380. Commit 7cc83f0d8e / rf2-5atkk repaired the sharpest failure: the skill taught nine tabs while its own eval required ten and rejected a nine-tab answer. The next improvement should reduce the number of places that must move, not preserve the catalogue in more forms.

## Recommended Action

Rebuild the published tour around one question-first route card:

- First fork on actor and interface. “Where in the visible Xray panel do I look?” stays here. “Inspect or change my running app for me” routes to re-frame2-pair, whether the requested runtime operation is read-only or mutating.
- For panel questions, route by the evidence sought: one dispatch/cascade; changed state; subscriptions/renders; raw ordering; machine or route activity; live server/runtime structure; dependency/image/Hicasso structure; registered definitions. Return the visible mode/tab label, why it is the first stop, and the first interaction (pick frame/event, open the tab, or flip Static). Name a second lens only when it is the natural next step.
- Keep one compact canonical inventory for explicit “list every tab” requests. Do not make every routine answer traverse that inventory.
- Replace the monolithic panels.md load with small one-level leaves divided by the existing evidence/scope questions. A deep question about one panel family should load only that family, not all 15 tabs. Keep normative implementation anatomy in linked Xray specs/source rather than duplicating it into the tour.
- Strip internal ids, sparse order values, source-file inventories, deleted-panel archaeology, and repeated “do not invent” clauses from the normal path unless they disambiguate a live user-visible control. Trust programmers with direct current guidance.
- Align README/package/plugin and the docs skill mirror around the role and the canonical route card. Where docs/xray/index.md or 02-panel-tour.md repeats a directly contradictory scope sentence, correct or link it; do not turn this into a broad docs rewrite.
- Repurpose the existing eval corpus toward route quality: representative questions across the existing scope families, one read-only Pair handoff, concise first-surface answers, and proof that a deep question loads only its focused leaf. Keep a small set of genuinely high-risk launch/control distinctions. Add no new runner, gate, policy layer, or generated compatibility table.

- docs/xray/index.md:20 says every Dynamic tab rebinds to one epoch; skills/re-frame2-xray/SKILL.md:222-240 and references/panels.md:71-92 document the three actual scope axes.
- evals/evals.json contains 30 fixtures (22 positive, 8 negative); its 14 answer-quality cases are dominated by launch/current-control and drift-rejection facts. The only Pair disqualifier is id 13's mutating dispatch request.
- Git history: 39 commits touch SKILL.md and 69 touch the package. b7798297d9 introduced the current body/leaf/eval shape; 7cc83f0d8e fixed rf2-5atkk's skill-versus-own-eval tab-count contradiction.
- Existing-bead search: all-status searches for surface-review(skill-xray), question-first, panel-tour, progressive disclosure, router, token burden, and panels.md found no current owner for this outcome. rf2-7htk7 owns the duplicate runtime seam, not the tour information architecture.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A concrete “where in Xray?” prompt returns one existing starting surface in the first paragraph: visible mode/tab, the reason, and the first interaction. It does not enumerate all 15 tabs unless the user asked for the inventory.
2. Representative route cases cover at least the existing focused-epoch, observed-frame/live-structure, process-global/registry, and Static-definition scopes. No new mode, panel, or aggregate is invented.
3. The panel-tour path is explicit and short: choose frame; choose an event only for event-shaped questions; start at Epoch for “what happened?”; branch to the exact state/render/raw/specialist lens; use Static for definitions. Non-epoch Dynamic surfaces do not pretend to follow the event.
4. The routing boundary is human panel versus agent runtime, not read versus write. A prompt asking the agent to inspect a running app routes to re-frame2-pair even when it requests no mutation; a prompt asking where a human should look in Xray remains in this skill.
5. Routine selection questions are answerable from SKILL.md alone. A deeper panel question loads SKILL.md plus at most one focused, one-level reference leaf that meets the repository's 250-line / 16-KB target. The PR reports before/after loaded words and bytes for one routine route and one deep-panel route; the 49,571-byte all-panels load is gone.
6. There is one canonical complete tab inventory and one canonical question-to-surface map inside the package. README, package/plugin descriptions, skills/README.md, and docs/skills/re-frame2-xray.md summarize the role or link to that authority instead of copying detailed tab anatomy and exception rosters.
7. Current visible guidance is retained where it changes the user's action: inline versus overlay, the visible pop-out button, passive inspect versus Reset rewind, Graph's local projection versus top-level Static mode, and the absence of a dedicated Issues tab. Internal ids/order/source paths and retired alternatives are absent from the normal route unless the question asks for them.
8. Existing evals are revised rather than surrounded by a new framework. They grade concise first-surface routing across the scope families, a read-only Pair handoff, the explicit full-inventory request, and the focused-leaf load. The PR reports observed manual outputs for those cases.
9. The skill package and its small mirrors have a net reduction in prose and no contradictory scope/hotkey sentence among the touched surfaces. Existing JSON, package, link/anchor, skill-doc, and Xray tab-inventory checks pass; no new prose-presence test, linter, generator, or CI job is added.

## Non-goals

title: surface-review(mcp-base): return the pair-only epoch diff codec to Pair-MCP
description:
## Scope

Restore tools/mcp-base to its documented role as the small library of primitives shared by the shipped MCP servers. Move the epoch :db-after diff codec and its section-grouping helper, specs, tests, Closure define, and conformance ownership from re-frame.mcp-base into tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp. Preserve Pair-MCP's tool names, arguments, result shapes, :rf.mcp/diff-from wire representation, defaults, ordering, and errors.

## Findings

- The base contract says it contains genuinely cross-cutting primitives consumed by every MCP server and explicitly says a primitive stays consumer-side until a second consumer needs it.
- Current production imports contradict that boundary: Pair-MCP alone requires re-frame.mcp-base.diff-encode; Story-MCP has no source reference. section-grouping is referenced only by diff-encode.
- These namespaces are substantial: 1,324 of 4,633 physical base source lines (28.6%), plus 1,276 focused test lines, two spec pages, Malli-specific validation/test setup, and Pair/global Closure-define wiring.
- The conformance suite's use of the builder is test evidence for Pair's wire shape, not an independent runtime consumer.
- History confirms this was never a stable cross-server seam: c4abf7f799 moved Pair's diff block into the new base, while neither Story-MCP nor the former Causa-MCP ever imported the namespace; the later section-grouping surface likewise serves only Pair epoch responses.
- Keeping a single-consumer codec in the common jar enlarges the API downstream MCP authors must understand, makes Pair's epoch representation look like a cross-MCP obligation, and violates the package's own admission rule.

## Recommended Action

Rehome the two pure .cljc namespaces under Pair-MCP with Pair-owned names, carrying their JVM/CLJS tests and specs with them. Retarget Pair production calls, its Closure define, and the wire-vocabulary conformance witness to that implementation. Remove the namespaces, Malli-only diff setup, focused tests, and index rows from mcp-base. Keep the existing :rf.mcp/diff-from vocabulary and observable wire shape stable; vocabulary constants intentionally reserved across MCP tools may remain shared.

Do not introduce a generic codec protocol, registry abstraction, forwarding namespace, or compatibility alias. The implementation remains useful; its truthful owner is the only server that emits it.

## Evidence

- tools/mcp-base/spec/README.md:4 calls the library genuinely cross-cutting primitives consumed by every MCP server; lines 107-111 require a second consumer before lifting.
- Only tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/snapshot_pipeline.cljs and wire_pipeline.cljs call base-diff functions; no Story-MCP production source imports diff-encode.
- tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/diff_encode.cljc is 911 lines and section_grouping.cljc is 413; their focused JVM tests total 1,276 lines.
- tools/mcp-base/spec/diff-encode.md defines epoch :db-after encoding; section-grouping.md identifies diff-encode as its consumer.
- tools/mcp-base/deps.edn carries Malli for the diff validation suite; Pair/global Shadow configs carry the re-frame.mcp-base.diff-encode/validate-patches? production define.
- tools/mcp-conformance/wire-vocab invokes the builder only to validate Pair's marker schema.
- History: c4abf7f799 introduced mcp-base and moved Pair's implementation; git log -S searches show no Story-MCP or Causa-MCP consumer. Commit 6191a6b316 later removed Causa-MCP.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. day8/re-frame2-mcp-base no longer publishes or documents diff-encode or section-grouping; its source/spec index and test/dependency configuration contain only genuinely shared surfaces.
2. Pair-MCP owns equivalent .cljc encode/decode and section-grouping namespaces. Its production pipeline, default epochs-mode, :rf.mcp/diff-from body, section ordering/classification, error ids, and full-mode pass-through remain unchanged.
3. The complete relocated corpus runs on JVM and CLJS, including map/vector/set round trips, malformed-marker failures, Malli-present validation, Malli-absent or Closure-disabled production behavior, and section losslessness/order.
4. The wire-vocabulary conformance gate exercises the Pair-owned canonical emitter and existing fixtures/schemas without changing the marker's observable wire shape.
5. Pair's local and root Shadow builds use the new Closure-define symbol; no tracked production, test, spec, generated-manifest, or conformance file requires the removed base namespaces.
6. mcp-base JVM/CLJS gates and Pair focused/descriptor/conformance gates pass non-vacuously; a package-content check proves the base jar excludes the pair-only namespaces.
7. No forwarding namespace or deprecated alias preserves the old internal API; current pre-alpha consumers migrate in the same change.

## Non-goals

- Removing diff encoding from Pair-MCP, changing its default, or redesigning the patch/section grammar.
- Renaming :rf.mcp/diff-from, changing epoch records, or changing any tool schema/result.
- Moving genuinely shared args, cursor, cap, dedup, egress, envelope, privacy, vocabulary, or descriptor-manifest primitives out of mcp-base.
- Unifying handler arities, registries, transports, or result-envelope representations.
- Adding a general plugin/codec framework, external runtime dependency, or automated two-consumers policy engine.
- Solving the separate Clojars group-verification/publish blocker.

## Related beads

- rf2-ahjbc is an adjacent open Pair-MCP simplification touching parts of the same tool surface; coordinate file ownership if both are implemented concurrently, but neither blocks the other.
- rf2-uelji is the deferred Clojars first-publish blocker; this task improves package ownership independently.
- Exact current and closed tracker searches for surface-review(mcp-base), epoch diff, pair-only, section grouping, mcp base, diff, and related descriptions found no duplicate outcome.

The boundary argument is true, but the move's hidden cost is disproportionate: the 1,276-line test corpus is JVM .clj with Malli, and tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp has NO JVM test lane (its :test alias is a shadow compile), so relocating means a new JVM alias + Malli dep in a CLJS-only npm artefact, a new test.yml job (hot zone), scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh roster + check_jvm_lane_rosters.py bijection edits, and wire-vocab's :local/root switching to Pair (dragging shadow-cljs/js-interop onto its JVM classpath). Cheap alternative, filed as the disposition: one sentence in tools/mcp-base/spec/README.md:107-111 recording diff-encode/section-grouping as a Pair-owned codec hosted in base for its JVM+Malli lane — fold into any later mcp-base prose PR. Mike may override; reopen if so.

THE FACT, MEASURED AT THE CLASSIFIER (paths handed to .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh directly, tip 447af7b539, both directions with a positive control):

                                                migration_hicasso_codemod=true,
                                                hicasso_controlled=true, hicasso_hmr=true
  implementation/hicasso/src/.../core.cljs   -> the IDENTICAL set

That identity is the point: the five operative contract documents rf2-ps7ia moved into implementation/hicasso/spec/ are classified exactly as production CLJS source, because the `implementation/hicasso/*` case arm does not discriminate `.md`. A one-word typo fix in a Markdown register therefore queues cljs_browser, hicasso_controlled and hicasso_hmr -- three Chromium lanes -- plus a ~10-minute CLJS compile.

WHY IT IS A CALL AND NOT A BUG. Two standing principles point opposite ways.
  FOR keeping it: TESTING.md's standing rule is 'when in doubt, over-classify'. Over-arming is the failure mode the repo deliberately prefers, and rf2-8a6s's own comment records that this arm exists precisely because a hicasso-only diff once classified to NOTHING and merged green.
  AGAINST keeping it: the comment block above the complaint-catalogue test in implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs says in terms that 'arming a ~10-minute CLJS compile for a Markdown edit is the trade TESTING.md's placement table exists to refuse'. That sentence was written about these very documents, at their old address.

THE NARROWING, IF MIKE WANTS IT. An `implementation/hicasso/spec/*.md` case placed BEFORE the `implementation/hicasso/*` arm, setting cljs_node_test only. Rationale: what these five documents actually gate is the invariants chain, which is pure Python -- check_complaint_catalogue.py, the budget-ledger reconciliation, the facade-inventory diff -- and Markdown cannot change what React puts on a page, which is the line rf2-drpa3.70 already drew for prose arms and which _changed-surfaces.test.cjs holds for every other prose arm in the file ('prose arms the JVM tier and NO browser/prod/Playwright tier').

WHAT ALREADY STANDS BEHIND THESE DOCUMENTS EITHER WAY, so the narrowing is not as exposed as it looks: all five carry UNCONDITIONAL test.yml jobs of their own -- hicasso-complaint-catalogue, hicasso-budget-ledger and hicasso-facade-inventory each carry no `needs: detect_changed_surfaces` and no `if:`, by design, precisely because a surface gate that did not cover a checker's inputs was the original defect (rf2-hic-021 / rf2-ibje). docs.yml separately arms the warm-allocation scan on implementation/hicasso/spec/budgets.md by name (rf2-ps7ia).

EXECUTION NOTE IF IT IS RULED. .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh and implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs are the one-toucher pair -- the test pins the script's outputs, so this lands in ONE commit touching both, and the row PR #8664 added (implementation/hicasso/spec/complaints.md arms cljs_node_test=true) stays true under the narrowing while the three Chromium outputs would need new false rows beside it.

title: Playwright→CLJS Wave-2: migrate tools/causa/testbeds/parallel_frames to multi-frame CLJS e2e (rf2-tglku Wave 2)
description:
Per Playwright migration manifest (tools/story/spec/Migration-Audit.md, rf2-tglku audit Wave 2). The testbeds/parallel_frames Playwright spec asserts parallel-frame isolation — that two frames mounted in the same process keep their app-db / subs / event-handlers fully isolated. This is rf2-7icrs's exact use case.

**Migrate**: tools/causa/testbeds/parallel_frames/spec.cjs → CLJS e2e test using multi-frame helpers (rf2-7icrs).

**Assertion contract** (read the existing spec.cjs to enumerate):
- Two frames mount in the same process
- Each frame has its own app-db (writes to one don't bleed into the other)
- Each frame's subs see its own state
- Events dispatched to one frame fire its handlers only
- Frames can be destroyed independently
- Cross-frame sub computation is REJECTED (per [[feedback_frames_are_isolated_contexts]])

**Migration target**:
- New CLJS test in `implementation/core/test/re_frame/multi_frame_isolation_test.cljs` (or extend existing multi-frame test if present)
- Use rf2-7icrs's frame creation + dispatch + assert helpers (multi-frame e2e is the canonical mechanism — see other tests for the pattern)

**Delete after verifying coverage**:
- `tools/causa/testbeds/parallel_frames/spec.cjs`
- Keep `core.cljs`, `index.html`, `README.md` (Causa-displayable showcase remains)

**Update manifest doc** (`tools/story/spec/Migration-Audit.md` §Per-spec classification) — mark parallel_frames row as Wave-2 migrated.

**Pre-alpha posture**: clean delete + clean new test. No transition.

**Acceptance**:
- `testbeds/parallel_frames/spec.cjs` removed
- New CLJS test asserts the same isolation contract
- Manifest doc updated
- Framework-testbeds Playwright gate (from #1688 split) still passes on the residual surfaces

**Out of scope**: Wave 3 (SSR migrations · 3 beads · likely cluster) handled separately.

title: [DISPATCHED - in flight, 018 surface held] False Static picker rationale: registrar catalogues are shared across frames
description:
Merged-PR audit #10110 (8e613c1bbbac67a106d95ccd821c9945f534c674). The correction correctly keeps the Static frame picker, but its new tools/xray/spec/018-Event-Spine.md:127 rationale says registrations live in a particular frame, so selecting a frame chooses which registrations are browsed. That is false for the Static registrar catalogues.

The same cited source explicitly distinguishes these axes: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/shell.cljs:25-48 says event/sub/route/interceptor/machine-definition catalogues are shared, while the picker scopes machine snapshots, the per-frame flows registry, app-db-schema side-table and current-route data. Actual source-store reads confirm it: static/interceptors/panel.cljs:482-495 reads rf/registrations {:source :store :kind :event}, with no selected-frame argument; static/schemas/panel.cljs:547-555 separates schemas-by-frame from the global event/sub catalogue reads. The new prose copied the contradictory ribbon docstring at static/shell.cljs:351-356 (and the same-frame-registrations comment at :328-330), instead of that file's corrected namespace contract.

This is an incorrect explanation of what choosing a frame changes: it makes a global catalogue remaining unchanged look like a broken picker. Keep the useful control and the correct availability change. Correct the new 018 rationale and the cited stale ribbon explanation to distinguish global registrar catalogues from the per-frame data Static actually projects. A concise statement plus examples or a pointer is enough; do not redesign the picker, make catalogues frame-filtered, or launch a terminology sweep. Flows and app-db schemas genuinely have per-frame stores, so do not replace the error with a blanket statement that all registration-like data is global.

Verified against the exact merge, production catalogue reads, unconditional ribbon composition and mode handlers (which only assoc :mode and preserve selection). No exact literally OPEN finding records this defect and correction among the 22 open Beads inspected. This is a documentation finding, not a mounted-runtime failure.
acceptance_criteria: 018 and the cited Static ribbon explanation accurately distinguish shared registrar catalogues from per-frame projections; picker visibility and selection preservation remain intact. Verify against actual source-store reads and per-frame data sources, not only prose/link-gate success.

title: False detach! requirement: 008 still makes a slot flip insufficient, but rf2-y8doi.17 made the flip self-acting
description:
## The claim

`tools/xray/spec/008-Embedding-Contract.md` still tells post-preload embed hosts that a
`configure!` flip of `:rf.xray/keybinding-enabled?` is **not enough** and that they **MUST**
additionally call `keybinding/detach!`. That was true when it was written and is now false:
`rf2-y8doi.17` put a watch on the slot, so the flip attaches and detaches the global listener
by itself, at any point in the boot sequence.

The chapter's reasoning is stale in the same place as its instruction. It says the slot
"declares intent but is read only at attach time" — the sentence that makes the `MUST` follow —
and that premise is the exact thing `rf2-y8doi.17` removed.

## Measured at trunk 395f0107a1

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/keybinding.cljs:634-664` carries the watch, under a comment
block naming `rf2-y8doi.17` and setting out why: `attach!` read the slot once, which made
`(configure! {:rf.xray/keybinding-enabled? false})` "a silent no-op for every host on the
`:devtools/preloads` path". The watch fires only on a genuine change and both directions are
idempotent via the `attached-state` CAS.

**The code says explicitly what survives, and it is not nothing** — so this is a correction and
not a deletion. Same comment block: "`keybinding/detach!` stays public and stays documented: a
host that wants the listener gone WITHOUT declaring the slot (or that must remove it from a
mount-time hook it does not own) still calls it, and calling it alongside the flip is harmless."

So the repair is: **`detach!` after a slot flip is no longer REQUIRED — it is redundant and
harmless.** The escape hatch itself is untouched, and every sentence describing `detach!` as an
idempotent public lifecycle call is still correct.

## The sites, enumerated rather than counted

Owned by this item (`008-Embedding-Contract.md`):

- **88-95** — the `MUST additionally call ... AFTER the slot flip` instruction and its fenced
  two-line sample. The instruction is the defect; the sample is still legal code that now does
  nothing the flip has not already done.
- **101** — `declares intent but is read only at attach time; without detach! ...` — the
  premise. Fixing 88-95 and leaving this standing leaves the chapter arguing for the sentence
  it no longer makes.
- **87-90** — the paragraph immediately above, telling pre-preload hosts they "need nothing
  further — the slot flip wins the read at attach time". Its OUTCOME is still right and its
  MECHANISM is now beside the point, because the read timing stopped mattering. Decide
  deliberately whether it needs a word; do not assume it does.
- **99, 104-105** — the idempotence sentence and the cross-reference to
  `015-Configuration.md`. **Measured correct; expected to survive untouched.** They are listed
  so a reader knows they were checked rather than missed.

NOT owned by this item, named so nobody re-derives them:

- `tools/xray/spec/015-Configuration.md:514-515` carries the same `read only at attach time`
  premise, and **`rf2-y8doi.42` owns that chapter** (open at filing). A note has been appended
  there pointing at the line. Do not edit 015 from this item.
- `015-Configuration.md:525-527` tells pre-preload hosts they do NOT need `detach!` — same
  shape as 008's 87-90.
- `tools/xray/spec/API.md:323, 339-342` and `tools/xray/spec/Conventions.md:375` describe
  `detach!` as a lifecycle pair member and an escape hatch. Read at filing and believed still
  correct, since that is precisely what the code comment preserves — but **re-read them, do not
  take this line as the verdict.**

## Provenance, and why it was not caught by the obvious sweep

Raised by the worker on `rf2-d6gna` while fencing an unrelated pop-out change, and verified
independently at source before filing: the `MUST` at 92, and the watch at
`keybinding.cljs:634-664`.

**The chapter was truthed against the code TODAY and this survived.** `491955e6c9`
(`rf2-y8doi.37`) rewrote 008 at +35/-13 and touched **zero** `detach`-bearing lines in it. That
is not a failure of that item — its fence was elsewhere in the chapter — but it does mean a
future reader who sees a recent "truthed against the code" commit on 008 will reasonably assume
this was covered. It was not.

## What to do

**Re-derive every line number above at tip and report the deltas including zeros.** They were
taken at `395f0107a1` and this chapter is in an active review wave, so movement is expected.

Correct the instruction and its premise. Keep the escape hatch documented. State plainly, in
the chapter, that a flip is now sufficient — a host reading the corrected chapter should not be
left wondering whether `detach!` is still needed for safety.

**Do not add a count of anything**, and do not restate the `rf2-y8doi.17` comment block at
length — cite it.

## Gates

`tools/xray/spec` is inside `check_doc_slugs.py`'s roots, so that gate does cover this chapter —
but if the edit changes no link and no heading, its green could not have failed on what
changed. Say so unfavourably and rest the evidence on a planted RED, restored and verified by
blob hash (`git hash-object` **default** form for an `i/lf w/crlf` file). Check the fenced
sample and any table columns by hand. Three line-ending numbers with Python on bytes. Never
`sed -i`.

A JVM suite slurps some Xray chapters at expansion; **008 is one of the four that is read**, per
the worker on `rf2-d6gna` — so check whether a suite reads this chapter before waving the CLJS
or JVM lane off, and note that an incremental build cannot see a slurped `.md` change
(CLAUDE.md item (x)): a cold rebuild is what makes that moot.

title: Honour the :ns image-selection stamp on reg-resource, reg-mutation, reg-resource-scope (forward it) and reg-route (accept it); delete the exception prose — ruled D
description:
RULED 2026-09-17 (delegated by Mike): option D. Read the notes in order — RULING first, then the preserved two-reviewer DOSSIER, then the IMPLEMENTATION BRIEF (for the dispatched worker), which is the dispatch text and is self-contained. The description this bead carried from creation to the ruling is preserved verbatim in notes under ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION (preserved before rewrite).

THE WORK. Four one-line code edits make the shared :rf/registration-metadata promise ("`:ns` is accepted on every reg-* kind") true on every registrar-backed kind, so a programmatic registration — fn-alias, JVM-direct, code-generated — becomes :select-ns image-selectable by stamping :ns exactly as reg-event already is:

  1-3. Forward the caller's :ns and :rf.provenance/ns through the three resource-family wrappers — reg-resource (resources/registry.cljc:518-522), reg-mutation (mutation_registry.cljc:314-318), reg-resource-scope (scope_registry.cljc:378-384). Each builds its own registrar map from the canonical spec today and drops both keys SILENTLY (descriptor recorded under nil provenance, nothing reports it). One (select-keys metadata [:ns :rf.provenance/ns]) in each merge.
  4.   Add bare :ns to routing's reserved-route-keys (routing/registry.cljc:135-167). reg-route REJECTS it today with :rf.error/route-bad-metadata, the app failing at boot, while the qualified :rf.provenance/ns already passes and is honoured. :ns only — not :file/:line/:column.

Then DELETE the exception prose PRs #9885 / #9896 added (core.cljc rf/image docstring :966-990 and the four fn-alias docstrings :339-408; spec/001-Registration.md:204) in favour of two categories — registrar-backed kinds honour the stamp, frame-owned kinds (reg-flow, reg-app-schema(s), reg-http-interceptor) record no descriptor and cannot be selected — and add one sentence to spec/012-Routing.md:254. RED tests first per kind, reading re-frame.source-store/descriptors-for. No diagnostic, no new API, no change to source-store precedence, no hot-zone file. Sequence against rf2-c5cub on routing/registry.cljc if it is in flight. Size M.

VERIFIED STILL UNRULED 2026-09-17 (mayor, §2 verify-before-surfacing). NOTHING HAS ANSWERED THIS ITEM ELSEWHERE, and one thing that looked like it might, deliberately did not.

WHY IT WAS CHECKED. loops.md §2 says a ruling can live in the close reason of a CLOSED dependency rather than on the item, and that work may already have landed in the tree. Says nothing about what reg-route does with :ns beyond today's behaviour (rf2-nrc93)."

**A SUBJECT-ONLY SEARCH MISSES IT ENTIRELY.** `git log --format='%s' | grep nrc93` reads 0; the body search reads 1. That is loops.md §2's "search the whole commit MESSAGE (subject-only fails open)" biting on a real case, on this very item.

AND rf2-v9fiu'S CLOSE REASON SETTLES IT EXPLICITLY: "NOT PRESUMED: reg-route + :ns (rf2-nrc93) is unruled, and the new prose states only today's behaviour, so it stays true under either ruling Mike makes."

THE OTHER THREE RULINGS WERE CHECKED THE SAME WAY IN THE SAME TICK and are likewise unanswered: rf2-c5cub, rf2-3aafh and rf2-20lwk each have zero blockers and zero commits naming them anywhere in the repository's full commit messages. So all four genuinely await Mike; none is a verified duplicate and none can be closed.

DECISION: D — forward the caller's :ns and :rf.provenance/ns through the three resource-family wrappers AND add bare :ns to routing's reserved-route-keys; one worker, one PR, no diagnostic, no new public API, source-store precedence unchanged; the routing addition is :ns alone (the four-coord-key variant is declined).
WHY: Both reviewers chose D and their evidence agrees wherever it overlaps, and every load-bearing line cite and the probe table were re-verified on trunk 8bb6041d0e before ruling (resources registry.cljc:518-522, mutation_registry.cljc:314-318, scope_registry.cljc:378-384, routing registry.cljc:135-167 / :199-228 / :464-471, source_store.cljc:267-271, merge-coords at source_coords.cljc:90-112). I checked the agreement against the posture rather than inheriting it: A is the cheaper option TODAY (zero code) but it is not the minimal SHAPE — it keeps a boot-time throw on a key the published :rf/registration-metadata schema lists as accepted on every kind, keeps a silent drop on three kinds where the store's own precedence step 2 exists precisely to honour a caller's :ns, and keeps roughly forty lines of exception prose across core.cljc and spec/001 that three bead-generations (rf2-17bbi -> rf2-1kqed -> rf2-v9fiu) grew explaining the difference. D is four one-line edits that make the schema true and let that prose be deleted, which is what "don't litigate the minutiae" cuts FOR here: the cheapest way to stop re-deciding which kinds honour :ns is to have them all honour it. "Trust the programmer" cuts the same way — the programmer who reads the shared schema and stamps :ns on a route should not get a boot failure for it, and the AI reading that schema should not need four retractions. Codex's independent review carried two things the dossier lacked and both are adopted: the probe under the real JVM production gate (the omission has an observable image consequence there too), and the second scope correction — with *pending-coords* bound, a resource-family caller stamping :ns still gets the CAPTURED namespace, so even the macro path cannot attribute a generated registration to its origin, which D also repairs for free via merge-coords' documented user-overrides-captured rule. Codex's other scope correction is written into the brief verbatim: D restores namespace stamping on these four kinds and is NOT full schema conformance on routes (:file / :line / :column / :schema / :platforms stay outside routing's bare set; do not widen). The dossier's census (zero live higher-order alias uses of any reg-* in the tree, all data-driven loops already on the macro) is why this is P3 and cheap, not a reason to leave it; its own two "what would change my mind" conditions are not met, because the source store reads :ns as an explicit, documented step for exactly the programmatic case, and the silent three are the kinds with NO programmatic route to selectability at all. The four-coord-key variant is declined because it would put :column / :file / :line into the typo error's "Reserved keys:" list — noise for the one question that message answers — and nothing raised needs it.
WHAT CHANGES MY MIND: If Mike regards the reg-* fn-aliases as tooling conveniences never meant to participate in image selection, then A with the dossier's one-line rider (the qualified :rf.provenance/ns is ALREADY accepted and honoured on a programmatic route — measured by both reviewers) is the right call and the docstrings already say the rest; if only the loud failure is worth a worker, C alone is a quarter-morning and stands on its own.

No new beads: the analysis produced no split follow-on and no docs-reconciliation item outside this PR's own surface.

Provenance of the dropped status line: the dossier was written 2026-09-17 08:43:13 AUSEST at trunk 634b085f12 (P3, bug); the Codex Recommendation section was reviewed at 6a3bf87c1885ef66531bc70eb64378a52f6e41fc. Only the file's title line and status line are dropped; everything else is verbatim, in order, across the numbered chunks below.

[DOSSIER chunk 1 of 2]

Depends on / feeds: raised by rf2-1kqed (closed, PR #9885, docs only); fenced by rf2-v9fiu (closed, PR #9896, whose close reason says its prose was written to stay true under EITHER ruling). No blockers, no dependents. rf2-pk4i6.8 (open) also targets `spec/001-Registration.md`, so whatever is dispatched here must not share that file with it at the same time.

## The decision in one sentence

Four registration kinds cannot be made image-selectable by stamping `:ns` the way the shared registration-metadata vocabulary says every kind can — three drop it silently, one throws — and Mike must say whether that is the intended shape (leave it, A) or a wart to close with about four lines of code (B, C, or both).

## The problem, carefully

**The mechanism.** `registrar/register!` hands its metadata map to `source-store/record-descriptor!` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/registrar.cljc:655`), which resolves the descriptor's provenance in three steps (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_store.cljc:225-231`): an explicit `:rf.provenance/ns` on the map, else the map's `:ns` slot, else the live `*pending-coords*` binding the `reg-*` MACRO establishes. A programmatic registration — the CLJS fn-alias used as a value, or a direct call to the owning artefact's fn on the JVM — has no macro binding, so it depends on steps 1-2, i.e. on the caller's map reaching the store intact. Image selection (`:select-ns {:include [globs]}`, EP-0026 `docs/EP/EP-0026-image-api-simplification.md:235-275`, replacing EP-0023's `:include-ns`) matches ONLY `:rf.provenance/ns`; a nil-provenance descriptor is reachable through the default image alone, and nothing reports that (`core.cljc:966-973`).

**The promise.** `:ns` is in the base bare-key vocabulary "accepted on EVERY `reg-*` kind" (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/reg_meta.cljc:50-55`), and the public schema `:rf/registration-metadata` — "the metadata map every `reg-*` accepts in its middle slot" — lists `[:ns {:optional true} :symbol]` (`spec/Spec-Schemas.md:326-333`). `RouteMetadata` "composes with `:rf/registration-metadata`'s open shape" (`spec/Spec-Schemas.md:3859`).

**The four sites that break the promise.** Three build a fresh registrar map from the canonical spec and never forward the caller's:

```clojure
;; implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/registry.cljc:519-522   (reg-resource)
(rf.source-coords/merge-coords
  (merge {:doc (:doc resource-spec)}
         {:rf/resource resource-spec
          :handler-fn  (:request resource-spec)}))
;; mutation_registry.cljc:315-318 and scope_registry.cljc:381-384 are the same three lines
;; with :rf/mutation / :rf/resource-scope in place of :rf/resource.
```

The fourth forwards the caller's map intact but guards it first: `validate-route-metadata!` rejects any BARE key outside `reserved-route-keys` (`implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/registry.cljc:135-167` the set, `:209-228` the throw) and runs on the user map BEFORE `merge-coords` adds the macro's coords (`:464-471`, the comment says so in terms) — which is exactly why the macro form sidesteps the guard and the fn form cannot. Namespaced keys always pass (`:212`, `remove qualified-keyword?`).

**Measured today (my probes, JVM, `clojure -M -e` from each artefact directory; the bead's own measurements agree):**

| call | result | provenance keys recorded |
|---|---|---|
| `registrar/register! :event … {:ns 'probe.control …}` (control) | ok | `("probe.control")` |
| `routing.registry/reg-route :probe/with-ns {:ns 'probe.ns} "/x"` | THROWS `:rf.error/route-bad-metadata`, `ex-data :keys [:ns]` | nothing registered |
| same route, no `:ns` | ok | `(nil)` |
| same route, `{:rf.provenance/ns "probe.qualified"}` | **ok** | **`("probe.qualified")`** |
| `resources.registry/reg-resource :probe/res {… :ns 'probe.ns}` | ok, returns id | `(nil)`; stored entry keys `(:doc :rf/resource :handler-fn)`; `:ns` still sits INSIDE `:rf/resource`, unread |
| same resource, `{:rf.provenance/ns "probe.qualified"}` | ok | `(nil)` — dropped too |
| `mutation-registry/reg-mutation … {:ns 'probe.ns}` | ok | `(nil)` |
| `scope-registry/reg-resource-scope … {:ns 'probe.ns}` | ok | `(nil)` |

The fourth row is new relative to the bead: **a programmatic route can already be made image-selectable today** by stamping the NAMESPACED key, because routing's guard only polices bare keys and the store reads `:rf.provenance/ns` first. That does not close B (the resource family drops that spelling too) and does not close the vocabulary disagreement in C (the bare `:ns` the spec promises is the one refused), but it changes what C buys: consistency, not capability.

**Who realistically registers these four kinds programmatically.** Nobody in this tree today, and the census carries its controls:

- The fn-aliases exist so "a higher-order caller can write `(map rf/reg-sub …)` where a macro cannot ride" (`implementation/core/test/re_frame/registrar_alias_concordance_cljs_test.cljc:4-16`, rf2-kuky.23). A search for `(map|mapv|apply|run!|partial|comp) rf/reg-<any kind>` over every `.clj/.cljs/.cljc` file returns ONLY that docstring — zero live higher-order uses of any `reg-*` alias, the four kinds included.
- Every data-driven registration in the tree loops over the MACRO: `implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_runner.cljc:466,725` and `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_conformance_test.clj:476` (`(rf/reg-route id (dissoc meta :path) (:path meta))` inside `doseq`), `routing_concurrency_stress_test.clj:170,277,409`, `routing_registry_test.clj:1215,1220`, the resources SSR/classification tests. A macro call with a symbol id still captures the LOOP SITE's coords, so all of these get the looping namespace as provenance and are selectable today with no `:ns` at all.
- JVM-direct calls to the owning fns appear in tests only (`resources_infinite_registration_cljs_test.cljc`, ~20 calls; `resources_skeleton_cljs_test.cljs:372`), none of which assembles a `:select-ns` image over them.
- `tools/story/` has 0 hits for any of the four names, against 26 hits in 10 files across `tools/` (all Xray testbeds, panels and tests) — so story tooling does not register these kinds at all.
- The AI generating code sees the macro form in every docstring, spec and guide; the fn-alias docstrings now say in capitals not to stamp `:ns` (`core.cljc:339-408`).

So the gap is theoretical for the current population. What is not theoretical is the cost already paid in prose: `spec/001-Registration.md:204` is a ~30-line paragraph enumerating the exceptions, `core.cljc:966-990` (`rf/image`) restates them, and three generations of doc drift (rf2-17bbi → rf2-1kqed → rf2-v9fiu) came from a remedy that is true for seven kinds and false for eight.

## Make it tangible

**A JVM-side resource catalogue, registered in a loop.** The shape a programmer (or an AI writing an SSR boot namespace) would actually write, using the artefact fn directly because the boot code is data-driven:

```clojure
(ns shop.boot)                                   ; JVM/SSR boot, or a test fixture
(def catalogue {:shop/products {:url "/api/products" :stale-after-ms 30000}
                :shop/orders   {:url "/api/orders"   :stale-after-ms 5000}})
(doseq [[id {:keys [url stale-after-ms]}] catalogue]
  (re-frame.resources.registry/reg-resource id
    {:scope :rf.scope/global :params-schema [:map] :stale-after-ms stale-after-ms
     :ns 'shop.boot}                             ; the remedy spec/001 offers most kinds
    (fn [_ _] {:request {:method :get :url url}})))

(def shop-image (rf/image {:id :shop/main :select-ns {:include ["shop.**"]}}))
```

Today: both registrations succeed, both are recorded under `nil` provenance, `shop-image` assembles from whatever else `shop.**` registered and is silently two resources short; the frame fails later, at first `ensure`, with an unregistered-resource error naming an id the programmer can see was registered. Nothing at registration time says why. (Had the loop called the `rf/reg-resource` MACRO instead, provenance would be `shop.boot` and it would work — that is the whole of today's remedy.) Under B: provenance `shop.boot`, selected, no change to the call.

**A route table, registered from data.** Same programmer, a `[[id path] …]` table and the fn-alias because `apply`/`doseq` is the natural spelling:

```clojure
(def route-table [[:page/home "/"] [:page/article "/articles/:id"]])
(doseq [[id path] route-table]
  (re-frame.core-routing/reg-route id {:ns 'shop.routes} path))   ; or (apply rf/reg-route …) in CLJS
```

Today, on the FIRST iteration, verbatim from the probe:

```
:rf.error/route-bad-metadata
route :page/home declares unknown metadata key :ns — bare keys outside the reserved set are
rejected as likely typos (e.g. :on-matched for :on-match). Reserved keys: :can-enter, :can-leave,
:doc, :head, :large, :on-match, :params, :parent, :path, :query, :query-defaults, :scroll,
:sensitive, :tags. Host/app extension keys must be namespaced (e.g. :myapp/analytics-id).
```

The app does not boot. The same call with `{:rf.provenance/ns "shop.routes"}` boots and is selectable (measured) — but no docstring or spec sentence tells the programmer that, and the shared schema told them `:ns`. Under C: the bare `:ns` is accepted and recorded, same as on `reg-event`.

**What each option changes, per kind and spelling:**

| kind | `:ns` today | `:rf.provenance/ns` today | under B | under C |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| reg-resource / reg-mutation / reg-resource-scope | dropped silently | dropped silently | both forwarded → selectable | unchanged |
| reg-route | REJECTED, app fails at boot | works | unchanged | accepted → selectable |
| reg-event / sub / fx / cofx / interceptor / head / error-projector | works | works | unchanged | unchanged |
| reg-flow / app-schema(s) / http-interceptor (frame-owned) | no descriptor exists; nothing can help | same | unchanged | unchanged |

## Options

### A. Leave as is — the macro form is the supported route (the bead's option a)
- What changes: nothing in code. Optionally (mine, a rider, not a new option) one sentence on the `reg-route` fn-alias docstring and `spec/001:204` saying the namespaced `:rf.provenance/ns` is accepted and honoured on a route — it is measured true today and costs a line.
- Consequences: programmer — a data-driven loop must use the macro or, for routes only, the namespaced key; the resource family has NO programmatic route to selectability. AI — reads `:rf/registration-metadata` (Spec-Schemas) promising `:ns` on every kind, then reads four docstrings retracting it. Tools — none affected. Spec — the ~30-line exception paragraph at `spec/001:204` and its `rf/image` twin stay, and the "accepted means validated, not stored" narrowing they introduced stays load-bearing.
- Cost: 0 (rider: 10 minutes, no worker).
- Risk: the drift class that produced rf2-17bbi → rf2-1kqed → rf2-v9fiu stays open — the next sweep that reads `:rf/registration-metadata` as true will re-generalise the remedy. A Conventions §No-silent-swallow reading: the resource family accepts a KNOWN bare key it cannot honour and says nothing.

### B. Forward `:ns` (and `:rf.provenance/ns`) through the three resource-family wrappers (the bead's option b)
- What changes: one line in each of `resources/registry.cljc:520`, `mutation_registry.cljc:316`, `scope_registry.cljc:382` — `(merge {:doc (:doc spec)} (select-keys metadata [:ns :rf.provenance/ns]) {:rf/<kind> spec :handler-fn …})`. Forwarding both spellings matches the store's two explicit steps; the caller's map still validates exactly as today (the resource validators check required keys and reject retired ones — `registry.cljc:225-274`, `mutation_registry.cljc:59-103`, `scope_registry.cljc:241-334` — none is a closed map, so `:ns` already passes them, which is why the drop is silent).
- Consequences: programmer — the resource family behaves like `reg-event`. AI — one rule fewer to carry. Spec — the resource-family clause leaves `spec/001:204` and `core.cljc:978-980`; the three fn-alias docstrings (`core.cljc:354-408`) drop their "DOES NOT HELP HERE" paragraphs. Production: `merge-coords` returns the user map unchanged under the prod gate, so the forwarded `:ns` survives elision exactly as it does on `reg-event` (the same path rf2-1kqed measured).
- Cost: half a worker-morning. Files: 3 resources src (1 line each), `core.cljc` (3 docstrings + the `rf/image` paragraph), `spec/001-Registration.md:204` (shrinks), one new JVM test ns under `implementation/resources/test/` with a provenance assertion per kind and the register! control. No hot-zone file (`spec/API.md`, the manifests and Spec-Schemas are untouched — no public name moves).
- Risk: low. No test in `implementation/resources/test/` pins the registrar-entry shape (0 hits for `:handler-fn`; the three `registrar/lookup` sites check `some?` only), so adding a key breaks nothing measured.

### C. Add `:ns` to routing's `reserved-route-keys` (the bead's option c)
- What changes: one entry in the set at `routing/registry.cljc:147-167`, with a comment naming it as the cross-kind `:rf/registration-metadata` source-coord key rather than a routing key. ## Codex Recommendation

**Choose D, scoped to namespace provenance:** forward `:ns` and `:rf.provenance/ns` from the caller's metadata in the three resource wrappers, and accept `:ns` on routes. Keep the existing precedence and add no diagnostic or public API. This is a small consistency repair with a useful reduction in rules programmers and AI tools must remember.

**Independent findings.** Reviewed at `6a3bf87c1885ef66531bc70eb64378a52f6e41fc`, including `bd show` and `bd history rf2-nrc93`. The problem remains present. The resource-family writers construct outer registrar metadata without either provenance key: `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/registry.cljc:516-522`, `mutation_registry.cljc:312-318`, and `scope_registry.cljc:375-384` (the latter two in the same directory). Routing validates before merging captured coordinates and rejects `:ns`: `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/registry.cljc:209-228,464-471`. The actual source-store implementation confirms the explicit-qualified-key, bare-key, captured-binding precedence (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_store.cljc:267-282`).

I ran isolated JVM probes against those owning functions using the existing cached classpath, once normally and once with `-Dre-frame.debug=false` set before namespace loading. Both corrected probes exited 0. For each resource-family kind, bare, qualified, and combined stamps produced nil provenance without capture. A route accepted the qualified stamp but rejected any metadata containing bare `:ns`. Full image assembly selecting `review.target` contained exactly the stamped registrar control and the qualified-key route among the probe registrations; the default image contained the omitted resource. Thus the source-store omission has an observable image consequence, including under the real JVM production gate.

**Two scope corrections matter.**

First, data-driven registration does not itself require a function alias. The existing `doseq` at `implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_runner.cljc:464-466` calls the route macro directly. Actual application examples also use macros, including `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/resources.cljs:110` and `scope.cljs:107`. Searches found no application higher-order use establishing a present production failure; test-only `apply` calls do exist (`implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_scope_registry_cljs_test.cljc:288-292`). The defensible conclusion is a supported composition capability with inconsistent behavior, not demonstrated widespread breakage.

Conversely, the defect is broader than function aliases: callers cannot override captured provenance reliably either. With `*pending-coords*` bound to `review.generated` and metadata stamping `:ns 'review.target`, all three resource kinds recorded `review.generated`; routing rejected the call. This executed binding probe models the macro's delegate environment, rather than executing a compiled CLJS macro. The intended override rule is explicit in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_coords.cljc:90-112`. Fixing the forwarding therefore also helps generators that need to identify their original namespace.

Second, D does **not** make the entire shared metadata schema true. That schema also includes `:file`, `:line`, `:column`, `:schema`, and `:platforms` (`spec/Spec-Schemas.md:329-338`), which routing's accepted set still omits. Describe this change as restoring namespace stamping across these four kinds; do not use it to claim complete metadata-schema conformance. Broader metadata alignment is unnecessary to settle this decision.

**Options and tradeoffs.** A is viable because macro calls already support ordinary SPA registration, but retains a surprising boundary for callers composing functions or generating registrations. B supplies the larger capability gain; C removes a rejection while preserving routing's existing qualified-key workaround. Together they offer one simple rule at nearly the same implementation cost. An inline-image workaround would require substantially more work: these four kinds are explicitly outside the implemented inline sections (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/image.cljc:295-308`). No new mechanism is justified here.

Keep the patch local: select the two provenance keys from the original metadata into each outer resource descriptor, retain the canonical nested resource data, and add bare `:ns` to routing's accepted keys. Update the exception prose and test the result through image assembly. A compact test should cover each kind, a no-stamp control, explicit override precedence, and the production gate. Existing routing typo rejection should remain covered.

History supports treating this as an unresolved behavior choice: `0ef4e44125` and `fafa46b572` changed documentation, while the routing guard predates them (`1c7a5dd173`). The rationale for D is predictable composition with negligible new mechanism, not the absence of tests asserting the old metadata shape. Validation here establishes current JVM behavior; no proposed patch, CLJS advanced build, full suite, or downstream application was run. The source changes and their cost estimates remain recommendations, not verified implementation results.

title: story: the registered run chain has no rejection path — a throw inside record-result-map strands run-variant's promise forever (measured TimeoutException)
description:
Discovered by the senior-developer review rf2-wd2t (2026-09-13, trunk 1c9ff9697b). Verified at source by the mayor; the measurement is the reviewer's, re-measure at tip.

WHERE: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/runtime.cljc:1135-1140 (finalise-run!: then only), :1521-1529 (resume-run!: then only); contrast :1749-1758 (run-inline-plan chains catch*); async.cljc:115-127 (then derives a new promise and never completes the outer one: JVM thenCompose, CLJS .then).

EVIDENCE: JVM eval, exit 0: with #'re-frame.story.runtime/record-result-map redefined to throw, (deref-blocking (run-variant ...) 3000) -> java.util.concurrent.TimeoutException; control without the redef -> [:settled :pass true]. Exposure at trunk: (rf/epoch-history variant-id) at 618 is unguarded (elsewhere wrapped: last-epoch-id, frame-tape), and result/run-result runs the causal/schema matchers over plan slots. The window is narrow (a frame torn down mid-run, or a malformed plan slot) but the outcome is a deref that never returns / an await that never resolves, with no error anywhere. story_runtime_cljs_test.cljs:149-150 describes exactly this hang class (rf2-9x5fm) and fixed it for teardown/token-swap only.

SMALLEST CHANGE: (rf.story.async/catch* (fn [e] (handle-run-error! resolve variant-id e start-ms) nil)) on both chains, as the inline path already does. JVM test beside story_runtime_test.clj:1671: with-redefs-fn on record-result-map -> promise settles :error inside the deref timeout (red today).

GATE: jvm-tools-story.

ALREADY-COVERED CHECK: not in the closed story roster.
notes: FENCE DISCHARGED BY CLUSTERING 2026-09-13 01:15:25 AUSEST (mayor): this bead is dispatched to rtfix-a in ONE PR with rf2-3okc, rf2-poty, rf2-izz5 and rf2-9ppq, in the reviewer's order (3okc, then poty, then izz5, then 9ppq). close_reason:
FIXED in PR #9723 (branch worker/rtfix-a), with rf2-3okc, rf2-poty and rf2-izz5 in one PR.

Fix: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/runtime.cljc changes in three places.
- finalise-run! (the registered run-variant chain) now chains rf.story.async/catch* into handle-run-error!.
- resume-run!'s chain does too. A local settle! still publishes superseded-result for an attempt that a newer prepare superseded, and fires done-cb exactly once on whichever path settles.
- handle-run-error! delegates to run-error-result, which NEVER throws. If the frame-bound assembly (record-result-map) throws again, it falls back to a frame-free :error result, so the catch path itself can no longer strand the promise.

The inline path already had a catch*, but its fail! re-threw through the same record-result-map. The probe showed it hanging as well, and it now uses run-error-result too. The bead's unguarded (rf/epoch-history ...) read in record-result-map is left as it is: any throw from it is now caught by the rejection path.

Evidence: a JVM probe with #'re-frame.story.runtime/record-result-map redefined to throw, deref-blocking at 3000 ms, times taken from System/nanoTime in the runner.
- run-variant: TimeoutException at 3020 ms before, settled [:error :error [:rf.error/exception]] in 14 ms after.
- resume-run!: TimeoutException at 3003 ms before, settled :error in 6 ms after.
- Inline run: TimeoutException at 3011 ms before, settled :error in 21 ms after.
- Control, no redef: settled :pass in 6 ms before and 12 ms after.

Tests: story_runtime_test.clj gains run-chains-settle-when-result-assembly-throws (all three chains under the throwing redef, plus a no-throw control).
