    WakeToRun                 = False   <- the machine is not woken at 00:33
    DisallowStartIfOnBatteries= True    <- on battery it will not start
    StopIfGoingOnBatteries    = True
    RunOnlyIfIdle             = False   State = Ready
So a machine asleep, off, or on battery at 00:33 skips silently, with no catch-up and no error anywhere.
That is stock `git maintenance start --scheduler=schtasks` behaviour, NOT a misconfiguration of this
arrangement and NOT something the adoption got wrong.

THE ARRANGEMENT IS CONFIRMED WORKING, and this is the positive control the reading needed — without it the
skip above is ambiguous between "machine was off" and "the whole thing is broken". The HOURLY commit-graph
task ran 2026-09-10 12:03:01 with result 0, today, on this machine. schtasks is invoking git maintenance
successfully; only the 00:33 slot was missed.

CORROBORATED THREE WAYS, all agreeing:
  * `prune-packable` reads 918 — IDENTICAL to this bead's own baseline, which was taken 2026-09-09 13:20,
    i.e. AFTER that day's 00:33 run. Unmoved means no daily run since.
  * Index CREATION times (the instrument this bead prescribed, explicitly not pack mtime): a `loose-*.idx` at
    2026-09-09 00:33:17 and a `pack-*.idx` at 2026-09-09 00:33:20 — the two daily tasks, stamped at the
    trigger minute — and NOTHING AT ALL at 2026-09-10 00:33. Newest artefact is 2026-09-09 07:55.
  * Health is clean either way: `garbage: 0`, no `.git/objects/maintenance.lock`, no `gc.log`. The 2026-07-11
    stale-lock failure that motivated `maintenance.auto=false` has NOT recurred.

WEEKLY TASK, checked because its numbers look alarming and are not: last run 30/11/1999, LastTaskResult
267011 = 0x00041303 = SCHED_S_TASK_HAS_NOT_RUN. It has simply never come due; its first Sunday is
2026-09-13. Benign, no action.

INSTRUMENT (h) REPRODUCED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS while taking reading 2: `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 schtasks /query
/fo LIST | grep -c "Git Maintenance"` reads 3; the bare form reads 0. The false zero is live on this box
today, so the CLAUDE.md entry is current rather than historical.

THE ONE AVAILABLE REMEDY, DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN — recorded so nobody re-derives it. Setting
`StartWhenAvailable = True` on the daily task makes Windows run a missed occurrence at the next opportunity.
It is a one-property change to Mike's own Task Scheduler entry, it is his machine and his call, and the cost
of leaving it alone is exactly one skipped incremental repack, measured: prune-packable 918, garbage 0, no
locks. That is not worth a project, and a mayor who "fixes" it is editing an operator's machine uninvited.

WHY THIS DISCHARGES THE BEAD RATHER THAN WAITING FOR A CLEANER READING TOMORROW: the bead existed to confirm
the arrangement runs. It does — the hourly proves invocation works today, and the 09-09 index stamps prove
the daily tasks do their work when they fire. A second reading would re-ask a question already answered, and
would be subject to the same machine-state lottery. What was learned that the bead did not know is written
above.

title: spec/Spec-Schemas.md attributes trace slots to the retired ui/frames emitter
description:
spec/Spec-Schemas.md:1248-1254, in the per-slot ownership commentary for the frame-destroyed error tags, names the emitter that stamps three slots:

  ;;   :event    router/emit-frame-destroyed! + ui/frames/emit-and-throw-frame-destroyed!
  ;;   :op       ui/frames (all four values) + capture-frame pre-check + router/subs
  ;;   :reason   router + ui/frames (the constant `:frame-destroyed`)

`ui/frames` is `re-frame.ui.frames` -- the retired and removed donor tree (rf2-0yp7w, PR #8322). git ls-files implementation/ui/ returns 0, and there is no defn of emit-and-throw-frame-destroyed! anywhere under implementation/; the only surviving mention is a past-tense docstring in implementation/core/test/re_frame/frame_destroyed_subscribe_devtrace_identity_cljs_test.cljc, which is history and correct as such.

Found while doing rf2-7s78 (PR #9175) and deliberately LEFT, for three reasons:

1. It is INSIDE a fenced block (odd fence-toggle count at line 1248 vs the even count at 3729), so neither check_doc_slugs.py nor mkdocs build --strict reads it -- a different exposure from the prose claim rf2-7s78 fixed.
2. It is a different defect class: producer attribution for a schema slot, not a consumer list.
3. The fix is a determination, not a name swap. Someone has to establish who stamps :event / :op / :reason now that the UI producer is gone -- and the live possibility is that nothing does, which is exactly the reasoning recorded three lines below it for :where / :rf.sub/query-v under rf2-63t1i: 'A schema slot is a claim about what an emitter produces, so a slot with no producer describes nothing.' If these slots have no producer either, the repair may be deletion rather than re-attribution.

Hot zone: spec/Spec-Schemas.md is sequential, so sequence this behind any other Spec-Schemas.md work rather than running it in parallel.

Gates: scripts/check_doc_slugs.py and mkdocs build --strict both apply to the file, but NEITHER reads the fenced block this defect lives in -- so whoever takes it verifies the commentary by hand and says so in the PR body.
notes:
MAYOR VERIFICATION 2026-09-04, before this is dispatched. The bead's premise HOLDS, and the population is LARGER than filed — two sites, not one. Also recorded here: the broken control that nearly made me report the opposite.

SITE 1, as filed — spec/Spec-Schemas.md:1248, inside a fenced block (71 toggles precede it, odd), reading:
    ;;   :event    router/emit-frame-destroyed! + ui/frames/emit-and-throw-frame-destroyed!
That line names TWO producers and they have OPPOSITE status:
  - `router/emit-frame-destroyed!` IS LIVE — implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:2207, `(defn- emit-frame-destroyed!`.
  - `ui/frames/emit-and-throw-frame-destroyed!` HAS NO DEFINITION ANYWHERE. `implementation/ui/` is retired and removed (rf2-0yp7w, PR #8322); git ls-files returns 0 there, against a live control of 224 under implementation/hicasso/.
So the fix is NOT to delete the line: half of it is correct and load-bearing.

SITE 2, WHICH THE FILING WORKER DID NOT FIND because it searched spec/ only — implementation/core/test/re_frame/frame_destroyed_subscribe_devtrace_identity_cljs_test.cljc names the dead emitter in TWO docstrings:
  :10  "`emit-and-throw-frame-destroyed!` now passes the raw query vector on BOTH the"
  :80  "The axis-2 dev-trace event `emit-and-throw-frame-destroyed!` fans (frames.cljc):"
That is a LIVE test file describing its own subject in terms of a retired emitter. Whoever takes this should decide both sites together, because they make the same claim.
NOTE the "(frames.cljc)" in that docstring is itself stale in a second way: the only frames.cljc in the tree today is tools/story/src/re_frame/story/frames.cljc, a different namespace entirely. The retired one was implementation/ui/frames.cljc.

WHAT THE FIX PROBABLY IS, but it is a determination and not a name swap: rf2-63t1i's note three lines below site 1 reasons that "a slot with no producer describes nothing", which argues for DELETING the dead half rather than renaming it — there is no live successor to point at, because Hicasso's route-link is a different subject. Weigh that against CLAUDE.md's ruling that donor references in spec/ prose are usually deliberate retirement bookkeeping. The discriminator is the same one that settled rf2-410b and rf2-7s78: this is a LIVE PRESENT-TENSE attribution of a trace slot to a producer, not a dated record of a retirement.

A BROKEN CONTROL THAT NEARLY REVERSED MY READING, recorded because the class recurs. I checked "does the emitter exist?" with `git grep -c -F 'defn emit-and-throw-frame-destroyed'` = 0, and controlled it with `git grep -c -F 'defn emit-frame-destroyed'` on the sibling — which ALSO returned 0. Had I read the first zero alone I would have reported the whole line dead. The control was broken by ONE CHARACTER: the real definition is `defn-`, not `defn`, so a fixed-string prefix search for "defn " misses every private definition in the repository. THE LESSON IS THE CAMPAIGN'S OWN: a pattern that fails on a feature the control also lacks passes without exercising anything. Search for the bare symbol first and read what surrounds it, rather than guessing the definition form.

FENCE WHEN DISPATCHED: spec/Spec-Schemas.md is HOT ZONE — sequential, never parallel. The test file is not. Neither doc gate reads inside a fenced block, and site 1 IS inside one, so NEITHER GATE IS THE GATE for that edit; check it by hand and say so. Site 2 is a docstring in a live test, so the CLJS suite compiles it but nothing validates its prose either.
SEQUENCED 2026-09-04 by the mayor — DO NOT DISPATCH UNTIL PR #9175 MERGES. A file-collision hold, not a ruling; no operator decision is needed.

WHY. This bead's site 1 is spec/Spec-Schemas.md:1248. PR #9175 (worker/schemadoc-a) is OPEN and edits spec/Spec-Schemas.md:3729 — confirmed by reading the PR's own file list, which names exactly that one file. Different lines, same file, and spec/Spec-Schemas.md is HOT ZONE: sequential, never parallel.

THE HAZARD IS NOT THE CONFLICT, IT IS THE STALE-COPY REVERT. A branch cut before #9175 lands would silently undo its RouteAddress correction while passing every gate, because a revert of a merged change is well-formed and every checker reads it as clean. That is the shape that has bitten this repository before and it is why the hot-zone rule is concurrency-based rather than diff-based.

RELEASE CONDITION: PR #9175 merged. Then RE-READ spec/Spec-Schemas.md at tip before briefing — #9175 changes the RouteAddress prose, and the line numbers in this bead and its notes will have shifted. THIS ALREADY HAPPENED ONCE ON THIS CHAIN: my brief for rf2-7s78 cited the sibling site as spec/012-Routing.md:806 and it was :815 by the time the worker read it, moved by #9174's own 12-line insertion. Take line numbers from a fresh read, never from a report.

AND bd ready CANNOT SHOW THIS — it filters dependency blockers only; a hold written in prose is invisible to the scheduler, and I dispatched a fenced bead off that list earlier today for exactly this reason. Read this bead's notes before briefing it.

SITE 2 IS NOT BLOCKED BY #9175 — implementation/core/test/re_frame/frame_destroyed_subscribe_devtrace_identity_cljs_test.cljc is a different tree entirely. But splitting buys nothing: both sites make the same claim about the same retired emitter, and the determination that governs site 1 governs site 2. Do them together.
FENCE STRUCK 2026-09-04 — PR #9175 MERGED, spec/Spec-Schemas.md is free. Site 1's line number did NOT shift (still 1248; #9175 edited 3729, below it) and it is still inside a fenced block (71 toggles, odd).

AND THE POPULATION IS LARGER AGAIN — THIRD CENSUS, THIRD DIFFERENT NUMBER, because each of the first two searched a narrower pattern than the bead is actually about. Recording all three so the pattern of the error is visible:
  - the filing worker searched spec/ for the one emitter and found 1 site;
  - I searched 'emit-and-throw-frame-destroyed' repo-wide and found 2 sites;
  - searching 'ui/frames' — THE RETIRED TREE, which is what this bead is about — finds more again.

THE FULL CENSUS AT TIP, counts taken separately from listings, .beads excluded, patterns quoted:

  Pattern 'ui/frames' -> 4 occurrences across 2 files
    spec/Spec-Schemas.md                                              3
      :1248  ;;   :event    router/emit-frame-destroyed! + ui/frames/emit-and-throw-frame-destroyed!
      :1250  ;;   :op       ui/frames (all four values) + capture-frame pre-check + router/subs
      :1254  ;;   :reason   router + ui/frames (the constant `:frame-destroyed`)
    implementation/core/test/re_frame/error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test.clj   1

    implementation/core/test/re_frame/frame_destroyed_subscribe_devtrace_identity_cljs_test.cljc
      :10  "`emit-and-throw-frame-destroyed!` now passes the raw query vector on BOTH the"
      :80  "The axis-2 dev-trace event `emit-and-throw-frame-destroyed!` fans (frames.cljc):"

SO IT IS THREE FILES, and the three Spec-Schemas lines are ONE CONTIGUOUS BLOCK — a per-slot ownership table listing which emitter stamps each trace slot. That matters for the fix: they must be decided together, and each line PAIRS a live producer with the dead one (router/emit-frame-destroyed! is live at implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:2207 as a `defn-`). So no line can simply be deleted; each needs its dead half removed and its live half kept.

THE DETERMINATION REMAINS AS FILED: rf2-63t1i's note three lines below reasons that "a slot with no producer describes nothing", which argues for removing the dead attributions rather than renaming them — there is no successor to point at, because Hicasso's route-link is a different subject entirely. The discriminator that settled rf2-410b and rf2-7s78 applies: these are LIVE PRESENT-TENSE attributions of trace slots to a producer, not dated records of a retirement.

STILL TRUE FROM MY EARLIER NOTE, and worth re-reading before briefing: my `defn ` control failed on a single character (the real definition is `defn-`), which would have made me report the whole line dead had I trusted the first zero.

title: hic docs: nothing chooses between a seq as a child and (into [:div] ...) when a for produces a view's children
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal - pilot 1 (RealWorld/Conduit), a
BLINDED agent reading only the 29 published pages under docs/core/hicasso/, at pin
6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba. NOT SECTION 13 EVIDENCE: a rehearsal on
:local/root does not satisfy the adoption proof and discharges no artefact gate.

The pilot's own friction-log entry follows verbatim. The 'Bead' field is the PILOT's
recommendation - evidence about the surface, not a ratified design, since a pilot
proposing a framework change is outside its brief by the log protocol's own rule.
Full log: ai/findings/2026-09-03.pilot-b-rehearsal-realworld.friction-log.md (local-only).

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P1-F14 · outcome 2 · `inferred` · `docs`

**Trying to**

Decide how to write a `for` that produces a view's children. I had two
spellings available and no way to choose between them:

```clojure
[:div.tag-list (for [tag tags] [:a.tag-pill {:key tag} tag])]   ;; sequence as a child
(into [:div.tag-list] (for [tag tags] [:a.tag-pill {:key tag} tag]))  ;; spliced
```

**Expected**

The corpus to prefer one. It uses both: chapter 06 and the cookbook write the
sequence directly in child position; chapter 02's `card` example splices with
`(into [:section.card …] children)`. Neither says the two differ.

**Instead**

They do differ, and I only found out while inducing a fault. Chapter 06 says
the entity-key check "runs where React never looks: **a sequence** passed as a
Hicasso view's children is flattened before reaching React, and the flattened
elements already appear validated to it." That sentence describes the sequence
form. I had written `into` throughout the port — five sites — which produces an
ordinary vector of children with no sequence for that check to inspect.

I could not confirm the consequence, because the check did not fire for me in
either spelling (P1-F16). But the asymmetry is real in the prose, and I chose
`into` for a reason that had nothing to do with it: I was translating
`^{:key …}` metadata sites and `into` made the rewrite mechanical.

**Looked at**

- `06-lists-and-collections.md` "Use stable domain keys", and the paragraph
  about where the check runs
- `02-views-and-reads.md` "Props, children, and fragments" (`card`/`into`)
- `cookbook.md` "A list, a row, and an intent"

**Resolved by**

Nothing definitive. I kept `into`. Recording it because a guess about which of
two documented spellings to use, made for an unrelated reason, may have
disabled a documented safety check — and that is exactly the kind of thing a
migrator cannot see.

A small self-inflicted note from the same edit, kept because the instruction was
to write down the small stuff: converting one `(into [tag] (for …))` back to
`[tag (for …)]` is a paren change as well as a bracket change, and I got it
wrong by one. The build failure was immediate, precise and named the line — no
friction at all, but it cost me a full measurement cycle because I did not check
the watch log before re-running the browser, and read the stale page as a real
result.
close_reason: Done in PR #9140. Chapter 06 - the page that owns lists and collections - gained a section 'Write the sequence in child position' that chooses the sequence form over (into [:div] ...) and gives the verified reason. Both spellings were checked at source and both work, but they diagnose differently: as-element routes a seq to expand-seq, which runs check-member-key! over every member, while a vector child goes to vec->element where nothing walks members; realize-children runs the same check at a boundary crossing's one-level flatten. into splices the sequence away before Hicasso ever sees one, so the entity-key check cannot run - and the spliced children arrive as direct createElement arguments, which React treats as already validated, so React's own missing-key warning does not fire either. The pilot's suspicion that its into rewrite had silently disabled a documented safety check was therefore correct, and it is now written down. The section also says when into is still right (assembling one children vector from several pieces), with the caveat that keyed members inside it are no longer inspected. Gates: check_guide_samples.py exit 0 (the new fenced sample's h/ verbs resolve), check_doc_slugs.py exit 0, mkdocs build --strict exit 0.

title: Clarify emitted template harness roles
description:
## Scope

tools/template/test/day8/re_frame2_template/emitted_test_run_test.clj, limited to private harness helpers and private locals; no generated resource filenames, template paths, public deps-new hook names, CLI flags, IDs, schemas, or emitted content.

## Evidence

- `enabled?` at lines 71-72 gates the emitted-app compile/browser tests using `RF2_TEMPLATE_RUN_EMITTED_TESTS`; the bare name does not identify what is enabled.
- `lf` at lines 589-590 normalizes CRLF/CR to LF for setup-skill leaf comparison; the one-letter helper obscures its representation-level role.
- `run-process!` uses `pb`, `p`, `out`, and `ec` (118-168), while `npm-install-closure` uses `pj`, `t`, and `next` (234-244). These are private locals in process/package traversal code, but their abbreviated names make it harder to distinguish a ProcessBuilder, child process, merged output, exit code, package JSON, package text, and pending dependency set while reviewing failure teeth.

## Impact

This harness validates emitted template behavior and deliberate red witnesses. Misreading a control variable can lead to changing the gate or witness rather than only improving names, especially where a green run may be a skipped proof. Role-explicit locals reduce that ambiguity without changing execution.

## Compatibility and exclusions

Rename only private helper Vars and local bindings in this test namespace. Preserve function arities, environment-variable names, process commands, test names, generated paths/content, template resource filenames, public deps-new hook names, CLI flags, IDs, schemas, and all behavior. Do not touch Phase-1 repo-split documentation bead rf2-6r9j.121 or retired-feature/removal targets rf2-6r9j.106/.108/.110; do not rename any target those beads fence.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The replacements state emitted-test enablement, line-ending normalization, process lifecycle/output roles, and npm package traversal roles; no opaque `enabled?`/`lf`/`pb`/`p`/`out`/`ec`/`pj`/`t`/`next` helper/local remains where it denotes these roles.
2. No public hook, generated path, resource filename, environment/CLI flag, protocol/storage key, test discovery name, command, or template content changes.
3. Focused template JVM tests and any enabled emitted-app proof pass with unchanged test/assertion totals; lint introduces no new diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: Private emitted-app harness names identify enablement, line-ending normalization, process lifecycle/output, and package traversal roles; public hooks, generated paths/content, flags, IDs, schemas, behavior, and test discovery remain unchanged; focused template tests and lint pass.
close_reason: Implemented in commit efa09701e6 on worker/naming-tools-template-20260903-r1. Renamed only private emitted-app harness bindings: enabled? to emitted-tests-enabled?, lf to normalize-line-endings, process/package traversal abbreviations to role-explicit names, and target file local. Public deps-new hooks, generated paths/resource filenames, environment and CLI flags, IDs, schemas, test discovery names, template content, and behavior are unchanged. Verified tools/template JVM 39 tests/296 assertions exit 0; clj-kondo exit 0 with 0 warnings/errors; malformed-signature negative control exit 3; diff check clean. Opt-in RF2_TEMPLATE_RUN_EMITTED_TESTS browser/CLJS proof was not enabled.

title: spec/Ownership.md calls spec/Security.md's decisions log a 38-decision BEAD log; it has 49 rows and an empty Bead column
description:
FOUND BY rf2-6r9j.138's worker (PR #9092) while repairing the twin count in implementation/SECURITY.md. Reported rather than taken: .138 was fenced to the IMPLEMENTATION catalogue, and this row describes a different document's log.

THE CLAIM — re-derive at origin/main HEAD before acting.

spec/Ownership.md:70 describes spec/Security.md and ends its Surface cell with "...the four-proposition pragmatic stance, and the 38-decision bead log."

TWO THINGS ARE OFF, and they are not the same defect.

1. THE COUNT. spec/Security.md's own "## Decisions log" section holds 49 data rows by a deterministic first-column count over the section, not 38. (The same count method on implementation/SECURITY.md gave 49 rows / 45 distinct ids, which is what .138 fixed there.)

2. THE WORD "bead", WHICH IS THE MORE INTERESTING HALF. Every row in spec/Security.md's decisions log has an EMPTY Bead column — the table still carries the `| Bead | Call | Rationale |` header and the leading `| |` cell, but no id was found in any row. So calling it a "bead log" describes a column that is present and blank. Establish WHY before editing: were the ids stripped deliberately (the parallel case is implementation/SECURITY.md, where rf2-efioe established that all 45 ids sit below the tracker's 2026-07-11 retention floor and a preamble sentence was added saying so), or were they lost? A verified "the ids were deliberately removed and the column should go / the description should stop calling it a bead log" is a complete answer. Do NOT invent ids, and do not copy implementation/SECURITY.md's ids across — they bind a different set of calls.

title: Name test-quiet JVM stream buffers and lifecycle roles explicitly
description:
## Naming finding

The JVM runner's two stream pipelines are implemented with representation-level names that conceal lifecycle ownership. In `implementation/test-quiet/src/re_frame/test_quiet/runner.clj:263-515`, `buf`/`state` are the held line candidate and its filter mode, while `sb` is the synchronized bounded stderr ring shared by two distinct writers. In `make-summary-replay-method` and `-main` (roughly lines 865-1129), `prior`, `m`, `ran`, `real-out`, `real-err`, `sys-err`, `filtering`, `stderr-sb`, `buffered-w`, `buffered-e`, and `summary-fn` make the ownership/restoration path hard to follow. The direct concurrency test repeats `:sb` and abbreviated channel names.

## Proposed names

Name the stdout filter by role (`banner-prefix-length`, `line-candidate`, `line-mode`, `emit-text!`, `consume-character!`, `consume-string!`). Name the stderr/lifecycle values `stderr-ring`, `append-to-ring!`, `captured-stderr`, `prior-summary-method`, `test-count`, `exit-for-claim-mismatch!`, `original-out`, `original-err`, `original-system-err`, `filtered-stdout`, `buffered-stderr-writer`, `buffered-stderr`, `system-err-bridge`, and `summary-method`; mirror the ring/channel vocabulary in the direct concurrency tests and update prose.

## Ambiguity cost

This code coordinates a mutable line candidate, a synchronized shared ring, two Java stderr adapters, a temporary multimethod, and restoration of three global resources. Abbreviations make it too easy to confuse the candidate buffer with the stderr ring or the original versus installed streams during maintenance of an already concurrency-sensitive path.

## Compatibility / risk

All renamed Vars/functions are private or lexical locals; the direct test accesses private Vars but no public symbol changes. Preserve Java Writer overload behavior, output bytes, bounded-ring synchronization/cap, shutdown-hook lifetime, reporter dispatch, summary/exit behavior, public `-main`, `discovery-dirs`, and `discovery-defects`. Phase-1 beads `.89` and `.92` target different CLJS/JVM test rows, not this plumbing.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The stdout filter's candidate/mode/helper names and comments describe their domain roles rather than `buf`/`state` abbreviations.
2. The stderr ring, original/installed streams, bridge, summary method, and claim-count locals are named consistently through construction, replay, restoration, and the direct concurrency test.
3. Exact searches find no stale old names where they refer to the renamed values, while Java override argument conventions may remain where required.
4. JVM contract/lifecycle/concurrency tests pass with identical output, exit, cap, synchronization, and restoration semantics; public symbols and wire contracts are unchanged.

title: ssr-node HTTP launcher: name buffers, parsed requests, and launch settings
description:
## Coverage and evidence

The HTTP/launcher edge has several names that conceal the represented phase. `src/http.cjs:92-123` calls buffered request chunks `parts`, the over-ceiling state `over`, and each chunk/error `c`/`e`; `handleRender` calls the decoded protocol request `parsed` and buffered response HTML `buffered`. `bin/serve.cjs` calls its numeric parser `integer`, the parsed number `n`, and the combined numeric launch settings `limits` even though the map also includes `port`; the live transport is `http` and its bound address is only `bound`. These all descend from the initial transport/launcher commits (b2b35bf6e9 and 608b2a24b1).

The ambiguity costs the most at boundaries: `parts` could be decoded request partitions, `buffered` could be a boolean mode, `limits.port` is not a limit, and `http` does not say that it is the closeable transport returned by `serve`.

## Recommendation

Use edge-role names such as `bodyChunks`, `receivedBytes`, `overLimit`, `chunk`, `renderRequest`, `bufferedHtmlChunks`, `parseIntegerFlag`, `minimum`, `numericOptions`, `transport`, and `boundAddress`. Keep conventional Node handler `req`/`res` names, public transport API, CLI flags, and wire fields unchanged.

## Compatibility and exclusions

This is private/local identifier work only. Preserve exported `serve`, `statusFor`, `STATUS`, the returned `{server, port, host, close}` object, CLI flags/help/ready-line/exit codes, request selection semantics, response headers, and serialized body/refusal shapes. Do not edit the stale help/README wording owned by rf2-6r9j.86 or the retired-selector behavior pinned by rf2-6r9j.72.
acceptance_criteria:
1. HTTP body intake names distinguish raw chunks, received byte count, and the over-limit state; rendering names distinguish decoded requests from buffered response chunks.
2. Launcher names distinguish flag parsing, numeric launch options, the running transport, and its bound address.
3. Exported API, returned object shape, CLI flags/help text, ready line, headers, status mapping, selector behavior, and all wire keys remain unchanged.
4. rf2-6r9j.86's documentation targets remain untouched.
5. Exact searches, serve/bytes/protocol tests, lint, and the full ssr-node gate pass.

Do not change runtime behavior or the documented permissive `:dedup` handling on ineligible tools.

title: Remove discarded stderr write from open-in-editor capability decline
description:
Evidence:
- tools/testbed-support/src/re_frame/testbed/open_in_editor_server.clj's private launch-shim writes editor-position-unsupported to stderr and immediately exits with position-unsupported-exit (3).
- launch! always drains that stderr, but on exit 3 it returns the namespace constant position-unsupported-error directly. The retained err value is consulted only by the generic non-3 failure branch.
- Repository-wide search finds no consumer of the private shim's decline stderr; tests and the Ring handler observe only launch!'s returned map/status.
- Both the write and exit-code mapping arrived in d6cd8f086f; the surrounding comment explicitly says the verdict is intentionally read from the exit code rather than scraped from stderr.

Impact:
The decline path performs dead output I/O and suggests a second diagnostic contract that does not exist. It also adds noise to the already delicate subprocess shim.

Recommendation:
Remove the position-decline process.stderr.write call and retain only the distinct exit code. Keep stderr emission for actual launch-editor callback failures.

Risks/contracts:
Do not change exit code 3, the returned editor-position-unsupported token, generic stderr diagnostics, pipe draining, or the endpoint's 422 mapping.

Acceptance:
- The capability-decline branch exits with position-unsupported-exit without writing an unread token.
- launch! still maps exit 3 to position-unsupported-error.
- real-node capability tests and JVM endpoint tests pass with required probes armed.
acceptance_criteria: Delete only the unread capability-decline stderr emission; retain exit-code classification, generic launch failure diagnostics, pipe draining, and the client-visible 422/token contract; JVM real-node probes pass.
close_reason: PR #9087. Removed the unread stderr write from launch-shim's position-decline branch; exit code 3, the client-visible editor-position-unsupported token, the generic launch-failure stderr, pipe draining and the endpoint's 422 mapping are all untouched. Verified two ways. Census: git grep -F editor-position-unsupported over tracked files finds it only in README prose, the source constant, and tests asserting launch!'s returned map or the JSON body - never scraped from child stderr; the control census on the token that IS scraped ('launch-editor: ') finds both the write and the test reading it back. Runtime control: diverting the shim's decline exit to 9 while launch! still compared against 3 turned three real-node assertions red with :message 'launch-editor exited 9' (the empty-stderr fallback), proving the suite is live on this path AND that stderr now carries nothing there; restored by blob hash. Worth recording for the next worker: mutating position-unsupported-exit itself is NOT a valid control - it changes both sides of the comparison and stays green, a reassuring non-result. testbed-support JVM 42 tests/260 assertions green with RF2_REQUIRE_NODE_PROBES=1 armed, so the node probes really ran.

title: Make the security runtime harness fail honestly
description:
Scope: `with-runtime*` in implementation/security/test/re_frame/security/validation_redaction_invariant_security_cljs_test.cljc.

Evidence: the namespace's outer `make-reset-runtime-fixture {:clear-app-schemas? true}` disposes any installed adapter before every test and, in its post-test finally, resets frames and calls the loaded flows reset hook. `with-runtime*` nevertheless catches every Throwable/default value from `rf/init!` and ignores it, even though `rf/init!` is documented as idempotent; in this fixture state an exception indicates a real setup failure or partial initialization and should fail the security test. The helper's own finally also catches and ignores a flow reset immediately before the outer fixture performs the same reset without swallowing failure. Finally, its docstring promises "then dispose" and says "we dispose eagerly too", but the implementation never disposes the adapter; disposal occurs only on the next fixture setup. All current callers use the helper once around their production-path test body, so no demonstrated intra-test lifecycle requires these hidden fallback paths. The broad catch and inaccurate lifetime prose have been present since the helper was introduced in b58952c673.

Impact: a broken runtime setup can become a misleading downstream assertion failure or even a false green, cleanup failures can be hidden, and future maintainers are told the adapter lifetime is shorter than it really is.

Recommendation: let initialization failures propagate; choose and document one truthful lifetime (either actually dispose in the helper's finally or explicitly delegate disposal to the outer fixture); and remove the duplicate swallowed flow cleanup unless a concrete within-test isolation need is demonstrated.

Risks/contracts: preserve the adapter-less behavior needed by app-schema rows, the plain-atom runtime for the flow/subscription production-path rows, per-test flow/schema/frame isolation, and CLJ/CLJS fixture compatibility. Do not move all tests onto an adapter if that would synthesize frame state for cases intentionally testing context behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `with-runtime*` no longer blanket-catches and discards `rf/init!` failures; a targeted setup-failure control proves such an error reaches the test runner.
2. Its adapter-lifetime documentation matches behavior: disposal is either performed in its finally or accurately delegated to the outer fixture.
3. Duplicate flow cleanup is removed, or a distinct within-test requirement is documented and cleanup failure is not silently swallowed.
4. Adapter-less app-schema/context tests and plain-atom flow/subscription tests retain their intended setup.
5. `clojure -M:test` from implementation/security and `npm run test:security` from implementation both pass.
close_reason: with-runtime* no longer blanket-catches rf/init!; setup failures propagate. Adapter-lifetime docstring now names the outer make-reset-runtime-fixture (reset-runtime! -> dispose-adapter! on the way IN) instead of promising a disposal the helper never performed; the duplicate swallowed :flows/reset-flows! removed (finish-runtime-reset! already does it unswallowed in the fixture finally). Control: planted (rf/init! nil) -> 4 ERRORs naming rf/init! + :rf.error/no-adapter-specified, exit 1; the pre-fix blanket catch on the SAME fault reported :rf.error/adapter-disposed from make-state-container instead - the bead's misleading-downstream impact, live. Plant restored, verified by blob hash. Gates: security clojure -M:test 94/723 exit 0; npm run test:security 95/730 exit 0. PR #9088.

title: reagent-slim: remove the unused pr-atom receiver argument
description:
## Finding

The private `reagent2.ratom/pr-atom` helper carries an unused receiver argument. Both call sites compute the printable body before entering the helper, so the argument cannot affect output, dispatch, identity, or reactive capture.

## Evidence

- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/ratom.cljs:143-153` defines `(defn- pr-atom [a writer opts type-tag body] ...)`; `a` is never referenced.
- The only calls are the `IPrintWithWriter` methods at lines 234 and 459: each passes its receiver as the first argument but separately dereferences it to construct `body` before the call.
- `clj-kondo --lint implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src --cache false` reports exactly `ratom.cljs:143:17 warning: unused binding a` for this helper.
- Repository-wide search finds no other call, and the helper is private, so there is no external arity contract.

## Impact

The vestigial parameter suggests the helper needs the ratom identity and obscures the actual contract: it only formats a supplied type tag/body to a writer. It also leaves a permanent production lint warning that can hide new warnings.

## Proposed disposition

Remove `a` from the private helper's parameter vector and both call sites. Do not alter when the RAtom/Reaction is dereferenced or the `*ratom-context* nil` binding around nested printing.

## Risks

Moving the deref into the helper could change reactive-capture timing; that is explicitly out of scope. This task is only the mechanical deletion of the unused argument while preserving the existing precomputed `body` expression.

## Duplicate search

Searched all bead states and descriptions for `pr-atom`, `ratom print`, `IPrintWithWriter`, `unused receiver`, and the path. No match owns this finding.
acceptance_criteria:
- `pr-atom` has only `[writer opts type-tag body]`, and both RAtom and Reaction print methods call that arity.
- Existing exact printed representations for RAtom and Reaction remain unchanged, including nested-value printing and the `*ratom-context* nil` guard.
- Focused ratom print tests pass for both types.
- `clj-kondo --lint implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src --cache false` no longer reports the `ratom.cljs:143` unused-binding warning; the intentional namespace-load `installed?` warning is not papered over as part of this task.
close_reason:
Done in PR #9127 (branch worker/slimdead-a, head c7d4c437f0). The unused receiver argument is REMOVED from pr-atom's signature and from both call sites, not renamed to _: the helper is defn- with exactly two call sites, both the IPrintWithWriter methods in ratom.cljs itself and both changed in the same commit, so there is no external arity contract that a rename would have to preserve. The *ratom-context* nil binding and the point at which each receiver is dereferenced are untouched, per the bead's fence.

Census, tracked files with .beads excluded, run twice (line-oriented, then over whitespace-flattened text since neither result is a superset of the other): three sites, all in ratom.cljs, all in the diff.

The 'printed representation unchanged' criterion had NO instrument on main - the suite asserted nothing about either type's printed form. ratom_cljs_test.cljs now pins the exact #object[reagent2.ratom.RAtom ...] / #object[reagent2.ratom.Reaction ...] strings, recursive value printing, and a nested ratom printing through the same helper.

Gates, exit codes captured to a file and read from the file: CLJS node-test focused on reagent2.ratom-cljs-test COMPILE=0 RUN=0, 24 tests / 66 assertions / 0 failures; clj-kondo exit 2 (warnings) with 2 warnings, both pre-existing in batching.cljs.

Control: on unmodified main the same clj-kondo invocation reports THREE warnings including ratom.cljs:146:17 warning: unused binding a. On the branch it reports two - that one gone, the deliberate batching/installed? namespace-load warning untouched and not papered over. Separately the CLJS gate bit before it passed: its first run came back red on an assertion existing only in this branch (CLJS pr-str emits a comma between map entries), so a run that had wandered into another checkout would have been green.

Premise drift, substance unaffected: the bead's line numbers are three low - the defn is at ratom.cljs:146 not 143, the call sites at 237 and 462 not 234 and 459. And the bead says clj-kondo reports 'exactly' the one warning; it reports three on main, the other two in batching.cljs and left alone.

Finding raised in the PR body rather than acted on, because the bead explicitly fences the binding: in pr-atom, (pr-writer (binding [*ratom-context* nil] body) writer opts) scopes the nil binding to evaluating body - an already-computed local - and pops it before pr-writer runs, so the guard covers no nested printing at all. Unchanged by this diff, but it is not doing what its position implies.

title: Xray: retire the unused perf-tier module
description:
## Finding

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/theme/perf_tier.cljc` is an orphaned duration-to-colour classification module. No production Xray namespace calls it; only its dedicated test and a theme variable-resolution test require it, while its namespace contract still presents retired panels as live consumers.

## Evidence

- A repo-wide exact namespace search for `day8.re-frame2-xray.theme.perf-tier` finds the source definition, `theme/perf_tier_cljs_test.cljc`, and `theme/var_resolution_cljs_test.cljs` only. Searches for its classification/render helpers find no production source, testbed, example, facade, or skill caller.
- The namespace doc says the Performance panel re-exports it and marks `performance` and `event_detail` tier-dot surfaces `LIVE`. Commit `646e38273d` removed the Performance panel and helpers in the dead-panel sweep. Commit `aeb34400c0` retired the Handler/Event panel and its caller. No replacement consumer was introduced.
- The module was hoisted as shared theme logic in commit `bef7bd83d9` while those surfaces existed. Current `tools/xray/testbeds/panel_gallery/fixtures.cljs` mentions perf-tier dots only in fixture prose/data; it does not require or call this module, so fixture comments do not establish reachability.
- `tools/xray/spec/014-Registry-Catalogue.md` retains active-looking Performance-panel catalogue prose despite the feature-matrix documentation recording that panel as retired; the source ledger is similarly stale.
- Bead title searches for `perf tier` and `perf-tier`, plus description search for `perf-tier`, found no existing issue.

## Impact

The bundle and test matrix maintain a design-system abstraction with no rendering consumer, while source/spec prose incorrectly says retired panels are live. This creates a false extension point and lets future duration thresholds drift between actual UI code and an unused supposed authority.

## Proposed disposition

Remove the orphaned module and tests that exist only to pin it, and reconcile stale Performance/Event catalogue and source-ledger claims. If a current tier-dot surface genuinely needs the shared classifier, wire that caller and add integration coverage before retaining the module; do not treat fixture prose as a consumer.

## Risks

Preserve any live duration display implemented independently in surviving panels. Recheck concurrent work for a newly landed require and published API policy before deletion; the module is currently internal and not facade-exported.
acceptance_criteria:

- Current source/spec/feature-matrix prose no longer labels retired Performance/Event tier-dot surfaces as live.
- Xray CLJS/JVM tests, theme checks, panel-gallery build, and relevant feature-gate smoke pass without changing surviving duration displays.

Cited commits verify (bef7bd83d9 hoisted the ladder 2026-05-14; 646e38273d deleted 8 dead panels including Performance 2026-05-18; aeb34400c0 retired the Handler/Event panel 2026-05-27). Removed perf_tier.cljc (138 lines) and its 153-line self-test. THE SECOND CONSUMER, read before deleting as the bead asks. theme/var_resolution_cljs_test.cljs required perf-tier for exactly one deftest, tier-colour-returns-css-variable-string, which asserted that for every tier in perf-tier/tier-order, perf-tier/tier-colour returns a var(--rf-xray-<key>) reference rather than a palette hex literal — layer 2 of the rf2-on4cm contract, 'every public colour helper routes through the token var-map'. NOTHING LIVE STILL NEEDS THAT GUARANTEE, and it is not being dropped off a live surface: the assertion is about that one helper, the helper has no rendering consumer, and the rf2-on4cm contract itself stays fully pinned in the same file by the sibling deftests for every SURVIVING colour helper (panel-accent, accent-stripe-style, severity-colour, op-family-colour, outcome-colour, event-status-colour), with tokens_cljs_test.cljc independently pinning that every token entry resolves to a var(). title: Remove routing tooling's obsolete private bundle sentinel
description:
## Problem

`implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/tooling.cljc` still defines the private `bundle-isolation-sentinel` string `rf.routing.tooling/sentinel:rf2-eiiifu-2026-06-12:do-not-rename`, with a comment asserting that `implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs` checks that exact string. That stopped being true in commit `4e43784ec7`: the routing-tooling gate now uses the live `route-fact` node-kind literal (checker lines 422-440), while the private var has no reader.

## Evidence

- Repo-wide fixed-string search finds the opaque string only at its definition; no checker, source, test, doc, example, or tool consumes it.
- `clj-kondo` reports `re-frame.routing.tooling/bundle-isolation-sentinel` as an unused private var on both CLJ/CLJS analysis.
- The current bundle-isolation checker names `route-fact` as the routing-tooling sentinel and its positive-control module emits that live literal.
- An existing compiled positive-control bundle contains `route-fact` but not the opaque private sentinel, confirming that the old value makes no gate claim under advanced compilation.
- The checker's derivation-egress commentary (lines 504-529) documents the same failure mode: unused private sentinels are dropped by Closure, and the prior derivation-egress var was removed after its gate moved to a live literal.
- `git blame` shows the checker switched routing-tooling to `route-fact` in `4e43784ec7`, but the source var/comment remain from `119e28916c0`/`f44a288a3d5`.

## Impact

This is dead production-source data plus actively false maintenance guidance. A reader is told to keep an unobserved string in lockstep with a checker that cannot see it, and may choose the dead value when extending or debugging the isolation gate.

## Proposed disposition

Delete the private var and its stale sentinel block. Keep the gate on the live `route-fact` marker and, if source-side guidance is useful, replace the block with a short pointer to the checker's live-sentinel rationale rather than planting another unused private value.

## Risks

Do not remove or rename the checker's live `route-fact` sentinel without updating its positive-control proof. Confirm no release/source scan outside `check-bundle-isolation.cjs` relies on the old opaque value before deletion; current repo-wide searches show none.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `bundle-isolation-sentinel` and `rf.routing.tooling/sentinel:rf2-eiiifu-2026-06-12:do-not-rename` are absent from routing production source, with no stale comment claiming the checker reads them.
2. `implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs` still uses a live emitted routing-tooling sentinel and its routing-tooling positive control is non-vacuous.
3. The focused bundle-isolation checker/tests pass, including both absence from the counter bundle and presence in the routing-tooling positive-control module.
4. A repo-wide fixed-string search confirms there is no remaining reference that expected the removed opaque value.
close_reason: Removed in PR #9148 (worker/routevest-a). Premise re-verified at branch tip before deleting: check-bundle-isolation.cjs's routing-tooling arm asserts the live route-fact node kind (sentinel: 'route-fact'), not the opaque string, so the private var had no reader. Repo-wide fixed-string search (excluding .beads) found 'rf.routing.tooling/sentinel:rf2-eiiifu-2026-06-12:do-not-rename' at its definition only, line-oriented and via a null-data whole-file sweep; the definition site itself was the control that proved the search bites. Deleted the defonce and replaced the false comment with the house-style pointer used by resources.tooling (rf2-6r9j.54) and derivation.egress (rf2-yk2d), naming node-for and route-slice-algebra-view as the live route-fact minting paths; also corrected the self-referential ns-header sentence claiming an explicit sentinel at the foot of the ns. Gates: npm run test:bundle-isolation exit 0 (release-building lane deliberately chosen over test:scripts because only it runs check-bundle-isolation.cjs itself) reporting 40 internal sentinels absent and 40 emitted positive-control sentinels present, with its self-test's 40 sentinel-removal mutations passing; pinned clj-kondo 2026.04.15 exit 0, errors 0, and re-frame.routing.tooling/bundle-isolation-sentinel no longer appears as an unused private var.

title: spec(008-Testing): the poll-until CLJS example calls done in a downstream .catch — the carrier the skill copied from
description:
FOUND BY worker skillgates-a while resolving rf2-519x5 (PR #9042).

The AUDIT PR #9034 note on rf2-519x5 asked to repair BOTH carriers of the
downstream-catch/done poll-until example. The skill leaf half landed in PR
#9042 (skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/testing-views.md). The SPEC
half did not: spec/ was outside that dispatch's allowed paths.

TRUTH AT TIP, verified by reading: spec/008-Testing.md, under "#### poll-until
example", carries the CLJS fence

    (deftest cross-frame-drain
      (async done
        (-> (ts/poll-until ...)
            (.then (fn [_] (is ...) (done)))
            (.catch (fn [e] (is false ...) (done))))))

which is exactly the shape implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc
warns against in poll-until's own CLJS docstring: "Put the rejection handler
UPSTREAM of the single trailing step that calls `done`, and call `done` exactly
once with nothing after it (rf2-d3tc / rf2-qpns / rf2-fyba). `cljs.test/run-block`
hands `done` a continuation that runs the WHOLE REMAINDER of the run
synchronously, so a `.catch` sitting downstream of `done` claims whatever a
later namespace throws as this row's failure -- printing it against this row's
label -- and then calls `done` a SECOND time, which re-forces `run-block`'s
unrealized delay and re-runs the offending namespace."

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE SPEC: this is the carrier the skill copied FROM. PR
#9034 cited this exact fence as its authority. Leaving it means the next skill
pass can re-derive the defective shape from it, which is the loop the rf2-519x5
audit note explicitly asked to close ("repair both carriers rather than letting
the skill copy it again").

FIX SHAPE: rewrite that one fence to the docstring's prescribed shape --
assertion .then, rejection .catch that reports and returns nil, ONE trailing
.then that calls done. Consider whether the surrounding prose should name the
run-block reason, as the skill leaf now does. Nothing else in 008 moves.

HOT ZONE: spec/008-Testing.md is a spec file -- sequence it, do not parallel it
with another spec toucher.

TRUTH AT TIP. The recipe assumes a deps.edn exists. The ordinary empty shadow-cljs project has none: shadow-cljs.edn carries `:dependencies [[...]]` and shadow resolves those with its own Maven resolver, which accepts Maven coordinates only -- no `:git/url`/`:git/sha`, no `:local/root` (git and local deps are exactly what `{:deps {:aliases [...]}}` + deps.edn exists for). title: ci(testbed-support): the jvm lane installs no node deps, so the real-node launch probes self-skip
description:
DISCOVERED-FROM rf2-1i1ec (PR #8932), reported by that worker as an observation it deliberately did not fix.

THE FINDING (verify at source before acting): CI's `jvm-tools-testbed-support` job runs no `npm ci`, so `launch-editor-installed?` is false and every node-backed block in the suite self-skips. The job reports **42 tests / 229 assertions** where a local run with the dependency present reports **42 / 260**.

WHY IT MATTERS: the exit code cannot distinguish a run from a skip. The suite is green either way, so the real-node launch probes — including the column-only refusal that PR #8932 added precisely because no existing test could reach that path — are exercised only on a developer's machine and never in CI. The 31-assertion delta is the only signal that the block ran at all, and nothing checks it.

WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: this is a pre-existing property of the lane, not something #8932 introduced, and the remedy is a CI decision rather than a test fix. Two shapes are available and they differ in cost: install the node dependency in that job so the blocks run, or assert the expected assertion count so a silent skip fails loudly. The second is cheap and catches the regression; the first is what actually buys the coverage.

SURFACE: `.github/workflows/` is HOT-ZONE and one-toucher — sequence this against any other workflow work. Adjacent: rf2-ohfym is the sibling observation for the http lane (no solo-namespace ordering), also workflow-touching; consider whether one dispatch should take both.
notes:
MAYOR RULING, 2026-09-01: install the node dependency in the jvm-tools-testbed-support job so the probes actually run. The assertion-count assert is the FALLBACK, not the answer.

The bead states the trade exactly: the count assert is cheap and catches the regression; installing the dependency is what buys the coverage. Take the coverage. PR #8932 added the column-only refusal precisely because no existing test could reach that path - a test written to cover an otherwise-unreachable refusal, which then never runs in CI, is dead weight, and dead weight is what the stance is against. Asserting the count converts silent non-coverage into loud non-coverage; that is an improvement over today but it is a guard on the hole rather than the fix, and it would leave the 31 assertions permanently unexercised outside a developer's machine.

FALLBACK WITH A MEASURABLE DISCRIMINATOR: if arming that job drags the whole implementation dependency tree in for one small package, the cost is disproportionate and the count assert is then correct. Decide it by measuring, not by estimating - check whether the launch-editor dependency can be installed on its own, and report the added wall-clock either way. If you take the fallback, say what you measured and why it crossed the line.

Either way the job must stop being able to report green on a run that skipped every node-backed block. That is the acceptance.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #8943 (branch worker/cilanes). Took the RULING'S PRIMARY BRANCH — install the node dependency — not the assertion-count fallback, and decided it by measuring as the ruling required.

PREMISE VERIFIED AT SOURCE, both directions, before any edit: tools/testbed-support 'clojure -M:test' with implementation/node_modules absent captured exit 0 at 'Ran 42 tests containing 229 assertions'; with launch-editor present, exit 0 at 42 / 260. The 229-vs-260 claim and the 31-assertion delta hold exactly.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT DECIDED THE BRANCH. The fallback was to be taken only if arming the job dragged the whole implementation dependency tree in for one small package. It does not. launch-editor@2.14.1 is a devDependency of implementation/package.json, so it comes from the same lockfile; 'npm ci' there installs 110 packages and fetches NO browsers (nothing in that lockfile carries an install script on Linux — only fsevents, macOS-only; playwright is not flagged hasInstallScript). Locally 10.9s cold-ish and 2.9s warm. On the runner it was better still: the PR's own job shows 'added 110 packages, and audited 111 packages in 2s', and the added wall clock from the run's step timings is 5 SECONDS (setup-node 2s + npm ci 3s) against a 23s whole-job time and a timeout-minutes: 10 budget. Nowhere near disproportionate, so the coverage branch is correct and the count assert is not needed.

CI EVIDENCE ON THE PR HEAD: 'JVM tools/testbed-support (clojure -M:test)' conclusion success, 'Ran 42 tests containing 260 assertions. 0 failures, 0 errors.' — 260, not 229. The launch-editor probes ran in CI for the first time, including the column-only refusal PR #8932 added because no existing test could reach that path.

THE ACCEPTANCE ('the job must stop being able to report green on a run that skipped every node-backed block') NEEDED MORE THAN THE INSTALL. Installing makes the blocks run today but leaves the self-skip in place, so the job could go green on a skip again tomorrow (the step breaking, a package rename, a classifier change). RF2_REQUIRE_NODE_PROBES now turns each self-skip into a FAILURE naming the missing prerequisite (skip-or-fail), and the job sets it; a node-less developer box, which sets nothing, still skips exactly as before, and it is one assertion either way so the suite's count does not move with the skip. All four combinations exercised locally with captured exits: deps absent + flag unset = 0 (42/229, developer box preserved); deps present + flag unset = 0 (42/260); deps present + flag set = 0 (42/260, the CI shape); deps ABSENT + flag SET = 1 (42/229, 2 failures naming the prerequisite). That last row is the acceptance.

SURFACE: .github/workflows/test.yml only (hot-zone, one-toucher, sole workflow change in the diff) plus the test namespace. .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh and its mirror were READ, never edited — rf2-f9f3p's worker holds that pair.

title: patterns/websocket: :ws/fatal out of :active strands in-flight requests (same class as rf2-b2jpr)
description:
rf2-b2jpr routed clean :ws/disconnect through the shared fail-in-flight helper so leaving :active settles every in-flight request exactly once. One door out of :active still bypasses that invariant: :ws/fatal {:target :failed :action :record-error} (examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs, :active :on). Fired from :connected with a non-empty :in-flight, it destroys the socket actor and strands every slot exactly as the clean-disconnect bug did — the scheduled timeout carries the destroyed socket id, :current-socket? rejects it after teardown, and the slot plus its waiting :reply-event survive forever, including across a later manual :ws/connect out of :failed.

Mitigating context: nothing in the example currently dispatches :ws/fatal — it is the documented app-level escape hatch (spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md, ':active / * --:ws/fatal--> :failed'), so the leak is reachable only by consumer code using the pattern as written. :ws/auth-failed -> [:failed] is provably safe by contrast: :in-flight only fills in :connected, and every door out of :active from :connected settles it once this is fixed.

Fix is small now the helper exists: compose fail-in-flight with :record-error on the :ws/fatal transition (one action that does both), plus a wrapper deftest mirroring websocket-clean-disconnect-fails-in-flight-request with :ws/fatal as the exit door. Same fence as rf2-b2jpr: examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs + implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/websocket_cljs_test.cljs.

title: docs: 013-Trace-Consumer.md says xray-internal-event? reads a top-level :frame — a pinned test says otherwise
description:
FOUND BY `selfnoise-a` WHILE INVESTIGATING rf2-6a4p, AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED THERE — that
investigation produced no code change at all, and this is an unrelated one-sentence drift.
VERIFIED AT TRUNK 59e8833f3a before filing.

## THE DRIFT: THE OWNING SPEC CONTRADICTS A PINNED TEST

`tools/xray/spec/013-Trace-Consumer.md:95-96` describes the predicate as:

    1. **`xray-internal-event?`** — any trace event whose `:frame`
       (top-level or `:tags :frame`) resolves to `:rf/xray`.

The top-level `:frame` fallback was REMOVED under rf2-7737vq. The code says so in terms
(`self_noise.cljc:74-76`): "The prior divergent top-level `:frame` fallback is removed: per the
ruling a raw trace event carries frame identity ONLY under `[:tags :frame]`."

And it is not merely documented — it is PINNED by a test that asserts the opposite of what the
spec claims (`self_noise_cljs_test.cljc:62-73`, `xray-internal-event?-ignores-stray-top-level-frame`):

    (is (false? (self-noise/xray-internal-event? {:frame :rf/xray})))
    (is (false? (self-noise/xray-internal-event? {:frame :rf/default})))

So the spec says a top-level `:frame` of `:rf/xray` resolves true; the test pins it false; the
test passes. The spec is the stale side.

## WHY THIS IS WORTH A BEAD DESPITE BEING ONE SENTENCE

A spec that contradicts a pinned test is worse than a spec that is merely vague: a reader who
trusts it will write a raw event with a top-level `:frame` and expect it to be filtered as
Xray-internal. It will not be. That is the self-noise filter failing open, arrived at by
following the owning document.

It also survived a rename campaign and at least one audit of this predicate, which is the usual
signature of a line nobody has cause to re-read.

## SCOPE — ONE SENTENCE, AND RESIST WIDENING

Correct the parenthetical so it names `[:tags :frame]` as the only slot, ideally citing
rf2-7737vq the way `self_noise.cljc` does. Nothing else on that page is known stale.

DO NOT take this as licence to audit the whole page or the whole `tools/xray/spec/` tree. If
while you are in there you notice another stale claim, RECORD IT IN YOUR REPORT AND LEAVE IT —
a second sighting is a finding, not a mandate.

## A RELATED CORRECTION WORTH CARRYING, SINCE IT COST A READER ONCE

The Xray embedding contract lives at `tools/xray/spec/008-Embedding-Contract.md`, NOT at
`spec/008-Embedding-Contract.md`. The shorter path returns "No such file" and has already
misdirected one reader this session.

## GATE

`scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` covers `tools/*/spec` for link targets and anchors, but NOTHING
validates this page's prose — that is the whole of why this drifted. So the verification is by
hand: quote the corrected sentence and the test that pins it, side by side, in the change body.

Note also that a fenced code block is invisible to both link gates, so if the correction lands
inside a fence, neither gate inspected it.
notes:
VERDICT (docsgate-a, PR #9682, awaiting merge): CORRECTED. The bead's premise held exactly as filed, re-verified at source rather than taken from the brief.

013-Trace-Consumer.md:95-96 said the predicate resolves a frame that is "top-level or `:tags :frame`". Now 95-103: it resolves `[:tags :frame]`, read through the contract-owned canonical reader `re-frame.trace/trace-event-frame`; a raw trace event carries frame identity ONLY under `[:tags :frame]`; the prior divergent top-level fallback was removed under rf2-7737vq, so a stray top-level `:frame` is ignored. It cites rf2-7737vq the way `self_noise.cljc` does, as the bead asked, and additionally names the pinning test so a future editor of the prose meets the pin.

EVIDENCE: `self_noise.cljc:74-76` says the fallback is removed in terms and delegates to `re-frame.trace/trace-event-frame`, whose own docstring (`trace.cljc:484-496`) says raw trace events carry frame identity only under `[:tags :frame]` while DERIVED records carry it at top level. title: False: #10161 closure accepts a non-redacting auth/store-session token path
description:
Adjacent finding verified during audit of https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/10161 at 644624cea350253879cb8812f807b2f7f08618ba. Closed source rf2-0aub0 explicitly evaluated and dismissed this candidate because the event handler destructures the vector and its docstring says [[1 :token]] reaches the positional slot. The shipped declaration in examples/real-apps/realworld_http/auth.cljs:174-197 is :sensitive [[1 :token]]. That rationale is false: handler destructuring does not change classification coordinates.

implementation/core/src/re_frame/classification.cljc:372-393 projects ONLY the event's second element with redact-with-paths. For [:auth/store-session {:username ... :token ...}], the classification root is the User MAP, so [1 :token] asks for a numeric map key 1 and never visits :token. redact-event-by-registration:424-458 uses that projector for egress. Direct/top-level auth/store-session dispatch therefore leaves its JWT raw in the event projection despite the claimed protection. Durable :auth :token classification does not repair this separate transient event boundary. Normal login/register/settings success handlers inline store-session-db and are not alleged to use this direct event.

Independent Babashka execution of the actual elision/walk-tree and classification path-walk/redact-event-vec functions, with the actual auth.cljs registration metadata, preserves a synthetic fixture token under [[1 :token]]. Control [[:token]] produces :rf/redacted and preserves username. Same probe ai/probe-settings-audit-sep21-monitor-10161-1.clj; captured exit 0 and guarded-root banner. This exercises actual projection functions; no full trace/runtime test or real credential was used.

Correction: declare the payload-relative :token path and correct the docstring's vector-relative explanation. Add a focused regression to the existing implementation-side coverage proving a directly dispatched auth/store-session event's token is absent/redacted at egress. Keep the existing nested-dispatch avoidance and durable token storage behavior.
acceptance_criteria: The registration and its rationale use arg-map-relative token classification. A direct auth/store-session event projects the token as :rf/redacted while preserving ordinary User fields; an existing implementation-side regression detects the old numeric-prefix declaration. ## A SECOND `:sensitive` SITE TO CHECK WHILE YOU ARE HERE — QUESTION, NOT FINDING (mayor, 2026-09-22)

Observed by the live `rf2-ktkhn` worker, flagged rather than acted on, and recorded here because it
otherwise lives only in a transcript and would evaporate with it.

**`examples/real-apps/realworld_http/settings.cljs`'s `rf/reg-machine` OPTS carries
`:sensitive [[1 :password] [1 :submitted :password]]`.** Shape-identical to the declaration this bead
is about — and it may well be CORRECT, for a reason that is the whole point of recording it.

**The two have DIFFERENT classification ROOTS, which is exactly why they look alike and only one can
be wrong:**

- **This bead's site** (`auth.cljs`'s `:auth/store-session`) is projected by `redact-with-paths`,
  which takes the event's SECOND ELEMENT. That element is a MAP, so an integer `1` is a map key that
  does not exist, and the path reaches nothing.
- **The `reg-machine` site** is rooted at the routed SUB-EVENT VECTOR, per its own comment. In a
  vector an integer `1` is a real positional index, so the same spelling may address exactly what it
  claims to.

**NOBODY HAS MEASURED THE SECOND ONE. No claim is made here in either direction**, and it is not part
of this bead's acceptance criteria. Do not "fix" it on the strength of resembling the first.

**If you check it, check it the way this bead's defect was established** — execute the actual
projector against a fixture and look at whether the value survives, with the alternative spelling as
a control, rather than reading the comment that asserts the answer. **Reading the comment is precisely
the error that produced the mayor's wrong dismissal of this bead** (recorded in `rf2-0aub0`'s notes):
a detailed, confident docstring was taken as authority over the mechanism it describes.

Report what you find either way. If it is correct, saying so with the measurement is worth as much as
a defect would be — it closes the question instead of leaving a shape-alike sitting next to a known
bad one.

THE DISTINCTION THAT MAKES THIS FIXABLE RATHER THAN RECURSIVE, and it is the reusable part: A REPLICATED
RULE IS SAFE; A REPLICATED FACT IS NOT. The derived-ordering rule can sit on every fenced item in
identical words for ever, because nothing it says can fall out of step with anything. A holder name is a

title: Correct invoke-handler docstring to await queued event effects
description: Discovered during authoring-skill review rf2-rc9jm. implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_helpers.cljc invoke-handler docstring (around line 442) calls an attached click handler and immediately asserts app-db. invoke-handler only applies the callback; router dispatch! schedules via interop/next-tick, so an ordinary view dispatch is not drained when invoke-handler returns. Update this source-owned example to use the documented JVM poll-until or CLJS async fixture/Promise shape, preserving frame lifetime through settlement. Skills PR #10189 corrects the matching authoring leaf without widening into runtime source. Evidence: local JVM probe of the skill recipe passes after waiting and a deliberately delayed scheduler makes an immediate assertion fail.
notes:
WORKER PASS 2026-09-22 — implemented, pushed, DRAFT->READY on PR #10201 (branch worker/docstrings-y2m5z, head 81763668fe). Clustered with rf2-8ppvm in one branch and one PR; the two files cannot conflict (one src, one test).

PREMISE VERIFIED AT SOURCE, not taken from the brief. `invoke-handler` in implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_helpers.cljc ends in `(apply h args)` — it only APPLIES the callback. router.cljc's `ensure-drain-scheduled!` wraps the drain in `rf.interop/next-tick`, and the `:router/reschedule-drain!` late-bind site does the same. So an ordinary view dispatch is genuinely not drained when `invoke-handler` returns, and the old example's next-line `(is (= 1 (:n (app-db-value :rf/default))))` read the pre-click value. The item's claim holds.

WHAT LANDED. The example now settles with `re-frame.test-support/poll-until`, which is the wait this namespace's OWN ns-docstring already nominates for the async case and which docs/core/testing/views.md section 3 shows. Added prose says three things and no more: why the wait is not optional; the per-platform shape (JVM synchronous returning the truthy value and throwing `:rf.error/poll-until-timeout`; CLJS returning a js/Promise to compose under cljs.test/async with `:async? true` on the fixture); and that the click and its settle stay in the FIXTURE-OWNED frame, because a `re-frame.core/with-new-frame` body returns and destroys the frame before the queued event can drain. That third clause is the "preserving frame lifetime through settlement" part the item names as the part a naive fix drops.

DELIBERATELY ALIGNED WITH THE MIRROR. Wording follows the leaf PR #10189 corrected (skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/testing-views.md), so source and mirror now agree rather than drifting apart again. #10189 did not touch this source; that premise held too.

GATE, AND WHY THIS ONE. Both files are CLJS-compiled, so per the rf2-z0pma finding a JVM green is not evidence about them — and a docstring is a string, the rf2-kk986 shape. Held the machine-wide shadow-cljs lane exclusively for the whole run. scripts/test-fast-pr.sh from the worker worktree, CAPTURED exit 0, PASS fast PR spine, on the REBASED final base (trunk had moved nine commits; re-run rather than relying on the pre-rebase green). The spine prints its own gate root and it named the worker worktree, so the gate is known to have read the right tree.

CONTROL — THE DELIVERABLE. Planted the rf2-kk986 shape (two stray quotes, an EVEN number, so it lexes) mid-line inside the very docstring this change edits. - explicit and tracked destroy, including the `:spawn-all` children teardown
- `:final?` finalize, then the completion carrier, then the parent fold
- the join fold and resolution
- frame destroy
- update-snapshot

Every candidate was confirmed with a bounded, process-local JVM probe (`clojure -M -i <probe>.clj`), each with a control. The probes ran from a scratch runner directory whose `deps.edn` points `:local/root` at the frozen tree. One early probe, run from inside the tree, created an ignored `implementation/machines/.cpcache`. I deleted it at once, and the tree reads 0 porcelain lines.

To check for duplicates, I ran `bd export` to a scratch file and searched its titles, descriptions, notes and close_reasons with Python.

I read back each of the six beads with `bd show --json` and a Python parse. Title, parent and a body phrase all matched, and the backtick count and length equalled the source file.

### Findings
| bead | P | title |
|---|---|---|
| rf2-3x7nj.9.1 | P2 | A :spawn-all child finishing after its parent was destroyed brings the parent back to life (the join carrier bypasses the stale gate) |
| rf2-3x7nj.9.2 | P3 | :final? auto-destroy never drops the actor's :sensitive/:large elision claims; the finalize commit re-installs the pre-drop registry |
| rf2-3x7nj.9.3 | P3 | A queued single-:spawn completion folds :on-done after the parent left or re-entered the spawning state (the stale carrier counts toward the new attempt) |
| rf2-3x7nj.9.4 | P3 | Exiting and re-entering a :spawn state in one macrostep wipes the parent's :rf/spawned mirror while the new child is alive |
| rf2-3x7nj.9.5 | P3 | Join resolution cancels a child that already finished but whose carrier has not folded (one attempt ends as completed, then cancelled, then suppressed) |
| rf2-3x7nj.9.6 | P3 | An invalid inline :definition spawns a zombie actor; its validation error is swallowed and every event reports :rf.error/no-such-handler |

All six were executed, not just inspected. The probes are probe_a.clj, probe_a3.clj, probe_c.clj, probe_d.clj, probe_e.clj and probe_f.clj in the reviewer's scratch directory.

Two of the findings reopen gaps that earlier beads recorded without a fix:
- .9.1 is the gap rf2-xjee's close reason names in item 4 ("No bead filed").
- .9.5 is the finding from merged-PR audit #9353 in rf2-kuky.14's notes. rf2-kuky.14 was re-closed without a fix, and the code at `034d0c8fc8` is unchanged.

### Considered and rejected
1. **An explicit destroy leaves the children running.** `[:rf.machine/destroy <parent>]` does not tear down the parent's `:spawn`/`:spawn-all` children, because the destroy-time exit cascade collects only `:exit` actions and builds no destroy fx. This is deliberate: Spec 005:2654 and 005:4638, "teardown is explicit in v1".
2. **A frame-destroy singleton straggler gets no timer cancel or resource release.** Timers are cancelled by the `:machines/on-frame-destroyed!` hook (`cancel-all-timers!`), and per-frame resource state dies with the frame.
3. **The frame-destroy resource release dispatches into a frame that is about to be destroyed.** That state is discarded, so it is harmless.
4. **Generated addresses collide across parents.** Two parents minting the same `child#1`, and a rejected spawn leaving `:rf/spawned` naming the occupant, both fall in the rf2-1sip ruled area (option f shipped, option e unruled).
5. **An `:all` join hangs after one child is destroyed imperatively,** because `join-unsatisfiable?` does not count `:cancelled`. That destroy is a deliberate programmer act; trust the programmer.
6. **A survivor that was already cancelled gets a second cancelled row at resolution.** Spec 005:4059 already specifies two cancelled rows per survivor.
7. **The completion carrier is queued before the finishing macrostep's own fx.** Machine callbacks cannot read app-db, and everything lands in the same drain, so no misordering is observable.
8. **An `:rf.machine/update-snapshot` `:state` patch bypasses timers, spawns and finality.** This is the documented escape-hatch trade-off.
9. **`resolve-actor-handler-meta` rebuilds and re-validates the handler on every event to a spawned actor.** The cost is linear, not pathological, and caching it is part of the fix direction on .9.6.
10. **A `reconcile-snapshot` reset leaves the old incarnation's children and timers.** This is restart semantics on hot reload, and an edge case.
11. **The `destroy-spawn-all-children!*` comment promises a post-terminal cleanup reason, but the code always requests `:explicit`.** Completed children are already gone, so this is comment drift with no behavioural effect.
12. **`[:rf.machine/destroy <plain-event-id>]` unregisters a non-machine handler.** This is spec-sanctioned cleanup of a stale entry.
13. **An exception in a join child's action is routed nowhere.** `:on-error` on `:spawn-all` children is rejected at registration by design.
14. **validation.cljc** (registration-time checks) was read in full. Its errors are loud at `reg-machine`, and I found no lifecycle defect there.
15. **A self-targeting `:on {:retry :loading}` from `:loading` is a no-op.** This is XState v5's `reenter: false` default, and it is machines-core scope.

### What could not be verified
- **The CLJS lane.** No shadow-cljs was run, per the brief. The paths involved are shared `.cljc`, and the only `:cljs`-led reader conditional in scope is a require flag (registration.cljc:41), so the JVM results should transfer. The CLJS gate still has to grade each fix.
- **The `:spawn-all` half of .9.4** (wiping the children-map mirror) was inspected, not probed. It goes through the same `teardown-actor` call.
- **The exit case of .9.3** is a design call, recorded under that bead's Decision needed section.
- **The cost of re-validating the handler on every event** was not measured.

I made no edits to any tracked file and no git writes.
