title: core-instrumentation: :rf.event/after-deltas on :rf.event/run-end ships the whole app-db unredacted (every [:rf.interceptor/path ...] handler), including in the off-box epoch projection
description:
## Defect

The `:rf.event/run-end` trace carries `:rf.event/after-deltas`, a per-`:after`-interceptor diff of `:coeffects` and `:effects`. The standard `[:rf.interceptor/path …]` interceptor's `:after` always rewrites both `[:coeffects :db]` and `[:effects :db]`, so every path-focused handler stamps the WHOLE app-db, before and after, into that slot. The emit-time classification chokepoint `re-frame.classification/project-trace-event` has no arm for `:rf.event/after-deltas`, so the frame's classified sensitive paths ship RAW in the trace stream, the per-frame ring, the epoch record, and — confirmed — the OFF-BOX `project-egress` projection of that epoch record, which is what the pair MCP `trace-window` / `watch-epochs` tools send. Any other user `:after` that edits `:effects :db`, or adds `:fx` entries, leaks the same way. In the `:fx` case the args also skip their fx registration's classification.

## Where

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/classification.cljc:1137-1241` — `project-trace-event` projects `:rf.event/v`, `:event`, `:rf.event/fx`, fx args, cofx maps, `:rf.event/db`, render args, sub values and machine slots. It never touches `:rf.event/after-deltas`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:2895-2909` — `emit-pipeline-trailers` stamps `(:rf/interceptor-after-deltas final-ctx)` onto `:rf.event/run-end` unprojected.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/interceptor.cljc:176-183, 219-234, 261-280` — `compute-ctx-delta` diffs `:coeffects` and `:effects` and keeps the full `:before` / `:after` values. Only `:rf/default?` interceptors are skipped.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/std_interceptors.cljc:180-229` — the path interceptor's `:after` does `(assoc-in [:coeffects :db] original-db)` (line 208) and widens `[:effects :db]` back to the full db (line 212).
- Off-box: `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:2248` — `elide-trace-events-slot` re-roots only `:rf.event/db`, then bulk-walks from `:path []`. A root-anchored declaration such as `[:auth :token]` can never match `[i :tags :rf.event/after-deltas 0 … :db :after :auth :token]`.
- Public entry: any `rf/dispatch` / `rf/dispatch-sync` of an event registered with `{:interceptors [[:rf.interceptor/path […]]]}`.

## Failure scenario

1. `(rf/reg-event :seed (fn [{:keys [db]} _] {:db (assoc db :auth {:token "SECRET-TOKEN-4242"} :counter 0) :sensitive [[:auth :token]]}))`, then dispatch it.
2. `(rf/reg-event :bump {:interceptors [[:rf.interceptor/path [:counter]]]} (fn [{:keys [db]} _] {:db (inc db)}))`, then dispatch it. The handler never reads `:auth`.
3. The `:rf.event/run-end` trace for `:bump` carries `"SECRET-TOKEN-4242"` twice, under `:rf.event/after-deltas 0 :rf.interceptor.delta/ctx-delta {:coeffects|:effects} :changed :db :after :auth :token`. `rf/trace-buffer` returns it, trace listeners and Xray receive it, and the epoch record stores it.
4. `(rf/project-egress <that epoch record> {:rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/off-box-tool})` still carries it at `[:trace-events 5 :tags :rf.event/after-deltas 0 :rf.interceptor.delta/ctx-delta :coeffects :changed :db :after :auth :token]` and the matching `:effects` path.

## Evidence

EXECUTED — bounded JVM probes from the reviewer scratch dir against the frozen tree at `034d0c8fc8` (core + epoch as `:local/root` deps; nothing written to the tree), running the scenario above:

- CONTROL `:rf.event/db-pending` `:rf.event/db :auth` → `{:token :rf/redacted}`. The secret is absent from that trace, so the declaration is live and the chokepoint works for its known slots.
- PROBE the `:rf.event/run-end` trace contains the secret, top-level `:sensitive?` is nil, and the after-delta ids are `[:rf.interceptor/path]`.
- PROBE `rf/trace-buffer :rf/default {:flat true}` contains the secret.
- PROBE the off-box-tool projected epoch record for `:bump` contains the secret at the two paths listed above.
- CONTROL the off-box projection of the `:seed` record, and of a `:bump2` record from a handler WITHOUT the path interceptor, contains the secret at 0 paths.

Grep `after-deltas` over `implementation/*/src` and `tools/*/src` → hits only in `interceptor.cljc` and `router.cljc`, and no projector names it. `spec/Conventions.md:122` documents the slot as a DEBUG-gated diagnostic for the Xray AFTER INTERCEPTORS lens and says nothing about redaction. A tracker full-text search for `after-deltas` / `ctx-delta` → 0 beads (control: `elide-wire-value` → 25).

## Smallest fix

Add a `project-trace-event` arm for `:rf.event/after-deltas`. For each record, walk the `:db` entries under `:coeffects` / `:effects` (`:added` / `:removed` values and `:changed` `:before` / `:after`) through `rf.elision/elide-wire-value` with `{:frame frame-id}`, failing closed on a nil frame exactly as `project-db-tags` does. Route a `:fx` entry's value through the existing `project-event-fx-entry`. Both helpers are already in the namespace. Fence: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/classification.cljc`, plus a test beside the rf2-izlr7f / `project-db-tags` tests. The alternative — summarising `:db` in `compute-ctx-delta` (`interceptor.cljc`) — would cost the Xray lens its diff. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

JVM core artefact: `clojure -M:test` from `implementation/core`. `classification.cljc` is plain cljc, and `project-trace-event` sits in no reader conditional. `npm run test:cljs` covers the CLJS lane. The epoch artefact's JVM suite (`implementation/epoch`, `clojure -M:test`) shows the off-box record follows.

## Decision needed

No.

notes:

### Tree
Frozen tree `C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/review-sep23` at `034d0c8fc87a0331e8803ff3f82d6f3b15e9b914` (detached, clean). Every cite is against it.

- Tool-Pair §Time-travel (the restore failure table, restore caveat, §Pair-tool writes, re-publication rule)
- 005 `:rf/snapshot-version`
- 015 and Privacy.md (registration-owned transient classification; recordable coeffects exclude secrets)
- Managed-Effects (restore must not revive host work)
- Spec-Schemas `:halt-reason`
- 002 depth-halt pseudo-code

### Method
Read all primary source top to bottom, weighing:

- capture: what a record holds and when it is taken
- restore and replace: partition consistency; in-flight work, timers and machines across a restore
- ring trimming and bounds (depth, trace-events-keep, anchors, mount attribution, silence ledger)
- replay determinism (strict token, capture-loss refusal, commit-observation identity)
- the off-box `project-record` projection, slot by slot

Traced each candidate from its producer to a public entry point. Confirmed the two filed defects with bounded, process-local JVM probes, run from a scratch `deps.edn` that uses `:local/root` into the frozen tree, and took a control for every result. The first probe ran from the artefact directory and left a gitignored `.cpcache` there. I removed it at once; the tree reads clean in `git status --porcelain --ignored` and later probes ran from scratch. Searched the tracker before filing each finding, with a control search that does find known beads.

### Findings

| Bead | P | Title |
|---|---|---|
| rf2-3x7nj.17.1 | P1 | epoch: a `:halted-depth` record's `:halt-reason :last-event` ships the last-settled event's args RAW through `rf/project-egress` (and the replay/restore refusal carriers), bypassing registration classification |
| rf2-3x7nj.17.2 | P3 | epoch: `restore-epoch!` treats an absent `:rf/snapshot-version` as compatible, so a restore across an added/removed version stamp succeeds and the machine then resets the restored snapshot to initial |

Both EXECUTED.

- .17.1: `SECRET-TOKEN` reaches the projected halt record under all three off-box profiles, and reaches the replay refusal envelope and the restore-non-ok-record trace. Control: the same drain's `:ok` records carry none, raw or projected.
- .17.2: control 1→2 refuses. absent→1 and 1→absent return `true`, then `:rf.error/machine-snapshot-version-mismatch` resets the snapshot on the next event.

Not refiled, per the brief: rf2-3x7nj.4.2 and rf2-fc84b (after-deltas), rf2-3x7nj.11.1.

### Considered and rejected
- **Cofx values and the record's top-level `:rf.cofx` replay token are not failed closed off-box, though event args and fx args are.** Spec Privacy.md "Recordable coeffects must exclude secrets" plus the emit-time `reg-cofx` classification make this deliberate. Replay also refuses a token carrying a substitution (`lost-replay-inputs`).
- **Sub `:query-v` args ride raw in `:sub-runs`.** Spec 015 names this the deliberate positional fail-open for query args.
- **Restore does not re-arm machine `:after` timers, leaving a snapshot restored into a timed state stuck there.** Tool-Pair's restore caveat and Managed-Effects rule this deliberate ("epoch restore MUST NOT revive host work").
- **Restore does not clear pending router-queue events or `:dispatch-later` timers.** This falls under the documented caveat that effects already fired are not reversed. It is a debug-gated tool.
- **Restore validates only the app-db partition against schemas, not the runtime-db partition.** The Tool-Pair failure table scopes the schema check to app-db explicitly.
- **Restore records no epoch of its own, and re-anchors back-fill onto the older restored record.** Documented ("the ring is not self-describing across a restore") and pinned by the inv-9 attribution tests.
- **`replace-frame-state!` into a frame with NO prior epoch cannot be undone.** Restore targets only `:frame-state-after`, while the synthetic record's `:frame-state-before` is unreachable; the same holds at depth 1. The "undo works after this call" rationale that refuses depth 0 does not hold here, but a real session almost always has a prior epoch, and the fix is a design change. Noted, not filed.
- **Post-settle renders from LOCAL (non-subscription) state are back-filled into the last-settled epoch, appending a row per render until the next event.** Dev-only and bounded by the next event or eviction. This is the designed "genuine re-render rides the settling cascade" rule (inv-3). Listener re-publication is coalesced per tick by Xray (`install.cljs note-epoch-recorded!`).
- **`harvest-buffer!` and `harvest-buffer-for-event!` read and write the capture buffer in two steps, so a concurrent JVM enqueue marker can be lost, and the docstring says "atomically".** The loss is one `:rf.event/dispatched` trace on a JVM multi-thread path where epoch is normally off. Not worth a morning.
- **`harvest-buffer-for-event!` keys the settle on the FIRST buffered run-start rather than the settling envelope's dispatch-id.** A run-start stranded by an exception escaping the drain would shift every later record by one. No reachable escape was found: `execute-chain` catches Throwable; fx, flows and listeners are isolated. So this is speculative hardening and not filed.
- **`:trace-events-keep` lowered at runtime elides only one record per append.** Documented as an append-time rule.
- **`run-cause` / `value-changed-epoch-for` scan cost per render.** O(buffer) and O(ring trace) per render, bounded by the per-run render cap and the drain depth. Not pathological.
- **The delayed-silence ledger (listener generations, observation continuum, terminal marks).** Read for correctness; nothing found beyond what the rf2-vxgfnd / rf2-uhouu / rf2-8b9twg rounds already closed.

### Could not verify
- No CLJS execution (no shadow-cljs, per the brief). The epoch source's reader-conditional branches are small (locks, catch classes) and were read by inspection only.
- The pair-MCP relay of the replay refusal envelope was established by reading the tool source and the preload docstring ("the framework's refusal envelope verbatim"), not by running the MCP server.
- Whether any path lets an exception escape the drain after run-start (see the harvest note above) was checked by reading core, not exhaustively.

title: core-reactive: live-derivation-graph throws (whole graph lost) when any live edge carries a float or fn query-vector arg
description:
## Defect

`re-frame.derivation.graph` sorts every assembled edge by `re-frame.identity/canonical-bytes`, the deterministic-edge-order fix from rf2-3fc89f.1. `canonical-bytes` THROWS `:rf.error/non-edn-identity` for any value outside the CEDN-1 domain: floats, fns, host objects. In the LIVE graph, edge endpoints carry each subscription's whole concrete query vector. So one cached layer-2+ subscription whose query vector (or one of its inputs' query vectors) has a float or a fn argument makes `live-derivation-graph` throw, and the whole graph is lost, not just the offending edge. Spec 006 §Value-keyed cache-key contract says the reference cache admits finite floats in query arguments, so these are legal, cached subscriptions.

## Where

Frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`.

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/graph.cljc:670-673` — `(->> (concat input extra) distinct (sort-by rf.identity/canonical-bytes) vec)`.
- `graph.cljc:183-195` — `sub-input-node-id` keeps the full query vector as the edge endpoint in `:live` mode. `graph.cljc:197-219` builds those `:input` edges.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/tooling.cljc:458-489` — the live `:subs` projection keys each node by its concrete query vector, and lowers its realized inputs to `[:sub q]` (`:300-302`).
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/identity.cljc:244-259` (`bad-number?`), `:319-350` (`encode` rejects non-integer numbers at `:340` and host values at `:350`), `:354-362` (`canonical-bytes` throws).
- Consumer: the Xray Graph panel's `:rf.xray/derivation-graph` sub body calls `live-derivation-graph` (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/derivation_graph.cljs:488-495`, `:536-539`). The throw is recovered as a sub-exception to nil, so the panel renders an empty graph.
- Public entry point: `re-frame.derivation.graph/live-derivation-graph`, reached from Xray's Graph tab in `:live` mode, and from the conformance fixtures.

## Failure scenario

```clojure
(rf/reg-sub :items (fn [db _] (:items db)))
(rf/reg-sub :items/within {:inputs [[:items]]} (fn [[items] [_ radius]] (filter #(< (:d %) radius) items)))
(rf/reg-sub :items/count  {:inputs [[:items]]} (fn [[items] _] (count items)))
;; a view reads @(rf/subscribe [:items/within 2.5]) and @(rf/subscribe [:items/count])
```

Open Xray's Graph tab and switch to Live. `live-derivation-graph` builds the edges `{:from [:sub [:items]] :to [:sub [:items/within 2.5]] :role :input}` and `{… :to [:sub [:items/count]] …}`. The sort calls `canonical-bytes` on the first edge, which throws `:rf.error/non-edn-identity` (`:reason :non-integer-number`). The whole live graph is replaced by nothing. A query vector carrying a predicate fn (`[:items/matching some-pred]`) fails the same way, with `:reason :unsupported-host-value`.

It needs at least two edges, because a one-element `sort-by` never calls its key fn. That is also why a single-edge fixture cannot see it.

## Evidence

Executed: `scratchpad/review-wave/core-reactive/probe_graph.clj`, one-shot `clojure -M` over the frozen `implementation/core/src`, run from the scratch dir. It calls `live-derivation-graph` with a `:subs` contributor whose live nodes are shaped exactly like `sub-cache-algebra-view`'s: `[:a]` with no inputs, and `[:b arg]` and `[:c]` each over `[:sub [:a]]`.

- Control, integer arg `5`: OK, 3 nodes, 2 edges.
- Float arg `0.5`: THREW `clojure.lang.ExceptionInfo`, `:rf.error/non-edn-identity`, `:reason :non-integer-number`.
- Fn arg: THREW, `:reason :unsupported-host-value`.

An earlier single-edge run of the same probe did NOT throw. That run is the evidence for the two-edge precondition.

The static graph is unaffected: `sub-input-node-id` drops the arguments in `:static` mode.

The tracker export has no bead mentioning `canonical-bytes` together with `graph-edges`, or `live-derivation-graph` together with `float`.

## Smallest fix

Keep the deterministic order, but make the key total. For example, sort by `(fn [e] (try (rf.identity/canonical-bytes e) (catch … _ (str "￿" (pr-str e)))))`, so CEDN edges keep their current order and anything outside the domain sorts after them, stably. Alternatively, canonicalize endpoints through a tolerant projection. The fence is `implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/graph.cljc` only. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

`graph.cljc` is `.cljc`, so both lanes grade it:

- JVM: the `implementation/core` suite (`implementation/core/test/re_frame/derivation_graph_test.clj`) and `implementation/derivation-conformance`;
- CLJS: `npm run test:cljs`, which picks up `derivation_algebra_conformance_cljs_test.cljc`.

A regression row should assemble at least two edges, one of them float-bearing.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
## Fix: PR #10280 (worker/reactive-graph-3x7nj), 2026-09-23 AUSEST

**Reproduced at trunk `2c8b8847a3`** (the source was unchanged from the frozen `034d0c8fc8` for every fenced file). A one-shot `clojure -M` probe over `implementation/core` called `live-derivation-graph` with a `:subs` contributor over `[:a]`, `[:b arg]` over `[:sub [:a]]` and `[:c]` over `[:sub [:a]]`:
- integer arg `5`: OK, 3 nodes, 2 edges;
- float `0.5`: THREW `:rf.error/non-edn-identity`, `:reason :non-integer-number`;
- fn: THREW, `:reason :unsupported-host-value`.

After the fix all three return 3 nodes and 2 edges.

**The fix** is in `graph.cljc` only. `graph-edges` now sorts by a new private `edge-order-key`, which never throws. Both source claims and regression coverage inspected at merge 8ff2143962c9328267948eb8717327dbc3e0c1ab. title: core-images-and-rest: inline image :reg-fx/:reg-cofx/:reg-event registrations silently drop :platforms, :sensitive/:large and :interceptors (a #{:client} fx runs on :server, its args go unredacted, a declared guard never runs)
description:
## Defect

An `rf/image` inline registration (`:registrations {:reg-event [...] :reg-fx [...] :reg-cofx [...]}`) does NOT lower to the runtime descriptor shape a namespace-authored `reg-*` of the same kind produces, and the difference is silent. The lowering hooks keep the inline metadata only under the descriptor's NESTED `:metadata`, while every runtime reader looks at the descriptor's TOP LEVEL, where `reg-*` puts it. Three metadata contracts are dropped this way:

1. **Inline fx and cofx `:platforms` is ignored.** A `#{:client}` fx runs on the `:server` host.
2. **Inline fx and cofx `:sensitive` / `:large` are ignored.** `registration-classification` reads nil, so the egress redaction derived from it has nothing to redact.
3. **Inline event `:interceptors` references are discarded.** `event-handler-meta` overwrites the key with the wrapper-only chain, so a declared guard interceptor never runs. Assembly's missing-reference check also passes an unregistered interceptor id, because it reads the top-level chain (keyword-free) first.

Registration-time validation is also skipped on the inline event, fx and cofx paths:
- `validate-registration-metadata!` (the retired/unknown key check)
- `validate-classification!` (a malformed `:sensitive` fails loud at `reg-fx`, but not inline)
- `reject-at-boundary-without-schema!` for events

The sub lowering does not have this defect: `lower-inline-sub` validates and hoists classification (rf2-vxgfnd.219).

EP-0026 §Inline Registration Grammar states the intended contract: the inline form "lowers through that kind's own registrar parser, so the inline contract is exactly the registrar's contract". EP-0023 §Image Fragments says the same: "Both paths should lower to the same runtime descriptor shape".

## Where

Frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`.

**Assembly:**
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/image.cljc:385-389` builds the inline descriptor with metadata NESTED: `(seq metadata) (assoc :metadata metadata)`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/image_assembly.cljc:438-459` (`lower-inline-descriptor`) merges the hook's return UNDER the descriptor, and nothing hoists the nested metadata.
- `image_assembly.cljc:1005-1006` makes `check-references!` read `(or (:interceptors d) (get-in d [:metadata :interceptors]))`. The top-level wrapper-only chain wins, so the nested reference is never checked.

**Lowering hooks:**
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:179-187`: `lower-inline-fx` returns ONLY `{:handler-fn impl}`. Its docstring says the runtime `:platforms` predicate "reads that map directly", and that is false.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/cofx.cljc:296-307`: `lower-inline-cofx` returns only `:handler-fn :recordable? :provided?`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc:1489-1531`: `lower-inline-event` calls `(event-handler-meta meta [] impl)`. `events.cljc:644-665` `event-handler-meta` then `assoc`s `:interceptors` to `[wrapper]`, overwriting the inline `:interceptors` refs. The docstring at `events.cljc:1518-1521` says author-declared `:interceptors` "remains an advanced inline shape out of this slice's scope", but nothing refuses it.

**Readers of the top level:**
- `fx.cljc:193-202`: `runs-on-platform?` reads `(:platforms meta #{:client :server})`. The descriptor reaches it via `resolved-fx-meta` (`fx.cljc:1217-1236`, `rf.registrar/lookup`) at `fx.cljc:1513`, and at `cofx.cljc:820` for cofx.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/classification.cljc:189-198`: `registration-classification` reads the top level of `rf.registrar/handler-meta`. The egress chokepoint uses it at `classification.cljc:395-402`.

**Registered path, for contrast:** `fx.cljc:53-63` (`register-with-classification!`) validates and then stores the metadata at the TOP LEVEL.

## Failure scenario

Here is the ordinary shape for a story or test double, and equally for any app image that uses inline registrations:

```clojure
(rf/make-frame
  {:id :app/f
   :images [(rf/image
              {:id :app/one
               :select-ns {:include ["app.*"]}
               :registrations
               {:reg-fx    [[:app/save-token {:platforms #{:client} :sensitive [[:token]]}
                             (fn [_ args] (write-token-to-local-storage! args))]]
                :reg-event [[:app/login {:interceptors [:auth/guard]}
                             (fn [_ _] {:fx [[:app/save-token {:token "s3cr3t"}]]})]]}})]})
```

Dispatching `[:app/login]` on the JVM/SSR host (`:server`) has three effects:
- `:auth/guard` never runs.
- The client-only fx RUNS on the server.
- The fx args are not classified, so the `:rf.fx/handled` trace and any off-box projection carry `{:token "s3cr3t"}` unredacted.

The identical declarations made with `rf/reg-event` / `rf/reg-fx` behave correctly: the guard runs, the fx is skipped on `:server`, and the token is classified.

## Evidence

**EXECUTED:** a bounded JVM probe, run from `implementation/core` in the frozen tree, `clojure -M <scratch>/probe_inline.clj`, with `CLJ_CACHE` set to scratch. The tree was clean after the run (`git status --porcelain` 0 lines). The JVM host's `active-platform` is `:server`.

Pure assembly:
- **1a.** An inline event naming the UNREGISTERED interceptor `:p/guard` makes `ia/assemble` return `:no-throw`.
- **1b.** The lowered descriptor's `:interceptors` count is 1, with keyword refs in the chain `[]` and nested `:metadata :interceptors [:p/guard]`.
- **1c.** CONTROL: a registered-shape event with the same ref gives `:rf.error/image-missing-reference`.
- **1d.** Inline fx: top-level `:platforms` is `nil`; the nested value is `#{:client}`.
- **1e.** Inline fx: `runs-on-platform? :server` is `true`, even though it was declared `#{:client}`.
- **1f.** Inline fx: `registration-classification` under its generation is `nil`.
- **1g.** CONTROL: a registered fx with the same metadata gives `runs-on-platform? :server` = `false`.
- **1h.** CONTROL: the registered fx's `registration-classification` is `{:sensitive [[:token]]}`.

End to end, through `make-frame` plus `dispatch-sync` in one frame:
- **2a.** CONTROL: the registered event runs the guard 1 time, and the client-only fx ran on the `:server` host `[]`.
- **2b.** The inline event runs the guard 0 times, and the client-only fx ran on the `:server` host `[[:inline {:token "s3cr3t"}]]`.

**Inspected, not executed:**
- The cofx arm (`lower-inline-cofx` hoists none of `:platforms` / `:sensitive` / `:large`; the same `runs-on-platform?` / `registration-classification` readers apply).
- The skipped registration-time validators.
- The trace egress path that derives redaction from `registration-classification`.

**Tracker:** searched open and closed beads by full-text over a `bd export` (title, description, notes, close_reason, design, acceptance) of 2116 issues:
- `lower-inline-fx`: 0 hits
- `lower-inline-cofx`: 0 hits
- `inline` + `platforms`: 4 hits, none about this (rf2-nrc93 is the `:ns` stamp; the others are unrelated)

The adjacent doc-normalisation fix rf2-mt1cvi touched this same seam without covering the dropped metadata. No bead covers it, and no other wave surface has filed it (rf2-3x7nj.1 through .4 checked at filing).

## Smallest fix

Make the fx and cofx lowerings do what `register-with-classification!` does, and make the event lowering either honour or refuse `:interceptors`. For fx and cofx:
- Call `rf.reg-meta/validate-registration-metadata!` and `rf.classification/validate-classification!`.
- Return the metadata merged at the TOP LEVEL, for example `(assoc meta :handler-fn impl)` for fx, with the grade flags added for cofx.

The merge in `lower-inline-descriptor` already lets the descriptor win shared keys, so `:impl`, provenance, `:kind` / `:id` and nested `:metadata` are preserved.

For events, pick one of two options:
- (a) Resolve inline `:interceptors` refs the way `register-event!` does. Once the refs sit where `check-references!` reads them, it validates their existence.
- (b) Until EP-0026's Open Question is ruled, REFUSE a non-empty inline `:interceptors` with `:rf.error/invalid-image`, rather than silently discarding it.

Also correct the false sentence in the `lower-inline-fx` docstring.

Files: `fx.cljc`, `cofx.cljc`, `events.cljc`, and optionally `image_assembly.cljc`. None is a hot-zone file.

## Gates

- `cd implementation/core && clojure -M:test` (the JVM core suite; the image and inline tests there are `.cljc`).
- `npm run test:cljs`. The lowering runs identically on CLJS, and the ep0023 / image_assembly `*_cljs_test.cljc` namespaces run in the node lane.

Add RED tests first:
- inline fx `:platforms` honoured on `:server`
- inline fx/cofx classification present under the generation
- inline event `:interceptors` either run or refused

## Decision needed

For inline event `:interceptors`: honour them (a), or refuse them loud until EP-0026's Open Question is ruled (b)? Silently discarding them is the one outcome that should not survive.

Priority is P2. The classification half is a redaction bypass, which is P1-shaped, but inline registrations are mostly test-double and story territory rather than the production path. Re-grade to P1 if production images are expected to carry inline fx.
notes:
== DOSSIER WRITTEN 2026-09-23 22:25:08 AUSEST (analysis only — no status change, no dispatch, no edit) ==

Dossier: ai/decisions/rf2-3x7nj.5.1.inline-registration-metadata.md. ai/ is local-only and gitignored, so the path is a convenience that can rot; the decisive findings are restated below. Read at trunk 4b627ee9e2 (= origin/main). git log 034d0c8fc8..4b627ee9e2 -- implementation spec docs tools is empty, so every cite in this bead still holds.

RECOMMENDATION: option (a), honour inline :interceptors. Fix it in the same PR as the fx/cofx metadata hoisting and the skipped validators, which are plain bugs needing no ruling. The governing text already decides the event half, so this is closer to a confirmation than a choice.

DECISIVE FINDINGS:
1. The spec already rules (a). EP-0026:455-457 says the inline form lowers through the kind's own registrar parser, "neither a looser superset nor a stricter subset". spec/Conventions.md:228 says "each lowering through that kind's own registrar parser". spec/002-Frames.md:2621 says an image listing inline :registrations "validates the refs at assembly". EP-0026 Open Questions item 2 (:694-705) calls the per-kind inline metadata grammar "implementation detail, left to the implementing agents ... not by an operator ruling". Option (b) would need a carve-out in hot-zone Conventions and 002.
2. The fix is small and measured. A bounded JVM probe from implementation/core re-published the three late-bind lowering hooks with the option-(a) shape inside that process only; no file was edited and git status read 0 lines after. Readings, trunk -> sketch:
   - unregistered inline guard at assemble: :no-throw -> :rf.error/image-missing-reference
   - inline #{:client} fx runs-on-platform? :server: true -> false
   - inline fx registration-classification: nil -> {:sensitive [[:token]]}
   - malformed inline :sensitive: :no-throw -> :rf.error/bad-classification
   - end to end, guard runs / client fx ran on :server: 0 / [[:inline {:token "s3cr3t"}]] -> 1 / []
   Every sketch reading equals its reg-* control. The event hook is events.cljc:1489-1531: it passes the validated refs as event-handler-meta's interceptors argument (events.cljc:661-665 currently overwrites them with [wrapper]). The fx/cofx hooks (fx.cljc:179-187, cofx.cljc:296-307) return the metadata at top level.
3. P2 stands; the P1 re-grade condition is not met. Exactly 1 production inline :reg-fx exists (tools/story/src/re_frame/story/network.cljc:206-211), and it carries only :doc. Bead addition: inline fx/cofx :schema is dropped by the same defect (fx.cljc:1534, cofx.cljc:684); inspected, not executed.

Probe files (scratch, not durable): decisions-sep23/rf2-3x7nj.5.1-probe-fix-sketch.clj plus .out files.
== RULING (delegated by Mike; mayor-dispatched ruling agent, 2026-09-23 23:05:10 AUSEST) ==

RULING: option (a). Inline :reg-event :interceptors are HONOURED exactly as reg-event honours them, and the same PR makes inline :reg-fx / :reg-cofx / :reg-event lower through the registrar's own preparation (metadata at the descriptor TOP LEVEL, and every registration-time validator reg-* runs), so an inline registration means exactly what the same declaration means in reg-*. No spec edit is required and no hot-zone file is touched; option (b) is rejected.

WHY
- The governing text already decides it; this is a confirmation, not a new product call. EP-0026 Inline Registration Grammar (docs/EP/EP-0026-image-api-simplification.md:456-458): "The inline form of a kind lowers through that kind's own registrar parser, so the inline contract is exactly the registrar's contract - neither a looser superset nor a stricter subset". spec/Conventions.md:228: inline grammar for four kinds, "each lowering through that kind's own registrar parser". spec/002-Frames.md:2621: an image listing inline :registrations "validates the refs at assembly". spec/Conventions.md:1133/1150: the reg-event metadata map is the one superset middle slot carrying :interceptors, "The image descriptor format is this exact shape", and "the silent-drop footgun is structurally gone (the chain is honoured, not dropped)". EP-0026 Open Questions item 2 (:694-705) assigns the per-kind inline metadata grammar to "the implementing agents ... not by an operator ruling". So (b)'s premise - hold "until EP-0026's Open Question is ruled" - does not hold: that question was never an operator question.
- (b) loses on every axis. It costs the same code as (a), but contradicts the three spec passages above, so it would need a carve-out in hot-zone spec/Conventions.md and spec/002-Frames.md, adds a second grammar the programmer must remember, makes an auth-guarded event impossible to inline (EP-0026 use case 3, the test-doubles image, is exactly where it would be wanted), and creates a "refused until later" state that EP-0026 says nobody will ever rule. Keeping the silent drop is ruled out by everybody: a security-relevant declaration (a guard, a #{:client} platform, a :sensitive path) that is ignored is the opposite of trusting the programmer.
- Dossier and Codex AGREE on (a), independently, each with an executed JVM probe. Codex adds two qualifications, both ADOPTED below: (1) full parity needs more than hoisting plus two validators - reuse the cofx grade preparation and the event boundary/interceptor shape checks, and fix a test fixture that relies on the looseness; (2) separate shape validation from the GLOBAL-registrar existence check: the image's authority for interceptor refs is assembly's check-references! against the sealed generation, never the global registrar. Where they differ, only in size: the dossier's "about 25 lines" is the minimum sketch; Codex's fuller parity list is the bar.

title: epoch: restore-epoch! treats an absent :rf/snapshot-version as compatible, so a restore across an added/removed version stamp succeeds and the machine then resets the restored snapshot to initial
description:
## Defect

`restore-epoch!`'s version-drift precondition treats an ABSENT `:rf/snapshot-version` on either side as compatible. It only refuses when the recorded snapshot AND the current definition both carry a version and the two differ. The machines artefact's own compatibility rule is exact equality, absent included: "Both absent matches; both present-and-equal matches; any other shape is a mismatch".

So a restore across a version stamp being ADDED (a machine's first incompatible change: absent to 1) or REMOVED (1 to absent) passes every precondition. It installs the old snapshot, emits `:rf.epoch/restored` and returns `true`. Then the machine's next event trips `:rf.error/machine-snapshot-version-mismatch` and resets the restored snapshot to the definition's initial state. The restore reports success, and its machine state is silently discarded one event later. That is precisely the outcome `:rf.epoch/restore-version-mismatch` exists to refuse up front ("the older snapshot can no longer be interpreted"; restore rejected, state unchanged).

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8` (frozen tree):

- `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:310-320` (`machine-version-mismatch`): `(when (some? recorded) ... (when (and (some? current) (not= recorded current)) ...))`.
- It disagrees with `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/registration.cljc:339-347` (`version-compatible?` is `(= (snapshot-version machine) (snapshot-version snapshot))`).
- Reached from `rf/restore-epoch!` through `check-restore-preconditions!` (`tool_pair.cljc:498-514`).

## Failure scenario

1. `(rf/reg-machine :m/tl {:initial :red :states {:red {:on {:tick :green}} :green {:on {:tick :red}}}})`, with no `:meta` version.
2. Dispatch `[:m/tl [:tick]]`, so the snapshot is at `:green` with no version. Take that epoch as the target. Dispatch `[:m/tl [:tick]]` again.
3. Hot-reload the machine with its first version stamp, `:meta {:rf/snapshot-version 1}`.
4. `(rf/restore-epoch! :p/main target-id)` returns `true` and the snapshot is back at `:green`.
5. Dispatch `[:m/tl [:tick]]`. A faithful restore goes `:green` to `:red`. Instead `:rf.error/machine-snapshot-version-mismatch` fires, the snapshot resets to initial `:red`, and the tick moves it to `:green`. The developer sees the wrong state after a restore the tool reported as successful.

The mirror case (1 to absent) behaves identically.

## Evidence

EXECUTED: a bounded JVM probe (scratch `deps.edn` with `:local/root` into the frozen tree, machines artefact on the classpath). The trace ops listed are the ones recorded after the restore call.

- CONTROL, versioned 1 to 2: `restore-epoch!` returned `false`. Trace ops were `[:rf.epoch/restore-version-mismatch ...]`, so the probe does see a refusal.
- absent to 1: `restore-epoch!` returned `true`, with trace ops `[:rf.epoch/restored :rf.error/machine-snapshot-version-mismatch]`. The snapshot after restore was `{:state :green ...}`. After the next `:tick` it was `{:state :green ... :meta {:rf/snapshot-version 1}}`, not the faithful `:red`.
- 1 to absent: same shape, `true` plus a machine-level mismatch on the next event.

Existing pins (`epoch_test.clj` `restore-failure-version-mismatch`, `actor_revertibility_restore_test.clj`) cover only the present-vs-present case.

Tracker searched (`snapshot-version`, `version-mismatch`, `machine-version-mismatch`, `version drift`, `restore` filtered for machine/version): no bead covers it. The rf2-ocg1 and rf2-rlt3sv ids cited in the tests no longer resolve.

## Smallest fix

Make `machine-version-mismatch` use the machines rule: a mismatch whenever `(not= recorded current)` for a snapshot whose current definition RESOLVES. Keep skipping the unresolved-definition case, which `missing-references` already reports as a missing handler. One wrinkle: `current-definition-version` (`tool_pair.cljc:279-290`) cannot currently tell "registered singleton with no version" from "no definition". `singleton-definition-version` returns nil for both (`:148-150`), and the nil then falls into the spawned-actor branch. So resolve the definition FIRST (singleton registration, or `:machines/spec-from-snapshot`), then compare the two version slots with `=`. The trace tags then carry a nil `:version-recorded` or `:version-current`. The 009 and API tag rows describe those as `<int>`, so widen them to `<int-or-nil>` if the schema pins them.

Fence: `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc` plus a test beside `restore-failure-version-mismatch` in `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_test.clj`. The optional doc touch to the tag-type wording would reach `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` / `spec/API.md` (both hot-zone). The code fix alone needs neither.

## Gates

JVM: `clojure -M:test` in `implementation/epoch` (`re-frame.epoch-test`, `re-frame.actor-revertibility-restore-test`). The changed form is in a `.cljc` outside any reader conditional.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
== IMPLEMENTED (worker epoch-3x7nj, PR #10301, branch head 963de37e11 on trunk 3f44c2e5f4) ==

The fix is the description's "Smallest fix".
- epoch/tool_pair.cljc: current-definition-version and singleton-definition-version are replaced by current-definition. It resolves the definition FIRST, returning {:spec :type}: registry-first by snapshot key, else :machines/spec-from-snapshot. That is the same order as the machines resolver's spec-from-id-or-snapshot.
- machine-version-mismatch skips a snapshot whose definition does not resolve (missing-references reports it). Otherwise it compares the two [:meta :rf/snapshot-version] slots with =, which is the machines artefact's version-compatible? rule. The docstring was updated.

- restore-refuses-a-version-stamp-added-since-the-recording (absent -> 1): false, frame state unchanged, :rf.epoch/restore-version-mismatch with :version-recorded nil and :version-current 1.
- restore-refuses-a-version-stamp-removed-since-the-recording (1 -> absent): the mirror.
- restore-admits-an-unversioned-machine-across-a-reload: CONTROL. Both absent, restore succeeds and rewinds past the later write.

Measured (JVM):

- Restore verified by blob hash against the committed object.
- The existing restore-failure-version-mismatch and actor_revertibility_restore_test pass unchanged. implementation/epoch 568 / 7508 / 0.

Tag-type wording: NOT changed, because spec/Spec-Schemas.md does NOT pin <int>. RestoreVersionMismatchTags (~:2063) and MachineSnapshotVersionMismatchTags (~:1533) both type :version-recorded / :version-current as :any, which admits nil. title: xray-data-layer: diff engine leaves every element :same when Editscript collapses a populated vector/map to one whole-value :r (all elements changed, reversed, all keys swapped) - changed values paint as unchanged, [N∆] reads 0
description:
## Defect

When every element of a populated vector changes, or every key of a populated map is replaced, Editscript A* emits ONE whole-value `:r` for it. The diff engine then shows the container as modified and every changed element inside it as unchanged.

`expand-collection-replacement` expands a whole-value `:r` into member-level edits for sets (any member count) but for vectors, lists and maps ONLY at the empty edge. Its docstring rests that scoping on two claims:

- "a populated↔populated vector swap is handled by Editscript's per-index `:+` / `:-` / `:r` edits already (it does NOT collapse to a whole-value `:r`)";
- "Multi-key populated↔populated MAP swaps are NOT a known Editscript `:r` pathology".

Both are false against the pinned Editscript 0.6.5. Once enough of the collection differs, A* chooses one whole-value `:r`: every scalar changed, a reversal, or every map key replaced. The engine then classifies the container `:modified` and leaves every member path with no entry, so `op-at` returns its no-entry default `:same` for each element, and `change-count-at` reads 0.

The inspector's `leaf-diff-op` takes `op-at` as the op for any leaf with both sides present. Every changed element is therefore painted as UNCHANGED (dimmed, no `← was` chip). This is the empty-edge "sea of red" defect rf2-yucxn and rf2-9d4j8 fixed, arriving from the populated side.

It affects every FULL+DIFF surface (App-DB tab, Epoch `:db` lens, Machine snapshot drill-in, Reactive sub values), on ordinary shapes: a vector of coordinates or counters that all tick, a list re-sorted in reverse, a selection map swapped wholesale.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/diff/engine.cljc:197-318` (`expand-collection-replacement`). The false premises are at `:238-240` and `:253-258`. The map arms at `:279-286` require an empty side, the sequential arm at `:300-316` requires an empty side, and `:317-318` passes everything else through unchanged.
- Classification: `engine.cljc:1078-1080` (whole `:r` becomes one `:modified` at the container path). `op-at` / `change-count-at` are at `:1202-1224`.
- Consumers:
  - `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector.cljs:3642-3650` (`leaf-diff-op`: `projection (engine/op-at projection path)` answers `:same`);
  - `edn_inspector.cljs:2995` (`[N∆]` chip from `change-count-at`, which reads 0).
- Public entry: `engine/project` via `project-for` (`edn_inspector.cljs:4388`).
- Contract: `tools/xray/spec/004-App-DB-Diff.md:59-75`. The per-path projection classifies each LEAF.

## Failure scenario

Executed (JVM). For each case the raw Editscript output is followed by what `engine/project` answers:

- `{:scores [10 20 30]}` → `{:scores [11 21 31]}`: `[[[:scores] :r [11 21 31]]]`.
  - `op-at [:scores]` = `:modified`, `change-count` 0.
  - `op-at [:scores 0|1|2]` = `:same`, `:same`, `:same`, while every value differs (10→11, 20→21, 30→31).
- `{:v [1 2 3 4]}` → `{:v [4 3 2 1]}`: `[[[:v] :r [4 3 2 1]]]`. All four `[:v i]` read `:same`. The root form `[1 2 3 4]` → `[4 3 2 1]` gives the same result.
- `{:user {:prefs {:a 1 :b 2}}}` → `{:user {:prefs {:c 3 :d 4}}}`: `[[[:user :prefs] :r {:c 3 :d 4}]]`.
  - `[:user :prefs]` = `:modified`, `change-count` 0, and `[:user :prefs :c]` = `:same`.
  - `:flat-rows` holds one opaque container row.
  - The inspector's own `::missing` pairing does repair the added and removed KEY rows in the map case, so the vector case is the one that paints wrong rows.

Controls, same run:

- `{:v [1 2 3 4]}` → `{:v [1 9 3 4]}` gives `[[[:v 1] :r 9]]`: `[:v 1]` `:modified :before 2`, the rest `:same`, count 1.
- `{:v [1 2 3]}` → `{:v [9 8 3]}` gives per-index `:r`: two `:modified`, count 2.

So the defect appears exactly when A* crosses to a whole-value `:r`, and the threshold is Editscript's cost model, not anything the programmer chose.

## Evidence

Executed with a one-shot `clojure -M` probe from my scratch directory, with nothing written to the tree. It loads the frozen tree's `tools/xray/src` and `juji/editscript 0.6.5` (the version `tools/xray/deps.edn` pins), and prints raw edits beside `op-at`, `change-count-at` and `:flat-rows` per element.

- The first sighting came from an independent accounting oracle run over 16 mixed vector scripts: mid, front and scattered inserts and deletes, duplicates, rotation, lists. All passed except the reversal, whose root `:r` left every element reading `:same`.
- The only other oracle FAIL was a false alarm in my oracle (`:modified` slots carry no `was-index`); the engine was correct there.
- Tracker: rf2-gwye.10 and rf2-yucxn cover only the empty edge. No bead covers a populated whole-value `:r`.

## Smallest fix

Expand every same-kind whole-value `:r`, not only the empty edge, the way the set arm already does:

- **Map ↔ map:** per-key union delta — `:+` for after-only keys, `:-` for before-only keys, `:r` per shared key whose value differs.
- **Vector/list ↔ same-kind sequential:** per-index `:r` for `0 … (min n m)-1` where the values differ, plus `:+` / `:-` for the tail. The removals must go in descending order, as the empty-edge arm already does for the replay.

This removes the need for the premise, and the docstring sentences go with it. Type changes (map ↔ vector, scalar ↔ collection) stay R7 `:modified` exactly as now.

Fence: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/diff/engine.cljc` and `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/diff/engine_cljs_test.cljc`. No hot-zone file. The fence overlaps the other two diff-engine beads filed under this surface, so sequence them.

## Gates

`clojure -M:test` in `tools/xray` (JVM: the engine and its test are `.cljc` with no `:cljs` branch on the changed forms). `npm run test:cljs` also runs the test on the node lane.

## Decision needed

No.

title: xray-chrome-config: re-popping after an opener reload reuses the named pop-out window, so the stale 'Opener gone' overlay and dead shell cover the fresh live shell
description:
## Defect

`popout!` opens its window with `(.open js/window "" "rf-xray-popout" …)`, which targets a fixed window NAME with an empty URL. When a window of that name is still open, the browser returns that window without navigating it. The HTML "window open steps" navigate an existing navigable only when the URL is not empty.

That is exactly the state an opener RELOAD leaves behind (rf2-uong):

- The old pop-out window stays open.
- Its document still holds the dead shell's `#rf-xray-popout-root`.
- It also holds the `#rf-xray-popout-opener-gone-overlay` that the reload announcer revealed: fixed, full-window, `z-index: 2147483647`.

After the reload, `popout-state` is `nil` (a fresh realm), so the next `popout!` does not see the old window as its own. It appends a SECOND `#rf-xray-popout-root` and a second, hidden overlay into that same document, then renders a live shell there.

The old visible overlay still covers the whole window, and the dead shell's DOM sits above the new root in the body. The user has just asked for a fresh pop-out, and the window they get still says "Opener gone … close this window and open a fresh pop-out" over a shell that is actually live. There are also duplicate element ids.

Inline mode already guards the equivalent case with `remove-stale-root!` (`mount.cljs:190-204`). The pop-out has no counterpart.

## Where

Cited at `034d0c8fc8` (frozen tree):

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount.cljs:1703-1814` is `popout!`.
  - :1735 short-circuits only on the in-realm `@popout-state`.
  - :1740 is `(.open js/window "" "rf-xray-popout" "popup,width=960,height=720")`.
  - :1744-1758 creates a new node, sets id `rf-xray-popout-root` and `(.appendChild body node)`. Nothing removes existing children first.
  - :1786 calls `(install-opener-gone-overlay! doc)`.
- `mount.cljs:1462-1531` is `install-opener-gone-overlay!`. It appends a new overlay (id `rf-xray-popout-opener-gone-overlay`, fixed, z-index 2147483647) and never looks for an existing one.
- `mount.cljs:1617-1652` is `register-opener-reload-announcer!`. On the opener's `pagehide`, it reveals the OLD overlay, and that reveal persists in the pop-out document.
- `mount.cljs:1681-1701` is `style-popout-document!`. It is idempotent, id-probing, and therefore not part of the problem.
- `mount.cljs:190-204` is `remove-stale-root!`, the inline precedent.
- Public entry points: the pop-out button (`⛶`), `(xray/popout!)` (`core.cljs:103`, `install.cljs:200`) and the palette's Ctrl+Enter (`palette/events.cljs:65-83`).
- Contract: `tools/xray/spec/011-Launch-Modes.md:493-505`. The pop-out does not survive an opener reload. It announces instead, and "The user closes the stale pop-out and opens a fresh one." The spec is silent on a user who re-pops WITHOUT closing, which is the natural move when the pop-out lives on a second monitor.

## Failure scenario

1. Pop out Xray. The pop-out window is named `rf-xray-popout`.
2. Hard-reload the host page. The pop-out now shows the "Opener gone" overlay, as designed.
3. Click the pop-out button in the reloaded host without closing the old window first.
4. The browser returns the same window. Xray appends a new live shell and a hidden overlay to it.
5. The window still shows "Opener gone … close this window and open a fresh pop-out", because the old overlay is visible and topmost. The live shell underneath cannot be used until the user closes the window and pops out a third time.

## Evidence

**Inspected only.** This is multi-window browser behaviour, and browsers are out of bounds for this review. The confidence rests on three things:

- `popout!` passes an empty URL with a fixed name. By the HTML window-open steps, the URL record stays null and an existing named window is returned un-navigated. It is the well-known `window.open('', name)` idiom.
- The reloaded opener is the pop-out's own opener browsing context, so the name lookup can reach it.
- Neither `popout!` nor `install-opener-gone-overlay!` queries for or removes an existing root or overlay. Grepping `mount.cljs` for `getElementById` finds only :201-202, both inside the inline path's `remove-stale-root!`. So the search can find such a lookup, and the pop-out path has none. The only `querySelector` hits, :219 and :325, are the layout-host lookup and the shell-node lookup, and neither is on the pop-out path.

The first step when fixing should be a browser reproduction.

Tracker: rf2-uong (closed) built the reload announcer and did not consider re-popping into the surviving window. `rf-xray-popout-root` appears in 0 records of the tracker export. The control term `install-opener-gone-overlay!` appears in 2 (rf2-uong, rf2-9vm0). No open bead covers this.

## Smallest fix

In `popout!`, once `win` is in hand, remove any existing `#rf-xray-popout-root` and `#rf-xray-popout-opener-gone-overlay` from `(.-document win)` before appending. This mirrors `remove-stale-root!`. Five lines or so.

An alternative is a per-open unique window name. That stops the reuse but leaves the stale window lying around, so the removal is the better fix.

Fence: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount.cljs`, plus an arm in `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount_cljs_test.cljs`, where rf2-uong's stub-window tests already live. No hot-zone files.

## Gates

`mount.cljs` is `.cljs`, so the node lane grades it with `npm run test:cljs` (`mount_cljs_test`). A JVM green says nothing about it. Real window reuse needs a manual two-window check.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
== FIXED (worker xray-chrome-3x7nj, 2026-09-24 06:50:20 AUSEST), PR #10307 ==
Re-verified at trunk 79af44357d: popout! opened (.open js/window "" "rf-xray-popout" ...) and appended a new #rf-xray-popout-root, then install-opener-gone-overlay! appended a new overlay, without removing any existing ones. The premise held.
Built: mount/remove-stale-popout-nodes! removes any existing #rf-xray-popout-root and #rf-xray-popout-opener-gone-overlay from the pop-out window's document (getElementById, then parentNode.removeChild), mirroring remove-stale-root!. popout! calls it right after style-popout-document! and before appending. It is a no-op when the document has neither node or has no getElementById.
Test: mount_cljs_test popout!-evicts-a-dead-realms-shell-and-overlay-from-a-reused-window, driven through the real popout! (with-driven-popout). It seeds the reused window's body with a stale root and a revealed overlay, then asserts exactly one root and one overlay, that the stale nodes are detached, that the survivors are the ones the state names, that the overlay is hidden, and that the opener's document is untouched. The stub pop-out document gained getElementById.
Control: with src reverted, exit 1 and this row red (5 fails, plus 4 reporter errors from printing the cyclic DOM stubs; a follow-up commit changed those assertions to booleans). With the fixes in, exit 0. Not checked by hand in a real two-window browser.
Merged-PR audit #10307 (d7ba113224aee095fef502a2daf42c018d90da82; merged 2026-09-23T21:14:38Z). Completeness: Sparse settings overrides cover user writes, individual column widths and inherited width clamps; configure no longer persists defaults; v2 reset follows the ruling. Pop-out focus, drag ownership/cleanup and stale-root/overlay removal cover the four source findings. Correctness: Reviewed changed persistence and document ownership paths and separate-document test controls. Accepted reported post-rebase node 12594/63474, JVM 1392/6790 and negative-control results; CI 37 successful checks. Real two-window manual behavior was not claimed by the implementer or rerun here. Implementation quality: Uses element ownerDocument/defaultView and stores ownership for teardown; preserves replace semantics and avoids migration machinery in pre-alpha. No material additional finding. Actionable findings: none. Existing finding updates: none.

title: xray-shell-views: in pop-out mode the modal focus trap pins Tab to the first control and column/table drags are dead (opener js/document)
description:
## Defect

In pop-out mode, the shell's document-scoped DOM code reads and listens on the OPENER's document, while the pop-out shell is painted into a different document, so three shell mechanisms fail there. The cause is that `popout!` renders `ShellView {:mode :popout}` from the opener's JS realm into `win.document`, so every `js/document` and `js/window` in these views names the opener. The spec already records this for keyboard input ("DOM key events do not" cross the realm), and rf2-61i5 fixed the global keybindings by giving the pop-out a listener on its own document. The first mechanism is the modal focus trap, `a11y/dialog-ref`. Its Tab handler sits on the dialog node and does receive the event, but it computes the current position from `(.-activeElement js/document)`. That is the opener's active element, never one of the pop-out dialog's focusables, so `trap-wrap-target` always takes its "focus outside the cycle" arm. It calls `preventDefault` and sends Tab to the FIRST control and Shift+Tab to the LAST, so a keyboard user can never Tab past the first control of any pop-out modal. The same read at mount records an opener-document element as the focus-restore target. The second mechanism is the shell's event-list column dividers. `col-divider-start-drag!` puts its `pointermove`/`pointerup`/`pointercancel` listeners (and the `col-resize` cursor) on the opener's document, so they never fire and the dividers cannot be dragged. The third is the `resizable-table` gutters, used by the Trace ops table among others. They fail the same way, with listeners on the opener's `js/window`.

## Where

Frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`:

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/theme/a11y.cljs:200` (mount-time `activeElement`), `:225` (Tab handler `activeElement`), `:242` (restore reads the opener `body`). `trap-wrap-target` `:122-139`, where `(nil? idx)` sends Tab to `first-el` and Shift+Tab to `last-el`.
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/theme/modal_chrome.cljs:129-131`: every modal defaults to `(a11y/dialog-ref)`. Consumers include Settings, the command palette, the filter edit popup, the spine filters, the EDN inspector popup and the cancellation-cascade modal.
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/shell.cljs:544-552`: document listeners and the cursor. The dividers are rendered at `:2017`, `:2042`, `:2051`, `:2292`, `:2301` and `:2310`, inside `ShellView`, which is also the pop-out body.
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/resizable_table.cljs:446-449`: window listeners.
- The same pattern outside this slice, for whoever owns it: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/resize_handle.cljs:291-296` and `:702-707`.
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount.cljs:1746-1784`: `popout!` renders the shell into `(.-document win)`.
- A search of `tools/xray/src` for `ownerDocument`, `defaultView` and `setPointerCapture` returns 0 hits. Nothing derives the document from the node.
- Contract: `tools/xray/spec/011-Launch-Modes.md:366-377`, "Runtime state crosses the realm boundary; **DOM key events do not**", which is the rf2-61i5 section.

## Failure scenario

1. Pop out Xray. Press the Settings key or open any filter or palette modal. Press Tab: focus lands on the first control. Press Tab again: it stays there. Shift+Tab jumps to the last control and stays there. No other control is keyboard-reachable.
2. In the pop-out, drag an event-list column divider or a Trace table gutter. Nothing resizes. The next pointerdown quietly detaches the stranded listener set.

## Evidence

- **Inspected**: the realm and document relationship comes from `mount.cljs:1746-1784` together with spec 011's rf2-61i5 section, which states the same mechanism for key events. Pointer and focus state are per-document in the same way: `document.activeElement` is per-document, and pointer events dispatch within the document that owns the target.
- **Inspected**: `trap-wrap-target` is pure. Given an `active` that is not in `focusables`, it returns `first-el` for Tab, and the handler then calls `preventDefault`.
- **Not executed**: this needs a two-window browser, which the brief rules out. That is the only unverified link.

## Smallest fix

Derive the document from the node or event instead of the global:

- In `dialog-ref`, use `(.-ownerDocument node)` for `activeElement` and `body`.
- In `col-divider-start-drag!`, use `(.. e -currentTarget -ownerDocument)` for listeners and cursor.
- In `resizable-table`, use that document's `defaultView` as the window.

The pure `trap-wrap-target` stays unchanged. Apply the same one-liner to `resize_handle.cljs` in its own slice.

Fence: `theme/a11y.cljs`, `shell.cljs` (the col-divider fns only) and `views/resizable_table.cljs`, plus their tests. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

`npm run test:cljs`, the node lane (`.cljs` only). The existing test seams stub `js/document`, so a unit test can pin "reads the node's `ownerDocument`". The real witness is a browser pop-out scenario under the Xray feature-matrix gate (`npm run test:xray-feature-gate`). Say which one the change relies on.

## Decision needed

No.

Re-verified at trunk 79af44357d: a11y/dialog-ref read (.-activeElement js/document) at mount and in the Tab handler and (.-body js/document) at restore; shell.cljs col-divider-start-drag!/detach used js/document; resizable_table.cljs used js/window; tools/xray/src had no ownerDocument/defaultView reads. The premises held.

The column dividers bind their listeners and cursor to resize-handle/pointer-document (the ownerDocument of the event's currentTarget, falling back to js/document) and keep that document in the drag state, so the detach removes them from the same document. resizable-table binds to the gutter document's defaultView and keeps that window in its drag state. title: story-ui-workspace: canvas, workspace cells and the multi-substrate grid resolve :component/:substrates from the raw body, and the switchers resolve :viewport/:background the same way, ignoring :extends
description:
## Defect

Several surfaces resolve a variant's `:component` from the RAW variant body and then fall back to the parent story. They ignore the `:extends` chain that the plan compiler folds. Those surfaces are:
- the canvas;
- the workspace cells;
- the multi-substrate grid;
- the viewport and background switchers, which read `:viewport` and `:background` the same way.

`:substrates` is resolved the same way by those surfaces.

Spec 017 §`:extends` says `:extends` inherits world context, including render fixtures. The plan does exactly that: `[:world :component]` is `(or (:component ctx) (:component story-body))`, where `ctx` is the `:extends`-merged chain. So an `:extends` child of a variant that declares its own `:component` renders the wrong view on the live canvas, or none at all. Meanwhile `run-variant`, the render prep, Docs, Explain and the plan hash all use the inherited one. Spec 014 and 001-Authoring both say that routing through the compiled plan "resolves an `:extends`-inherited or `:compose`-d `:component` that a bare-body read would miss". These renderers are exactly that bare-body read.

## Where

- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/canvas.cljs:257-268`, `variant-component`: the raw variant `:component`, else the story's. It is used at `:565` in `canvas-inner`, even though `canvas-inner` compiles the plan at `:587-589` and reads decorators, args and sub-overrides off it. The rf2-gwye.7 comment at `:576-586` records moving exactly these reads off the raw body.
- `canvas.cljs:521-545`, `variant-substrate-set`: raw variant and story bodies go into `multi-substrate/resolve-substrate-set`.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/workspace.cljc:305-315`, `variant-component-id`: the same raw read, used at `:360` in `variant-cell-inner`. That function also uses `canvas/variant-substrate-set` (`:426-428`).
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/multi_substrate.cljs:528-530` (outside this slice's scope): the same raw read.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/viewport_switcher.cljs:90-119` and `backgrounds_switcher.cljs:75-101`, `effective-*`: the raw `:viewport`/`:background` of the variant, else the story's. These are read by `shell.cljs:829-850` to frame the canvas.
- Plan side: `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/plan.cljc:1566-1610` and `:1769-1774` fold `:component`, `:substrates`, `:viewport` and `:background` through `ctx`, the `:extends` chain. The comment at `:1591-1595` notes that `:viewport`/`:background` are "read off the bodies by the UI".
- Public entry: select an `:extends` child variant in the sidebar, or place it in a workspace.

## Failure scenario

The story is `:story.mixed {}`, which names no `:component`, as in a story whose variants render different views.
- `:story.mixed/card-base` declares `{:component :app.ui/card ...}`.
- `:story.mixed/card-child` declares `{:extends :story.mixed/card-base :args {...}}`.

Selecting `card-child`, the canvas shows "variant has no :component registered", yet `run-variant` renders `:app.ui/card`.

title: http: on the JVM a same-:request-id re-issue landing in the superseded request's retry handoff leaves the successor live but unregistered (managed-abort / supersede / frame sweeps miss it)
description:
## Defect

On the JVM, a same-`:request-id` re-issue can leave the SUCCESSOR request live but unregistered. It happens when the re-issue lands while the superseded request is moving between retry phases. Both retry handoffs publish their new handle with an unconditional `record-in-flight!`, which is `(swap! in-flight assoc [frame id] handle)`:

- `schedule-backoff-handle!` (live-fetch → backoff);
- `run-attempt!`'s retry-handoff arm (backoff timer fired → attempt N+1).

Each handoff decided to proceed before the supersede landed: `maybe-retry!` sampled `:aborted?` as clear, or the timer won `fired?`. So it overwrites the successor's slot. Its own post-registration re-check then sees the shared abort cell set and clears ITS handle by identity. That leaves the slot EMPTY while the successor's request is still on the wire. From then on the successor cannot be reached by `[:rf.http/managed-abort id]`, is not superseded by the next same-id issue (so its reply is delivered out of order, which is exactly the debounce-search failure supersession exists to prevent), and is invisible to the frame-destroy and epoch-restore sweeps. CLJS is immune: the completion callback and the timer callback each run to completion without interleaving an event.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8` (frozen tree), host: **JVM only** (shared `.cljc`; only the JVM runs completions and timers on other threads).

- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc:1407-1417`: `maybe-retry!` samples `:aborted?` once (1412), then hands off at 1452.
- `transport.cljc:1247-1274`: `schedule-backoff-handle!` registers the backoff handle unconditionally. `:1372-1376`: its post-arm re-check clears that handle by identity, leaving the slot empty.
- `transport.cljc:1866-2004`: `run-attempt!` registers the attempt-N+1 handle unconditionally. `:2050-2053`: its re-check clears it by identity.
- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/registry.cljc:232-251` (`record-in-flight!`, the unconditional `assoc` at 237-238) and `:636-645` (`supersede!`, which clears the old slot, then the successor registers).
- Contract: `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:668` (a fresh same-id request REPLACES the prior one, and managed-abort aborts whichever request holds the id) and `:677-679` (§Frame scope clause 4: a cleanup that silently unregisters a live request leaves it unabortable).
- Entry point: two `[:rf.http/managed {… :request-id :q :retry {…}}]` issues, where the first's retry-eligible failure completes on the HttpClient thread while the second is issued on the event thread.

## Failure scenario

R1 = `{:request-id :race :retry {:on #{:rf.http/http-5xx} :max-attempts 3 …}}`. It gets a 500. R1's completion thread passes `maybe-retry!`'s abort sample. On the event thread the user re-issues R2 with `:request-id :race`: `supersede!` aborts R1 (reply suppressed) and R2 registers under `[:rf/default :race]`. R1's thread continues into `schedule-backoff-handle!`, whose `record-in-flight!` overwrites R2's slot. The post-arm re-check sees the abort and removes R1's backoff handle, and the slot is now empty. The user dispatches `[:rf.http/managed-abort :race]`: nothing is found and no cancellation is delivered. R2 then completes and delivers `:status :ok` to the app after the user aborted it. The timer-fire handoff shows the same outcome when the re-issue lands after the backoff timer has won `fired?`.

## Evidence

EXECUTED, deterministically, using the repo's own test interleaving seam (`re-frame.http.transport/set-test-interleave-hook!`, the same one `http_abort_retry_race_test.clj` uses). JVM probe against the frozen tree: server hit 1 returns 500, later hits park on a latch; `:retry {:on #{:rf.http/http-5xx} :max-attempts 3 :backoff 2000ms}`. The hook calls `managed-handler` for the same-id R2 at the named point.
- CONTROL (R2 issued normally after R1 settled into backoff): slot `PRESENT attempt=1 issuance=2`; `abort-in-flight-in-frame! :rf/default :race :user` returns `true`; replies `[[:cancelled :user [:rf.work/http :race 2 1]]]`.
- SUBJECT, point `:backoff/before-register`: the hook fired and R2 WAS registered inside the window (`true`). After R1's transition the slot read `EMPTY`; managed-abort returned `false`; replies `[[:ok nil [:rf.work/http :race 2 1]]]`. The aborted R2 delivered success.
- SUBJECT 2, point `:retry/before-attempt` (timer-fire handoff): identical. Slot `EMPTY`, managed-abort `false`, replies `[[:ok nil [:rf.work/http :race 2 1]]]`.
- Existing coverage: `http_abort_retry_race_test.clj` injects only a USER abort at these points, and `clear-in-flight-2arg-is-identity-conditional` pins the clear side. No test puts a successor registration in the window. Tracker full-text search (successor + overwrite / unregistered / record-in-flight) found no bead on this.

## Smallest fix

Give the registry a "take over the request-id slot only if it still holds `prev-handle`" publication: a compare-and-swap on the `[frame id]` key. Use it for the two handoff registrations in place of the unconditional `assoc`. When the swap fails, a successor or abort already owns the id, so do not publish to the request-id index. The existing `:aborted?` re-check then finishes the cancelled predecessor as it does today. The actor/anonymous-index publication and reconcile are unchanged. Fence: `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/registry.cljc`, `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc`, and a successor-in-window case in `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_abort_retry_race_test.clj`. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

JVM: `clojure -M:test` in `implementation/http`, which runs `http_abort_retry_race_test.clj` and `http_backoff_cancellation_test.clj`. The change is shared `.cljc` outside any reader conditional, so the node lane `npm run test:cljs` must still compile it, but only the JVM can exercise the race.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
== FIXED, PR #10320 (branch worker/http-3x7nj), 2026-09-24 10:00 AUSEST ==

Premise held at trunk 24cfb3141a: both handoffs published with an unconditional `(swap! in-flight assoc ...)` via `record-in-flight!`.

Reproduced deterministically with the transport's interleaving seam: new tests `successor-issued-at-backoff-registration-keeps-its-slot` (point `:backoff/before-register`) and `successor-issued-at-timer-fire-handoff-keeps-its-slot` (point `:retry/before-attempt`) in http_abort_retry_race_test.clj. From R1's thread, the hook issues the same-id successor R2 through `rf.http.managed/managed-handler` (supersede + register + send; the server parks R2). At trunk source both read the `:race` slot as nil after R1's handoff (expected issuance 2), and `[:rf.http/managed-abort :race]` reached nothing. The first red run also leaked the unregistered R2 into sibling tests (a late transport-error reply), which is the bug's own symptom; the test's finally now lets R2 answer before the server stops, and a later red run left the five sibling tests green.

Fix: `registry/record-in-flight!` gains a 4-arity `[request-id actor-id handle prev-handle]` that publishes to the request-id index only while the slot still holds `prev-handle` (a compare-and-swap on the `[frame id]` key; a nil `prev-handle` claims the slot outright, as the 3-arity and a first attempt do). `schedule-backoff-handle!` passes its live-fetch `prev-handle`; `run-attempt!` passes `(:prev-handle handoff)`, which is nil on a first attempt. When the swap fails, a successor or an abort owns the id, and the existing shared `:aborted?` re-check finishes the cancelled predecessor. Actor / anonymous publication and the reconcile are unchanged (the reconcile retracts the actor slot of a handle the request index did not take). The `:rf.http/aborted` emit sites are untouched (sibling rf2-s8kcj).

Assertions: R2 still holds the slot; managed-abort yields exactly `[[:cancelled :user [:rf.work/http :race 2 1]]]` and no success after the latch is released; the server saw 2 hits (R1 never re-issued); the registry is clean.

Control: a one-line plant making the take-over unconditional turned the namespace red (2 failures + 2 errors, only the two new tests; 7 tests / 40 assertions); restored, the blob hash equalled the committed blob. Green: the namespace 7 / 44 / 0; the http JVM suite 530 / 4155 / 0. JVM-only race; CLJS compiles the same shared code (node lane green on 555dd7fa71).
Merged-PR audit #10320 (a102c3545b8c019ad9c30b5fa65f289f5ff6c57b; merged 2026-09-24T00:06:45Z). Completeness: All four managed HTTP runtime findings land. The acknowledged cross-family work-id table residue remains incomplete and is separately tracked as a small documentation correction. Correctness: Reviewed structured-param wire-name redaction, keyword/UUID JSON projection, predecessor-identity handoff publication and actor-counter cleanup outside the live-handle loop. Accepted HTTP 530/4155, dependent JVM suites, CLJS red/green producer pins and 59 successful CI checks; no retest. Implementation quality: Uses existing policy and indexes, narrows retry ownership atomically and reclaims counters at owner teardown. No new author API or additional runtime finding. Actionable findings: rf2-09dl5. Existing finding updates: none.

So a same-:request-id re-issue during the old request's retry handoff keeps its registration. The test (http_abort_retry_race_test.clj) issues the new request inside EACH of the two handoff windows. title: story-ui-evidence: add-expectations snippet extends the source but drops its :script/:plays (child-only), so a scripted story's regression test runs no interaction and fails on a correct app
description:
## Defect

The "add expectations..." dialog turns a story into a regression test by emitting `(reg-variant <new-id> {:extends <source> :assertions [<source's assertions + authored atoms>] :tags #{:test}})`. But under the plan compiler's merge rules `:script` and `:plays` are CHILD-ONLY ("context flows down, verdict is local"), and the snippet never copies them. So for any story whose behaviour lives in `:script`/`:plays` (a play-function story, the S5 case), the generated test runs NO interaction at all. It then checks the source's own passing assertions, plus the new ones, against the pre-interaction state. The result is a regression test that fails on a correct app, or passes vacuously when the asserted value happens to equal the pre-script state. In both cases the evidence misstates what the story does.

## Where

- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/author_expectations.cljc:468-481` (`build-snippet`, `#?(:cljs ...)`) passes `{:extends source-id :existing (existing-assertions source-id) :authored ...}`. `existing-assertions` is at `:142-152` and reads only `:assertions` / `[:expect :assertions]` off the source body.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/author_expectations.cljc:447-477` (`gen-expectations-snippet`, common code) emits only `:doc`, `:extends`, `:assertions` (merged) and `:tags #{:test}`. No `:script`/`:plays`.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/plan.cljc:218-232`: `:script` and terminal `:assertions` are taken from the child only.
- Contract: `tools/story/spec/021-Story-UI-Test-And-Evidence.md` §1a (lines 115-163). S5 is "a useful story becomes a regression test without a separate fixture". The saved expectations are "merged with the source variant's already-declared :assertions ... authored via :extends of the source".
- Entry points: the Controls panel `add expectations...` button, or the palette command `Add expectations to this story`. Either produces the snippet the author pastes.

## Failure scenario

1. Take a source variant `{:script [[:dispatch [:probe/submit]]] :assertions [[:rf.assert/path-equals [:submits] 1]]}`. It passes, with submits 1.
2. The author adds `[:rf.assert/dispatched? :probe/submit]` through the dialog and pastes the generated form.
3. The new variant compiles to `:script []`. Running it gives `:fail`:
   - "expected 1 at [:submits] but got nil" (the source's OWN assertion, copied over as passing evidence);
   - "no dispatched event matched :probe/submit".

   The author's new regression test is red on a correct app on its first run.

## Evidence

EXECUTED as a bounded JVM probe on the tools/story `:test` classpath, run in the frozen tree at `034d0c8fc8`. The tree stayed clean (`git status --porcelain` empty). The probe fed `gen-expectations-snippet` the exact arguments `build-snippet` passes, then pasted the output with `read-string` + `eval` and ran both variants:

- SOURCE `:story.probe/submitted`: status `:pass`, app-db `:submits 1`.
- SNIPPET: `(rf.story/reg-variant :story.probe/expects-1 {:extends :story.probe/submitted :assertions [[:rf.assert/path-equals [:submits] 1] [:rf.assert/dispatched? :probe/submit]] :tags #{:test}})`
- compiled source `:script` is `[[:dispatch [:probe/submit]]]`; compiled new `:script` is `[]`.
- AUTHORED run: status `:fail`, with path-equals actual `nil` and dispatched? actual `[]`.

The control is the source variant passing under the same runner.

The UI wrapper `build-snippet` is a `:cljs` branch. It was INSPECTED only, and it passes exactly the probed arguments.

Scope: scripted variants are common. In `tools/story/testbeds` there are 45 `:script`/`:plays` lines against 35 `:setup` lines. Setup-driven stories are unaffected, because `:setup` is inherited.

Dedup: rf2-uiihg (closed) made `:assertions`-only variants testable. It did not touch script inheritance. No open or closed bead covers this.

## Smallest fix

Have the snippet carry the source's behaviour. `gen-expectations-snippet` should accept the source's declared `:script`/`:plays` (read off the source body the same way `existing-assertions` does) and emit them verbatim. The generated test then replays the story and checks the expectations against its end state.

The alternative is to refuse or flag a scripted source in the dialog. That is worse for S5.

Fence:
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/author_expectations.cljc` (common);
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/author_expectations.cljc` (the `:cljs` `existing-*` reader).

No hot-zone file. The substrate file sits in the story-authoring-data slice (rf2-3x7nj.31) fence, so check there for a sibling before dispatch.

## Gates

- The substrate change is JVM-gradeable: run `clojure -M:test` in `tools/story`, adding a round-trip test that pastes and runs the snippet for a scripted source.
- The `ui/author_expectations.cljc` change sits inside `#?(:cljs ...)`, so it is compiled only by the CLJS lane (`npm run test:cljs`). A JVM green says nothing about it.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
## Fix — PR #10326 (worker story-ev-3x7nj, 2026-09-24)

The pasted test read status `:fail` with `:submits` nil, while the source passed with `:submits` 1. A `:plays` source failed the same way.
