title: Test-suite pruning, fourth pass: every unit-test surface, cut to the tests that earn their place and simplified
description:
MIKE'S INSTRUCTION (2026-10-08 17:58 AUSEST, verbatim)

"I'd like to run that EPIC again. Rerun all the children. Except tweak the prompt for the beads to even better simplify unit tests. LLMs have a tendency to create too many low value unit tests."

"That EPIC" is rf2-n6gq4 (test-suite pruning, third pass, closed 2026-10-07 with all 38 children merged). This fourth pass has the same 38 surfaces, one child each. The prompt below is the third pass's prompt, tweaked by the mayor under that instruction. What changed and why follows the prompt. Mike may reverse any of it.

== THE PROMPT

For your surface, simplify the unit tests. Do not change the code under test. LLMs tend to write too many low-value unit tests, and this suite was largely written by them.

Assume the suite has more tests than it needs, and that many of its tests are longer than they need to be. Every test costs CI time, reading time and refactoring friction, and the low-value ones hide the tests that matter. I want a lean suite: each test earns its place by guarding a behaviour a caller relies on, against a regression that could plausibly happen and would matter. Each surviving test should be as short as the thing it proves.

Work in this order:
1. Run the suite and record the result: tests, assertions, failures, lines.
2. Read the code under test and list what it promises its callers: normal results, each boundary that takes its own path, each promised failure, and any past bug the tests refer to.
3. Map every test to the promise it checks. Most of the work shows up in this map: promises with five tests, tests with no promise, and tests of something no caller relies on.
4. Decide each test: keep, simplify, merge or delete.
5. Run the suite again and prove the pruned suite still guards every promise (see "Prove it").

Decide each test with two questions:
- If this test were deleted, what bug could ship that no remaining test would catch? If you cannot name one, delete it.
- If you can name one: is that bug plausible in this code, would a caller notice it, and would nothing else surface it at once (a compile or load error, a boot-time validation, most of the suite going red)? If the bug is implausible, harmless, or loud anyway, delete the test.

Delete:
- A test another test implies. If A cannot pass while B fails, drop B.
- Extra examples of one behaviour that take the same path through the code.
- Existence and smoke checks: a function exists or is a fn, a var resolves, something "is registered", a result is non-nil, a call "does not throw", when another test exercises the same call with a real assertion.
- Change detectors: a test that copies a constant, a data table, a default config, a roster or a string out of the source and asserts equality. It fails on every intended change and catches no bug. The exception is a value callers depend on exactly, such as a public id or a documented default, that nothing else pins: keep one test for it.
- Absence checks for things nothing produces, and negative-input tests for inputs no caller passes and the contract does not mention.
- Exhaustive enumeration: one row per enum member, keyword or field when they all take one path. Keep one representative plus the members that take a different path.
- Tests of the language, a library or the framework: a constructor sets a field, a getter returns it, a map holds the key just put in it.
- Tests that pin how the code works instead of what it does: private helpers already exercised through the public path, call order, internal data shapes, greps of the implementation's own source, and log, trace or error wording that is not part of the contract.
- Tests whose expected value is computed by the same logic as the code under test.
- Assertions that a mock returned what it was told to return, and tests whose mock setup is most of the test while the assertion checks the mock.
- Separate JVM and CLJS test files asserting the same thing about platform-neutral code. A single .cljc test that runs on both platforms is one test, not two: keep it.
- Tests of test helpers and fixtures.
- Tests of code that has no logic in it, and tests whose only subject is production code that no production caller uses. List that dead code in the report.

Simplify every test you keep:
- Assert the whole result with one equality instead of one assertion per field. Drop an assertion that a later one in the same test implies, such as a map? or count check before an equality on the whole value.
- Cut setup, fixtures and data to what the assertion needs. Remove unused bindings, requires, helpers and fixtures.
- Tests that vary one input become one table-driven test. Keep the boundary rows and drop the mid-range ones.
- Tests that repeat the same setup for one assertion each become one test.
- Delete comments and docstrings that restate the code or narrate history. Keep a one-line why where a test's purpose is not obvious from its name and body.
- Rename a test only when its name no longer says what it asserts, and first check that nothing matches on the name, such as a CI filter or a skip list.

Keep, however small:
- The only test of a promise a caller relies on: a normal result, a boundary that takes a different path (empty, one, many; zero; the limit and one past it), a promised failure.
- A regression test for a bug that actually happened, unless a stronger test now covers it.
- The last guard of a security, privacy or redaction promise.
- The last test that keeps a gate able to fail, and the last test holding a published doc or spec claim to the code. For these, the "code" you break in a plant is the thing they guard: the gate, the doc sentence, the redaction.
When a weak test and a strong test overlap, keep the strong one: the one that would fail on more bugs.

Do not:
- Weaken an assertion, or swap an exact check for a looser one, to make a merge or a simplification easier.
- Delete a test because it fails, is slow or is flaky. Report it.
- Leave unused helpers, fixtures or requires behind.
- Add new tests. If you find a promise with no test, report it.
- Change production code. Report dead code and defects instead.
If anything pins test counts or names, such as a count floor or a roster, update it in the same change. Commit one file or module at a time, so each change can be reviewed against its code.

Prove it:
- The suite passes before and after. Report both sets of counts.
- For each group of deletions that rests on a surviving cover, break the code in a place the deleted tests guarded and confirm a surviving test fails. Then restore the code. One plant per group of deletions sharing a cover is enough. If nothing fails, you removed real coverage: put the tests back.
- A deletion made under the second question (implausible, harmless or loud anyway) needs no plant. Give its one-line reason in the report instead.
- A simplification must not change what a test can catch. Where you removed an assertion, name the assertion that implies it.

Report:
- Before and after: tests, assertions, lines.
- Deleted tests, grouped by reason. For each, the surviving cover, or the one-line reason it was not worth keeping.
- Merges and simplifications: what went into what, and the lines each simplified file lost.
- Notable keeps: tests you considered deleting but kept, and why.
- Plants, and which test caught each.
- Dead code found, and gaps (promises with no test). One line each, not filed.

If you are unsure whether a promise a caller relies on is still covered, keep the test and say so. Losing the only guard of a real promise is still the one mistake that matters more than leaving an extra test in. But being unsure whether a test is worth keeping is not a reason to keep it. If you cannot say in one line what plausible regression it catches that a caller would notice, delete it.

== WHAT CHANGED FROM THE THIRD PASS, AND WHY (mayor, 2026-10-08)

The third pass asked for "the smallest suite that still catches every bug the current one catches". Its children obeyed carefully, and most cut between 3 and 15 per cent of their tests, because that rule protects any test that catches anything, however trivial. Mike's instruction asks for more, so:
- The deletion question has a second half. A test that catches only an implausible, harmless or loud-anyway bug goes.
- Surviving tests are simplified, not just kept. The third pass forbade rewriting survivors for style. This pass wants shorter survivors, never weaker ones.
- The delete list names the low-value kinds LLMs generate most: existence and smoke checks, change detectors, absence and impossible-input checks, exhaustive enumeration, twin JVM and CLJS files, mock-heavy tests, tests of test helpers, and tests of dead code.
- The proof burden is lighter. One plant per group of deletions that share a cover, and none for a value judgement, which is stated in one line instead. Third-pass children spent between 15 and 80 plants each.
- "Expect less than the earlier passes found" is gone. A surface where nothing low-value remains still closes with no PR, and that is a good result. Do not manufacture removals.
Carried over unchanged: no keep-by-rule, the scope, and the repo mechanics below, except the three marked CHANGED.

== SCOPE

Unit tests only. Gate-shaped harnesses are out: e2e, acceptance, feature-matrix, live and integration harnesses, and the docs playground smoke. The three tiny surfaces the third pass left without a child (the docs pilot tests, implementation/spec-resource, and the skills/reagent-migration and skills/re-frame2 fixtures) stay out.

== REPO MECHANICS (each measured or ruled in an earlier pass)

- Step 1 also confirms that a runner executes each file in scope, and which lane: JVM `clojure -M:test`, :node-test, :browser-test, a production gate, `node --test`, `bb`, or a Python `--self-test`. A file no runner executes cannot be pruned on evidence. Report it.
- Batches. Work in small batches by contract group. Before each, predict the change in test and assertion counts from the diff. After it, run the lane and confirm the counts moved by exactly that much. The quiet reporter does not list namespaces, so the count delta is how you know your tests ran.
- Names. Before a test name leaves, search the repo for it three ways: fixed-string, whitespace-collapsed and comment-stripped. A test cited by name in a spec, a doc, another test, a workflow or a roster stays unless the citation moves in the same change. A citation in a dated, commit-pinned findings snapshot does not keep a test (the rf2-n6gq4 RULING of 2026-10-05); list such names in the PR body.
- CHANGED: cross-surface covers. A cover in another surface's files is a claim on that surface. Prefer covers inside your own files. Before deleting a test, check whether a third-pass close reason (rf2-n6gq4.1 to .38) or this epic's notes name it as another surface's cover. If one does, it stays unless you name another surviving cover and prove it with a plant. Name every cover you rely on in another surface's files in your PR body and your report, under CROSS-SURFACE COVERS. The mayor appends them to this epic's notes, so later siblings see them.
- CHANGED: count floors. Some production gates carry a test-count floor (RF2_MIN_TESTS: core, routing, ssr, epoch). Prune on evidence. Then, as the branch's last commit and in a commit of its own, lower the floor by exactly the number of tests your branch removed from that gate's lane, starting from the floor's value on trunk, and give the before and after counts in the message. Never lower a floor without deletions beside it. Several children share one floor line (the five core children share scripts/test-core-prod-gate.sh), so that line conflicts on rebase by design. On a conflict there, take trunk's value and subtract your own removal count again.
- Hot zones. Do not edit implementation/deps.edn, implementation/shadow-cljs.edn or .github/workflows/* in a pruning PR. If test wiring must change, stop and report.
- CHANGED: the shadow-cljs lane. JVM lanes run freely. CLJS counts come from your PR's CI: the whole-lane :node-test and :browser-test deltas against main's run at your merge base. A CLJS-only deletion may rest on a structural argument: a kept test drives the same code path with an equal or stronger assertion. Say "structural" and name that test. Where a CLJS plant is genuinely needed, finish everything else first, ask the coordinator for the lane once, and run all such plants in that one window. Never run a shadow-cljs build without a grant (AGENTS.md).
- Plants. Never commit or push a plant. After each, restore the file and confirm it matches the committed blob (`git diff --quiet HEAD -- <path>`).
- Parallel. Children run in parallel, because each owns one surface's test files plus at most its own gate's floor line. A child that would touch another surface's tests stops and tells the coordinator.
- One worktree and one PR per child, opened as a draft and marked ready as the last act. Production code untouched. No .beads paths and no AI attribution in commits or the PR (CLAUDE.md).
- The report goes in the PR body, with a `## Quality gates` section, and as a summary appended to the child's notes (`bd update --append-notes`, from a file, never `--notes`). The worker does not close its child; the mayor closes it when the PR merges.

== ORDER

Largest suites first: tools/xray (four children), tools/story (four), implementation/core (five), then machines, fresco, implementation/scripts, re-frame2-pair-mcp, adapters, resources, machines-viz, bench/fresco, ssr, routing, http, epoch, schemas, mcp-base, story-mcp, ssr-ring, flows, ssr-node, mcp-conformance, and the small clusters the earlier passes shipped as one PR each. Child N of this epic is the surface of rf2-n6gq4.N.

Mike, verbatim: "Monitor how sucessful each child of the EPIC is in reducing unit tests. If, say, the first 5 produce little bennefit, then abondon the EPIC. Or change the prompt used by each child."

HOW THE MAYOR APPLIES IT
- Wave one is six children: .1 (tools/xray panels/), .5 (tools/story ui/), .9 (core frames), .14 (machines), .15 (fresco), .16 (implementation/scripts). NO FURTHER CHILD IS DISPATCHED until five of them have reported. A freed slot stays empty until then; the fleet is deliberately unsaturated.
- Each child's result is scored in the SCORECARD below, from the worker's own before and after counts: tests, assertions and test-file lines, each as a percentage cut, plus the plant count and wall time from dispatch to report.
- After five reports, the mayor decides one of three things and records it here:
  (a) CONTINUE with this prompt, if the cuts are clearly larger than the third pass's (which mostly cut 3 to 15 per cent of tests) and no removal is shown to have dropped a real promise;
  (b) REVISE the prompt, if the cuts are modest but the reports show a fixable cause (workers keeping a category the prompt meant to cut, or the proof burden eating the run);
  (c) ABANDON the epic, closing the unstarted children with this note as the reason, if the cuts are little better than the third pass and nothing in the reports points to a prompt change that would help.
- "Little benefit" is judged on tests AND lines together. A child that cuts few tests but shortens many survivors is still a benefit, because simplifying survivors is half of this pass's instruction.

PROMPT v2 = this description's prompt PLUS the four additions below, which win where they differ. Each comes from a wave-one report.

3. Throughput. Work the surface in contract groups and commit as you go. If the Agent tool lets you, read-only analyst subagents speed the mapping step (xray used nine); if it refuses (a session-wide concurrency limit), work solo and do not retry. If the surface plainly will not finish in about four hours, stop at a coherent group boundary, open the PR with what is done, and list the uncovered files by name in your note, as machines did.
4. Dead code and stale spec text you find go in the report as a list, not into your PR. The mayor files them as follow-ups.

title: reagent-slim fork defects: static export diverges, FORM-3 boundary recipe never catches, dead source-coord, keyword warning
description:
## Bug reagent-slim has four defects that come from being its own renderer fork rather than from copying stock Reagent. Each makes its docs promise something the code does not do, or makes the code complain about correct code: 1. **Static HTML export is a different evaluator from the live renderer.** A Form-3 render that reads its instance throws, a frame Provider's `:value` is ignored, and every other interop subtree becomes an HTML comment. The docs promise shape parity. 2. **FORM-3.md teaches an error-boundary recipe the installed code breaks.** The guide says slim ships "logging-only" boundaries and drives the fallback from a closure atom flipped in `:component-did-catch`. The code installs `getDerivedStateFromError`, and with that installed the documented recipe does not catch at all. 3. **Native source-coord stamping is advertised but never wired.** 4. **Correct keyword props on interop heads warn** (`[:> Provider {:value :tenant/a}]`). Retiring reagent-slim is Mike's open decision. If it retires, this bead closes as moot. It is filed so the defects are not lost if slim stays. ## Evidence Trunk 475bdcaacf. Paths are under `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/`. **1. Static export** - `src/reagent2/dom/server.cljs:1313-1325`: `emit-reagent-class` calls `.-cljsReagentRender` directly, with no instance and no `*current-component*` binding. `src/reagent2/impl/component.cljs:182-189`: `state-atom` reads `(.-cljsState c)`, so `(r/state-atom (r/current-component))`, a browser-valid Form-3 render, throws a JS `TypeError` on this path. The repo's own boundary tests render exactly that shape in the browser (`test/reagent2/dom/error_boundary_dom_cljs_test.cljs:38-49`). - `src/reagent2/dom/server.cljs:1172-1199`: a context Provider is walked through but its `:value` is ignored. Its docstring says descendants resolve "through the ambient `with-frame`". So `[rf/frame-provider {:frame :b} …]` exports against the ambient frame, or fails for lack of one. Every other `:>`/`:r>`/`:f>` emits ``. - The promises: `IMPL-SPEC.md:912` ("a view that renders in the browser must render to HTML, not throw") and `DESIGN-RATIONALE.md:217` ("change the require to `reagent2.dom.server` and the rest works"). **2. Error boundaries** - `src/reagent2/impl/component.cljs:494-504`: whenever `:component-did-catch` is present, the class gets a static `getDerivedStateFromError` returning `{cljsHasError: true}`. `:520-544` bridges that marker into the public state atom. The user's render must read it, because nothing suppresses the children. - `FORM-3.md:474-504`: the worked example renders `child` unless a closure `(r/atom nil)`, set in `:component-did-catch`, is non-nil. It then says "reagent-slim ships logging-only error boundaries". - *Probed*, at the React level with a stand-in class (React 19.3.0 dev build in headless Chromium): a class with a static `getDerivedStateFromError` whose render ignores the derived state and checks a closure flag set in `componentDidCatch`, around a child that throws in render: | Boundary render reads | Result | |---|---| | the derived state | `
fallback
`; `onCaughtError: boom`, then `componentDidCatch` | | only the closure flag (FORM-3.md's recipe) | container emptied; `onUncaughtError: boom`; `componentDidCatch` never runs | The derived-state re-render renders the throwing child again, and the error escapes the boundary. **3. Source-coord stamping** - `src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs:838-845` and `:1073`: `*source-coord*` and `merge-source-coord-attr` exist, but no source anywhere binds the var (`git grep` over `implementation/` and `tools/`). Active stamping comes from core's shared walk (`core/src/re_frame/views.cljs:580-668`). - `DESIGN-RATIONALE.md:30`, `:311` and the §9-§11 tables claim "Source-coord stamping is native to the renderer". **4. Keyword-prop warning** - `src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs:427-437`: only `:class`, `:id`, `:role`, `data-*` and `aria-*` stringify keyword values. `:624-637`: any other keyword value passes through unchanged and calls `warn-once-keyword-prop!` (`:460-469`), so correct data such as a Provider's `{:value :tenant/a}` produces a console warning. The warn-once cache needs a test-fixture clear hook (`:441-458`). ## Expected slim's docs describe what the code does, the documented boundary recipe catches, and correct code produces no warning. ## Fix direction Only if slim stays: - (1) Narrow the static-export promise in IMPL-SPEC and DESIGN-RATIONALE to what the walker does. Make the unsupported shapes (an instance-reading Form-3, a Provider whose frame differs from the ambient one, an opaque interop subtree) fail with a typed error rather than an `#object` `TypeError` or a silent comment. - (2) Rewrite FORM-3.md's boundary section around the marker the code installs, which is the pattern the DOM tests verify, and delete the "logging-only" sentence and the closure-atom recipe. - (3) Delete `*source-coord*` and `merge-source-coord-attr`, or bind them from the wrapper, and correct DESIGN-RATIONALE §9-§11. - (4) Remove the keyword-prop warning, its cache and its clear hook, and explain the import-time difference once in the guide. ## Acceptance - A slim static-export test exports an instance-reading Form-3 and a distinct-frame Provider. Each either renders correctly or raises the named error; neither produces a `TypeError` or silent placeholder output. - A DOM test of FORM-3.md's boundary example, as rewritten, catches a render throw. The current text's recipe, run as written, fails that test. - `git grep '\*source-coord\*'` finds either no hits or a binder plus a test that stamps. - Rendering `[:> Provider {:value :tenant/a} …]` logs nothing, and keyword identity is preserved, as the existing conversion tests check. ## Notes - Origin: Sol review (report 20, §2, §3, §4 and §7), verified in the Opus adapters cross-review (decision 5, action 4 "if kept"). title: ssr-node admission is bounded in wait time but not queue length, contradicting its 'never a queue with no bottom' claim
description:
## Bug

ssr-node's admission is bounded in waiting time but not in queue length. Every request that finds no idle isolate is appended to `waiters` with its own timer, and each waiting request keeps its validated body (up to `maxRequestBytes`, 1 MiB by default) alive until it is served or its admission timer fires. Under a burst, retained work grows with the arrival rate. The code and README claim the opposite ("Never a queue with no bottom", "Back-pressure, not an unbounded queue"). In practice the JVM caller's own request-thread pool bounds the population, so this is a false claim plus an unguarded edge, not a measured failure.

## Evidence

- `implementation/ssr-node/src/pool.cjs:168-191` (trunk 475bdcaacf) — `acquire()`, documented "An idle isolate, or a `Refusal`. Never a queue with no bottom.", pushes every caller onto `this.waiters` with a per-caller `setTimeout(admissionTimeoutMs)`; there is no length check.
- `implementation/ssr-node/src/service.cjs:92-99` — `renderFrames` validates the request before `await this.pool.acquire()`, so each waiting generator holds its validated request.
- `implementation/ssr-node/README.md:165-168` — "Back-pressure, not an unbounded queue: a request that waits forever for capacity is a request whose outcome is being decided by the caller's timeout."
- `implementation/ssr-node/test/concurrency.test.cjs:92-104`, titled "a saturated pool REFUSES rather than queueing without a bottom", checks only that one excess request is refused once its 20 ms admission timer fires; nothing bounds the waiter count.
- *Read*, not load-tested.

## Expected

The admission contract is stated truthfully, and the waiting population has a bound the service itself enforces or explicitly delegates to its caller.

## Fix direction

Smallest: correct the `acquire()` docstring and README §3 to say waiting is bounded in time, queue length follows the arrival rate, and the caller bounds concurrency. Optionally add a fixed waiter cap (for example the pool size) that refuses `service-saturated` immediately once reached, with no new flag.

The Opus review's broader remedy (ssr-hosts A5) is to make the JVM the single owner of the admission budget: send `admissionMs` per request as `timeoutMs` already is, cap it on the sidecar, delete `--admission-ms`, and let `admissionMs 0` mean immediate refusal. That also removes the hand-matched `:admission-ms` / `--admission-ms` pair; it is a launcher-flag break and can be its own bead if wanted.

## Acceptance

- Docs-only fix: the docstring and README no longer claim a bounded queue; README link and slug checks pass (`scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci`).
- With a cap: a test that fires more concurrent requests than the cap against a busy pool sees the excess refused immediately with `service-saturated` rather than queued (fails today: all are queued until their timers fire), and `node implementation/ssr-node/test/run.cjs` passes.

## Notes

- Origin: Sol review (ssr-node §2); Opus's cross-review accepted the correction to its own wording (ssr-hosts D8, conflict C4).
- Related: the ssr-node failed-replacement bead filed in the same batch also edits `pool.cjs`; sequence the two.
- Hot zones: none.
- Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/ssr-hosts.md` D8, D11, A5; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/30-ssr-node.md` §2.
notes:
== DONE IN PR #11088 (2026-10-10 22:45 AUSEST, worker contract-truth, commit 9d3f4a8ef6) ==

Took the waiter cap, which needed no new flag. In pool.cjs acquire(), once as many callers wait as the pool has isolates (waiters.length >= size), the next caller is refused at once with :rf.ssr-node/service-saturated, detail {poolSize, waiting}. It used to be queued with its own admission timer. Waiting is therefore bounded twice: in time by the admission budget and in length by the pool size. A burst holds at most two validated requests per isolate, one rendering and one waiting. The acquire() docstring, the pool's ADMISSION header note, README section 3 and the refusal-code table now state both bounds. The old test "a saturated pool REFUSES rather than queueing without a bottom" was renamed "... once its admission budget expires", because it tests the time bound only.

Red, green, red-again: a new test in concurrency.test.cjs uses a pool of 1 with a 10 s admission budget. It holds one render, queues one waiter, then expects the third caller refused with service-saturated in under 200 ms, with waiting still 1 and the queued caller still served.
- Before the cap: concurrency.test.cjs exit 1, 5 of 6 passing. The third caller was queued and served, not refused.
- With the cap: exit 1 -> 0, 6 of 6.
- Red-again: pool.cjs alone reverted to its pre-cap blob (5482ebd5f8) gave exit 1, with the new test the only failure. Restoring from HEAD gave a blob hash matching HEAD's pool.cjs blob a98632109f.
Existing tests queue at most pool-size waiters (the 2N-on-N test queues exactly N), so none changed behaviour.
Gate: node implementation/ssr-node/test/run.cjs exit 0, 9 suites. scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci exit 0 (a planted broken link in README section 3 went red, exit 1, restored by blob hash).
The broader remedy (the JVM owns the admission budget per request, --admission-ms deleted) is not done. One line on it: it would remove the hand-matched :admission-ms / --admission-ms pair, but it breaks a launcher flag, and the cap already closes the unbounded edge, so it only earns a bead if that pair causes drift.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #11088, merged at 1c303f639c (2026-10-10 AUSEST). The waiter cap was taken: once as many callers are waiting as the pool has isolates, the next one is refused immediately with service-saturated. It is about six lines in pool.cjs, with no new flag. The acquire() docstring, the pool header, README §3 and the refusal-code table now state both bounds, wait time and queue length. The new concurrency test went red at base, green with the fix, and red again with pool.cjs reverted alone; the restore was verified by blob hash. ssr-node run.cjs (9 suites) exit 0; check_readme_links --ci exit 0; CI 88/88. The broader "JVM owns the admission budget" remedy is not taken: it is not wanted unless the hand-matched :admission-ms / --admission-ms pair drifts, and it would break a launcher flag.

title: re-frame2-pair-mcp: delete the dormant response-cache precheck path end to end (server step, preload per-epoch app-db hash, :via marker slot, wire-vocab fixtures, spec text)
description:
DECISION FOR MIKE. Should re-frame2-pair-mcp's dormant response-cache PRECHECK path be deleted end to end?

WHAT IS TRUE NOW (rf2-wzo45, PR #11005, merged 2026-10-08 at 477be3a947): precheck-target returns nil for every tool on purpose, so the :precheck cache-hit route never fires. Evidence: tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec Principles.md, Per-session response cache, "Precheck eligibility": no tool qualifies, because every read goes through project-egress, whose redaction rules live outside app-db, so an app-db hash cannot see a redaction change; a precheck hit could serve a stale, differently redacted payload. Two invoke_test tests pin it inert: precheck-target-get-path-is-ineligible and single-frame-appdb-only-snapshot-no-longer-precheck-hits. Commit 62a10dcf36 removed the last eligible case. CONTROL: with precheck-target forced eligible, both pins go red (3 of 3 assertions), and one failure shows a :via :precheck hit served beside a differently egressed payload. The spec text now says :precheck is reserved and every hit is :result-hash.

THE COST OF KEEPING IT: the preload keeps a per-frame app-db hash cache that exists only for this path, so it hashes app-db on every mutation in the user's running app, for a route that never fires.

THE WORKER'S RECOMMENDATION: delete the dormant path end to end, including the preload's per-frame hash cache, the :precheck reservation and the two pin tests, and say in Principles.md that every hit is :result-hash. It deleted nothing, because Principles.md keeps the path deliberately and no tracker ruling abandons it. rf2-wzo45's notes lay out the deletion scope.

MAYOR'S READ: under the stance (elegance, no gold plating, low friction), a dead route that costs a hash per mutation in the user's app is worth deleting. But Principles.md chose to keep it, so the call is yours. If you say delete, this becomes a normal P2 implementation bead for tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp, touching spec/Tool-Pair.md (hot zone).
notes:
== RULING (delegated by Mike; decided 2026-10-10 23:51:23 AUSEST at HEAD 57b1acab35) ==

DECISION: Delete re-frame2-pair-mcp's response-cache PRECHECK path end to end (option A). That covers the server step, `cache/precheck`, the `:precheck-hash` storage and `tools/precheck.cljs`; the preload's per-epoch app-db hash cache and its `app-db-hash` accessor; the `:precheck` wire value and its conformance fixtures; and the spec sentence that keeps the path "as infrastructure for a future tool". SUB-CHOICE: drop the `:via` slot from the `:rf.mcp/cache-hit` marker entirely, so the marker becomes `{:hash :unchanged-since :tool :hint}`. The cacheable-tool list and the operating-frame cache flush keep their behaviour. Only their stated reasons change.

WHY:
- The path has been dead since commit 62a10dcf36 (2026-07-08). `precheck-target` is `(case tool nil)`, so no tool can reach it. What keeps it is one sentence in Principles.md that a worker wrote in that fix commit. It is not a recorded ruling, and no Mike or mayor ruling keeps the path.
- It is not free. Once the pair attaches, the preload runs `(hash db-after)` on every settled epoch in the developer's running app, whether or not the cache flag is on, and the dead path is the only reader of that hash.
- Its prose misleads the code's readers and the AI pair. The instructions text the AI reads puts "precheck cache" first in the pipeline.
- Reviving it for any tool whose output goes through egress would break Tool-Pair's stated cache privacy guarantee. rf2-wzo45's control showed exactly that: a `:via :precheck` hit served beside a differently egressed payload.
- Under the stance, plumbing kept for a hypothetical tool is gold plating, and trusting the programmer means git history holds the design if anyone ever wants it.
- The justification is that nothing uses the path now, not a proof that no use could ever exist (Codex's qualification, accepted). A future tool that is pure over app-db and does not go through egress is conceivable. If one appears, it builds a hash over all of its inputs, starting from the design in history.
- WHY DROP `:via`:
  - With one hit path left, `:via` is a discriminator with one value forever. Describing it in present tense means explaining a slot by a path that no longer exists. That is the same "kept for a second path" reasoning this ruling rejects for the precheck itself.
  - The AI-facing docs already omit it: `skills/re-frame2-pair/references/wire-size-budget.md` (the line 71 `cache` row and the line 112 marker list), and mcp-base's cross-MCP vocabulary (the `cache-hit-key` docstring in `vocab.cljc` and the `spec/vocab.md` row). Dropping it makes the server match what the AI is already taught.
  - No production code reads `:via`. Its only consumers are tests, the wire-vocab schema, spec prose and one descriptor example.
  - The extra cost inside this PR is small: one descriptor example string and a regenerated `tool-descriptors.edn`. The `tool-contract` fingerprint does not move, because `registry.cljs` `contract-fingerprint` is built from tool names and argument keys only.

REJECTED:
- B (keep the server plumbing, compute `app-db-hash` on demand, stop the per-epoch hashing). It removes the app cost, but it keeps an unreachable pipeline step, a second cache model in the docs, and a reserved enum value, all for a tool nothing needs.
- C (fix the stale text only). Honest, but every attached app keeps paying a per-epoch hash for nothing.
- D (make the precheck sound by hashing every egress input: app-db, the runtime-db elision and sensitive registries, the egress profile, the per-call `include-sensitive` gate, and for `snapshot` also machines, sub-cache, epochs and traces). That is new design and new correctness risk. The saving applies only to opt-in repeat reads, it still costs one round trip to fetch the hash, and it saves no tokens beyond what `:result-hash` already saves. No latency need has been measured.
- Keeping `:via :result-hash` (both reviews' sub-choice). Their objections are real but small: an AI-facing descriptor edit and a wire-shape change, at pre-alpha, with no reader of the field. See WHY.
- Widening the cacheable list, or removing the operating-frame flush. Out of scope, and no bead is filed (see PRESERVED ANALYSIS).

WHERE THE REVIEWS AGREED / DISAGREED:
- They agreed on option A and on the facts:
  - the path is dead;
  - the preload hashes on every epoch, cache on or off;
  - the epoch listener stays, because it also drives pair-epoch attribution;
  - the cacheable list stays as it is;
  - the cache_test tests that use `cache/precheck` as a probe get re-instrumented, not dropped.
- They disagreed on FRAMING. The dossier author said no future eligible tool can exist; Codex said the contract shows only that today's candidates are unsuitable. Settled for Codex: deletion rests on there being no present use, which is enough.
- The dossier's benchmark was not reproduced by Codex. It is not load-bearing: the ruling needs only that the hashing happens and serves nothing, and both reviewers verified that by reading the code.
- SUB-CHOICE: both reviews said keep `:via`. This ruling drops it, overriding both, for the reasons in WHY.
- ADDED BY THIS RULING, all verified at HEAD:
  - the `wire_vocab_test` vacuous-row trap (probe below);
  - the instructions-line ordering trap;
  - stale reasoning in places neither review listed: the operating-frame flush comments, the `cache-key` docstring, the `get-operating-frame` reasoning in registry.cljs, Principles.md and 003, the preload listener comments, `pure.cljc`, `test/README.md`, `live-fresco-wire.cjs`, 000-Vision, and mcp-base vocab's `:digest`.

EVIDENCE (HEAD 57b1acab35; none of the cited files changed since the dossier's reads at 2fdf565945 and 3ae452324e):
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/precheck.cljs:20-31`: `(defn precheck-target [tool _raw-args] (case tool nil))`. Its only call into the preload is line 48, `(ef/emit (ef/rt-call 'app-db-hash frame))`. A repo-wide search finds no other reader of `app-db-hash`.

  - The pipeline at `tools.cljs:309-323` is: `:canonicalize-build`, `:precheck`, `:dispatch` (`:skip-when? (some? result)`), `:apply-cache`, `:apply-cap`.
  - The context starts with `:result nil` (`tools.cljs:450`), so only a precheck hit could make `:dispatch` skip.

  - Lines 1302-1332 hold the `frame-db-hashes` atom, `update-frame-db-hash!` (`(swap! frame-db-hashes assoc frame-id (hash db-after))`) and `app-db-hash`.
  - `on-epoch-settled` (1527-1537) calls `update-frame-db-hash!` for every record carrying `:frame`, then `attribute-pair-epoch!`.

  - Tests: `cache_test.cljs:51`, `invoke_test.cljs:48`, `wire_cap_test.cljs:78`, `structured_content_test.cljs:48`.

title: UIx hydrate parity: :identifier-prefix ignored, a sibling window closer shifts useId, and stale hydration text
description:
Found by the rf2-mn2ht.44 worker (PR #11072, merged at ef96089c07). These are CLAIMS: re-check each at tip.

PR #11072 made Reagent and reagent-slim hydration honour the host's root options. Hydrating roots there now report mismatches, call :on-recoverable-error and take :identifier-prefix. The window closer also WRAPS the tree instead of sitting beside it as a sibling, because a sibling shifts React's useId values (probed on React 19.3). The UIx adapter was outside that fence:
- The UIx hydrate path ignores :identifier-prefix.
- Its window closer probably sits beside the tree as a sibling, so it shifts UIx useId values the same way. Verify this with a probe before changing it.
- Stale hydration text: the uix.cljs render! docstring, docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md, docs/ssr/concepts.md, and the SSR tutorial page under docs/.

Fix direction: mirror what PR #11072 did for the Reagent adapters (read its diff in spine.cljs and the two adapters), within implementation/adapters/uix. Then make the four texts say what every React-family root now does. A DOM test that is red at base and green after, plus red-again with the src reverted alone.

Gates: CLJS browser lane (DOM tests) via CI; check_doc_slugs.py and mkdocs build --strict for docs.
notes:
== WORKER SUMMARY (ssr-uix, 2026-10-10 AUSEST) ==
CODE HALF NOT DONE. The fix needs a new edit to `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs`, which the dispatch fenced off: the substrate worker holds that file. The stale text is corrected in PR #11093, commit 9a3e5a2241 on branch worker/ssr-uix, based on trunk 10680b13ed.

THE PROBE. React 19.3.0's `react-dom/server` `renderToString` ran under identifierPrefix `rf-pfx-`. The tree was `[section [h2] probe]`, where `probe` reads `useId`. Server and client share the useId tree-position algorithm, so the id the server gives each wrapping is the id a client hydrating that wrapping computes.

    _rf-pfx-R_2_  the bare tree, which is what a host renders on the server
    _rf-pfx-R_b_  the spine today, reporter installed: Fragment[sentinel, closer, tree]
    _rf-pfx-R_b_  the spine today, no reporter: Fragment[sentinel, nil, tree]
    _rf-pfx-R_a_  #11072's shape on this spine: Fragment[sentinel, closer(tree)]
    _rf-pfx-R_2_  closer(tree)
    _rf-pfx-R_9_  Fragment[closer(tree), sentinel]
    _rf-pfx-R_2_  sentinel(closer(tree))

WHAT IT SHOWS:
- The premise holds, and it goes further than the bead says. The window closer is not the only cause of the useId shift. The after-render sentinel, the first child of the Fragment that `make-mount-client-root!` builds, is also a sibling ahead of the tree.
- So the ids move even with no reporter installed, which is the production posture when there is no host callback.
- Mirroring #11072, with the closer wrapping the tree, still moves them (`R_a`). Only a single-child chain restores parity: the sentinel and the closer each render their children, wrapping the tree.

WHY IT CANNOT BE FIXED IN THE ADAPTER:
- `:identifier-prefix` is never read. `make-mount-client-root!` builds the root options from `hydrate-root-options` alone.
- Both fixes belong in `spine.cljs`: in `make-mount-client-root!`, and in `make-after-render-sentinel`, whose component renders nil.
- UIx is the only consumer of `make-react-spine`, and implementation/adapters/uix has no mount code of its own. Fixing it there would duplicate the spine's mount path.
- #11072's spine change covered `make-ratom-spine` only.
- Before the sentinel becomes a wrapper, check that it still drains the after-render queue on every commit and that its own tick re-render still works. It also mounts in the after-render driver root.

TEXT CORRECTED NOW (true at tip):
- The uix `render!` docstring, the client-root comment and `docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md` said the Reagent adapters hydrate without root options. They now give the real difference: a hydrating UIx `render!` takes no `:identifier-prefix`.
- `docs/ssr/concepts.md`'s substrate table and `docs/ssr/tutorial.md`'s Native UIx section now give Reagent and reagent-slim adoption beside the hash, and name the client root's `render!` as a hydrate door.
- When the spine fix lands, its follow-up drops the `:identifier-prefix` exception from `uix.cljs` and from the API page.

SUGGESTED RED-AT-BASE DOM TEST FOR THE FOLLOW-UP: mirror the `hydrated-root-carries-prefix-closes-its-window-and-stays-live` row of `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/adapter_hydrate_root_options_dom_cljs_test.cljs` through `uix-adapter/render!`, with a server `renderToString` of the bare element under identifierPrefix.

PR #11093 (ssr-uix) did .68's text half only. The code half is both changes in implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs, which the substrate worker holds:
- make-mount-client-root! should pass :identifier-prefix to React and wrap the tree, instead of placing the sentinel and closer beside it;

The ssr-uix worker probed this on React 19.3. The UIx hydrate wrap moves useId even with no closer, because the after-render sentinel is also a sibling ahead of the tree. Only a chain where BOTH the sentinel and the closer wrap the tree matches the server. Its notes above carry the probe table and a suggested red-at-base DOM test. Once the code lands, drop the :identifier-prefix exception from uix.cljs and docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md. Released by: PR #11096 merged. Do NOT close this bead when #11093 merges.

title: perf gate never checks performance.mark, and the no-marks / clear-after-emit tests run with the flag off in every lane
description:
## Bug

Spec 009's performance contract makes two promises:
- the bracket allocates no `performance.mark` entries, so neither advanced bundle may contain `performance.mark`;
- each bracket clears its measure after emit, so the User-Timing buffer stays bounded.

Nothing grades either promise:
- `check-perf-bundle.cjs` never looks for `performance.mark`.
- The two runtime tests for "no marks" and "clear after emit" are guarded by `(when enabled? …)`, and no lane compiles their namespace with the flag on. They pass with zero assertions everywhere.

So a change that adds a mark per bracket, or drops the clear, ships green. Dropping the clear lets the buffer grow without bound in a long-running production RUM session.

## Evidence

All file:line references are at trunk 475bdcaacf (unchanged at b375cd0e42).

- **Contract.**
  - `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1543`: the off bundle "MUST NOT contain `performance.measure`, `clearMeasures`, or any `"rf:` entry-name fragment (and — since the bracket allocates no marks — MUST NOT contain `performance.mark` either, in *both* bundles)".
  - `:1482`: "No `performance.mark` entries are allocated".
  - §"Why clear after emit": the host buffer is unbounded (`maxBufferSize` Infinite), so re-frame2 clears each measure.
- **Bundle gate** (`implementation/scripts/check-perf-bundle.cjs`, *read*):
  - The header (`:29-31`) repeats that `performance.mark` "must be ABSENT from BOTH bundles".
  - `PERF_SENTINELS` (`:59-66`) holds `performance.measure`, `clearMeasures` and `"rf:`.
  - The count scan (`:149-151`) holds `performance\.measure`, `clearMeasures` and `re-frame\.performance`.
  - `performance.mark` occurs in the file only in the header comments (`:11`, `:29`).
- **Runtime tests** (`implementation/core/test/re_frame/performance_cljs_test.cljs:41-56`, *read*):
  - `mark-and-measure-clears-after-emit-when-enabled` and `mark-and-measure-allocates-no-marks-when-enabled` each wrap their only `is` in `(when (and rf.performance/enabled? …))`.
  - The namespace runs in `:node-test` (`implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:676`, `"cljs-test$"`), which leaves `enabled?` at its false default.
  - `:node-test-perf-nightly` (`:763-784`) sets `enabled? true`, but it selects only `-emit-nightly-test$` and sets `retain-entries? true`, which suppresses the clear.
  - The test's docstring (`:6-8`) and `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1548` both admit it: "no lane compiles that namespace with it on, so no test grades the observer-first contract."
- **Effect of adding the check.** The perf-off bundle on disk in the primary checkout (`implementation/out/examples/counter/main.js`, built 2026-07-29) contains 0 occurrences of `performance.mark`, so an absence check is not expected to red the off side. The on side (`out/examples/counter-perf`) was not available; one release build confirms that no third-party code contributes the string.

## Expected

A `performance.mark` call in either bundle turns `npm run test:perf-bundle` red. A bracket that stops clearing its measure, or starts allocating marks, turns a runtime test red in some lane.

## Fix direction

- **(a)** In `check-perf-bundle.cjs`, add `performance.mark` as an always-absent check over **both** bundles. It must not go into `PERF_SENTINELS`, whose entries must be present in the on bundle.
- **(b)** Make the two guarded assertions run. Either:
  - add one small node-test build (`enabled? true`, `retain-entries? false`) that selects `re-frame.performance-cljs-test`; or
  - delete the two guarded tests and reword Spec 009:1548 to say the contract is graded statically only.

  Choosing between these is Mike's call. The build costs a hot-zone edit plus CI scheduling; deleting costs the runtime evidence.
- (a) alone is a one-line, no-risk change and can land first.

## Acceptance

- A `(.mark js/performance "x")` planted on the perf-on bracket path reds `check-perf-bundle.cjs`, and so does one planted in the off bundle. Removing the plant returns it to green.
- If (b) keeps the tests: removing the `clearMeasures` call in `re-frame.performance` reds `mark-and-measure-clears-after-emit-when-enabled` in its lane, and that namespace's executed assertion count is non-zero.

## Notes

- **Origin:** Sol review (surface 34, insight 2), adopted by the Opus tooling cross-review (Insight 3, action 2b).
- **Related:** rf2-qyw01 (closed) corrected a docs page that claimed the channel makes `performance.mark` calls; the gate gap remained.
- **Hot-zone files:** none for (a). (b) touches `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` and possibly `.github/workflows/test.yml` if it adds a build, or `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` if it deletes the tests. All three are hot-zone, so sequence (b).
- **Supporting detail:** `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/tooling.md` Insight 3; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/34-build-verification.md` §2.
notes:
== RULING (delegated by Mike; decided 2026-10-11 00:03:00 AUSEST at HEAD f678139da9) ==
DECISION: Part (b): run the contract, don't delete it. Replace the two flag-guarded tests in `re-frame.performance-cljs-test` with ONE unguarded test in the existing per-PR `:node-test` lane. It rebinds `enabled?` true and `retain-entries?` false with `with-redefs`, attaches a `PerformanceObserver` on `mark`+`measure` before 25 brackets, and asserts three things: the observer received all 25 measures (`takeRecords()`, the positive control), the retained buffer holds none of them (clear after emit), and no mark of any name was allocated. No new build, npm script, workflow step or lane. Then reword Spec 009:1548 and the three code comments that cite the tests.
PART (a) IS DONE, NOT RULED HERE: `check-perf-bundle.cjs` refusing `performance.mark` in both bundles is commit 29b83b2f10 "fix(perf-bundle): refuse performance.mark in either bundle" in PR #11100 (branch worker/build-config, worktree re-frame2-worktrees/build-config). `gh pr view 11100 --json state,mergedAt` read state OPEN, mergedAt null at 2026-10-11 00:02 AUSEST. The same PR carries rf2-mn2ht.64 (`:warnings-as-errors` for the `:node-test` family), and its commit message says part (b) "is left open". This ruling is that part.

WHY: Under the stance, this is the elegant option. It gives the runtime evidence Spec 009 wants on every PR that touches core, for one test of about 20 lines and no extra machinery. The bead framed (b) as "add a build or delete" because a flag-on run looked as if it needed a build. In the unoptimised node-test lane it doesn't: the goog-define compiles to a plain property that is read at call time, and the probe below shows `with-redefs` flips it, takes effect and restores it. It compiles with zero CLJS warnings, so it is safe under #11100's `:warnings-as-errors`. Deleting (B) would leave a gap for good: a clear that is present in the bundle but doesn't empty the buffer (wrong name, or run before the measure). That class can be caught cheaply, and nothing else catches it. A dedicated build (A) is gold plating for three assertions.

REJECTED:
- A (add a flag-on node-test build `:node-test-perf-on`): it means two or three hot-zone edits (shadow-cljs.edn plus a workflow step, and a new job key would move the check band), plus one more shadow-cljs compile and scheduling (`check_gate_scheduling.py`). Even then the tests would still need a positive control, and the cheapest one is the same runtime flip that C uses. It is the most machinery for the least gain, and nightly scheduling would report a regression the next morning rather than on the PR.
- B (delete the two tests and say Spec 009 grades statically only): honest, and the smallest diff. But it permanently gives up the one class only a runtime test catches. It was the right fallback only if the runtime flip didn't take. The probe shows that it does.
- The dossier's variant of C (bare `set!` in try/finally, with a positive control that toggles `retain-entries?` true and counts 25 buffered entries): it works (probe line 4), but the Codex variant is better on both counts. `with-redefs` is the idiomatic scoped form and restores the flags in its own `finally`. The observer control tests the production configuration (retention OFF throughout) and the observer-first promise itself. It also catches marks that are cleared at once or that lack the `rf:` prefix, which the old `count-rf-marks` helper (buffered `rf:` marks only) misses.
- Codex's fallback (extend the nightly emit namespace): moot. It would rely on the same runtime flip, because that build sets `retain-entries? true` at compile time.

WHERE THE REVIEWS AGREED / DISAGREED:
- Both chose C, and both agreed (a) is a no-risk change that lands first (it now has, in #11100). Both agreed the bead's "drops the clear, ships green" is false at HEAD (see EVIDENCE).
- Mechanism: the dossier proposed `set!`, Codex `with-redefs`. Settled by probe: both compile with 0 CLJS warnings and both take effect at runtime. `with-redefs` was chosen for scoping. Codex's "precedent" was only approximate: `image_inline_metadata_normalization_cljs_test.cljc:49,59` does `with-redefs [rf.interop/debug-enabled? false]`, but `debug-enabled?` is a plain `def` of `goog/DEBUG` (`interop.cljs:216`), not a `goog-define` var. performance.cljc holds the only `goog-define`s under implementation/*/src. So the probe, not the precedent, is the evidence.
- Positive control: the dossier toggled `retain-entries?` true and counted buffered entries; Codex used `takeRecords()` with retention off throughout. Codex's version was adopted (see REJECTED). The dossier's note that observer callbacks run later as a queued task is correct, but it doesn't apply to `takeRecords()`, which reads the observer's buffer synchronously (W3C Performance Timeline 5.3/6.1; Node 24 documents it). The probe confirms 25 observed synchronously.
- Fallback: dossier B, Codex extend-nightly. Moot, as above. If the in-lane run nonetheless shows the flip not taking (not expected), take B, not A.

EVIDENCE (HEAD f678139da9 unless noted):
- The tests are vacuous today. `implementation/core/test/re_frame/performance_cljs_test.cljs:41-56`: `mark-and-measure-clears-after-emit-when-enabled` wraps its only `is` in `(when (and rf.performance/enabled? (not rf.performance/retain-entries?)) ...)`, and `mark-and-measure-allocates-no-marks-when-enabled` wraps its only `is` in `(when rf.performance/enabled? ...)`. The namespace runs in `:node-test` (`implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:674`, `:ns-regexp "cljs-test$"`, no closure-defines), so the flag is off and both execute 0 assertions. `:node-test-perf-nightly` (`:764`) selects only `-emit-nightly-test$` and sets `retain-entries? true` (`:782-783`), so it cannot see the clear.
- The macro (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/performance.cljc`): `(goog-define ^boolean enabled? false)` at :77 and `(goog-define ^boolean retain-entries? false)` at :100. The CLJS expansion (:198-219) is `(if re-frame.performance/enabled? (let [nm (build-name ..) start (.now js/performance)] (try body (finally (try (.measure js/performance nm (js-obj "start" start "end" (.now js/performance))) (when-not re-frame.performance/retain-entries? (.clearMeasures js/performance nm)) (catch :default _ nil))))) (do body))`. Errors from measure/clear are swallowed.
- The bead's "or drops the clear, ships green" is FALSE at HEAD. `check-perf-bundle.cjs` `PERF_SENTINELS` includes `clearMeasures` and checks it with mustContain=true on the perf-on bundle (`checkBundle(... onDir, true)`). `:examples/counter-perf` sets only `enabled? true` (`shadow-cljs.edn:1350`), so retention is off, and deleting the clear or inverting its guard folds the string out under `:advanced`. Either change reds `npm run test:perf-bundle` today. "Adds a mark per bracket, ships green" was true until #11100.
- What only a runtime test catches, given (a): a clear that is present but ineffective (wrong name, or ordered before the measure), and a measure that throws under the flag and is swallowed (the bracket goes silent; both old zero-count assertions would still pass). The dossier's host probe (Node v24.13.0, exit 0, no build): clear by WRONG name left 25 retained against 0 with the right name; `performance.measure` with start+end+duration throws TypeError; an observer after a task received 25/25/25 across retain/clear/wrong-name. Codex's host probe (Node v24.13.0, exit 0) via `takeRecords()`: right-name clear observed 25, retained 0, marks 0; wrong name 25/25/0; emit nothing 0/0/0; an unprefixed mark per iteration 25/0/25.
- RULING PROBE 1: the real macro, plain CLJS 1.12.145, `:optimizations :none`, `:target :nodejs`. The probe namespace `probe.flag` requires `re-frame.performance` from `implementation/core/src` and defines `observe-run`: `new PerformanceObserver(noop)`, `.observe #js {:entryTypes #js ["mark" "measure"]}`, 25 x `(rf.performance/mark-and-measure :test id :ok)`, `.takeRecords`, then it counts observed measures named `rf:test:<id>`, observed marks of any name, and buffered `getEntriesByType("measure")` entries of that name, and `.disconnect`s in a `finally`. Command: `cd implementation/core && clojure -M <scratch>/build_probe.clj none` (cljs.build.api/build with a warning handler). Exit 0, `BUILD DONE mode :none cljs warnings: 0 []`. `node <scratch>/probe-out-none/run.js` exit 0:
    default flags enabled?/retain?: false false
    1 flag off (default): {:observed-measures 0, :observed-marks 0, :buffered 0}
    2 with-redefs enabled? true, retain false: {:observed-measures 25, :observed-marks 0, :buffered 0}
    3 after with-redefs, enabled?: false
    4 set! in try/finally, retain true: {:observed-measures 25, :observed-marks 0, :buffered 25}
    5 after set!, enabled?/retain?: false false
    6 flag off again: {:observed-measures 0, :observed-marks 0, :buffered 0}
  Emitted JS: `re_frame.performance.enabled_QMARK_ = goog.define("re_frame.performance.enabled_QMARK_",false);` and, at the call site, `if(re_frame.performance.enabled_QMARK_){`. The `with-redefs` compiles to `(re_frame.performance.enabled_QMARK_ = ..._temp_val__530)`, restored in `finally`.
- RULING PROBE 2: the same source under `:advanced`. `clojure -Sdeps '{:paths ["src" "<scratch>/probe-src"]}' -M <scratch>/build_probe.clj advanced` exit 1, 8 Closure errors, the first: `ERROR - [JSC_NON_CONST_DEFINE] @define re_frame.performance.enabled_QMARK_ has already been set at .../re_frame/performance.js:9:21.` Closure REFUSES to compile a reassigned @define. So this approach is valid only in `:none` lanes, and it fails closed: an optimised lane that ever selects this namespace goes red at compile time rather than passing vacuously.
- No optimised lane selects the namespace today. Every build matching `cljs-test$` is a `:node-test` target compiled with `shadow-cljs compile` (`compile-node-test.cjs`). The `:fresco-release` comment (shadow-cljs.edn ~944) states that `:node-test`, `:browser-test` and the bench lane are all `:none`. No `package.json` script runs `shadow-cljs release` on a node-test build.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE:
- The test (`implementation/core/test/re_frame/performance_cljs_test.cljs`, not hot): delete the two guarded deftests and the `count-rf-marks` helper, keep `build-name-shape`, `count-measures` and `clear-measures!`, and add roughly:
    (deftest mark-and-measure-observer-first-when-enabled
      (testing "flag on, retention off: an observer receives every measure, the retained buffer stays empty, and no mark is allocated"
        (let [nm  (rf.performance/build-name :test :observer-first)
              obs (js/PerformanceObserver. (fn [_ _]))]
          (clear-measures!)
          (.observe obs #js {:entryTypes #js ["mark" "measure"]})
          (try
            (with-redefs [rf.performance/enabled?        true
                          rf.performance/retain-entries? false]
              (dotimes [_ 25] (rf.performance/mark-and-measure :test :observer-first :ok)))
            (let [recs (.takeRecords obs)]
              (is (= 25 (count (filter #(and (= "measure" (.-entryType %)) (= nm (.-name %))) recs))) "every bracket emitted a measure")
              (is (zero? (count-measures nm)) "each measure was cleared after emit")
              (is (zero? (count (filter #(= "mark" (.-entryType %)) recs))) "no mark of any name was allocated"))
            (finally (.disconnect obs) (clear-measures!))))))
  The callback must stay a no-op: Node may still dispatch its scheduled callback after `takeRecords`. Rewrite the ns docstring present-tense: the flags are rebound for one test with `with-redefs`, which works because the `:node-test` builds compile `:none`. Closure rejects reassigning a @define (JSC_NON_CONST_DEFINE), so an optimised lane selecting this namespace fails to compile.
- Prose (present tense, no provenance):
  - `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1548` (HOT; free per the mayor at 2026-10-11 00:0x): say the namespace grades the observer-first contract in the per-PR `:node-test` lane, rebinding `enabled?` on and `retain-entries?` off for one test, and asserting that an observer receives every measure (`takeRecords()`), that the retained buffer is empty afterwards (clear after emit), and that no mark entry of any name is allocated. Keep the sentence on the nightly emit test, dropping its "either".
  - `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:780-781` (HOT, `;; re-frame.performance-cljs-test carries those assertions, guarded / ;; by the flag, and no lane compiles it with the flag on.`; at :792 on #11100's branch): say that namespace grades clear-after-emit in the per-PR `:node-test` lane by rebinding both flags for one test. SEQUENCE AFTER PR #11100 MERGES: that PR holds shadow-cljs.edn and the shadow-cljs lane, and rewrites the file by about 79 lines. Rebase on its merge before editing.
  - `implementation/core/test/re_frame/performance_emit_nightly_test.cljs:70-72`: replace "the assertions for it in `re-frame.performance-cljs-test` are guarded off in the flag-off lane that runs that namespace" with a pointer to the per-PR test. The neighbouring sentence (:68-70), that "a synchronous PerformanceObserver read is unreliable on the node runner (the callback runs later, as a queued task)", is imprecise, because `takeRecords()` is synchronous. Reword it to "the observer callback runs later, as a queued task" or leave it. Don't change the nightly runner itself.
  - `bench/fresco/src/re_frame/bench/fresco/arm1/render_measure_emit_nightly_test.cljs:26`: "is asserted in `re-frame.performance-cljs-test`" becomes TRUE under this ruling. Leave it, and confirm it reads true.
  - `tools/story/spec/Migration-Audit.md` cites only `build-name-shape` and a resolved item. Leave it.
- Failing-first, by planting in `performance.cljc` with the lane granted. Each plant must red exactly the named assertion, and reverting it returns green:
  1. Clear by a wrong name (`(.clearMeasures js/performance (str nm# "x"))`): "cleared after emit" goes red while `npm run test:perf-bundle` stays green. This is the coverage nothing else gives.
  2. Remove `rf.performance/enabled?` from the `with-redefs`: the positive control goes red. This proves the flip is what makes the test live.
  3. Add `(.mark js/performance "x")` (unprefixed) beside the measure: "no mark" goes red.
  4. Add `"duration" 1` to the options bag (TypeError, swallowed): the positive control goes red.
  Also, per the bead's acceptance: deleting the `clearMeasures` call reds "cleared after emit".
- Gates:
  - `npm run test:cljs`, and then `npm run test:cljs-isolation`, both needing a build-lane grant. Instrument (z): a green log won't name the namespace, so predict the delta and compare it with a merge-base baseline. Expect tests -1 (two deftests become one) and assertions +3 (this namespace executes 2 today, from `build-name-shape`, and 5 after).
  - clj-kondo on the test file.
  - For Spec 009: `mkdocs build --strict` and `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`.
  - The bench and nightly-test comment edits have no gate; check them by hand.
- Interaction with #11100: it turns on `:warnings-as-errors` for the `:node-test` family. Probe 1 measured 0 CLJS analyzer warnings for `with-redefs` and `set!` on these goog-defines, so the test compiles under it. The final proof is the lane run.
- Close rf2-mn2ht.57 once (b) merges. Part (a) rides #11100. No other bead depends on this one.

PRESERVED ANALYSIS:
- Coverage after both parts:
  - (a) catches a mark pair returning to the bracket, in either bundle.
  - The existing `clearMeasures` must-contain check catches a deleted clear or an inverted guard.
  - The runtime test catches a present-but-ineffective clear, a silently throwing measure, marks of any name (even ones cleared at once), and a flag that stops taking at runtime in this lane: the positive control goes red, so the test cannot pass vacuously.
- Leak risk if the flag stayed on: brackets would run in every later namespace of the consolidated `:node-test` bundle. `with-redefs` restores the flag in `finally`, the test is synchronous (`with-redefs` is unsafe across async boundaries, so keep it synchronous), and `test:cljs-isolation` runs the namespace alone.
- Why per-PR is fine: the nightly build's reason for running nightly ("Perf-timing assertions are noisy under per-PR CI runners", shadow-cljs.edn ~749) is about timing. These assertions count entries (25 against 0) and read no durations.
- Who is affected: an app opting into `enabled? true` for production RUM with `retain-entries?` off, the documented setting. A broken clear means the tab's User-Timing buffer grows for its whole life (W3C `maxBufferSize` is Infinite for measures): a silent leak with no error. The feature is opt-in and pre-alpha, and the residual class is narrow, so P3 stands.
- The bigger everyday cost was misleading coverage. title: Spec 016's frame-qualified request-id rationale says the managed-HTTP registry is process-global; it is frame-scoped, and the surviving reason is the any-frame teardown abort
description:
Follow-up to rf2-q02oa (PR #11140), found by its worker. Spec 016 gives the same two-premise rationale for the frame-qualified transport request-id that #11140 corrected in the resources docstrings, and premise (a) is false.

At 87ecb30b5f, spec/016-Resources.md:
- line 73: "the transport request-id the runtime hands a process-global transport registry includes the issuing frame id";
- line 568 (Ledger row retention and identity): "the managed-HTTP in-flight registry keys by :request-id process-globally and supersedes/aborts by equal request-id (Spec 014 §:request-id)" and "It is a transport-facing token with a distinct job (process-global uniqueness)";
- line 1142 (§Transport): "The managed-HTTP in-flight registry keys by :request-id process-globally and supersedes/aborts by equal request-id".

What the code does (verified by the rf2-q02oa worker at 9a805e1272):
- implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/registry.cljc keys in-flight by [frame-id request-id]; supersede! (handlers.cljc:537) and :rf.http/managed-abort (:575) act per frame.
- The one any-frame seam is abort-in-flight! (registry.cljc:408-429), which resources' out-of-cascade teardown reaches through the :http/abort-in-flight! hook.
- The work-id carries no frame, and two frames CAN still hold the same work-id (a generation is a recorded value that replay or a dispatch token supplies; resources_work_ledger_cljs_test.cljc:332 and resources_mutation_cljs_test.cljc:540 assert bare work-ids collide across two frames at {:generation 1}).
- So the surviving reason for the frame qualification is the any-frame teardown abort, which the [:rf.req frame-id work-id] token keeps on the issuing frame. #11140's docstrings carry this wording; match it.

Fix: rewrite those three passages so they state today's reason. Keep the token shape and every MUST unchanged; no behaviour change, and no ruling on the open "opaque correlation ids" proposal. Spec 014:699 is consistent with the code (leave it). Gates: check_doc_slugs.py, mkdocs build --strict.

FENCE: spec/016-Resources.md request-id rationale passages only (about lines 73, 568, 1142). Wording only; matches PR #11140 docstrings.
== WORKER RESULT 2026-10-11 17:09:15 AUSEST: PR #11144 (draft until the worker marks it ready), branch worker/resources-reqid-spec, commit 05706922cc. The base is trunk e2fc3e2af2, which is 87ecb30b5f plus two beads checkpoints. The PR changes spec/016-Resources.md only, with 3 insertions and 3 deletions. Wording only.

PREMISE VERIFIED at source at 87ecb30b5f:
- http registry.cljc keys in-flight by [frame-id request-id]; its namespace docstring calls this "PROCESS-GLOBAL storage with FRAME-SCOPED KEYS".
- supersede! (registry.cljc:596) is frame-scoped, and handlers.cljc:537 calls supersede! frame-id request-id.
- handlers.cljc:575 sends :rf.http/managed-abort to abort-in-flight-in-frame!.
- The one any-frame seam is abort-in-flight! (registry.cljc:408-429), which matches through the 1-arity lookup-in-flight. managed.cljc:236 publishes it as the :http/abort-in-flight! late-bind hook, and resources work_ledger abort-handle! fires that hook with [:rf.req frame-id work-id] for the clear-resource and frame-destroy teardown.
- Two frames can hold the same work-id: resources_work_ledger_cljs_test.cljc:332 and resources_mutation_cljs_test.cljc:540 assert that the bare work-ids collide at {:generation 1}.

PASSAGES REWRITTEN so the reason they give is the any-frame teardown abort, in the same terms as the PR #11140 docstrings:
- Line 73, the request-correlation identity rule. "hands a process-global transport registry" becomes "hands the transport", and the sentence adds "even through the teardown abort that matches a request-id in any frame".
- Line 568, the second-identity bullet in Ledger row retention and identity. The "frame-local work-id" and "process-global registry" premises are replaced by two points. First, the work-id carries no frame, and a recorded or token-supplied generation can give two frames the same one. Second, the registry is keyed [frame-id request-id] and supersede and managed-abort work within the frame, while the out-of-cascade teardown aborts through the any-frame :http/abort-in-flight! hook. The parenthetical "(or, across frames, resolve a sibling frame's colliding request)" on the opportunistic abort is dropped, because managed-abort is frame-scoped. The bullet adds one link, to the existing part-1 allocator anchor.
- Line 1142, Transport. Same correction, and "isolates frames" becomes "keeps that abort on the issuing frame".
The token shape, every MUST and SHOULD, and every heading anchor are unchanged. The process-global statements about the generation allocator (about lines 1701 and 1709) and the SSR cache (line 1653) were left alone, as was Spec 014.
