Measured: the fx registry does validate a :schema when present (re-frame.fx default branch, :schemas/validate-fx! late-bind, dev-only via debug-enabled?), so the production-cost condition holds. What decides it is ordering: that check runs BEFORE the handler and, on failure, skips the fx with a generic :rf.error/schema-validation-failure :where :fx-args. The :rf.machine/* handlers already refuse malformed args with their own catalogued errors (for example :rf.error/machine-spawn-bad-shape for a spawn with no :machine-id or with a :definition, pinned by machine_spawn_definition_refused_test and others), so attaching SpawnFxArgs would swap that error for the generic one in any dev build carrying the schemas artefact, and the error a user sees would depend on whether schemas is loaded.

title: Correlate resource attempts by [:rf.work/resource <resource-id> <generation>] so no transport, internal reply or HTTP failure map carries the scoped key
description:
## Ruling

Correlate resource attempts by an opaque per-frame attempt id (the review corpus's D5), now:

- A resource attempt's work id becomes `[:rf.work/resource <resource-id> <generation>]`. The transport request id keeps its frame: `[:rf.req <frame-id> <work-id>]`.
- The internal reply addresses (the `:on-success` / `:on-failure` payloads the resource runtime hands managed HTTP) carry `:work/id`, `:generation` and `:rf.frame/id`, and no `:resource/key` or `:scope`. The reply handler resolves the scoped key through the receiving frame's ledger row, then verifies the entry's `:current-work` and `:generation` exactly as today. A missing row means the attempt is gone: the reply is suppressed as stale.
- The scoped key stays the cache identity, and entries stay keyed by it. The ledger row is the one place that records which key an attempt serves.
- D5 removes identity from **internal transport correlation**, not from the app's own reply contract. App-facing read continuations (`:reply-to` targets) keep their documented top-level `:resource`, `:params`, `:scope` and `:resource/key` facts, now sourced from the ledger row and entry instead of the transport payload. Request payloads and URLs are the application's own and are untouched.
- No random-id service and no new public API.

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original
> recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then
> remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

Both the dossier (`resource-identity-privacy-and-correlation`) and the Codex review said yes now, with this shape, after the scope rule and coordinated with any work-ledger fold. Codex's clarification that app-facing continuations keep their facts is folded in above.

Decisive facts, read in source at trunk 89517e8f54:

1. **The scoped key is copied into every attempt carrier, including production error envelopes.** The work id embeds it (`implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/work_ledger.cljc:104-118`); the request id embeds the work id (`:141-163`); both internal reply payloads carry `:work/id`, `:resource/key` and `:scope` (`implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/transport/http.cljc:137-150`); HTTP's work id embeds the request id (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/reply.cljc:91-110`); and `self-identify-failure` stamps `:request-id` and `:work/id` on every HTTP failure map (`http/reply.cljc:124-155`). So after a 503 the resource entry's `:error` carries the scoped key - scope included - twice, on what HTTP calls "the one surface that survives production (the reply the app's error reporting is built from)" (`http/reply.cljc:112-122`). `:rf.http/issued` carries `:request-id` and `:rf.reply/work-id` too (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/handlers.cljc:325-359`), and HTTP's privacy composer scrubs URL, body and header carriers, not request ids.
2. **The generation already makes an attempt unique; the key adds nothing.** One process-global, host-side, monotone allocator serves reads and mutations (`spec/016-Resources.md:1704-1715`), and mutations already use a key-free work id, `[:rf.work/resource [:rf.mutation <instance-id>] <generation>]` (`spec/Managed-Effects.md:191`). Caveat: recorded allocations are replayed, and a token-supplied allocation can hand two frames the same generation (`work_ledger.cljc:110-115`) - which is why the frame stays in the request id and is checked first.
3. **The lookup needs no new index.** Non-terminal ledger rows are never pruned (`work_ledger.cljc:499`), so every live attempt's row is there when its reply lands.

Rejected options:

- **No (keep the key in transit):** every new carrier of the key needs another projector arm, and production failure maps keep carrying the principal.
- **Later (after the work-ledger fold):** the fold would then need a `generation -> key` index on entries; doing this first keeps the ledger as the one attempt-to-key index.
- **A random-id service or a new public id API:** unneeded; resource id, generation and frame suffice.

Supersedes: `spec/016-Resources.md:63` (the key as "the request-correlation token's payload") and `:73` ("Request-correlation ids MUST include the full scoped resource key"); the resource work-id shape at `spec/Conventions.md:626` and `:1042` and `spec/Managed-Effects.md:190`. No earlier bead ruled on this.

## Work

The dossier proposed this as an epic; split it into children if that helps, in roughly this order.

1. **Work id, request id, ledger keying.** `resource-work-id` (`work_ledger.cljc:104`) takes the resource id. The ledger is keyed by the work id, so the canonical-bytes keying in `work-id-id` (`:120-139`), which exists only because embedded params collide under `=`, goes unless something else needs it.
2. **Internal reply payload and verifier.** `build-managed-args` (`transport/http.cljc:128-150`) drops `:resource/key` and `:scope`. The resource `path-fn` in `reply_handlers.cljc` (`:20-25`) resolves the entry from the frame's ledger row; a missing row is stale-suppressed. The canonical resource reply's `:correlation` (`resource-correlation`, `events.cljc:2483-2490`) and the continuation facts (`read-continuation-reply`, `events.cljc:235-251`) read the key from the ledger row or entry.
3. **Trace rows, attempt half.** Attempt-scoped rows (`fetch-started`, `succeeded`, `failed` and their kin) carry `:resource/id` and `:work/id`. The one row that states which key an attempt serves (`work-started`) keeps `:resource/key`, under the off-box scope rule. Entry rows keep the key: `cache-hit`, `owner-attached`, the GC, stale and poll timers, `invalidated` `:matched`, `route-plan` `:identities`, `hydrated`.
4. **HTTP.** Docstrings and tests in `http/reply.cljc` and `http/handlers.cljc`: failure maps and `:rf.http/issued` now carry no identity, with no projector. HTTP's work-id tuple `[:rf.work/http logical-id issuance attempt]` keeps its shape; only the logical id it wraps shrinks.
5. **Graph egress.** `project-work-id` and `project-host-transient` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/egress.cljc:292-319`) become no-ops; delete them once a test shows no work id carries a key. The HMAC policy for live resource node identity (`:210-254`) stays.
6. **Trace egress and Xray.** Delete the embedded-key arms for work ids and request ids in `trace_egress.cljc`, and Xray's `work-id-text` redaction (`tools/xray/spec/024-Resources-Panel.md:199-214`), once verified. Xray joins attempts on `:work/id` and `:resource/id`.
7. **Spec.** Rewrite `spec/016-Resources.md:63`, `:73`, §Frame work ledger and §Ledger row retention and identity (correlation by generation and frame; identity in one place); `spec/Conventions.md:626` and `:1042`; the work-record schema in `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` (`:3116`); `spec/Managed-Effects.md:190`; and the resource rows in `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`.

Deliberately stays: the scoped key as cache identity and entry key; the mutation work-id shape; the frame in the request id; the monotone host-side generation allocator; app-facing `:reply-to` continuation facts; request payloads and URLs.

## Sequencing

- Hot zones: `spec/Conventions.md`, `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` and `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` - each edit sequenced against other holders of that file. No `spec/011-SSR.md` edit expected; if one is made, it is the one i/crlf file.
- Depends on: rf2-sifcp (resource identity off-box: the standing scope rule). It decides which rows still carry the key and under what rule.
- Precedes: any work-ledger fold bead (resources decision 6 in the adversarial-review corpus; none filed yet). Coordinate so the attempt-to-key mapping has one owner.
- Cross-dossier: sequence with, not in parallel to, the `http-one-request-record` ruling's bead(s): both edit `http/reply.cljc` and `http/handlers.cljc`. This bead does not need that dossier's per-frame HTTP work-id allocator.

## Evidence

Read in source at trunk 89517e8f54: every carrier in fact 1, the allocator and the mutation work-id shape in fact 2, the no-prune rule in fact 3, and the continuation and correlation builders. Not yet run: nothing was compiled or tested. These still need a run: the restore and replay suites, to confirm that every reply whose ledger row is gone really is stale (if a legitimate reply is found with no row, stop: D5 moves to later and is redesigned around an entry-side index); real issued traces, failure envelopes and internal reply addresses, to confirm they carry no scoped key. The size is unmeasured; the corpus withdrew its 2.5K to 3.5K line estimate.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A resource attempt's work id is `[:rf.work/resource <resource-id> <generation>]` and its transport request id is `[:rf.req <frame-id> <work-id>]`; tests pin both shapes.
2. The internal `:on-success` / `:on-failure` reply payloads carry no `:resource/key` and no `:scope`. The handler resolves the entry through the receiving frame's ledger row and verifies `:current-work` and `:generation`; a reply whose row is gone is suppressed as stale (tests).
3. Production HTTP failure maps carry no scoped key: after a 503 on a resource fetch, the entry's `:error` map's `:request-id` and `:work/id` contain neither the scope nor the params (test).
4. No `:rf.http/*` trace row carries a scoped key: tested on `:rf.http/issued` and on a completion row.
5. Invariants hold, each by a test: the generation allocator never rewinds across restore, so no id is recycled; cross-frame replies stay separated (the `cross-frame-request-id-does-not-collide` control in `implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_work_ledger_cljs_test.cljc` stays green); restore suppression is unchanged; two distinct live attempts in one frame (same resource, different params) get distinct work ids and each settles only its own entry; joined read `:reply-to` targets still transfer to a superseding attempt and are delivered exactly once (`resources_reply_to_reads_cljs_test.cljc` stays green).
6. App-facing read continuations still receive top-level `:resource`, `:params`, `:scope` and `:resource/key` (test).
7. Attempt-scoped resource trace rows carry `:resource/id` and `:work/id` and no `:resource/key`, except the one row that states which key the attempt serves; entry rows are unchanged.
8. Projector arms for embedded keys (graph `project-work-id` / `project-host-transient`, trace-egress work-id and request-id arms, Xray `work-id-text` redaction) are deleted only after tests 3 and 4 pass; the graph's HMAC policy for live resource nodes is unchanged.
9. Spec 016 (`:63`, `:73`, §Frame work ledger, §Ledger row retention and identity), `spec/Conventions.md:626` and `:1042`, the `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` work-record schema, `spec/Managed-Effects.md:190` and the `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` resource rows describe the new shapes; `mkdocs build --strict` and `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` pass.
10. `npm run test:cljs`, `npm run test:xray-feature-gate` (both from `implementation/`) and `scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh` pass, with exit codes quoted in the PR body.

title: Frames: publish a reprojected generation only onto the incarnation it was computed from (compare-and-publish, core-frames A6)
description:
Reprojection can publish a frame generation by bare id over a same-id successor. Make that publication a compare-and-publish against the incarnation captured when reprojection started (core-frames A6). This is a source-derived overlap risk; it has not been reproduced.

## Ruling

Decided 2026-10-16. The JVM concurrency ruling is filed as rf2-ti8wz, rf2-a19oz, rf2-qa3ab and rf2-6fdhf. It narrows the JVM contract to "one lifecycle writer per frame id". The decision dossier would have closed A6 as out of contract. An independent Codex review disagreed: a permitted operation can start a framework writer for frames other than the caller's target, so A6 does not vanish under the new rule. Mike directed: "file necessary beads for the "Largely in agreement" list as outlined above". That settles A6 on the Codex side: a small compare-and-publish, not another locking system, and not a claim that A6 is out of contract.

## Evidence (read in source at trunk 89517e8f54)

- A normal dispatch or subscribe resolution can flush dirty projections (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/live_frame.cljc:474-520`).
- That flush enumerates ALL image-loaded frames (`live_frame.cljc:1629-1644`), not only the caller's target.
- Reprojection eventually publishes by bare id (`live_frame.cljc:1473-1519`).
- `set-generation!` checks only that the id exists (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:1696-1708`).

So a generation computed against incarnation N can be published onto a same-id incarnation N+1 that replaced it in between.

## Work

1. Capture the target frame's incarnation (its identity, or the generation it started from) when reprojection begins.
2. Publish only if the registry still holds that same incarnation, as a compare-and-set.
3. Otherwise drop the stale generation. No retry and no lock.
4. Add a spec sentence to `spec/002-Frames.md` so the rule is stated beside the one-lifecycle-writer paragraph that rf2-ti8wz writes.

## Sequencing

- Comes after rf2-ti8wz, which writes the contract paragraph this sentence sits beside.
- Touches `frame.cljc` and `live_frame.cljc`, the same region as rf2-qa3ab (reservation and A2) and rf2-uwsy0 (one registration table). Sequence it with both; never run it in parallel with them.
- `spec/002-Frames.md` is a HOT ZONE.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Add a JVM test, red at base and green after. It starts a reprojection of frame id X, replaces X with a same-id successor before the publish, and asserts that the successor's generation is NOT overwritten.
2. When the incarnation is unchanged, publishing behaves as before. The existing reprojection and hot-reload tests stay green.
3. No new lock or monitor is introduced.
4. `spec/002-Frames.md` states the compare-and-publish rule.

title: check_lint_export.py: run the self-test's mutations on temporary copies, never on the shipped config and fixture
description:
## Defect

`self_test` in `implementation/fresco/scripts/check_lint_export.py` (~236-306) writes each fault into `CONFIG_FILE` and `FIXTURE`, which are shipped checkout files, then restores the saved text in `finally`. That causes two problems:

- an external kill skips the restore;
- a concurrent edit can be overwritten by the saved text.

## Change

Give `check` an explicit fixture argument; it already accepts an export directory. Copy the small export and fixture into a unique temporary directory, and mutate only the copies, following `implementation/scripts/lib/scratch-fixtures.cjs`.

## Acceptance

The red and green findings are identical to today's, and the checkout bytes are unchanged after both ordinary completion and a forced interruption.

Checked at trunk f4e5adad0a.
notes:
== WORKER SUMMARY (test-tooling, 2026-10-19 02:13 AUSEST) — DONE, PR #11505, commit 3e79edc702 ==

Premise verified at tip 9a69891d05 (path is implementation/fresco/scripts/check_lint_export.py; the dispatch brief said scripts/check_lint_export.py).

Change: check(export_dir, fixture) takes the fixture beside the export directory. Each self-test case calls _mutated_copy, which copies the export and the fixture into a fresh tempfile.mkdtemp directory (system temp, not the checkout), keeps the fixture's lint-fixtures/macro_shapes.cljs name, mutates only the copy and returns it; the case lints the copy and removes only that directory. The final green half still lints the shipped files, read-only. System temp rather than in-repo .scratch: scratch-fixtures.cjs lives in the repo only because bash needs relative paths, which clj-kondo does not, and a killed run then leaves nothing in the checkout.

Evidence: self-test and gate output byte-identical to trunk's (cmp), both exit 0. Forced interruption (TerminateProcess, so no finally runs) after each of the five mutation cases: checkout unchanged by blob hash and git status empty every time; the killed run leaves only its own temp directory. Trunk script planted and killed while it had config.edn mutated: config.edn left MODIFIED in the checkout (git status " M"). Restores verified by blob hash.

title: Resources: one framework event for a principal change, so old-scope entries cannot be refetched with the new user's credentials
description:
## Problem

Measured at trunk 3959d2a5bf.

Switching user is an app recipe today: resolve the old scope, dispatch `:rf.resource/clear-scope` for it, commit the new identity, then dispatch `[:rf.route/replan-resources {:cause …}]`. RealWorld writes that recipe out at several sites in `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/auth.cljs` (login and logout clear both the session and viewer scopes; session restore and failed restore replan). Forgetting any step is the cross-credential leak that scope exists to stop.

The automatic refetches do not guard against it either. `active-stale-scan` (focus and reconnect) and `poll-fired-handler` in `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc` refetch every owned stale or polled entry, with no current-principal check. If old-scope entries are still owned and HTTP sends the ambient new credentials, an automatic refetch writes the new user's bytes under the old user's scope.

## Change

One framework event performs the whole transition: clear the old scope, retire its owners, then replan the active route. Settle the id and argument shape against `spec/Conventions.md`'s reserved event ids (for example `[:rf.resource/change-principal {:from <scope> :cause …}]`).

**Explicit, not automatic.** Running the transition automatically whenever the scope resolver's answer changes was considered and rejected: it misfires in frames that hold several principals on purpose, and when a resolver depends on arbitrary app-db. The app dispatches the one event where it changes identity.

Rewrite RealWorld's sites onto it, and replace the recipe in the docs.

Whether a frame is one principal (frame-wide invalidation) stays open and is not decided here.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `spec/016-Resources.md`, the scope and principal sections.
- `docs/resources/tutorial/03-auth-and-forms.md` and any how-to that spells the recipe.
- `spec/API.md` with both manifest sidecars and `spec/Conventions.md`, if the event id is catalogued. **Hot zones.**

## Acceptance

- After the event runs, no focus, reconnect, poll or invalidation refetch touches an old-scope key. Test each trigger.
- RealWorld's login, logout and session-restore paths use the one event, and its auth flows still pass.
- Resources suites (JVM and `npm run test:cljs`) green.

## Sequencing

Hot zones: `spec/API.md` with its sidecars, `spec/Conventions.md`. Touches RealWorld beside the route-bound read bead (linked as related).

Additive. Effort M.
notes:
== WORKER SUMMARY 2026-10-19 16:48:14 AUSEST (branch worker/resources-principal-route, PR #11536, draft)

Done; NOT closed (the mayor closes). One commit on the PR carries the event, a second the where-sym fix, a third (local, see PUSH HELD) the Spec 012 recipe.

WHAT LANDED
- [:rf.resource/change-principal {:from [<departing concrete scope> ...] :cause <cause>}] (events.cljc change-principal-handler, registered in resources.cljc with an event :schema). It validates every :from member through canonicalize-scope before anything changes (one bad member clears nothing; a non-vector :from is :rf.error/resource-invalid-scope), skips nil members, runs clear-scope-handler* per distinct scope, and, when the frame has an active route, dispatches [:rf.route/replan-resources {:cause <cause>}].
- The guard the bead asked for sits in ensure-load, so it covers every trigger at once: an ownerless refetch whose cause is :focus, :reconnect, :poll or [:invalidate ...] and whose entry no longer exists is DROPPED with a :rf.resource/refetch-decision row, :decision :no-entry. User/explicit refetches and owned ensures are unaffected.
- RealWorld auth.cljs: login, logout, session-restored and session-restore-failed all dispatch the event; the hand-written clear-scope/replan sequence is gone.
- Spec 016 §Changing principal (new), re-key bullets, events block, the race bullet, the replan recipe, the trace list; docs/resources concepts, glossary, testing, tutorial 04/05; Spec 012's identity-switch recipe now names the event (made directly once the mayor released 012).

EVIDENCE
- Red at trunk: the new test ns resources_change_principal_cljs_test.cljc does not compile at trunk (No such var change-principal-handler). The decisive red is a trunk-recipe probe (the four triggers queued around the old clear-scope recipe, on trunk code): 5 tests, 15 assertions, 10 failures — a queued focus, reconnect, poll tick or invalidation refetch RE-CREATED the cleared old-scope entry and sent its request.
- Green: the new ns 8 tests / 25 assertions, 0 failures. Resources JVM 558 tests / 1650 assertions, 0 failures (trunk baseline 544 / 1610; the delta is the two new namespaces plus the skeleton change).

DELTA FROM THE BEAD TEXT
- The bead says login cleared scopes at tip. It did not: at tip only logout and the restore-failure path (both through :auth/clear-session) cleared; :auth/session-established neither cleared nor replanned (it relied on its post-login redirect), and :auth/session-restored replanned without clearing. All four now go through the event.

HELD FOR THE MAYOR (hot zones, non-blocking)
- spec/009 :rf.error/resource-invalid-scope row: add the trigger "or :rf.resource/change-principal's :from is not a vector".
- spec/Conventions.md line 110 (:rf.resource/* row): add :rf.resource/change-principal to the public resource events.

PUSH HELD: see the PR body's "Held for Mike". The coordinator asked for a rebase onto origin/main to pick up the released 012; publishing the rebased branch needs a force-push, which this dispatch forbids, and the classifier refused the non-force alternative (reset to the published tip, then merge origin/main). The rebased branch with the 012 commit is local only.
== WORKER UPDATE 2026-10-19 18:13:44 AUSEST (supersedes the "PUSH HELD" and "OUTSTANDING" lines of the 16:48 summary)

PR #11536 is READY FOR REVIEW at head 8e1a2a19ea. Nothing is outstanding on this bead.
- The branch took origin/main by MERGE (no force-push, no rewrite): #11532 routing, #11534 core, #11533 http, #11535 views.
- Spec 012 (released by the mayor): the identity-switch recipe is :rf.resource/change-principal; the route :resources section names [:rf/route-resource <resource-id>].
- Spec 009 (released by the mayor): the :rf.error/resource-route-read-ambiguous row (after resource-route-blocking); resource-invalid-scope names the change-principal :from check; resource-bad-spec and resource-invalid-params treat :params-schema as optional. check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py exit 0; core error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test 19 tests / 48 assertions, exit 0.
- A CLJS-only red found and fixed: in a CLJS build a url-bound frame starts on the :rf.route/not-found slice for "/", so the no-route change-principal test now asserts what holds on both hosts (scope cleared, nothing fetched, slice untouched).
- Fast-PR spine exit 0 at 765bdbc343: JVM core 1192/3594, resources 558/1652, CLJS node 6181/17438, all 0 failures; kondo 0 errors. check-examples-compile exit 0 (56 builds, zero warnings) at a4b9fa8775.
- Routed edits also on the PR: #11533 (tutorial 03/04/06: JSON error bodies arrive parsed; :sensitive covers [:error :body-text]) and #11535 (009 no-frame-context firing case).
- Still held for the mayor (not this bead's blocker): Conventions lines 34/46/110/669/673 and Spec-Schemas lines 1624/3170/3207, text in the PR body.
Merged-PR audit #11536: follow-up rf2-d07p3 — Use change-principal in the Resources tutorial's real sign-in handler. This is a separate open finding; the source status and ruling are preserved.
close_reason:
Merged in PR #11536 (squash, commit f756175334). One framework event handles a principal change: [:rf.resource/change-principal {:from [scopes…] :cause …}]. It validates every scope first, clears each one, then replans the active route.

A guard in ensure-load drops an ownerless focus, reconnect, poll or invalidation refetch whose entry has gone, recording it as :decision :no-entry. So an old-scope entry can no longer be refetched with the new principal's credentials. RealWorld's login, logout, session restore and failed restore all use the event.

The bead text was wrong at tip about RealWorld: login cleared no scopes, :auth/session-established neither cleared nor replanned, and session-restored replanned without clearing. The event fixes all three.

Evidence: queuing the four triggers around trunk's clear-scope steps gave 5 tests with 10 failures, each trigger re-creating the cleared entry and sending its request. With the change, the fast-PR spine passed (resources JVM 558 tests, test:cljs 6181), and so did mkdocs --strict, check-examples-compile and the catalogue gates. CI was green at 79 checks.

Follow-ups: rf2-3moeo covers the docs outside the fence. The Conventions and Spec-Schemas lines are routed to machines-data-spawn and wait for #11540.

WHAT LANDED. implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/subs.cljc goes from 622 to 561 lines. The nine focused subs were bespoke fns that re-derived the view-model's facts a second time: :rf.resource/data, status, loading?, fetching?, stale?, error, refresh-error, has-data? and previous-data. Each is now one key of the :rf/resource view-model (state-sub-fn), registered from a [sub-id key doc] table over the same frame-state signal. WHY NOT THE LITERAL "ORDINARY reg-sub LAYERED OVER [:rf/resource q]". title: subscribe is a plain function on both hosts (bounded experiment), usable as a value on the JVM
description:
## Ruling

Mike ruled on 2026-10-20: `subscribe` becomes a plain function on both hosts, as a bounded experiment. The alternative was to keep the macro for its call-site stamp.

`dispatch` and `dispatch-sync` are not part of this ruling and stay macros.

## Problem

Measured at trunk 8fc6369484.

- **A macro on the JVM.** `re-frame.core/subscribe` is a macro (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:1344`, built by `build-subscribe-form` in `core_call_site_macros.cljc`). On the JVM it cannot be passed as a value, so `(map subscribe qs)` or `(partial subscribe …)` fails there.
- **Two things on CLJS.** CLJS adds a value-position alias with the same name (`core.cljc:452-463`), so `subscribe` is a macro in call position and a function in value position.
- **The stamp often adds nothing.** The macro stamps the call-site coordinate onto the read. Inside a registered view that stamp adds nothing, because `reg-view` injects a lexical `subscribe` bound to the view, and its reads carry the view's coordinate (see `reg_view_injection_test.clj`, `injected-subscribe-stamps-view-call-site-on-error`).
- **What the stamp is worth.** It only has value outside views (handlers, tools, tests). There it attributes errors such as `:rf.error/no-such-sub` to the call site.

## Change

- `re-frame.core/subscribe` is a plain function on both hosts with the same two arities, `(subscribe query-v)` and `(subscribe query-v opts)`.
- Delete the macro, `build-subscribe-form`, and the CLJS value alias. Keep the `subscribe-impl` seam only if something still needs it.
- Keep the `reg-view` injected `subscribe`, which still attributes reads to the view.
- Keep `:rf.trace/call-site` in `opts` as an internal carrier, if `capture-frame`'s `:subscribe` op still needs it.

**The experiment's exit.** Record what the stamp loss costs outside views: which tests, Xray panels or pair-MCP tools read a subscribe call-site. If a tool loses a fact it needs, stop and report the loss on this bead rather than adding a second subscribe form.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `spec/API.md` §Dispatch and subscribe, with both manifest sidecars (`subscribe`'s kind changes from macro to fn). **Hot zone.** Hand-edit `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn` and regenerate with `generate!`.
- `spec/Conventions.md:1510`, which names "the `dispatch` / `dispatch-sync` / `subscribe` macros". **Hot zone.**
- `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` where it describes subscribe call-site capture. **Hot zone.**
- `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:295`.
- About 11 files call `subscribe` a macro. Find them with a case-insensitive search for `subscribe` within a few characters of `macro` across `spec/`, `docs/`, `skills/`, `migration/`, `implementation/` and `tools/`.

## Acceptance

- `(map rf/subscribe [[:a] [:b]])` works on the JVM and on CLJS.
- Reads inside a registered view still carry the view's coordinate.
- The two tests pinning the subscribe macro's stamp (`source_coord_jvm_test.cljc` `subscribe-macro-stamps-call-site-on-no-such-sub`, and the subscribe half of `source_coord_cljs_test.cljs`) are deleted or rewritten to pin the plain-fn contract.
- JVM suite, `npm run test:cljs`, Xray and pair-MCP suites green.
- The `api-manifest` lint job is green.

## Sequencing

Hot zones: `spec/API.md` with its sidecars, `spec/Conventions.md`, `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md`.

Breaking only for code that relied on the JVM macro's call-site stamp. Effort S–M.
notes:
== DISPATCH (mayor), 2026-10-20 08:32:30 AUSEST: subscribe-plain-fn; sole holder of spec/API.md with its manifests, spec/Conventions.md and spec/006.
== WORKER (subscribe-plain-fn), PR #11562 (draft): subscribe is a plain fn on both hosts

DISPOSITION: done.

CHANGE. re-frame.core/subscribe is a def-alias of re-frame.subs/subscribe on both hosts, with arities [query-v] and [query-v opts]. Deleted: the JVM macro, build-subscribe-form, the CLJS value alias, and the subscribe-impl seam. Nothing still needed subscribe-impl, so the public var is now the seam. The late-bind key :core/subscribe-impl became :core/subscribe and reads the var at call time, so a with-redefs on rf/subscribe still reaches a capture-frame :subscribe op. rf.subs/subscribe no longer reads :rf.trace/call-site from opts: capture-frame's :subscribe op wraps rf.trace/with-call-site itself and never used the opts carrier. subscribe-with-opts folded back into the 2-arity. The reg-view injected subscribe is unchanged.

EXPERIMENT EXIT (census of subscribe call-site readers outside views). No tool loses a fact it needs.
- Xray reads :rf.trace/call-site in two generic, nil-tolerant places, both in panels/epoch/projection.cljc: the dispatch row's :coord, and exception-source-coord, which falls back after the registration coord. shell.cljs reads it only off a dispatched event. Xray has no subscribe-specific reader.
- pair-MCP has no :rf.trace/call-site reader.
- Two tests pinned the stamp: source_coord_jvm_test subscribe-macro-stamps-call-site-on-no-such-sub, and the subscribe half of source_coord_cljs_test. Both are rewritten to pin the plain-fn contract.
- reg_view_injection_test injected-subscribe-stamps-view-call-site-on-error is unchanged and green, so reads inside a view still carry the view's coord.
- The loss: a subscribe outside a view no longer attributes :rf.error/no-such-sub to its own line. That attribution was dev-only, and it was already absent on CLJS in value position.

title: Commentary diet, core event pipeline: router and fx comments and docstrings cut to the reason plus a spec pointer
description:
## Ruling

Mike ruled on 2026-10-20: source commentary is cut to the reason plus a spec pointer. A comment or docstring says what the code is for and why, then points at the spec section that holds the contract. It does not restate the spec.

This extends the present-tense rule in `CLAUDE.md` § Conventions & Patterns (the closed epic rf2-tv5ac removed provenance). This rule removes restatement. This bead applies it to the core event pipeline. A sibling bead (linked) applies it to `implementation/resources/src`. Further surfaces get their own beads.

## Problem

Measured at trunk 8fc6369484, classifying non-blank lines as code, `;` comment, or string literal (overwhelmingly docstrings):

| File | Code | Comment | String |
|---|---|---|---|
| `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc` (4,404 lines) | 1,250 | 1,364 | 1,521 |
| `fx.cljc` | 496 | 500 | 586 |
| `frame.cljc` | 1,506 | 1,295 | 1,763 |
| all of `implementation/core/src` (60,077 lines) | 17,147 | 14,766 | 23,013 |

Much of the prose restates spec text. Reading the router costs an AI pair a large share of its context before it reaches the code, and a restated contract can drift from the spec it copies.

## Change

Scope: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc`, `router/*.cljc` and `fx.cljc`, the per-event pipeline. Leave the rest of core to later beads.

- Each docstring states the fn's contract in a sentence or two: args, return, and what it refuses. It carries the reason when the reason is not obvious, and a `§` pointer to the owning spec section.
- Each `;;` comment keeps only the why that the code cannot show: an ordering constraint, a hazard, a non-obvious invariant. Delete restatements of what the next form does and copies of spec paragraphs.
- No fixed line cap. The test for each sentence: would a reader who has the spec section open lose anything if it went?
- Do not change code, emitted strings, keywords or ex-data. Strings the program emits or a test asserts on stay byte-identical.
- Keep the anchors code comments cite, such as `CLAUDE.md` instrument-hazard letters and spec section names.
- Add one sentence to `CLAUDE.md` § Conventions & Patterns stating the rule. This bead owns that sentence, and the resources bead does not repeat it.

## Acceptance

- The comment and string counts above fall substantially for the files in scope. Report before and after with the same classifier.
- No code form changes: a whitespace-and-comment-insensitive diff of the forms is empty. State how you checked.
- Every `§` pointer resolves to a heading that exists.
- JVM suite and `npm run test:cljs` green.

## Sequencing

`implementation/core/src` is shared with any core bead in flight, so check open PRs touching `router.cljc` or `fx.cljc` before starting, and rebase rather than fight conflicts. Mechanical. Effort M.

title: Routing skill: distinguish saved scroll cache from runtime-db
description:
PR #11564 (merge 6ab00a8226a305a5b7500f153e412ef147eb691f) updates the routing skill's scroll vocabulary but leaves its Multi-frame routing bullet at skills/re-frame2/references/tooling/routing.md:183 saying the route slice, nav-token counter and saved-scroll map all live under [:rf.runtime/routing ...] in runtime-db and can be read through the route subscriptions.

The saved-scroll claim is false. At that merge, routing/scroll.cljc:50-62 holds positions in a separate per-frame scroll-positions-cache atom; frame-scroll-cache (96-101) reads that atom, save-scroll-position! (103-108) writes it, and release-frame! (111-118) drops it. routing/plan.cljc:127-166 takes scroll-cache separately from rdb. Spec 012, Scroll restoration, Storage -- host-side transient cache explicitly says the positions are outside runtime-db and epochs/SSR snapshots.

An AI or developer following this authoring reference is directed to nonexistent runtime-db scroll state and given the wrong persistence/reactivity model. The PR body's Found outside the fence section also identifies this mismatch, but leaves it uncorrected.

Small correction: split that one bullet's ownership statement. Keep the route slice and nav-token counter in runtime-db; describe saved scroll positions as a per-frame host cache, bounded and released on frame destruction. Do not imply the framework route subscriptions expose the saved-position map. Link to Spec 012's storage contract if helpful.

Acceptance: the Multi-frame routing bullet agrees with the existing Spec 012 storage contract and scroll-cache accessors, without changing runtime behavior. A hand check of this prose is sufficient; no new test or cache redesign is needed.
close_reason:
Already fixed on trunk; verified at 2026-10-20 12:55:39 AUSEST (trunk e77398f20a).
- PR #11568 (rf2-s0et7, merged 2026-10-20T01:51:40Z) rewrote the Multi-frame routing bullet at skills/re-frame2/references/tooling/routing.md:183. Saved scroll positions are now "not runtime-db state: they sit in a host-side per-frame cache, released when the frame is destroyed (Spec 012 §Scroll restoration)".
- One correction to this bead's suggested split. The nav-token COUNTER is not runtime-db either. Spec 012 L28 says the routing counters (:nav-token-counter, :pending-nav-counter) are "held in a host-side transient cache (module-private process-global atom, not runtime-db)".
- Trunk says the route slice, with its active :nav-token value, lives in runtime-db, and the allocator is "host-side too, one process-wide counter". That agrees with Spec 012.

title: HTTP: :retry :on accepts status integers, so a 429 retries without retrying every 4xx
description:
## Ruling

Mike ruled on 2026-10-20 that `:retry :on` accepts HTTP status integers beside the category keywords, e.g. `#{:rf.http/http-5xx 429}`.

Today the only way to retry a rate limit is to opt into all of `:rf.http/http-4xx`, which also retries 400, 401, 403, 404 and 422. A status check is still transport retry by Spec 014's own definition: it is a pure function of the failure, read before decode, with no body and no app state.

## Problem

Measured at trunk cb9cb3c074.

- **Validation:** `retryable-categories` and `validate-retry!` (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/handlers.cljc:42-117`, the membership check at `:102-108`) accept only the four retryable categories.
- **Matching:** `maybe-retry!` (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc:994-1029`) matches only `(:kind failure)` (`:1021`, `:1029`).
- **The status is available:** a status failure carries it at `:http-status` (`transport.cljc:1083`).
- **Spec 014 names the gap itself:** its `:rf.http/http-4xx` rationale (`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:397`) cites 429 as the reason that category is retryable, then warns against blanket-retrying 4xx.

## Change

- An `:on` member is a retryable category keyword or an integer from 400 to 599.
- A failure is retried when its `:kind` is in `:on`, or when it carries an `:http-status` that is in `:on`.
- An integer outside 400-599 is refused by the existing `:rf.error/http-bad-retry-on`, with its `:retryable-set` ex-data describing both forms.
- A 1xx or 3xx status already becomes a 4xx-shaped failure that keeps its real status (`transport.cljc:1270`). That status is outside the admitted range, so it can only be retried by the `:rf.http/http-4xx` category, as today.
- Honouring `Retry-After` is out of scope.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md`:
  - the request-table row (`:145`) and the `:on` row (`:372`);
  - §Retry and backoff (`:357-359`: "pure function of the failure category and the attempt count") and the boundary test (`:420`);
  - §Closed-set `:retry :on` validation (`:382-414`).
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2230`, the `:rf.error/http-bad-retry-on` row. **Hot zone.**
- Docs that teach categories only: `docs/api/re-frame.http.md` (`:75`, `:102`, `:248`), `docs/core/how-to/build-a-form.md:338` and `skills/re-frame2/patterns/managed-http.md:142`. Add the 429 example to the API page and the skill.
- Fix in passing: `docs/api/re-frame.http.md:248` says "first five kinds", but four kinds are retryable.

title: Handlers read machine and route state with (rf/compute-sub <vector> rt), not spelled runtime-db paths
description:
## Ruling

Mike ruled on 2026-10-20 that event handlers stop spelling framework storage paths to read a machine's state or the current route. Handlers keep receiving the whole runtime-db in their coeffects, with no declaration required. That half of the ruling is recorded on rf2-py1v5.

The route for the read is the one read grammar that `spec/Conventions.md` already mandates: "A runtime-db framework read is a subscription vector", with no named read-sugar function. A handler holds frame state, not the sub cache, so it reads the same vector with the existing public `compute-sub` against its own runtime-db:

```clojure
(rf/compute-sub [:rf/machine :ui/article-editor] rt)   ; rt = (:rf.db/runtime cofx)
(:nav-token (rf/compute-sub [:rf/route] rt))
```

So no new public name is needed.

## Problem

Measured at trunk cb9cb3c074.

- **Views read a machine with the `[:rf/machine id]` sub.** It is `reg-runtime-sub` over `snapshot-path` (`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc:297-300`). No public function reads a snapshot from a runtime-db value; `paths.cljc`'s `snapshot-path` is undocumented and internal.
- **Handlers spell the storage path.** For example, `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/article_editor.cljs:371` has `(get-in rt [:rf.runtime/machines :snapshots :ui/article-editor :state :mode])`.
- **The examples invent their own helpers.** `realworld_http/settings.cljs:78-83` has `machine-data`. `realworld_http/http.cljs:179-183` has `current-nav-token`, which reads `[:rf.runtime/routing :current :nav-token]` and has 11 uses.
- **`compute-sub` already does this read.** `(compute-sub query-v db)` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:2423`) accepts an app-db value, a runtime-db value or a whole frame-state value. Its docstring names `:rf/machine` as the case. It is pure and cache-free, but it is tiered and taught as testing-only (`spec/API.md:818`, `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1154`).
- **The route slice carries the nav-token.** `:rf/route` reads the slice directly (`spec/012-Routing.md:25`, `:724`).

## Change

- **Tier:** `compute-sub` moves from the `:testing` tier to the tier `subscribe` has. Its docstring and API row describe the handler use beside the test use.
- **Conventions:** add one sentence to the one-read-grammar rule (`spec/Conventions.md`, around `:679`): in an event handler the vector is read with `compute-sub` against the handler's `:rf.db/runtime`, so it is still the one grammar.
- **Examples:**
  - `article_editor.cljs:371` uses `compute-sub`;
  - `settings.cljs` drops `machine-data` for it;
  - `http.cljs` drops `current-nav-token` for `(:nav-token (rf/compute-sub [:rf/route] rt))`;
  - fix the comments and docstrings that point readers at the path (`settings.cljs:80`, `:232`; `schema.cljs:89`, `:126`; `auth.cljs:16`, `:375`; `examples/core/login/stories.cljs:223`).
- **Docs:**
  - `docs/api/re-frame.machines.md:53` ("Read it with the `[:rf/machine machine-id]` subscription, or once with `subscribe-once`") gains the handler form;
  - so do the machines how-to and concept pages, and `docs/core/where-state-lives.md`.
- **Skills:** update the reg-machine and tags skill lines (`:177`, `:47`) and the skill prose that teaches handlers to read the path.
- **Tests:** new tests read machine state with `compute-sub`. Converting the existing per-file `machine-state` test helpers (56 files) is optional, not part of this bead.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- **Hot zones:** `spec/API.md` with both manifest sidecars (the `compute-sub` row's tier; regenerate), and `spec/Conventions.md`.
- `spec/008-Testing.md` §compute-sub, for a sentence on the handler use.

## Acceptance

- A handler test reads `(rf/compute-sub [:rf/machine id] (:rf.db/runtime cofx))` and gets the snapshot.
- `(:nav-token (rf/compute-sub [:rf/route] rt))` returns the current token.
- No example handler spells `:rf.runtime/machines :snapshots` or `:rf.runtime/routing :current`.
- The api-manifest check, `npm run test:cljs`, the JVM suites, `mkdocs build --strict` and `check_doc_slugs.py` green.

title: RealWorld resources README: explain mutation scopes at issuance
description:
PR #11574 (merge 9cdb8d495330bd1155bc7b5b3886d81477fd2317) changes every mutation consequence's {:from-db ...} resolution to the app-db at issuance. The PR body and source Bead acknowledge this residue outside the worker's fence. This is the independently trackable audit follow-up.

Small correction: change that one sentence to say each scope resolves against the app-db the mutation was issued in. Keep the example code unchanged. title: Epoch record drops a machine {:rf/sub} recorded fact, so :strict replay from the record fails missing-required
description:
## Problem

A machine's `{:rf/sub query-v :as fact-id}` recordable source is evaluated live and written onto the in-flight `:rf.cofx` token (`deliver-sub-source` in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/cofx.cljc`). But the value never reaches the epoch record's `:rf.cofx` replay token.

The cause is that epoch capture (`find-trigger-event` in `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/capture.cljc`) merges mid-run facts only from `:rf.cofx/generated` traces, and `deliver-sub-source` emits none. So a `:strict` replay from the real epoch record of any event that evaluated the source fails `:rf.error/missing-required-cofx`, which contradicts Spec 005's "strict replay re-presents it verbatim".

## Measured

Measured on trunk d6261b9482, found while measuring rf2-7y7ii. The setup:
- A machine whose `:go` action declares `{:rf/sub [:meas/cfg] :as :meas/cfg-v}`.
- The event is dispatched with an explicit `{:rf.cofx {:rf/time-ms 1}}`.
- The epoch is restored with `restore-epoch!`, then the record's `:rf.cofx` is replayed under `:strict`.

The results:
- The live run reaches `:done` with `:c 250`.
- The recorded token is `{:rf/time-ms 1}`; the sub fact is missing.
- The replay stays `:idle`, with 1 missing-required.

Control: in the same harness, a generator-backed fact read by a guard, an action, an `:entry` and a raise IS on the record's token (`{:rf/time-ms 1 :meas/gen 1}`), and its replay reproduces the live run.

The existing pin `machine_cofx_sub_source_test.clj` (sub-fact-resolves-live-and-replays-verbatim) passes only because it hand-builds the strict token rather than reading it off an epoch record.

## Fix direction

Make a live sub-source evaluation visible to epoch capture. Two candidate routes:
- emit the same `:rf.cofx/generated` op, or a sibling op that capture also merges, from `deliver-sub-source`;
- have capture read the post-ensure token.

Either way, add a pin that replays from the real epoch record. The epoch lane has machines and epoch on one classpath; `join_strict_mint_epoch_replay_test.clj` is the model.
notes:
== DISPATCH (mayor), 2026-10-20 17:42:42 AUSEST: dispatched to worktree epoch-sub-fact (branch worker/epoch-sub-fact), cut from origin/main at 30f143c43c. Owns deliver-sub-source (core cofx.cljc) and epoch capture.cljc at the change; the flows worker's PR #11576 touches neither. Prefers the route that adds no trace vocabulary.
== WORKER (epoch-sub-fact), PR #11581 (draft until CI green): DONE, pending merge.

Route: deliver-sub-source (core cofx.cljc) now emits the existing dev-only :rf.cofx/generated op ({:rf.cofx/id <:as fact-id> :frame <id> :rf.cofx/value <value>}) on its live-evaluation branch, after the recordable-EDN check. A present fact (replay, or a same-macrostep :raise re-ensure) emits nothing, as with a generator. Epoch capture's find-trigger-event already folds that op into the record's :rf.cofx, so no capture code change and no new trace vocabulary. The other route (capture reads the post-ensure token) has nothing to read: no trace carries the machine's post-ensure record, so it would need a new op or tag plus a router-side write-back.

Measured, same deftest (epoch lane, re-frame.machine-minted-cofx-replay-token-test/sub-fact-reaches-the-epoch-record-and-strict-replay-reproduces-the-run, which reads the REAL epoch record, EDN round-trips it, restore-epoch!, then :strict replay):
- before the fix: exit 1. The record token was {:rf/time-ms 1} with the sub fact absent. The replay stayed :idle and raised :rf.error/missing-required-cofx.
- after the fix: exit 0. The token is {:rf/time-ms 1 :subfact/cfg-v 250}. The replay reaches :done with :c 250, and the query is evaluated 0 times during replay (once live).

Epoch capture already folds that op into the record's token, so capture.cljc changed only in its docstring. Route chosen because it adds no trace vocabulary; reading a post-ensure token had nothing to read (no trace carries it). Pin: a new deftest in epoch/test/re_frame/machine_minted_cofx_replay_token_test.clj takes the token from the REAL epoch record, round-trips it through EDN, restore-epoch!, replays under :strict. title: Cost Fresco's page-global entry cache against a per-boundary ref; adopt the ref only if it wins
description:
## Ruling

Mike approved on 2026-10-21 a costed comparison of two designs:
- Fresco's provisional entry cache;
- a component-local ref per boundary.

The comparison covers total lifecycle concepts, retained memory and a real multi-row workload. Adopt the ref only if it wins. Commit-owned cells and explicit incarnation evidence stay in either design.

## Problem

Measured at trunk c383c6a92e. Collector paths are in `implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/collector.cljs`.

**Today: one page-global entry cache.**
- **The table.** `!entries` (`:645-648`) is keyed by an order-sensitive hash of the whole read sequence (`bucket-key-of`, `:650-671`).
- **Minting.** `entry-for` (`:765-789`) builds one entry per read sequence: keys, key set, `refs`, and the `subscribe` and `snapshot` closures. Every boundary that reads that sequence shares it, so a hit allocates nothing.
- **The reaper.** An unclaimed entry is dropped after `entry-reap-horizon-ms`, 4 ms (`:713-725`), "A MARGIN, NOT A CONTRACT". It is re-armed when the last boundary releases (`make-subscribe`, `:818-842`).
- **Eviction.** `retire-entries-naming!` (`:685-711`) evicts entries when a cell is disposed.
- **Two other users.** Native `use-sub` shares the same cache through `hook-entry` (`:873-881`, `native.cljc:75`), and so "needs no useMemo and no useRef". The tool door finds mounted boundaries by walking `!entries` (`implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/tool.cljs:170-182`, `:188-206`). That walk includes read-free boundaries, which the cell table cannot see.

**The shell is two hooks:** `useContext` and `useSyncExternalStore` (`:1192-1210`). That is the contract:
- invariant I9, "The two-hook ceiling" (`implementation/fresco/spec/invariants.md:24`);
- HD-020(b) (`docs/design/fresco/decisions.md:1498`);
- `shell-hook-ledger` (`implementation/fresco/test_kit/src/re_frame/fresco/test/runtime.cljs:205-210`), which `hook_budget_cljs_test.cljs:166` counts at React's dispatcher. Its claim 1 is that neither hook is `useRef` or `useState`.

A per-boundary ref is a third hook on every boundary.

**`reset-runtime!` stays in either design.** It (`:1310-1338`) empties the entry table and its reaper. It also empties:
- the page-global cells;
- the dirty and deferred sets;
- the cell reaper;
- the generation basis;
- the frame ops.

Outside the collector, 116 files name it: 79 under `implementation/fresco/test/`, 4 in the test kit (2 of its sources, 2 of its tests) and 33 under `tools/xray/test/`.

**The test kit** already wraps it: `reset-bracket` (`runtime.cljs:288-313`) and `render-and-commit!` (`:216-251`). Its `quiesced!` waits past the entry horizon (`:103-124`), and `stats`/`residue` count `:entries` (`:71-101`).

**Retained memory.** `docs/design/fresco/product/budgets.md` records the figures:
- per-read retained heap: Fresco 1,417 B/read against Reagent's 948 (S3, `:404`). That is 1.49×; `docs/design/fresco/product/decision-brief.md:44` rounds it to "~1.4x". The K3 line itself is 943 B/read (`docs/design/fresco/validation.md:159`).
- against UIx: 2,115 against 2,980 (S4, `:405`);
- the read-free boundary shell: 1,100 B and 1,095 B, against a 1,024 B line (S1, S2, `:402-403`).

The instrument is `bench/fresco/src/re_frame/bench/p0_heap.cljs`. Its arms are:
- `p0_fresco.cljs`, which is the shipped package;
- `p0_reagent.cljs` and `p0_uix.cljs`.

It is hand-run (`bench/fresco/README.md`, `npm run bench`).

## Change

**Measure first.** On a branch, build the ref variant:
- the shell holds its boundary's entry in a `useRef`;
- drop `!entries`, the bucket hash and the entry reaper;
- give native `use-sub` and the tool door a source of their own, and count that cost.

Compare the two designs on three axes:
1. **Lifecycle concepts.** List the tables, timers, horizons, reset steps and test-kit instruments each design needs. Include the `use-sub` and tool-door replacements.
2. **Retained memory.** Measure the S1 and S3 rows on `p0_heap`, both arms in the same rounds.
3. **A multi-row workload.** Use the grid example (`implementation/fresco/test/re_frame/fresco/examples/grid/`, 10x10) or `bench/fresco/src/re_frame/bench/fresco/hd8_rows.cljs`. Measure retained heap, body runs and mount time.

**The exit.**
- The ref wins only if it removes concepts and shows no regression beyond the instrument's band on axes 2 and 3. Then adopt it: amend I9, the ledger and `hook_budget_cljs_test`, and drop `quiesced!`'s entry wait and `:entries`.
- Otherwise keep today's design and record the numbers on this bead.

**What stays in either design:** commit-owned cells, the generation basis and incarnation evidence, and `reset-runtime!`.

## Spec and docs that move with it

Only if the ref is adopted:
- `implementation/fresco/spec/invariants.md:24` (I9);
- the collector section of `docs/design/fresco/architecture.md` (`:365-740`, the entry cache at `:567` and the reapers at `:600`);
- the shell's section comment and docstring (`collector.cljs:1166-1201`).

No hot zone.

## Acceptance

- The bead records the three axes for both designs, with each instrument and its run date.
- If the ref is adopted, `npm run test:cljs` (which runs `hook_budget_cljs_test` and the test kit's own tests) and `npm run test:browser` are green.
- If it is not adopted, nothing changes in the tree.

title: Story's enabled?=false production elision is claimed gated but nothing builds it; stale example docstrings say the same
description:
Found by the rf2-mezk2 worker (PR #11622, merged as 5db7f05e31) while re-describing the bundle-isolation gate.

## Problem

**Nothing gates Story's `enabled?=false` production elision, but three places say something does.**
- `tools/story/bench/bundle-size.cjs`'s header says `check-bundle-isolation.cjs` enforces that path.
- tools/story/spec/005-SOTA-Features.md §Verification says the bench exercises it.
- 005's bundle-size section ends "Elision verified by `scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs`."
Neither the gate nor the bench builds a Story-importing app with `enabled?=false`. The old sentinels were also only checked in the no-Story counter, so the gap predates the manifest switch.

**Stale claims in the same family:**
- `examples/core/login/stories_host.cljs` :42-44 and `examples/patterns/nine_states/stories_host.cljs` :45-47 say the bundle-isolation gate fails if a Story or Xray sentinel reaches `:examples/login` / `:examples/nine-states`. No gate checks those builds for Story or Xray: `check-login-bundle-isolation.cjs` checks view-substrate fingerprints only, and nine-states is not released by the gate.
- `tools/story/test/story_feature_load.cjs` :1470: a roster `why` string says "elision is asserted by grepping production bundle outputs".

## Change

Measure first: release-build one Story-importing app with `enabled?=false` (the login example already hosts stories) and count Story body strings in its main.js, with a control from the same build at `enabled?=true`.
- If the body is eliminated and a check is cheap (one counted-string claim beside the trace-tooling elision claim in check-bundle-isolation.cjs, or a bench assertion), add it, so the three claims become true.
- If the body is NOT eliminated, that is a bug in Story's production posture: stop and report it with the numbers.
- Either way, correct the two example docstrings and the roster string to say what is actually checked.

## Acceptance

No doc, docstring or roster string claims a check that does not run. If a check is added, a planted Story body in an `enabled?=false` build turns it red.

title: Trim the reply substrate: no target mapper, no :delivery, no :stale?/:cancelled? flags, no suppress target
description:
## Ruling

Mike approved on 2026-10-21 that the reply substrate drops its unused generality. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/reply.cljc` loses `map-completed-event` and its `::post` transform, the single-valued `:delivery` key with its error `:rf.error/reply-unknown-delivery`, the `:stale?` / `:cancelled?` booleans that restate `:status`, and `suppress`'s unused `target` argument. The Managed-Effects SHOULD about a target-mapping helper is relaxed.

Kept: the status taxonomy, work-id correlation, `:rf.reply/work-status` (Xray's reply panel reads it) and universal stale non-delivery.

## Problem

Measured at trunk c383c6a92e. Paths are under `implementation/` unless stated.

- **The mapper has no production caller.** `map-completed-event` (`reply.cljc:296-333`) is called only by `reply_cljs_test.cljc` and `timer_probe_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:105-109`. `complete` applies `::post` (`:285-286`); `durable-target` refuses it (`:457-462`).
- **`:delivery` has one legal value.** `normalize-target` defaults it to `:append` (`:221`, `:236`); `complete` throws `:rf.error/reply-unknown-delivery` for any other (`:272-284`, `:168`). Only `reply_cljs_test.cljc:287` passes another.
- **The booleans restate `:status`.** `validate-reply` demands them (`:566-574`). Writers: `suppress` (`:786`); `http/src/re_frame/http/reply.cljc:221`; `resources/src/re_frame/resources/reply.cljc:119`; `machines/src/re_frame/machines/reply.cljc:290`, `:404`, `:511`, `:622`, `:654`; `core/test/re_frame/timer_probe.cljc:270`. No production code reads them (Xray's same-named row fields come from trace phases).
- **`suppress` ignores `target`** (`reply.cljc:764-767`). HTTP and resources pass nil (`http/reply.cljc:266`, `:339`; `resources/reply.cljc:134`). Routing threads one through for nothing (`routing/src/re_frame/routing/nav_token.cljc:179`, `:205-208`, `:419`; `routing/reply.cljc:215-218`), as does `timer_probe.cljc:311-313`.

## Change

- Delete `map-completed-event`, `post-key` and the `::post` branches of `complete` and `durable-target`. A normalized target is `{:event … :suppress …}`; `complete` is `(conj event reply)`; `durable-target` keeps its data-only check.
- Delete `:rf.reply/unknown-delivery` from `reply-category->error-id` (three ids remain). A leftover `:delivery` key is ignored.
- `validate-reply` stops requiring the booleans; `:rf.reply/cancelled-missing-marker` and `:rf.reply/stale-missing-flag` go. The writers stop emitting them.
- `suppress` takes `[carried current]` / `[carried current extra]`, and every caller drops its first argument. Drop `target` from `rf.routing.reply/suppress`, `emit-stale-suppressed!`'s `:target` and `timer-probe/suppress`. `:deliver?` stays, always false.
- Docstrings on removed parts go too, including `routing/reply.cljc:130-138`, `:172-175` and `nav_token.cljc:334-336`.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `spec/Managed-Effects.md`: `:103-118`, `:139`, `:141`, `:167-168`, `:226`. §Reply mapping (`:238-251`): SHOULD becomes MAY, the law stays for any helper a runtime ships, the mapped-target paragraph (`:251`) goes.
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`: delete row `:2021`; drop the mapping clauses at `:2019`, `:2022`. **Hot zone.**
- `spec/Conventions.md:66`: drop the three retired `:rf.reply/*` kinds. **Hot zone.**
- `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:3296`, `:3337`, `:3339`, `:3361`, `:3365`. **Hot zone.**
- `spec/005-StateMachines.md:4125`. **Hot zone.**
- `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:561`, `:747`; `docs/api/re-frame.http.md:126`, `:170`; `docs/async/http.md:71`; `examples/core/managed_http_counter/core.cljs:108`; `tools/xray/testbeds/managed_http/core.cljs:225`; Xray's `panels/reply_envelope.cljc:102`.
- "Functor laws" comments: `implementation/README.md:227`, `reply-conformance/deps.edn:9-10`, `shadow-cljs.edn:239` (**hot zone**, comment only).
- Leave `docs/EP/EP-0011` as the record.

## Acceptance

- `completion-keeps-target-vector-metadata` green: a stored continuation completes to the addressed event.
- Delete `functor-laws`, `durable-target-refuses-a-mapped-target`, `suppress-is-universally-non-delivering`, `reply-target-functor-law`, the unknown-delivery row of `reply-throws-carry-canonical-rf-error-id` and the mapped case of `durable-target-is-data-only`.
- `reply-map-schema`: `:cancelled` with a reason and `:stale` with a reason are valid with no boolean; the marker rows go.
- Drop the booleans and `:delivery` from expected maps in `suppress-extra-cannot-override-stale-boundary`, `timer_probe_conformance_cljs_test.cljc`, `machines_reply_cljs_test.cljc`, `spawn_all_reply_envelope_test.clj:29`, `resources_reply_lowering_cljs_test.cljc:53-56`, `http_reply_lowering_cljs_test.cljc:45`, `managed_http_counter_cljs_test.cljs:73`, `resources_mutation_cljs_test.cljc:952` and `reply_envelope_egress_security_cljs_test.cljc:104-107`.
- `git grep` for `map-completed-event`, `unknown-delivery`, `cancelled-missing-marker` and `stale-missing-flag` hits only `docs/EP/` and `.beads/`; a control search for `normalize-target` must hit.
- `scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh`, `npm run test:cljs`, `mkdocs build --strict`, `check_doc_slugs.py` green.

## Sequencing

Five hot zones, one of them comment-only. `rf2-aor6y` (in progress) works in the same security test; land after it or rebase onto it.

title: Fresco defview's top-level mint-view! defeats dead-code elimination: unreferenced views ship, and Xray stays in Story OFF builds (measure first)
description:
Found by the rf2-qgx8q worker (PR #11632, merged 6580cb66e6) while removing Story from enabled?=false production builds.

## Finding

Every Fresco `defview` expands to a top-level `mint-view!` call that Closure keeps, so an UNREFERENCED view is never dropped from an :advanced build. A diagnostic `@pureOrBreakMyCode` on the mint call changed nothing. In Story OFF builds this is what keeps Xray: 1,478,596 B gz remain for counter-with-stories at enabled? false, of which Xray is about 1.08 MB gz (Story's four static Xray requires stubbed: Xray sources 138 -> 3, -3,884,676 raw / -1,082,117 gz). Xray's own ungated top-level forms (register-first-mount-hook!, add-watch, registrations) are a second root.

## Why it matters beyond Story

If defview defeats DCE, every Fresco app ships every view it compiles, referenced or not. Fresco is the taught default. That cost has not been measured.

## Change: MEASURE FIRST, then propose

1. Measure in a plain Fresco app (examples/login-fresco or a scratch app): plant N unreferenced defviews and count what survives :advanced, against a control where the same views are plain defns.
2. Find why mint-view! is kept (registry write at load, a side-effecting top-level call, metadata) and what a view's registration is FOR at runtime (lookup by id, HMR, tooling).
3. If a DCE-friendly expansion keeps every runtime behaviour (HMR, tooling lookups, ids), implement it in Fresco and re-measure Story OFF (the Xray residue should fall). If it changes registration semantics (e.g. views no longer discoverable by id until referenced), STOP and report the options with numbers: that is Mike's call.
4. Option for the Story residue specifically, independent of 3: Story reaches Xray through late-bind seams instead of static requires, plus gating Xray's top-level registration forms.

## Acceptance

The bead records the measured per-view cost and the cause. Either the fix lands with Fresco's suites, test:bundle-isolation and the Fresco budgets green and the Story OFF residue re-measured in 005, or the options go to Mike with numbers.
notes:
== DISPATCHED (mayor), 2026-10-22 01:00:52 AUSEST: worktree fresco-defview-dce, branch worker/fresco-defview-dce, alone, holding no hot zone; measure first, implement only if registration semantics are kept, otherwise stop for Mike with options RE-DISPATCH FENCE: do not put a second worker on this bead or branch until that worker reports.
== WORKER RESULT (fresco-defview-dce), 2026-10-22 AUSEST: DONE for defview; Story residue measured, not cut (not small)

PREMISE HELD IN A PLAIN FRESCO APP. Instrument: `:fresco-release` (consumer app, `:advanced`, goog.DEBUG false) released through the lane helper with `--config-merge` swapping the entry for a probe namespace; main.js bytes, gzip level 9, marker strings. At base 36822444a4: 20 unreferenced defviews (4-element bodies) cost +9,976 B raw / +548 B gz over the bare consumer app (706,106 / 209,834), and all 60 body markers and all 20 view names survived. Control, the same 20 bodies as plain defns: +70 B raw, 0 markers. So about 495 B raw per small view (the gz figure is low only because the 20 bodies are near-identical); a real view costs its body.

CAUSE. Not registration: `publish-view-alias!` already sat behind `debug-enabled?`, so a release build registered nothing. Closure dropped the `def` assignment but kept the bare `mint-view!` call as a statement, because two things in the mint were impure to it. (1) The stamps were written through a goog.DEBUG-folded REBINDING of the component (`component (if debug (traced-boundary …) component)` folds to an alias, and a property write through an alias is not provably local), and through codec helpers that write their argument (`mark-boundary!`, `memoize-boundary!`). (2) `React.memo`, an npm call Closure cannot see into, ran at the mint. Micro-probes isolated it: a local fn with writes on the `fn` literal's own binding drops; the same through the folded alias is kept; helper calls on the local are kept even as statements; the defview do/try/finally wrapper is irrelevant (it drops).

FIX (implemented; registration semantics unchanged). `mint-view!` stamps displayName, frescoBoundary and a new `frescoMemoize` opt-in straight onto the `fn` literal's binding. In dev only, the traced wrapper takes the same stamps by `Object.assign` and the body by `retain-body!`. The codec builds the `React.memo` wrapper at the head's FIRST element (`element-type`) and caches it on the head, so it is still one stable wrapper per head (HMR re-mint gives a fresh head and so a fresh wrapper, as before). Census of runtime readers: in a goog.DEBUG=false build nothing reads the :view registrar for a Fresco view, nothing enumerates minted heads, and `frescoMemo` is read only by `element-type` itself; `(rf/view id)` was already nil in release. A referenced view is still minted once at load: pseudo-names builds show views referenced once inside another view's body and once inside a function called repeatedly stay top-level `var` initialisers.

RE-MEASURED (same instrument, base vs fix):
- plain app, 20 unreferenced + 3 referenced probe views: 716,837 / 210,598 -> 707,023 / 209,987 (-9,814 raw / -611 gz); with 20 unreferenced only the fix's delta over the bare app is +70 raw, identical to the defn control, 0 markers.
- bare consumer app: 706,106 / 209,837 -> 706,149 / 209,845 (+43 / +8, the lazy-memo path).
- :examples/login-fresco: 1,279,600 / 376,271 -> 1,279,640 / 376,290 (+40 / +19; it references every view).
- Story OFF (counter-with-stories, enabled? false): 5,293,788 / 1,476,683 -> 5,293,828 / 1,476,689. UNCHANGED: all 85 Xray view names and all 47 Xray view mints survive both, because Xray is held by other load-time roots.

STORY RESIDUE (step 3): measured, NOT implemented, not small. A root trace over a pseudo-names Story OFF release found the roots holding Xray: Story's `xray-embed` descriptor feeding `panel-catalog` (derived with into/map at load) -> panel mount fns -> registry -> install-fx! -> popout! -> ShellView; Xray's `register-popout-keydown-installer!` call and keybinding `add-watch` -> ShellView; 28 top-level `h/as-component` bridges; 7 `register-first-mount-hook!` forms; 2 `extend-type`s; plus the settings-applier `reset!` and typed-predicate `defmethod`s. Diagnostic builds with those 40 forms in 30 files wrapped in `(when ^boolean js/goog.DEBUG …)` (restored by blob hash afterwards): with this fix 4,009,055 / 1,121,947 (-354,742 gz; all Xray view mints gone, rf-xray- 953 -> 22); WITHOUT this fix 4,939,047 / 1,378,032 (-98,651 gz; rf-xray- 926). So the defview fix is load-bearing for any gating route, but gating alone still leaves about 728 KB gz above the requires-removed diagnostic (393,909 gz), because the libraries Xray requires (zprint still 617 hits) keep their own load-time forms. Only Story reaching Xray without a static require (late-bind seams) takes it out. Gating Xray's load-time forms on goog.DEBUG would also change Xray in any release build that deliberately carries it. Both routes are their own item.

FINDING, NOT FIXED: `h/as-component` is the same class of root. It stamps a displayName built with `str` (an IFn call Closure treats as impure), so every top-level `(def x* (h/as-component x))` keeps itself and its view whether referenced or not. Building the label without `str` would make it droppable like defview; not done here.

GUARD. coord-sentinel-source declares `dropped-row`, never referenced; check_source_coord_elision.cjs (run by npm run test:browser-prod-elision, CI job cljs-browser-prod-elision) requires its view name absent from the :advanced goog.DEBUG=false bundle that carries sentinel-row's. Sabotage: routing one stamp back through `codec/mark-boundary!` -> build exit 0, check exit 1 naming dropped-row; restore matched the HEAD blob.
== PR #11638 (worker/fresco-defview-dce, head ff2601d1b0): local gates all exit 0 — test:browser-prod-elision (40 tests/101 assertions; sabotage of the new unreferenced-view row went red as intended), build:fresco-release, test:fresco-invariants, test:fresco-compile, test:cljs (6584/19133), test:browser (785/3776), test:bundle-isolation, JVM fresco/story/xray (1/41, 1134/2997, 600/1618), check_doc_slugs, mkdocs --strict. CI 80 checks, 56 success / 24 skipped / 0 failing. 005 §Residue carries the re-measured Story OFF numbers. HELD FOR THE MAYOR (classifier hot zone): no Fresco path arms cljs_prod, so test.yml's cljs-browser-prod-elision job (Fresco's elision prod suites and the new guard row) never runs on a Fresco PR; suggested row in the PR body.

Premise held in a plain Fresco app (:fresco-release with a probe entry via --config-merge at 36822444a4): 20 unreferenced defviews cost +9,976 B raw with all 60 body markers and 20 names surviving; the same bodies as plain defns cost +70 B with 0 markers. Cause was not registration (the :view registry write was already debug-only): Closure kept the bare mint-view! call because the stamps went through a goog.DEBUG-folded rebinding of the component and codec helpers that write their argument, and because React.memo (an npm call) ran at the mint. Fix: mint-view! writes its stamps straight onto the fn literal's binding (the dev traced wrapper copies them with Object.assign); the codec builds the React.memo wrapper at the head's first element and caches it on the head (one wrapper per head). Runtime behaviour kept (release builds read no :view registrar entry for a Fresco view, enumerate no heads, and read frescoMemo only in element-type; referenced views still mint once at load). Re-measured: 20 unreferenced views now cost +70 B, identical to the defn control; login-fresco +40 B; Story OFF unchanged (the Xray residue is held by other roots). New guard: coord-sentinel-source gains an unreferenced dropped-row that check_source_coord_elision.cjs requires absent; a planted stamp through codec/mark-boundary! made it fail naming dropped-row. CI at head ff2601d1b0: 80 checks, 56 pass, 24 skip (cljs-browser-prod-elision not armed for Fresco paths; ran locally; the classifier row is routed to the rf2-1m1j0 worker). Story OFF Xray residue measured, not cut: gating 40 top-level forms in 30 Xray/Story files drops every Xray view (1,121,947 gz with this fix, 1,378,032 without, so the fix is load-bearing for any gating route), but about 728 KB gz stays above the requires-removed figure (393,909) because Xray's libraries (zprint) carry load-time roots; only late-bind seams get there, a redesign, left as a decision for Mike. 005 §Residue carries the numbers.

title: nightly red (issue #11639) is a false red: the alert read MCP live conformance as in_progress on a run where it had completed green; re-read non-terminal jobs before calling them unfinished
description:
GitHub issue #11639 (nightly-red, alert signature 9a4f893d0a65, opened 2026-10-21T15:47Z by .github/scripts/nightly_failure_alert.py) is a FALSE RED.

Evidence (mayor, read 2026-10-22):
- The flagged run, scheduled expensive-tests run 39625990407 on 9eca9f177c, concluded SUCCESS. Every job completed success, including "MCP live and client conformance" (started 15:28:22, completed 15:31:13).
- The alert job "Nightly result -> tracking issue" (job 119321331891) ran last, 15:47:37-15:47:55, and printed at 15:47:53: "RED  MCP live and client conformance -> (job in_progress, no verdict)".
- The script's own self-test includes "ANOTHER job still in_progress is red, and named as unfinished", so one in_progress reading of a finished job is enough to open a red issue.
- Likely cause, a CLAIM to confirm: the GitHub API returned a stale in_progress record for a job that had finished 16 minutes earlier. The same class of stale record was seen on PR #11636's check runs (IN_PROGRESS with completed=null while the runs had succeeded).
- Every expensive-tests run since 2026-10-19 is green. The issue now reads greens=1, and it closes itself after 3 consecutive greens.

Change: make the alert script stop reading a finished job as unfinished. Two options:
- re-read jobs the API reports non-terminal, with a short bounded retry, before calling them unfinished;
- or use the workflow graph: if the alert job needs that job, it has terminated by construction, so re-read until terminal and report a stale API record distinctly, rather than as a red step.
Keep a GENUINELY unfinished job red, since the script is right to fail closed on that. Add a self-test case for the stale-record path. Replay with --replay 30 to show no other false reds.

Rules: never close #11639 by hand, and never reference it with Fixes/Closes in a PR. It closes itself after 3 green runs.

Acceptance:
- the script's --self-test passes, with a new case where a job the API reports in_progress resolves to success on re-read and the run reads green;
- a genuinely unfinished job is still red;
- --replay 30 output is attached.
notes:
== DISPATCHED (mayor), 2026-10-22 07:32:56 AUSEST: worktree nightly-alert-stale-job, branch worker/nightly-alert-stale-job, dispatched alone; owns nightly_failure_alert.py and, if needed, expensive-tests.yml; never touches issue #11639 RE-DISPATCH FENCE: do not put a second worker on this bead or branch until that worker reports.
== WORKER (nightly-alert-stale-job), 2026-10-22 AUSEST: done, draft PR #11648 (branch worker/nightly-alert-stale-job)

CAUSE, verified at source: the stale-record claim holds. Run 39625990407 has one attempt and 13 jobs (filter=all), all on one page under per_page=100, with no duplicate names. The alert read the right run id. Its own runner (GitHub Actions 1000990598) differs from mcp-live's (…415). The only read is GET runs/{run}/jobs, which listed a job in_progress although the alert job needs it, so it had terminated by construction. Every endpoint reads it completed success today.

FIX (.github/scripts/nightly_failure_alert.py only; no workflow edit): settle_unfinished re-reads each non-own job the listing reports unfinished, through GET actions/jobs/{id}. It does at most 5 rounds, the first immediate and the rest 15 s apart, so at most 60 s. A record that re-reads finished replaces the listed one whole and is graded by its own conclusion and steps. Its listing is logged as "STALE listing, graded by its re-read", never as a RED line. A job still unfinished after the last round stays red as (job <status>, no verdict). Replay is unchanged.

EVIDENCE: 7 new self-test checks; 6 went red against a no-op stub (exit 1). After the fix the self-test exits 0 with 53 checks (46 baseline + 7). A planted fault (re-read record not substituted) gave exit 1 with 5 FAIL; the restore matches the committed blob hash. Of 47 CI check_*.py invocations run locally, 40 exit 0; 7 could not run (missing pymdownx/markdown/PyYAML, or CI-only jvm_legs input), and CI is relied on for them.
