title: skill(re-frame-migration): guided-views-m11 tells a callback to call the captured :subscribe, a ref-counted hold nothing releases; a one-shot read there wants subscribe-once (reaction bodies excepted)
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 62a62c7472.

## Skill file and section

skills/re-frame-migration/references/guided-views-m11.md:

- §M-11 Decision shape 1 (line 22);
- §"The async listener timer and error-handler class": the general rule (:248), remedy 2 (:262), and "The same two remedies cover …" (:294).

## What it says

- :22: "take (rf/capture-frame) during the render — in a plain fn too — and call its ops from the callback".
- :262: "capture the frame api under an existing scope, then call its :dispatch / :subscribe from the callback. The captured handle … survives the async boundary".
- :248 states the general rule for a bare `rf/dispatch` and a bare `rf/subscribe` alike.
- The ownership caveat appears only inside Form-3 route 2. :118 says "a lifecycle body has no reactive owner: dereferencing the captured :subscribe inside :component-did-mount … neither establishes render ownership nor tears itself down". :122 gives `(rf/subscribe-once query-v {:frame frame})` for a one-shot read. `subscribe-once` occurs only at :120, :122 and :125 of the leaf, all three inside route 2.

## What happened (generic)

v1 code often reads a sub's current value inside a click handler or a timer:

    (fn [_] (let [x @(rf/subscribe [:sel])] (rf/dispatch [:go x])))

Following Decision shape 1, a migrator captures the frame at render and calls the captured :subscribe in the callback. The read returns the right value, so nothing fails. But each call takes a share in the frame's sub cache, with no reactive owner and no `unsubscribe`, so the slot is held for the frame's life. A callback that fires repeatedly takes one share per fire.

Async remedy 2 has the same result. So does remedy 1's `with-frame` at fire time when the callback body subscribes. The spec's one-shot read for this case is `subscribe-once`.

Not every subscribe outside a render is a leak, though. A subscribe taken inside a reaction body is owned by that reaction and released when it disposes (see rf2-ula8a). There, `subscribe-once` would lose reactivity. So the leaf needs to say which op fits which place, not just "use subscribe-once".

## Evidence

- implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:787 (kept-ref-count): "An explicit `subscribe` is a ref-counted hold on every adapter".
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc:619: re-frame.subs "holds ONE reference per (owning reaction, cache slot) and releases it on that owner's dispose". The owner is the reaction currently capturing derefs, which is nil outside a reactive context.
- spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:990: subscribe-once is "the right call from event handlers … and any non-reactive consumer".
- spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:1038: "Every `subscribe` … adds one share; every `unsubscribe` returns one. Imperative subscribers are responsible for the pairing".
- `rf/capture-frame` returns `{:frame :dispatch :dispatch-sync :subscribe}` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:1385). The bundle offers no non-retaining read.
- Observed on a ~170-file app. Two units hit this independently (report-page click handlers, and shared app components). Each learned from the spec, not the skill, that a callback read wants subscribe-once.

## Suggested change

In Decision shape 1, and again in async remedy 2, split the ops:

> - **dispatch**: call the captured op from the callback.
> - **subscribe, one-shot read of the current value**: `(rf/subscribe-once query-v {:frame (:frame captured)})`. It retains nothing. Or capture the value at render and close over it, where the callback should see the render-time value.
> - **subscribe, live read**: a captured `:subscribe` called outside a render takes a share that nothing releases. Call it there only inside a reaction body, which owns it (see the reaction-body case), or with a paired `unsubscribe`, as route 2's imperative recipe does.

A helper that is called both at render and from a callback needs the reactive op on the render path and the one-shot op on the callback path. Comments on rf2-vhqcz describe that case.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
More evidence from the same downstream migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main d53a3faf09: guided-views-m11.md is unchanged since 62a62c7472 (:22, :118, :122 and :262 as quoted above).

1. **A third unit hit this, and found the leaf contradicts itself.** This unit's whole job was converting callback reads to subscribe-once. It found that async remedy 2 (:262: "call its `:dispatch` / `:subscribe` from the callback") collides with the same leaf's Form-3 rule (:118: "never `@(subscribe …)` in a lifecycle hook"). A callback, like a hook, has no reactive owner, so the leaf both prescribes the call and forbids it. (The "shared app components" unit cited above is the second unit; its report asked for the same split.)

2. **Priority.** Following :22 / :262 as written produces a rewrite that leaks one sub-cache share per callback fire, with no error. That is skill text leading a migration into a wrong rewrite. Suggest P2.

3. **The suggested one-shot form drops the capture's incarnation fence.** The change above suggests `(rf/subscribe-once query-v {:frame (:frame captured)})`. But:
   • The bundle's `:frame` is the id the capture was given (implementation/core/src/re_frame/capture_frame.cljc:196, `{:frame frame …}`).
   • The captured `:subscribe` passes `:rf.frame/expected-incarnation` (capture_frame.cljc:216-218). That fence is why core.cljc:1415-1420 can say the api is "pinned to the frame INCARNATION live at capture … even after a new frame is created under the same id".
   • `subscribe-once` with `{:frame <id>}` carries no pin. After a same-id frame re-creation, it reads the successor frame.
   • The bundle offers no non-retaining read that keeps the fence (core.cljc:1400-1403 lists only `:frame`, `:dispatch`, `:dispatch-sync` and `:subscribe`).
   Two suggestions:
   • Skill side: say that the `{:frame (:frame captured)}` form follows the id, not the captured incarnation. That matters only where a frame can be destroyed and re-created under the same id while the callback is still live.
   • API side, for the framework owners (it may deserve its own item): add a `:subscribe-once` op to the capture-frame bundle that reads under the same incarnation pin. A callback's one-shot read then keeps the fence the bundle's other ops already have.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): guided-views-m11 never says a plain defn Form-2/Form-3 outer fn or an r/with-let init is a render-time capture site, and route 2 makes reg-view* registration look required
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 0783705626.

## Skill file and section

skills/re-frame-migration/references/guided-views-m11.md §M-11:

- Decision shape 1 (line 22);
- the Form-2 recipe (:57);
- the Form-3 introduction (:77) and route 2 (:116);
- the "dominant real Form-3" paragraph (:187);
- the `defmulti` paragraph (:234);
- "Scope — fix the call sites, do not over-convert" (:236).

## What it says

- :22: "take `(rf/capture-frame)` during the render — in a plain fn too".
- :57 (Form-2, for `reg-view` only): "The injected `dispatch` / `subscribe` locals are visible to both the outer (once-per-mount) body and the inner render fn".
- :116, route 2: "Register the outer fn through `reg-view*` and capture the frame's non-reactive ops once, in that outer callable … The `reg-view*` outer callable runs during the render, under the live resolver scope, and once per mount — the one site in a Form-3 that both resolves a frame and closes over every lifecycle hook".
- :234 says it plainly for a `defmulti` method: "take `(rf/capture-frame)` in the method body, which runs during the render". Nothing says the same of a plain `defn`'s outer fn or of an `r/with-let` init.
- :236: "Leave as `defn` every other fn".

## What happened (generic)

In Form-2 and Form-3 components, most M-11 sites sit in callbacks the outer fn closes over: a window listener set up in a Form-2 outer fn, or a Form-3 class's did-mount / did-update hooks. The leaf leaves a migrator two readings:

1. Route 2's wording ("Register the outer fn through `reg-view*`", "the `reg-view*` outer callable runs during the render") suggests that registration is what puts the outer fn under the resolver. Every plain-`defn` Form-3 with a frame-touching hook would then need registering through `reg-view*`. By :236's own rule that is over-conversion, and it also mints view ids.
2. :22's "in a plain fn too" suggests that a capture in the plain `defn`'s outer fn is enough.

At runtime, reading 2 is correct. Reagent calls a plain fn component's outer fn inside the wrapper's first render, with `*current-component*` bound, and re-frame2 resolves the frame from the tree whenever a component is in flight. So these are valid capture sites, once per mount:

- the outer fn of a plain `defn` Form-2;
- the outer fn of a plain `defn` Form-3;
- an `r/with-let` init, which also runs in the first render.

Route 2's capture-once retarget caveat (:225) applies to them unchanged.

## Evidence

- Reagent 2.0.1, reagent/impl/component.cljs:115-117: `do-render` binds `*current-component*` around `wrap-render`. At :76-99, `wrap-render` calls the outer fn, and when it returns a fn or a Reagent class it installs that as the render fn. The outer fn therefore runs once per mount, inside the first render.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/provider.cljs:254-297, `current-frame`: tier 1 reads the tree whenever `(current-component)` is non-nil. `tree-frame` (:242-252) reads the shared context slot for a component without `reg-view*`'s `:contextType`, "so a plain fn resolves its provider too" (:263).
- implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/plain_fn_frame_from_tree_dom_cljs_test.cljs pins plain-fn render resolution. No test pins a capture taken in a plain-`defn` outer fn or a `with-let` init.
- In re-frame-migration, the strings "outer fn", "outer callable", "outer body" and "with-let" occur only in guided-views-m11.md (`grep -l` lists that file alone). Control: `reg-view*` occurs in three other leaves.
- Observed on a ~170-file app: three units independently captured in a plain `defn`'s Form-3 outer fn, a Form-2 outer fn, and an `r/with-let` init. Each cited adapter source for why the capture resolves, because the skill does not say.

## Suggested change

In Decision shape 1, or in a short note under the Form-2 and Form-3 recipes, state:

"A plain `defn`'s outer fn (Form-2 returning a render fn, or Form-3 returning `create-class`) and an `r/with-let` init run inside the component's first render, once per mount. A `(rf/capture-frame)` taken there is therefore a valid capture site for the hooks and callbacks they close over, provided the component is mounted in hiccup position (`[my-view …]`). The capture does not need `reg-view*` registration. Register through `reg-view*` only for registry addressing, or for a bare singleton class that has no outer fn."

Then reword route 2's "Register the outer fn through `reg-view*`" so that registration reads as optional for frame capture. The capture-once retarget caveat stands as written.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): M-73 codemod reports a chain that evaluates to valid refs (a def, a helper, into) as an unresolved-M-70 defect it says hard-fails at ns load; the flag cannot be cleared
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 0783705626. Four separate units of one migration hit this independently, so it is merged here into one filing.

## Skill file and section

- skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-call-site-rewrites.md §M-73, the Type B bullet "a chain entry with no mechanically derivable v2 reference" (line 593).
- migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod/README.md §Interceptor chains, "Anything else flags the whole site" (lines 106-113).
- The codemod itself: migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod/src/re_frame/migration/reg_event_codemod.clj, `analyse-meta-map` (lines 826-845), `convert-entry` (775-786) and `interceptors-flag-finding` (1089-1108).

## What it says

- auto-call-site-rewrites.md:593: "Any *other* inline interceptor — a custom value, a var, `(rf/debug)`, a `path` call with a non-literal arg — has no derivable registered id, so the codemod surfaces the whole site as an unresolved **M-70 Type B** finding (`:flag :interceptors`) and leaves it unchanged rather than certifying output v2 rejects at namespace load ... Register the interceptor with `reg-interceptor`, reference it by id, re-run."
- Codemod :834-835: `;; a non-vector `:interceptors` value cannot be certified (v2 rejects it)` then `{:kind :unresolved :offending v}`.
- The finding text (:1099-1108): "... unresolved M-70 (Type B). v2 chains are reference-only: register the interceptor with reg-interceptor and reference it by id ... then re-run the codemod. Left unrewritten — inline values / positional chains hard-fail v2 registration at namespace load."

## What happened (generic)

The codemod is lexical. It accepts a chain only when the `:interceptors` value is a literal vector whose entries are literal keyword ids or literal `[id arg]` 2-vectors. Anything else is reported as the same unresolved-M-70 defect, including chains that are already valid v2 because they EVALUATE to a vector of refs:

- `{:interceptors chain}`, where `chain` is a def bound to a literal ref vector;
- `{:interceptors [x]}`, where `x` is a def bound to a ref;
- `{:interceptors (into [:auth/required] extra)}`, and a helper fn that returns a ref vector.

Those sites register clean: v2 validates the evaluated value at registration (`validate-meta-interceptors!` in implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc, which requires a vector of refs). The flag cannot be cleared, though. Its remedy ("register ... reference it by id ... re-run") is already done, so every rescan re-reports a correctly migrated site, and the finding says the site will "hard-fail v2 registration at namespace load", which is false for it. The comment at :834 says the same thing ("v2 rejects it"). A migration that gates each unit on a clean codemod rescan then gets a choice of two bad options. It can keep a permanent false defect list, or it can rewrite valid computed chains into literals, which is churn the migration does not need and which loses the shared definition.

Failing closed is correct. The codemod cannot see a var's value, and the rf2-8odvg invariant says it must never certify output v2 rejects. The problem is that the docs and the finding do not tell "cannot verify" apart from "is invalid".

## Evidence

- Codemod test reg_event_codemod_test.clj:113 locks `(rf/reg-event :x {:interceptors [my-ic]} ...)` as `:flag :interceptors`, so a var entry is flagged by design.
- `convert-entry` returns `:unresolved` for any entry that is neither a literal ref nor a standard `path` call (:782-786), and `analyse-meta-map` returns `:unresolved` for any non-vector value (:833-835).
- The same pattern was reported four times, by four units of a ~170-file app: a helper returning ref vectors; a def bound to a literal ref vector; `{:interceptors <symbol>}` and `(into [...] sym)`; and "any chain that is not a literal vector, even one that evaluates to refs".

## Suggested change

1. In the docs (auto-call-site-rewrites.md:593 and codemod README:106-113), split the `:flag :interceptors` case in two.
   - An inline interceptor VALUE (a custom `->interceptor` result, `(rf/debug)`, a non-standard `path` call) is a real defect.
   - A symbol or a computed expression, used as the whole chain or as one entry, is INDETERMINATE: the codemod cannot see its value, and the site may already be valid v2. Say that the check for an indeterminate site is the registration itself: load the namespace, or run the boot smoke-test. An invalid value throws `:rf.error/reg-event-bad-interceptors` or `:rf.error/inline-interceptor-removed` there.
2. In the codemod, report the indeterminate case with its own flag or note (for example `:flag :interceptors-indeterminate`, "cannot verify statically; v2 validates at registration"), and drop the "hard-fail at namespace load" sentence for it. Fix the comment at :834 to match. Optionally, resolve a same-file `def` whose value is a literal keyword, ref or ref vector, and accept it when the shape fits its position: an entry, or the whole chain.
3. Say that a rescan gate should count indeterminate sites separately rather than require zero flags, and should not rewrite a valid computed chain into a literal just to silence the codemod.

close_reason: Fixed in PR #11677 (commit "an interceptor chain the codemod cannot see is :interceptors-unverified"). An unresolved chain is now two verdicts, split by certainly-invalid?. (1) :flag :interceptors, note unchanged, means v2 rejects the chain whatever the program binds: a non-reference literal, an inline interceptor map, any re-frame.core call (v1's constructors build values), a standard path call with a non-literal arg, or a structural middle-slot shape. A certainly-invalid entry outranks an unverifiable one in the same chain. (2) :flag :interceptors-unverified means a symbol or other call whose value only evaluation shows: a var, a helper, (into [:auth/required] extra), a custom */path. Its note says the site may already be valid v2, and that the check is registration (load the namespace, after the hand migration for a v1 form): references register clean, and an inline value throws :rf.error/inline-interceptor-removed. It no longer says the site hard-fails. A bare symbol that a same-file top-level def binds to a reference (entry) or to a vector of references (whole chain) is accepted, unless a scope around the registration rebinds it or the name is defined twice. The integration suite registers that output against the real v2 core. Control: the new tests went red on the old source (22 unit failures, 1 integration failure). Six planted faults each went red, and each restore was verified by blob hash. The README and the skill's Type B bullet split the case, and say a rescan gate counts unverified sites separately rather than rewriting a valid computed chain into a literal.

title: migration corpus M-42 #legacy-mount-path presents client-root render! as the drop-in for reagent.dom/render, but legacy render committed synchronously and a React 19 root does not (r/flush does not flush it)
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 0783705626.

## Skill file and section

- migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md, the `#legacy-mount-path` anchor under M-42 (lines 1887-1908).
- skills/re-frame-migration/references/guided-handlers-state.md §M-42 (line 203), which routes there.

## What it says

The recipe swaps `(reagent.dom/render [app] el)` for `(reagent-adapter/render! app-root [app] el)` and explains (:1908): "The first `render!` through the handle creates the React root at the container; every later one … updates that same root". It says nothing about timing.

## What happened (generic)

v1's `reagent.dom/render` used React's legacy root, which committed synchronously: code that mounted and then read the DOM saw the tree. `render!` goes to a React 19 root, whose render is scheduled. `r/flush` drains Reagent's ratom queue only, not the pending root render. So a test (or measuring code) that mounts, flushes and then reads the container sees it empty, and the recipe presented as a drop-in changes that behaviour without saying so.

The one place the corpus names the replacement, `re-frame.test-support/flush-views!` (which wraps React's `act()`), is in O-13, the UIx switch (README:3310). That is not the default path a Reagent migration reads.

## Evidence

- implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs:145-146: `:create-root (rdc/create-root …)`, `:render-root (rdc/render root tree)`.
- README:3310 is the only mention of `flush-views!` as the `r/flush` successor, under O-13.
- Observed on a ~170-file app, where a mount-then-assert test read an empty container.

## Suggested change

Add to `#legacy-mount-path`: "`render!` commits asynchronously. A caller that reads the DOM right after mounting must commit the first render synchronously: in tests, wrap the mount in `re-frame.test-support/flush-views!`; in app code, use React's `flushSync` around `render!`." Also copy the "`r/flush` → `flush-views!`" line from O-13 into the default path's test-layer guidance.

README §M-42 #legacy-mount-path gains two sentences. Unlike the legacy reagent.dom/render, which committed before it returned, render! schedules its commit, as every React 19 root does, and r/flush does not reach it, because r/flush drains only Reagent's own render queue. Code that reads the DOM right after mounting commits the mount synchronously: in a test, (re-frame.test-support/flush-views! #(reagent-adapter/render! app-root [app] el)); in app code, the render! inside React's flushSync. The routing sentence in skills/re-frame-migration/references/guided-handlers-state.md §M-42 gains one clause naming it.

(implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc:1027) runs f inside React's act(), and it is a public row in spec/API.md. The adapter's own adapter_client_root_dom_cljs_test.cljs wraps every render! in react-dom/flushSync before it reads the DOM.

title: nightly: implementation/core :slow-test fails to load login_static_classification_test (login/model not on the :slow-test classpath) — GH #11652
description:
Nightly alert: GitHub issue #11652 ("Nightly `expensive tests` is red"), comment of 2026-10-28T11:55Z. Newly failing step: `JVM implementation/core (slow-test) -> Run JVM slow/stress tests`. Run https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/actions/runs/40680026284 at head 940b600d6e, job 122788345194.

## What fails (from the job log)

    clojure -M:slow-test
    Running tests in #{"test"}
    Execution error (FileNotFoundException) at re-frame.login-static-classification-test/eval51673$loading (login_static_classification_test.clj:1).
    Could not locate login/model__init.class, login/model.clj or login/model.cljc on classpath.

## Cause (measured at trunk 9a1893f835)

- implementation/core/test/re_frame/login_static_classification_test.clj (added by PR #11676, the static-classification slice, rf2-o5rtr) requires the login example's model (`login.model`, examples/core/login/model.cljc).
- implementation/core/deps.edn `:test` puts `../../examples/core` (and other example buckets) on `:extra-paths`, so the PR-time JVM lane loads it fine.
- `:slow-test` (around deps.edn:204) has `:extra-paths ["test"]` only, and runs `re-frame.test-quiet.runner -i :slow -i :stress`, which LOADS every namespace under test/ before filtering to `^:slow`/`^:stress` vars — so a test namespace that requires an example source fails to load under `:slow-test`, and the whole lane exits 1.
- The nightly is the only place `:slow-test` runs, so PR CI could not see it.

Open question for the fix: implementation/core/test/re_frame/examples_test.clj also requires example sources, yet the slow lane was green until tonight — find what keeps it out (runner exclusion, ns metadata, namespace naming) before choosing between (a) giving `:slow-test` the same example `:extra-paths` as `:test`, and (b) whatever mechanism already keeps examples_test out.

## Acceptance

`clojure -M:slow-test` from implementation/core exits 0 locally (it is long — run detached), with the slow/stress test count reported; the fix covers any OTHER test namespace that loads example sources, not just this one; and the `:test` lane is unchanged. Do NOT close issue #11652 by hand: it closes itself after three green nightlies.

title: pair-mcp: stdin EOF exits without answering a tools/call in flight, so a client that pipes its frames and closes stdin gets only the initialize response
description:
On stdin EOF the Pair MCP server closes its nREPL socket and exits 0 without answering a tools/call still in flight. So a client that writes its frames and closes stdin, for example a file or heredoc piped in whole, gets the initialize response and nothing more.

Measured against the live pair fixture, with out/server.js built from 2cf21742af: the three handshake lines (initialize, notifications/initialized, tools/call discover-app) were piped from a file with `--port-file <fixture>/.shadow-cljs/nrepl.port`. Server exit 0; stdout carried only the id-1 initialize result; stderr ended "stdin EOF — client closed stdin — closing nREPL socket and exiting". The same frames from a client that keeps stdin open until the last response returned discover-app and read-sub results, and the server exited 0 once stdin closed.

The documentation now states the rule: skills/re-frame2-pair/references/mcp-transport.md §Headless use, step 5, says to close stdin only once the last response has arrived. bin/call.cjs follows it. The open question is whether shutdown! (server.cljs lifecycle step 6; tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/001-Wire-Protocol.md §Lifecycle) should drain in-flight calls before it exits, so that a naive piped client works. The stdin-eof-shutdown.cjs contract (EOF closes the socket and exits promptly) would need to keep holding, with a bound on the drain.

This is a suggestion, not a defect against the current spec, which says only "client closes stdin → Node EOF → process exits". It is fine to close it as wontfix with the documented rule as the answer.
notes:
COORDINATOR DECISION (mayor, 2026-10-29 01:40:53 AUSEST), under the project stance (low friction for the programmer and the AI they use): ship a BOUNDED drain of in-flight calls on stdin EOF, so a client that pipes its frames and closes stdin gets its answers; EOF with nothing in flight still exits promptly (stdin-eof-shutdown contract holds). Wontfix with the documented rule remains the fallback if the drain needs a new process model. Clustered with rf2-synuj.4, rf2-p36ux, rf2-8czvd; QUEUED until PR #11708 (worker/pair-epoch-reads) MERGES.

     RELEASES ON: THE PR MERGING. Not on the report.
     A reported worker still has an open PR editing those files; a second worker
     branched off trunk would not carry them, and the two diffs collide at merge.
     The test is: has the PR that edits this surface MERGED?

but DO NOT dispatch onto that surface.
close_reason:
Done in PR #11715 (commit "pair-mcp: on stdin EOF the server answers the tools/call requests already in flight ..."). This was the coordinator's decision: ship a bounded drain. It needed no new process model.

How it works. server.cljs tracks each tools/call handler's Promise by JSON-RPC request id (track-call!, wired in boot!). On stdin EOF, shutdown! does the following in order:
- waits one macrotask, because a request read in the same chunk as the EOF reaches its handler only after the stdin end event fires;
- waits for the tracked calls;
- gives the SDK a macrotask to write their responses;
- flushes stdout;
- runs the existing teardown: close the nREPL socket, close the server, exit 0.

With nothing in flight it costs one macrotask. The unchanged test/stdin-eof-shutdown.cjs still passes all three cases inside its 4000 ms bound.

The bound is nrepl/default-timeout-ms (30000 ms), one nREPL round-trip's own deadline, now public; it was reused rather than adding a new constant. At the bound the server logs "drain bound 30000 ms reached — abandoning tools/call <tool> (id <id>)" on stderr and exits 0.

Control: test/stdin-eof-drain.cjs writes initialize, notifications/initialized and one eval-cljs tools/call to a file and hands the file to the server as stdin. A fake nREPL answers each op 300 ms late.
- Against the pre-change build: exit 1, "stdout carried ids [1]". That is the bead's measurement.
- Against the branch build: exit 0, id 2 answered before exit, stderr "answering 1 tool call(s) in flight before exit: eval-cljs (id 2)".

The drain test runs after stdin-eof-shutdown.cjs inside npm run test:stdin-eof-shutdown, so the test.yml and expensive-tests.yml steps run it with no workflow change.

Bound path, checked by hand: with no --port-file, the call waits on a roots/list that the closed stdin cannot answer. The server exited 0 at 30448 ms with the abandon line naming eval-cljs (id 2).

spec/001-Wire-Protocol.md §Lifecycle and mcp-transport.md §Headless use step 5 now say that closing stdin early is safe within the bound. Step 5 keeps the --port-file advice, because a closed stdin cannot answer roots/list.

Gates, all exit 0: build, test:stdin-eof-shutdown (shutdown and drain), stdio-roundtrip, test:call-cli, npm test (397 tests, 1153 assertions) and MCP conformance.

title: Routing navigate error ids: update the four texts that still name schema-validation-failure for every refusal
description:

That change made a `:rf.route/navigate` whose `route-url` throw is NOT a schema verdict report the throw's own `:rf.error/id` at `:where :event` (an unregistered `:to` is `:rf.error/no-such-route`, a missing path param `:rf.error/missing-route-param`, an uncaptured one `:rf.error/route-url-validation`); only a `:params` / `:query` schema verdict still reports `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` (or `:rf.error/malformed-schema`). title: check_skill_redirect_anchors.py resolves SKILL-REDIRECT.md and skills/ against the cwd, so it fails outside the repo and grades a sibling's tree from inside one
description:
`scripts/check_skill_redirect_anchors.py` resolves `REDIRECT_FILE = pathlib.Path("SKILL-REDIRECT.md")` and `SKILLS_DIR = pathlib.Path("skills")` (lines 34-35) against the CURRENT DIRECTORY, not against the script's own location. The fast-PR spine therefore fails the gate when launched from outside the repo, even when the spine is given by absolute path. And launched from a sibling worktree's directory, the gate silently grades THAT tree, which is the failure AGENTS.md §Running Gates describes for gates that do not pin their root.

Resolve both paths from `pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]`, as the other `scripts/check_*.py` gates do. Prove it by running the gate from an unrelated directory (it must pass) and from a sibling tree carrying a planted dead label (it must still grade its OWN tree).

Found by the skills review of re-frame2-pair-retro (rf2-0ov0l.6, PR #11747), whose first spine run failed this way.
